Forty are supramundane; the supramundane consciousnesses are forty. In summary, all consciousness-arisings are one hundred and twenty-one. In brief, there are one hundred and twenty-one. Hereafter, having extracted from these consciousnesses I have mentioned the arising of those factors beginning with contact, one by one, I will explain and teach them for the sake of the monks' study of consciousness and mental factors.

93. Ekaggatā cittekaggatā manakkāro manasikāro jīvitaṃ phassapañcakaṃ ete aṭṭha cetasikā avinibbhogā aññamaññato avigatā ekuppādā samānuppādā sahakkhayā sahavayā.

93. One-pointedness (ekaggatā), one-pointedness of mind (cittekaggatā), attention (manakkāro), application of mind (manasikāro), life (jīvitaṃ), and the pentad beginning with contact (phassapañcakaṃ): these eight mental factors are inseparable, not departed from one another, arising together, arising simultaneously, ceasing together, and decaying together.

94. Phasso ca vedanā saññā, cetanā jīvitindriyaṃ ekaggatā manakkāro ime cetasikā sabbasādhāraṇā sabbacittehi sādhāraṇā, sabbacittānaṃ sādhāraṇā vā.

94. Contact, feeling, perception, volition, the life faculty, one-pointedness, and attention—these mental factors are universals, common to all consciousnesses, or common for all consciousnesses.

95. Vitakko pañcapaññāsa-cittesu samudīrito. Cāro chasaṭṭhicittesu vitakko tāva dvipañcaviññāṇavajjitakāmāvacaresu ceva ekādasasu paṭhamajjhānacittesu cāti pañcapaññāsacittesu [M 0.0025] bhagavatā samudīrito. Vicāro dvipañcaviññāṇavajjitakāmāvacaracittesu ekādasasu paṭhamajjhānacittesu ca ekādasasu dutiyajjhānacittesu cāti chasaṭṭhicittesu jāyati. Ettha etasmiṃ vacane saṃsayo natthi.

95. Initial application is declared in fifty-five consciousnesses. Sustained application is in sixty-six consciousnesses. Initial application is declared by the Blessed One in fifty-five consciousnesses: that is, in the sense-sphere consciousnesses excluding the ten sense consciousnesses, and in the eleven first jhāna consciousnesses. Sustained application arises in sixty-six consciousnesses: that is, in the sense-sphere consciousnesses excluding the ten sense consciousnesses, in the eleven first jhāna consciousnesses, and in the eleven second jhāna consciousnesses. In this statement there is no doubt.

96. Ekapaññāsacittesu, pīti tesaṭṭhiyā sukhaṃ pītidomanassupekkhāsahagatakāyaviññāṇacatutthajjhānavajjitesu ekapaññāsacittesu jāyati. Sukhaṃ domanassadukkhupekkhāsahagatavajjitesu tesaṭṭhicittesu jāyati. Upekkhā somanassasukhadukkhasahagatavajjitesu pañcapaññāsacittesu jāyati. Dukkhaṃ akusalavipākakāyaviññāṇapaṭighasahagatesu tīsu cittesu jāyati.

96. In fifty-one consciousnesses, rapture; in sixty-three, pleasure. Rapture arises in fifty-one consciousnesses, those being the ones excluding consciousnesses accompanied by displeasure, equanimity, body-consciousness, and the fourth jhāna. Pleasure arises in sixty-three consciousnesses, excluding those accompanied by displeasure, pain, and equanimity. Equanimity arises in fifty-five consciousnesses, excluding those accompanied by joy, pleasure, and pain. Painful feeling arises in three consciousnesses: in the unwholesome resultant body-consciousness and in the two consciousnesses accompanied by aversion.

97. Hoti dvāsaṭṭhicittesu, somanassindriyaṃ pana domanassadukkhasukhupekkhāsahagatavajjitesu [V 1.0021] dvāsaṭṭhicittesu jāyati. Dukkhindriyaṃ panekasmiṃ akusalavipāke kāyaviññāṇe jāyati. Tathekamhi sukhindriyaṃ tathā ekasmiṃ puññapāke kāyaviññāṇe hoti.

97. The faculty of joy is in sixty-two consciousnesses; it arises in those consciousnesses that exclude ones accompanied by displeasure, pain, pleasure, and equanimity. The faculty of pain arises in the one unwholesome resultant body-consciousness. Likewise, the faculty of pleasure is in the one wholesome resultant body-consciousness.

98. Pañcuttarasate citte, vīriyaṃ āha nāyako jino pañcadvārāvajjanadvipañcaviññāṇasampaṭicchanasantīraṇavajjite pañcuttarasate citte vīriyaṃ āha kathesi. Catuttarasate citte, samādhindriyamabrvi vicikicchāsahagatadvipañcaviññāṇasampaṭicchanasantīraṇapañcadvārāvajjanavajjite catuttarasate citte samādhindriyaṃ avoca.

98. The Leader, the Conqueror, said that energy arises in one hundred and five consciousnesses; he stated that it arises in the one hundred and five consciousnesses that exclude five-door adverting, the ten sense consciousnesses, receiving, and investigating. He spoke of the faculty of concentration in one hundred and four consciousnesses; he said it is in the one hundred and four consciousnesses that exclude those accompanied by doubt, the ten sense consciousnesses, receiving, investigating, and five-door adverting.

99. Sabbāhetukacittāni, ṭhapetvā cekahetuke sabbāni aṭṭhārasa ahetukacittāni ekahetukacittadvayañca ṭhapetvā sesasmiṃ ekuttarasate citte chandassa uppattiṃ uddise paṇḍito katheyya.

99. Having excluded all eighteen rootless consciousnesses and the two single-rooted consciousnesses, a wise person should point out the arising of desire-to-do in the remaining one hundred and one consciousnesses.

100. Ṭhapetvā [M 0.0026] dasa viññāṇe cakkhuviññāṇādike dasa viññāṇe ca vicikicchāyutampi cittaṃ ṭhapetvā sesasmiṃ dasuttarasate citte adhimokkho bhagavatā udīrito.

100. Having excluded the ten consciousnesses beginning with eye-consciousness, and also the consciousness conjoined with doubt, the Blessed One declared that determination arises in the remaining one hundred and ten consciousnesses.

101-2. Saddhā sati hirī ottappaṃ alobho adoso tatramajjhattaṃ cha yugaḷā ca iti ime ekūnavīsati dhammā niyatā hutvā ekanavutiyā citte jāyanti. Ekūnavīsati dhammā ahetukesu aṭṭhārasasu apuññesu dvādasasu akusalesu na jāyare na jāyanti.

101-102. Faith, mindfulness, moral shame, moral dread, non-greed, non-hatred, neutrality of mind, and the six pairs—these nineteen factors, being constant, arise in ninety-one consciousnesses. These nineteen factors do not arise in the eighteen rootless consciousnesses nor in the twelve unwholesome consciousnesses.

103. Ekūnāsītiyā citte, paññā jāyati sabbadā paññā dvādasaakusalaaṭṭhārasaahetukamahākusalañāṇavippayuttamahāvipākañāṇavippayuttamahākiriyāñāṇavippayuttavajjite ekūnāsītiyā citte jāyati. Aṭṭhavīsatiyā citte, karuṇāmuditā siyuṃ karuṇāmuditā aṭṭhasu mahākusalesu, aṭṭhasu mahākiriyāsu, rūpāvacarapañcamajjhānavajjitesu dvādasarūpāvacaresu cāti aṭṭhavīsatiyā cittesu siyuṃ bhaveyyuṃ.

103. Wisdom arises in seventy-nine consciousnesses; it arises in those consciousnesses that exclude the twelve unwholesome, the eighteen rootless, the great wholesome dissociated from knowledge, the great resultant dissociated from knowledge, and the great functional dissociated from knowledge. Compassion and appreciative joy may be in twenty-eight consciousnesses; they may be in the eight great wholesome, the eight great functional, and in the twelve form-sphere consciousnesses that exclude the fifth jhāna.

104. Kāmāvacarapuññesu, sabbalokuttaresu ca kāmāvacaramahākusalesu cittesu sabbesu lokuttaresu cāti saha aṭṭhake cattālīsavidhe citte viratittayaṃ hoti.

104. The three abstinences occur in the sense-sphere wholesome consciousnesses and in all supramundane consciousnesses; that is, they occur in the eight great wholesome sense-sphere consciousnesses and in all forty supramundane consciousnesses, thus in forty-eight types of consciousness.

105. Saddhā [V 1.0022] sati hirottappaṃ alobhādittayampi ca yugaḷāni cha ca majjhattaṃ karuṇāmuditāpi ca.

105. Faith, mindfulness, moral shame, moral dread, the triad beginning with non-greed, the six pairs, neutrality, and also compassion and appreciative joy.

106. Tathā tisso viratiyo sabbe te pañcavīsati dhammā mahākusalacittasampayuttaabyākatacittasampayuttāti kusalena sabbesuyeva dhammesu chekena vijitaṅgaṇena pakāsitā.

106. Likewise the three abstinences. All these twenty-five factors—associated with great wholesome consciousness and indeterminate consciousness—have been declared by the Skillful One, the expert in all things, the conqueror of the battleground.

107. Ahirīkaṃ [M 0.0027] anottappaṃ, moho uddhaccameva cāti ime cattāro dhammā niyatā hutvā dvādasāpuññacittesuyeva dvādasaakusalacittesuyeva jāyare jāyanti.

107. Shamelessness, lack of moral dread, delusion, and restlessness—these four factors, being fixed, arise only in the twelve demeritorious consciousnesses, that is, only in the twelve unwholesome consciousnesses.

108-9. Lobho doso ca moho ca, māno diṭṭhi ca saṃsayo vicikicchā middhaṃ uddhaccaṃ kukkuccaṃ thinaṃ macchariyampi ca ahirikaṃ anottappaṃ issā ca domanassakaṃ ete dhammā akusalā akusalacittasampayuttā ekantena mahesinā vijitaṅgaṇavigatamalena vuttā.

108–109. Greed, hatred, and delusion; conceit, wrong view, and doubt or indecision; torpor, restlessness, worry, and sloth; stinginess, shamelessness, and lack of moral dread; envy and displeasure—these factors are unwholesome, associated with unwholesome consciousness, and have been declared by the Great Sage—the victorious one, free from stain—to be exclusively so.

110. Lobho aṭṭhasu lobhamūlesu cittesu bhagavatā niddiṭṭho dassito. Diṭṭhi catūsu diṭṭhisampayuttesu cittesu vuttā. Māno diṭṭhivippayuttesu catūsu gāhūpavādappabhindanena vutto. Doso dvīsu eva paṭighasampayuttesu cittesu munindena vutto.

110. Greed is pointed out by the Blessed One in the eight types of consciousness rooted in greed. Wrong view is stated in the four types of consciousness associated with wrong view. Conceit is stated in the four types of consciousness dissociated from wrong view, by way of breaking up grasping and disparagement. Hatred is stated by the Lord of Sages in the two types of consciousness associated with aversion.

111. Issāmaccherakukkuccā dvīsu dosamūlesu cittesu jāyanti, no saha saha no jāyanti, ekekova jāyantīti attho. Vicikicchā panekasmiṃ vicikicchā pana ekasmiṃ vicikicchāsahagatacitte jāyati. Thinamiddhaṃ pañcasu sasaṅkhārikaakusalacittesu jāyati.

111. Envy, avarice, and remorse arise in the two types of consciousness rooted in hatred; they do not arise together but one at a time—this is the meaning. Doubt, however, arises in the one consciousness accompanied by doubt. Sloth and torpor arise in the five prompted unwholesome types of consciousness.

112-3. Phasso ca vedanā saññā, cetanā jīvitaṃ mano vitakko ca vicāro ca pīti vīriyaṃ samādhi ca chando cevādhimokkho ca manasikāro ca cuddasa dhammā kusalā ca kusalacetasikā ca honti. Akusalā ceva akusalacetasikā ceva abyākatāpi ca abyākatacetasikā ca honti.

112–113. Contact, feeling, perception, volition, life faculty, mind, applied thought, sustained thought, zest, energy, concentration, zeal, decision, and attention—these fourteen states are wholesome mental factors, unwholesome mental factors, and also indeterminate mental factors.

114. Ekūnatiṃsacittesu, jhānaṃ pañcaṅgikaṃ mataṃ catūsu somanassasahagatākusalesu, dvādasasu somanassasahagatamahākusalamahāvipākamahākiriyacittesu, sukhasantīraṇahasituppādacittesu[M 0.0028][V 1.0023], tīsu rūpapaṭhamajjhānacittesu, aṭṭhasu lokuttarapaṭhamajjhānacittesu cāti ekūnatiṃsacittesu pañcaṅgikaṃ pañcāvayavajhānayuttaṃ jhānaṃ sugatena mataṃ. Upekkhāsahagatāni cattāri lobhamūlāni ca dve dosamūlāni ca dve mohamūlāni ca manodhātuttikañca upekkhāsahagatā tisso ahetukamanoviññāṇadhātuyo ca dvādasupekkhāsahagatāni mahākusalamahāvipākakiriyacittāni tīṇi rūpadutiyajjhānacittāni aṭṭha lokuttaradutiyajjhānacittāni cāti sattatiṃsa cittāni catujhānaṅgayuttāni catujhānāvayavayuttāni iti evaṃ niddise katheyya.

114. In twenty-nine types of consciousness, jhāna is considered five-factored: in the four unwholesome consciousnesses accompanied by joy; in the twelve great wholesome, great resultant, and great functional consciousnesses accompanied by joy; in the investigating consciousness accompanied by pleasure and the smile-producing consciousness; in the three first jhāna consciousnesses of the form sphere; and in the eight supramundane first jhāna consciousnesses. Thus in these twenty-nine types of consciousness, the five-factored jhāna, endowed with five components, is regarded by the Well-Gone One. The following thirty-seven types of consciousness are yoked with four jhāna factors: the four types of consciousness rooted in greed accompanied by equanimity, the two rooted in hatred, the two rooted in delusion, the mind-element triad, the three rootless mind-consciousness-elements accompanied by equanimity, the twelve great wholesome, great resultant, and functional consciousnesses accompanied by equanimity, the three second jhāna consciousnesses of the form sphere, and the eight supramundane second jhāna consciousnesses. Thus one should declare that these are endowed with the four jhāna factors.

115. Ekādasavidhaṃ cittaṃ, tivaṅgikamudīritaṃ tīṇi rūpāvacaratatiyajjhānacittāni, aṭṭhalokuttaratatiyajjhānacittāni cāti ekādasavidhaṃ cittaṃ tivaṅgikaṃ tiavayavajhānayuttaṃ, cha rūpāvacaracatutthajjhānapañcamajjhānacittāni, dvādasārūpāvacaracittāni, soḷasa lokuttaracatutthajjhānapañcamajjhānacittāni cāti catutiṃsavidhaṃ cittaṃ duvaṅgikaṃ dviavayavajhānayuttaṃ udīritaṃ jinena īritaṃ.

115. Eleven types of consciousness are declared as three-factored: the three third-jhāna consciousnesses of the form sphere and the eight supramundane third-jhāna consciousnesses. Thus these eleven types of consciousness are three-factored, endowed with three jhāna components. Thirty-four types of consciousness are declared as two-factored: the six fourth-jhāna and fifth-jhāna consciousnesses of the form sphere, the twelve formless-sphere consciousnesses, and the sixteen supramundane fourth-jhāna and fifth-jhāna consciousnesses. Thus these thirty-four types of consciousness are two-factored, endowed with two jhāna components, as proclaimed by the Conqueror.

116. Sabhāvenāvitakkesu, jhānaṅgāni na uddhare sabhāvena pakatiyā avitakkesu vitakkavirahitesu dvipañcaviññāṇesu jhānaṅgāni jhānāvayavāni jino na uddhare. Ayametthādhippāyo – aññattha vitakko jhānacittena vippahīno bhāsito, imesu pana neva jhānacittena pahīnā, pakatiyā vitakkavirahitāni dvipañcaviññāṇāni sabbāhetukacittesu maggaṅgāni maggāvayavāni jino na uddhare na deseyya.

116. In consciousnesses that are by nature without applied thought, the jhāna factors are not pointed out. Naturally, in the two sets of five sense-consciousnesses, which are without applied thought, the Victor did not point out the jhāna factors or their components. The meaning here is this: elsewhere, applied thought is said to be abandoned by a jhāna consciousness, but in these cases, it is not abandoned by a jhāna consciousness, as they are naturally devoid of applied thought. In all rootless consciousnesses, the Victor does not point out or teach the path factors or their components.

117. Budho jino dvipañcaviññāṇesu manodhātuttike ca tīsu santīraṇesu cāti soḷasacittesu tīṇindriyāni [M 0.0029] vade katheyya. Ekasmiṃ pana cattāri ekasmiṃ vicikicchāsahagatacitte cattāri indriyāni honti, ekādasasu akusalacittesu vicikicchāyuttacittavajjitesu hasituppāde ceva voṭṭhabbanacitte cāti terasasu cittesu pañca indriyāni budho bhagavā uddhare uddhareyya.

117. The Enlightened One, the Victor, would declare three faculties in sixteen types of consciousness: the two sets of five sense-consciousnesses, the mind-element triad, and the three investigating consciousnesses. In one consciousness, however, there are four faculties; that is, in the one consciousness accompanied by doubt there are four faculties. In thirteen types of consciousness—the eleven unwholesome consciousnesses apart from the one accompanied by doubt, the smile-producing consciousness, and the determining consciousness—the Enlightened One, the Blessed One, would point out five faculties.

118. Satta dvādasacittesu, indriyāni jinobrvi jino buddho ñāṇavippayuttamahākusalamahāvipākamahākiriyāsaṅkhātesu dvādasacittesu satta indriyāni abrvi kathesi, ekenūnesu aṭṭheva, cattālīsamanesu ca jino ñāṇasampayuttamahākusalamahāvipākamahākiriyāsaṅkhātesu [V 1.0024] dvādasasu cittesu, pañcadasasu rūpesu, dvādasasu arūpesu cāti ekenūnesu cattālīsamanesu aṭṭheva indriyāni abrvi.

118. The Victor declared seven faculties in twelve types of consciousness. That is, in the twelve consciousnesses dissociated from knowledge—the great wholesome, great resultant, and great functional—the Victor declared seven faculties. And in thirty-nine minds, he declared eight faculties. That is, in the twelve great wholesome, great resultant, and great functional consciousnesses associated with knowledge, in the fifteen form-sphere consciousnesses, and in the twelve formless-sphere consciousnesses—thus in these thirty-nine minds—the Victor declared eight faculties.

119. Cattālīsāya lokuttaracittesu navakaṃ indriyanavakaṃ nāyako abrvi kathesi. Evaṃ indriyayogopi, veditabbo vibhāvinā evaṃ iminā mayā vuttappakārena cittesu indriyayogo vibhāvinā visesena paññaṃ bhāvetuṃ pakāsetuṃ sīlametassāti vibhāvī, tena veditabbo.

119. In the forty supramundane types of consciousness, the Leader declared a set of nine faculties. Thus the combination of faculties should be understood by the discerning one. That is, in this way that I have explained, the combination of faculties in the types of consciousness should be understood by a discerning one, that is, by one whose nature it is to develop and manifest wisdom with distinction.

120. Amaggaṅgāni nāmettha, aṭṭhārasa ahetukā ettha etesu cittesu aṭṭhārasa ahetukā natthi maggo etesūti amaggaṅgāni nāma, jhānaṅgāni na vijjanti, viññāṇesu dvipañcasu dvipañcaviññāṇesu jhānaṅgānipi na saṃvijjanti.

120. Herein, the eighteen rootless types of consciousness are named 'without path factors.' That is, because there is no path in these eighteen rootless types of consciousness, they are named 'without path factors.' Jhāna factors are not found in the two sets of five sense-consciousnesses; the jhāna factors do not exist there.

121. Ekaṃ cittaṃ dumaggaṅgaṃ ekaṃ vicikicchāsahagatacittaṃ dumaggaṅgaṃ dumaggāvayavaṃ, catūsu diṭṭhivippayuttākusalacittesu ca dvīsu paṭighayuttesu ca uddhaccayuttesu cāti sattasu cittesu ca timaggaṅgāni timaggāvayavāni honti. Cattālīsāya cittesu[M 0.0030], maggo so caturaṅgiko catūsu diṭṭhisampayuttākusalesu ñāṇavippayuttamahākusalamahāvipākamahākiriyāsaṅkhātesu dvādasasu cittesu ca rūpāvacaradutiyatatiyacatutthapañcamajjhānasaṅkhātesu dvādasasu rūpāvacaresu, dvādasasu arūpāvacaresu cāti cattālīsāya cittesu caturaṅgiko maggo caturāvayavo maggo hoti.

121. One type of consciousness has two path factors; that is, the one consciousness accompanied by doubt has two path components. In seven types of consciousness there are three path factors: in the four unwholesome types of consciousness dissociated from wrong view, the two associated with aversion, and the one associated with restlessness. In forty types of consciousness, the path is four-factored: in the four unwholesome types of consciousness associated with wrong view; in the twelve great wholesome, great resultant, and great functional consciousnesses dissociated from knowledge; in the twelve form-sphere consciousnesses of the second, third, fourth, and fifth jhānas; and in the twelve formless-sphere consciousnesses. Thus in these forty types of consciousness, the path is four-factored, a path with four components.

122. Pañcaddasasu cittesu, maggo pañcaṅgiko mato ñāṇasampayuttamahākusalamahāvipākamahākiriyāsaṅkhātesu dvādasasu, tīsu rūpapaṭhamajjhānacittesu cāti pañcaddasasu cittesu pañcaṅgiko pañcāvayavo maggo bhagavatā mato. Dvattiṃsacittesu maggo sattaṅgikopi ca lokuttaradutiyatatiyacatutthapañcamajjhānasaṅkhātesu dvattiṃsacittesu maggo sattaṅgiko sattāvayavo hoti.

122. In fifteen types of consciousness, the path is considered five-factored: in the twelve great wholesome, great resultant, and great functional consciousnesses associated with knowledge, and in the three first jhāna consciousnesses of the form sphere. Thus in these fifteen types of consciousness, the path is five-factored, a path with five components, as regarded by the Blessed One. In thirty-two types of consciousness, the path is seven-factored: in the thirty-two supramundane consciousnesses of the second, third, fourth, and fifth jhānas. Thus in these thirty-two types of consciousness, the path is seven-factored, a path with seven components.

123. Maggo aṭṭhasu cittesu maggaphalavasena aṭṭhasu lokuttaracittesu maggo aṭṭhaṅgiko aṭṭhāvayavo hoti. Iti parisamāpane. Tu padapūraṇe. Evaṃ iminā mayā vuttappakārena sabbacittesu maggaṅgāni maggāvayavāni dhīro uddhareyya, deseyyāti attho.

123. In eight types of consciousness, the path is eight-factored; that is, in the eight supramundane consciousnesses of the first jhāna, by way of path and fruition, the path is eight-factored, having eight components. The word `iti` marks the conclusion. The particle `tu` is a mere expletive. Thus, in the manner described by me, a wise person should point out and teach the path factors and path components in all types of consciousness—this is the meaning.

124. Balāni dve dvicittesu hasituppādavoṭṭhabbanasaṅkhātesu dvīsu cittesu dve balāni honti[V 1.0025]. Ekasmiṃ tīṇi dīpaye ekasmiṃ vicikicchāyutte tīṇi balāni dhīro dīpaye pakāseyya. Vicikicchāyuttato sesesu ekādasasu akusalesu cattāri balāni honti. Cha dvādasasu ñāṇavippayuttamahākusalamahāvipākamahākiriyāsaṅkhātesu dvādasasu cittesu cha balāni hontīti dhīro niddise katheyya.

124. There are two powers in two types of consciousness: in the two consciousnesses designated as smile-producing and determining. In one, a wise person should show three powers; that is, in the one consciousness associated with doubt, a wise person should show and declare three powers. In the remaining eleven unwholesome types of consciousness, there are four powers. In the twelve great wholesome, great resultant, and great functional consciousnesses dissociated from knowledge, there are six powers—thus a wise person should point out.

125. Ekūnāsītiyā [M 0.0031] satta ñāṇasampayuttamahākusalamahāvipākamahākiriyāsaṅkhātesu dvādasasu kāmāvacaracittesu, sattavīsatiyā mahaggatacittesu, cattālīsalokuttaracittesu cāti ekūnāsītiyā cittesu satta balāni honti. Soḷasevābalāni tu dvipañcaviññāṇāni ca tisso manodhātuyo ca tīṇi santīraṇāni cāti soḷasa eva cittāni abalāni balavirahitāni honti, evaṃ iminā mayā vuttappakārena cittaṃ sabalaṃ balena sahagataṃ abalampi ca balavirahitañcāpi cittaṃ viññeyyaṃ dhīrena vijānitabbaṃ.

125. In seventy-nine types of consciousness, there are seven powers: in the twelve sense-sphere consciousnesses termed great wholesome, great resultant, and great functional, associated with knowledge; in the twenty-seven sublime types of consciousness; and in the forty supramundane types of consciousness. Thus in these seventy-nine types of consciousness, there are seven powers. Sixteen types of consciousness, however, are without powers: the two sets of five sense-consciousnesses, the three mind-elements, and the three investigating consciousnesses. Thus these sixteen types of consciousness are powerless, devoid of power. In this way, a wise person should understand consciousness that is with power, accompanied by power, and also consciousness that is without power, devoid of power.

126. Jhānaṅgamaggaṅgabalindriyāni, cittesu jāyanti hi yesu yāni yesu cittesu yāni jhānaṅgamaggaṅgabalaindriyāni jāyanti, mayā samāsena samuddharitvā asaṃsaṭṭhaṃ uddharitvā tesu cittesu sabbānipi tāni jhānaṅgamaggaṅgabalaindriyāni samāsena saṅkhepena mayā buddhadattācariyena vuttāni kathitāni.

126. The jhāna factors, path factors, powers, and faculties that arise in the various types of consciousness—all these, having been extracted concisely and without confusion, have been stated and explained by me, the teacher Buddhadatta, in summary and in brief.

Iti abhidhammāvatāraṭīkāya

Thus in the Subcommentary on the Abhidhammāvatāra.

Cetasikavibhāganiddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Exposition of the Division of Mental Factors is concluded.

Tatiyo paricchedo.

The Third Chapter.

4. Catuttho paricchedo

4. The Fourth Chapter.

Ekavidhādiniddesavaṇṇanā

An Explanation of the Exposition on the Onefold and Other Modes.

127.

127.

Ito [V 1.0026] paraṃ pavakkhāmi, nayamekavidhādikaṃ;

Ābhidhammikabhikkhūnaṃ, buddhiyā pana vuddhiyā.

Henceforth I shall explain the method, the onefold and so on, for the monks versed in Abhidhamma, and for the growth of their wisdom.

Ahaṃ ito paraṃ ito paricchedato paraṃ ekavidhādikaṃ nayaṃ ābhidhammikabhikkhūnaṃ buddhiyā vuddhitthāya pavakkhāmi desessāmi.

Henceforth, beyond this chapter, I shall explain the method of the onefold and other modes for the growth of wisdom of the monks versed in the Abhidhamma.

128. Sabbamekavidhaṃ [M 0.0032] cittaṃ, vijānanasabhāvato sabbaṃ cittaṃ vijānanasabhāvato ekavidhaṃ, duvidhañca bhave cittaṃ ahetukasahetukato idaṃ cittaṃ duvidhaṃ bhaveyya.

128. All consciousness, by its nature of cognizing, is of one kind. And consciousness can be of two kinds, as rootless and rooted; thus this consciousness can be of two kinds.

129. Puññāpuññavipākā hi, kāme dasa ca pañca ca hi saccaṃ kāme kāmāvacare kusalākusalavipākā dasa pañca ca kiriyā tisso iti sabbe aṭṭhārasa cittuppādā ahetukā.

129. Indeed, the results of merit and demerit in the sense sphere are fifteen. In the sense sphere, there are fifteen wholesome and unwholesome resultants and three functional types of consciousness. Thus, all eighteen types of consciousness are rootless.

130. Ahetukato cittuppādato sesā ekasattati cittuppādā sahetukāti sahetukā nāmāti mahesinā tādinā aviparītasabhāvena hetuvādinā paccayavādinā niddiṭṭhā.

130. Apart from the rootless types of consciousness, the remaining seventy-one types of consciousness are rooted. Thus they are called 'rooted,' as designated by the Great Sage, the Such-like One, who is of unerring nature, a proponent of causes, and a teacher of conditions.

131. Savatthukāvatthukato savatthukaavatthukavasena tathā ubhayavasena savatthukavasena, avatthukavasena ca sabbaṃ vuttappakārena ca mānasaṃ tividhaṃ hoti.

131. In terms of being with a physical basis and without a physical basis, and likewise as both, all consciousness is threefold. That is, by way of being with a physical basis, without a physical basis, and in the manner stated, consciousness is threefold.

132-4. Sabbo kāmavipāko ca, rūpe pañcadasāpi ca cittuppādā ādimaggo paṭhamamaggo hasituppādo manodhātukiriyāpi ca domanassadvayañcāpi tecattālīsa mānasā vinā vatthuṃ vatthuṃ vajjetvā na uppajjanti, ekantena savatthukā nāma. Arūpāvacaravipākā ca ekantena [V 1.0027] avatthukā, mayā vuttato cittuppādato sesāni dvecattālīsa cittāni ubhayathā savatthukāvatthukavasena siyuṃ.

All sense-sphere resultants, the fifteen form-sphere types of consciousness, the first path-consciousness, smiling consciousness, the functional mind-element, and the two consciousnesses accompanied by displeasure—these forty-three types of consciousness do not arise without a physical basis; they are exclusively with a physical basis. The formless-sphere resultants are exclusively without a physical basis. The remaining forty-two types of consciousness can be of both kinds, that is, with or without a physical basis.

135. Ekekārammaṇaṃ cittaṃ, pañcārammaṇameva ca cittaṃ chaḷārammaṇakañceti evaṃ iminā mayā vuttappakārenāpi tividhaṃ cittaṃ siyā.

135. Consciousness may have a single object, five objects, or six objects. Thus, in this way that I have stated, consciousness can be threefold.

136-8. Viññāṇāni ca dve pañca, aṭṭha lokuttarāni ca abhiññāmānasaṃ ṭhapetvā sabbaṃ mahaggatañcevāti tecattālīsa cittuppādā pana ekekārammaṇā viññeyyā dhīrena. Tattha [M 0.0033] citte manodhātuttayaṃ pañcārammaṇaṃ īritaṃ bhagavatā. Mayā vuttacittato sesāni tecattālīsa cittāni chaḷārammaṇikāni matāni satthunā, tathā evaṃ cittaṃ kusalākusalādito tividhaṃ. Ādi-saddena abyākataṃ gahetabbaṃ.

The two sets of five sense-consciousnesses, the eight supramundane consciousnesses, and all the sublime consciousnesses except for the supernormal knowledge consciousness—these forty-three types of consciousness, the wise should understand, have a single object each. Therein, the threefold mind-element has been declared by the Blessed One to have five objects. The remaining forty-three types of consciousness are considered by the Teacher to have six objects. Likewise, consciousness is threefold as wholesome, unwholesome, etc. By the word 'etc.,' the indeterminate should be understood.

139. Ahetukaṃ cittaṃ ekahetukañca cittaṃ dvihetukañca cittaṃ tihetukañca cittanti evaṃ iminā pakārena cittaṃ catubbidhaṃ vibhāvinā viññātabbaṃ.

139. By this method, consciousness should be understood by the discerning as fourfold: rootless consciousness, one-rooted consciousness, two-rooted consciousness, and three-rooted consciousness.

140-2. Heṭṭhā mayāpi niddiṭṭhā aṭṭhārasa cittuppādā ahetukā, vicikicchuddhaccasaṃyuttaṃ cittaṃ ekahetukaṃ evaṃ udīritaṃ bhagavatā. Kāme kāmāvacare puññavipākakriyato kusalavasena ca vipākavasena ca kiriyāvasena ca dvādasadhā cittuppādā akusalā ca dasadhā cāti bāvīsati cittuppādā duhetukā. Kāme kāmāvacare puññavipākakriyato puññavasena ca vipākavasena ca kiriyāvasena ca dvādasadhā cittuppādā. Sabbaṃ mahaggatañceva appamāṇaṃ lokuttaracittañca tihetukaṃ.

As I have previously explained, there are eighteen rootless types of consciousness. The consciousness associated with doubt and the one associated with restlessness are declared by the Blessed One to be one-rooted. In the sense sphere, ten unwholesome types of consciousness and twelve types that are wholesome, resultant, or functional are two-rooted, making twenty-two in total. In the sense sphere, twelve types of consciousness that are wholesome, resultant, or functional, as well as all sublime and supramundane consciousness, are three-rooted.

143-50. Rūpīriyāpathaviññatti-janakājanakāditoti rūpairiyāpathaviññattijanakavasena rūpairiyāpathajanakavasena ca rūpajanakavasena ca tikiccājanakavasena cātiādīhi pakārehi sabbaṃ cittaṃ catubbidhaṃ hoti. Tattha tasmiṃ citte dvādasākusalā, kāmadhātuyā kusalā, tathā kāme dasa kiriyā, abhiññāmānasaṃ dvayaṃ, ime bāttiṃsa mānasā rūpāni samuṭṭhāpenti, iriyāpathaṃ kappenti, viññattiṃ janayanti. Kusalā mahaggatamānasā kiriyā ca mahaggatamānasā, aṭṭha anāsavacittāni, chabbīsati ca mānasā rūpāni samuṭṭhāpenti, iriyāpathaṃ [V 1.0028] kappenti. Copanaṃ na pāpenti viññattiṃ na janayantīti attho. Ime cittuppādā dukiccaniyatā[M 0.0034], dasa viññāṇe ṭhapetvā dvīsu bhūmīsu vipākā manodhātudvayasantīraṇattayamahāvipākarūpavipākānaṃ vasena aṭṭhārasa pākā manodhātu kiriyā cevāti imāni ekūnavīsati cittāni rūpāni samuṭṭhāpenti, itaradvayaṃ na karonti, puna dvepañcaviññāṇā paṭhamaṃ “dasa viññāṇe”ti vuttattā “punā”ti vuttā. Arūpīsu vipākā ca sabbesaṃ sattānaṃ paṭisandhicittañca arahato cuticittañca ime soḷasa mānasā tikiccāni na karonti.

Consciousness is fourfold according to such modes as generating or not generating material form, posture, and intimation. Therein, (1) the twelve unwholesome types, eight sense-sphere wholesome types, ten sense-sphere functional types, and two supernormal knowledge consciousnesses—these thirty-two types of consciousness produce material form, regulate posture, and generate intimation. (2) The wholesome and functional sublime types and the eight supramundane types—these twenty-six types of consciousness produce material form and regulate posture, but do not generate intimation. (3) Eighteen resultants—namely, the two mind-elements, three investigating consciousnesses, eight great resultants, and five form-sphere resultants—and the functional mind-element, these nineteen types of consciousness produce material form but do not perform the other two functions. (4) The ten sense-consciousnesses, the four formless resultants, the rebirth-linking consciousness of all beings, and the death-consciousness of an Arahant—these sixteen types of consciousness do not perform the three functions.

151. Ekadviticatuṭṭhāna-pañcaṭṭhānappabhedato ekakiccadvikiccatikiccacatukiccapañcakiccabhedena pañcadhā cittaṃ pañcapakāraṃ cittaṃ pañcanimmalalocano buddho akkhāsi kathesi.

151. The Buddha, with his fivefold pure vision, declared and taught that consciousness is of five kinds, distinguished by performing one, two, three, four, or five functions: as single-functioned, double-functioned, triple-functioned, quadruple-functioned, and quintuple-functioned.

152.

152.

Kusalākusalā sabbe, cittuppādā mahākriyā;

Mahaggatā kriyā ceva, cattāro phalamānasā.

All wholesome and unwholesome types of consciousness, the great functional consciousnesses, the sublime functional consciousnesses, and the four fruition consciousnesses.

153. Sabbeva pañcapaññāsa cittuppādā javanaṭṭhānatoyeva javanakiccavaseneva ekaṭṭhāne ekakicce nippapañcena satthunā taṇhāmānadiṭṭhivirahitena satthunā niyāmitā kathitā.

153. These fifty-five types of consciousness have been declared by the Teacher—who is free from proliferation, craving, conceit, and wrong views—to be fixed in one place and to have one function, namely, the function of impulsion in the impulsion stage.

154. Puna dvepañcaviññāṇā cittuppādā dassane savane tathā ghāyane sāyanaṭṭhāne phusane paṭipāṭiyā satthunā niyāmitā.

154. Again, the two sets of five consciousnesses are determined by the Teacher to function sequentially in seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting, and touching.

155. Manodhātuttikaṃ āvajjane paṭicchane, ete aṭṭhasaṭṭhi cittuppādā ekaṭṭhānikataṃ ekakiccabhāvaṃ gatā pattā bhavanti.

155. The threefold mind-element has the functions of adverting and receiving. Thus, these sixty-eight types of consciousness are established as having a single function.

156-8. Cittadvayaṃ dviṭṭhānikaṃ nāma udīritaṃ bhagavatā, somanassayutaṃ cittaṃ pañcadvāre santīraṇaṃ siyā. Chadvāre tadālambaṇañca balavārammaṇe atimahantārammaṇe sati siyā[M 0.0035], tathā voṭṭhabbanaṃ pañcadvāresu voṭṭhabbanaṃ hoti. Manodvāresu pana sabbesaṃ ārammaṇānaṃ āvajjanaṃ hoti, idaṃ cittadvayaṃ dviṭṭhānikaṃ nāma hoti.

156-8. Two types of consciousness, called 'two-functioned,' have been declared by the Blessed One. (1) The investigating consciousness accompanied by joy can function as investigating at the five doors, and as registration at the six doors when the object is strong or very great. (2) The mind-door adverting consciousness functions as determining at the five doors, and as adverting to all objects at the mind door. These two types of consciousness are called 'two-functioned'.

159. Paṭisandhiyā ṭhānato paṭisandhiyā kiccavasena bhavaṅgassa ṭhānato bhavaṅgassa kiccavasena cutiyā ṭhānato [V 1.0029] cutiyā kiccavasena te mahaggatavipākā nava tiṭṭhānikā tikiccāti muninā matā.

159. By way of the function of rebirth-linking, the function of the life-continuum, and the function of death, those nine sublime resultant states are considered by the Sage to be three-functioned.

160-3. Aṭṭha kāmā mahāpākā, paṭisandhibhavaṅgato paṭisandhibhavaṅgavasena tadārammaṇato ceva tadārammaṇavasena ca eva cutiṭṭhānavasena ca aṭṭha cittāni catuṭṭhānikacittāni honti, iti vacanaṃ dhīro niddise, kusalākusalapākopekkhāsahagatadvayaṃ pañcadvāre santīraṇaṃ bhave, chadvārikesupi balavārammaṇe sati tadārammaṇatā siyā. Paṭisandhibhavaṅgānaṃ ṭhānavasena ca cutiṭṭhānavasena ca idaṃ cittadvayaṃ pañcaṭṭhānikacittaṃ nāmāti udīritaṃ muninā.

160-3. The eight great sense-sphere resultants have four functions: rebirth-linking, life-continuum, registration, and death. Thus the wise should explain. The two resultant investigating consciousnesses accompanied by equanimity have five functions: they can function as investigating at the five doors; as registration at the six doors when the object is strong; and also as rebirth-linking, life-continuum, and death. Thus these two types of consciousness are declared by the Sage to be five-functioned.

164. Pañcakiccaṃ dvayaṃ cittaṃ, aṭṭhakaṃ pana catukiccaṃ, navakaṃ tikiccaṃ, dve cittuppādā dvikiccā, imesaṃ imehi cittuppādehi sesaṃ ekakaṃ kiccaṃ.

164. Two types of consciousness perform five functions; eight perform four functions; nine perform three functions; two perform two functions; and the remaining types of consciousness perform a single function.

165.

165.

Bhavaṅgāvajjanañceva, dassanaṃ sampaṭicchanaṃ;

Santīraṇaṃ voṭṭhabbanaṃ, javanaṃ bhavati sattamaṃ.

Life-continuum and adverting, seeing and receiving, investigating, determining, and impulsion is the seventh.

166. Chabbidhaṃ hoti taṃ channaṃ taṃ cittaṃ channaṃ cakkhusotaghānajivhākāyamanoviññāṇānaṃ pabhedato chabbidhaṃ hoti, cakkhusotaghānajivhākāyamanodhātumanoviññāṇadhātūnaṃ sattannaṃ vasena cittaṃ sattadhā hoti.

166. Consciousness is sixfold by the distinction of the six consciousnesses: eye-, ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness. Consciousness is sevenfold by way of the seven consciousness-elements: eye-, ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, mind-, and mind-consciousness-element.

167. Ekekārammaṇaṃ chakkaṃ, pañcārammaṇabhedato chaḷārammaṇato ceva chaḷārammaṇacittavasena mano cittaṃ aṭṭhavidhaṃ hoti.

167. Consciousness is eightfold: as the six types that take a single object, as that which takes five objects, and as that which takes six objects.

168. Tattha [M 0.0036] tasmiṃ citte dvepañcaviññāṇā ekekagocarā honti, dve cittuppādā rūpārammaṇikā, dve dve cittuppādā saddādigocarā.

168. Herein, the two sets of five sense-consciousnesses each have a single, specific object. Two types of consciousness have form as their object; two by two, the other types of consciousness have sound, odor, taste, and tangible objects respectively.

169. Pañcābhiññāvivajjitaṃ sabbaṃ mahaggataṃ, sabbaṃ lokuttarañca iti idaṃ cittaṃ ekekārammaṇaṃ bhave.

169. All sublime consciousness, excluding the five supernormal knowledges, and all supramundane consciousness—this consciousness has a single object.

170. Idaṃ [V 1.0030] chakkaṃ ekekārammaṇaṃ vibhāvinā ñeyyaṃ, manodhātuttayaṃ pañcārammaṇikaṃ nāma bhave.

170. This group of six should be understood by the discerning as each having a single object. The threefold mind-element is said to have five objects.

171. Kāmāvacaracittāni cattālīsaṃ tathā ekekaṃ sabbāni abhiññāni ca chaḷārammaṇikānīti chaḷārammaṇikāni nāma paṇḍitena viññeyyāni.

171. The forty sense-sphere types of consciousness, and likewise all the individual supernormal knowledges, are said to have six objects; thus they should be understood by the wise as having six objects.

172. Sattaviññāṇadhātūsu pacchimaṃ manoviññāṇadhātuñca kusalākusalābyākatavasena tidhā katvā navavidhaṃ cittaṃ hoti.

172. Among the seven consciousness-elements, by dividing the last, the mind-consciousness-element, into three as wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate, consciousness becomes ninefold.

173. Manoviññāṇadhātuyā bhedo puññāpuññavaseneva vipākakiriyabhedato chasattatividho hoti.

173. The division of the mind-consciousness-element becomes seventy-sixfold by way of the distinction between meritorious and demeritorious, and between resultant and functional.

174. Manodhātuṃ vipākakiriyabhedato dvidhā katvā pubbe vuttehi navadhā cittehi mānasaṃ dasadhā hoti.

174. By dividing the mind-element in two by the distinction of resultant and functional, consciousness, from the previously mentioned ninefold classification, becomes tenfold.

175. Pacchimaṃ dhātudvayaṃ manodhātumanoviññāṇadhātudvayaṃ, manodhātuṃ kusalavipākaakusalavipākakiriyāvasena tidhā katvā, manoviññāṇadhātuñca kusalākusalābyākatavasena tividhā katvā cakkhusotaghānajivhākāyaviññāṇehi saha cittaṃ ekādasavidhaṃ hoti, iti idaṃ vacanaṃ paṇḍito paridīpaye.

175. Regarding the last two elements—the pair of the mind-element and the mind-consciousness-element: by dividing the mind-element into three by way of wholesome-resultant, unwholesome-resultant, and functional, and by dividing the mind-consciousness-element into three by way of wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate, then together with eye-, ear-, nose-, tongue-, and body-consciousness, consciousness becomes elevenfold. This statement a wise person should elucidate.

176. Manoviññāṇadhātumpi kusalākusalādito kusalākusalavipākakiriyāvasena catudhā vibhajitvāna taṃ [M 0.0037] cittaṃ cakkhusotaghānajivhākāyaviññāṇehi saha tippakārāya manodhātuyā ca saha dvādasadhāpi dhīro vade.

176. A wise person might also speak of consciousness as twelvefold: when the mind-consciousness-element is divided fourfold by way of wholesome, unwholesome, resultant, and functional, it is taken together with the eye-, ear-, nose-, tongue-, and body-consciousness, and with the threefold mind-element.

177-9. Cittaṃ cuddasaṭṭhānabhedena cuddasadhā bhave, paṭisandhiyā vasena ca bhavaṅgavasena ca cutiyā vasena ca āvajjanassa vasena ca pañcannaṃ dassanādīnaṃ kiccānaṃ vasena ca sampaṭicchanacetaso vasena ca santīraṇassa vasena ca voṭṭhabbanajavanānaṃ vasena ca, yathā evaṃ tadārammaṇacittassa vasena [V 1.0031] cāti evaṃ iminā pakārena ṭhānabhedato kiccabhedena cuddasadhā cittaṃ hoti, iti idaṃ vacanaṃ dhīro paridīpaye paridīpeyya.

177-9. Consciousness becomes fourteenfold by the division of its fourteen functions: by way of rebirth-linking, the life-continuum, death, adverting, the five functions of seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting, and touching, receiving, investigating, determining, impulsion, and registration. Thus, in this manner, by the division of its occasions and the difference of its functions, consciousness becomes fourteenfold. This statement a wise person should elucidate and explain.

180. Bhūmipuggalanānattavasena bhūminānattavasena, puggalanānattavasena ca cittānaṃ pavattito idaṃ cittaṃ bahudhā hoti, iti vacanañca dhīro vibhāvaye pakāseyya.

180. Because consciousness occurs in accordance with the diversity of planes and the diversity of individuals, it becomes manifold. This statement, too, a wise person should clarify and proclaim.

181. Idha imasmiṃ sāsane yo bhikkhu matimā imasmiṃ ekavidhādinaye kusalo cheko hoti, abhidhamme pavattā atthā tassa bhikkhuno hatthagatā hatthapaviṭṭhā āmalakā viya suddhamaṇikā viya honti.

181. Here in this Dispensation, for whatever intelligent bhikkhu is skilled and clever in this method beginning with the onefold, the meanings that occur in the Abhidhamma are in his grasp, fully comprehended, like a myrobalan fruit on the palm of his hand, like a pure gem.

Iti abhidhammāvatāraṭīkāya

Thus in the Subcommentary to the Abhidhammāvatāra.

Ekavidhādiniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Exposition of the Method Beginning with the Onefold is finished.

Catuttho paricchedo.

The Fourth Chapter.

5. Pañcamo paricchedo

5. The Fifth Chapter.

Bhūmipuggalacittuppattiniddesavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Exposition of the Arising of Consciousness according to Planes and Individuals.

182.

182.

Ito paraṃ pavakkhāmi, buddhivuddhikaraṃ nayaṃ;

Cittānaṃ bhūmisuppattiṃ, puggalānaṃ vasena ca.

Hereafter I shall explain the method that enhances wisdom: the arising of consciousness in the planes and according to the various kinds of individuals.

Ahaṃ [M 0.0038] ito paraṃ buddhivuddhikaraṃ nayaṃ mativaddhikaraṃ nayaṃ pavakkhāmi desessāmi. Cittānaṃ bhūmisuppattiṃ puggalānaṃ vasena ca bhūmīsu cittānaṃ uppattiṃ, puggalānaṃ vasena bhūmīsu cittānaṃ uppattiñca pavakkhāmi.

Hereafter, I will explain and teach the method that increases wisdom, the method that enhances intelligence. I will declare the arising of consciousness in the planes, and the arising of consciousness in the planes according to individuals.

183. Devā [V 1.0032] ceva manussā ca, tisso ca apāyabhūmiyo honti, gatiyo pañca tesaṃ devamanussatiracchānapetanirayagatīnaṃ vasena pañca gatiyo niddiṭṭhā satthunā dassitā bhagavatā. Tayo bhavā pana kāmarūpārūpabhavavasena tayo satthunā niddiṭṭhā dassitā.

183. There are devas and human beings, and the three woeful planes. There are five destinations. By way of the destinations of devas, humans, animals, ghosts, and hell-beings, five destinations have been pointed out and shown by the Teacher, the Blessed One. Furthermore, the three kinds of existence—by way of the desire existence, the form existence, and the formless existence—have been pointed out and shown by the Teacher.

184-5. Bhūmiyo tattha tiṃseva, tāsu tiṃseva puggalā tattha tesu tīsu bhavesu tiṃsa eva bhūmiyo honti, tāsu bhūmīsu uppannā puggalā tiṃsa eva honti, etāsu bhūmīsu uppannā sabbe ca pana puggalā paṭisandhikacittānaṃ vasena ekūnavīsati honti. Paṭisandhi ca nāmesā esā paṭisandhi ca nāma duvidhā dvippakārā samudīritā satthunā kathitā.

184-5. Therein there are just thirty planes, and in them just thirty individuals. Therein, in those three existences, there are just thirty planes. The individuals arisen in those planes are just thirty. However, all the individuals arisen in these planes are nineteen by way of the rebirth-linking consciousnesses. This is named rebirth-linking, and this rebirth-linking has been declared and spoken of by the Teacher as being of two kinds, twofold.

186. Acittakā paṭisandhi, sacittakā paṭisandhi ca iti duvidhā paṭisandhi hoti, asaññibrahmānaṃ paṭisandhi acittakā rūpapaṭisandhi hoti. Sesā rūpapaṭisandhito sesā sacittakā sacittakapaṭisandhi ñeyyā paṇḍitena jānitabbā. Sā pana sacittakā paṭisandhi ekūnavīsati hoti.

186. Rebirth-linking is twofold: that without consciousness and that with consciousness. The rebirth-linking of non-percipient beings is without consciousness; it is material rebirth-linking. The remaining kinds, other than material rebirth-linking, should be known by a wise person as rebirth-linking with consciousness. And that rebirth-linking with consciousness is of nineteen kinds.

187. Paṭisandhivaseneva sacittakapaṭisandhivasena eva vīsati puggalā honti. Idha imasmiṃ cittādhikāre cittādhikārattā acittakapaṭisandhi rūpapaṭisandhi na ca uddhaṭā na ca kathitā mayā.

187. By way of rebirth-linking with consciousness, there are twenty individuals. Here, in this chapter on consciousness, because it is the chapter on consciousness, rebirth-linking without consciousness—material rebirth-linking—has not been included or discussed by me.

188. Ahetudvitihetūti, puggalā tividhā siyuṃ ahetukadvihetukatihetukā iti tividhā tippakārā puggalā [M 0.0039] siyuṃ bhaveyyuṃ. Ariyā pana puggalā aṭṭha iti evaṃ iminā mayā vuttappakārena sabbe puggalā ekādasa īritā kathitā bhagavatā.

188. Individuals are of three kinds: rootless, two-rooted, and three-rooted. Thus individuals are of three kinds, of three types. Noble individuals, however, are eight. Thus, in this manner, all eleven individuals have been declared by the Blessed One.

189. Bhūmīsu tiṃsabhūmīsu cittānaṃ uppattiṃ etesaṃ pana sabbesaṃ puggalānaṃ pabhedato bhūmīsu cittānaṃ uppattiñca gaṇhato gaṇhantassa mama vacanaṃ nibodhatha, tumhe jānātha suṇātha.

189. Now, as I reckon the arising of consciousness in the thirty planes according to the distinctions among all these individuals, you should understand my words; you should know and listen.

190. Tīsu bhūmīsu kati cittāni jāyanti? Me mayhaṃ vada tāni cittāni tvaṃ kathehi, sabbāsu bhūmīsu cuddasa eva cittāni. Taṃ yathā –

190. How many consciousnesses arise in the three existences? Tell me, declare those consciousnesses to me. In all planes, there are just fourteen consciousnesses. They are as follows:

Voṭṭhabbaṃ [V 1.0033] kāmapuññañca, viyuttāni ca diṭṭhiyā;

Uddhaccasahitañceva, honti sabbattha cuddasa.

Determining, the wholesome consciousnesses of the desire sphere, those dissociated from wrong view, and that accompanied by restlessness: these fourteen occur in all planes.

191. Sadā vīsati cittāni, kāmeyeva bhave siyuṃ vīsati cittāni kāmeyeva bhave sadā sabbasmiṃ kāle siyuṃ bhaveyyunti. Taṃ yathā –

191. Twenty consciousnesses always exist only in the desire-sphere existence. That is, twenty consciousnesses would exist only in the desire-sphere existence, always, at all times. They are as follows:

Kāme aṭṭha mahāpākā, domanassadvayampi ca;

Tathā ghānādiviññāṇattayaṃ pākā apuññajā.

In the desire sphere are the eight great resultants, the two accompanied by displeasure; likewise the triad of consciousnesses beginning with smelling, and the resultants born of demerit.

Ghānādiviññāṇattayanti kusalavipākaghānādittayaṃ. Pākā apuññajā akusalato jātā ahetukā satta vipākā. Pañca rūpabhaveyeva pañca cittāni rūpabhaveyeva bhavanti. Cattāreva arūpisu cattāri cittāni arūpīsuyeva honti. Taṃ yathā –

‘The triad of consciousnesses beginning with smelling’ means the triad of wholesome-resultant consciousnesses beginning with smelling. ‘Resultants born of demerit’ means the seven rootless resultants born from the unwholesome. Five consciousnesses exist only in the form-sphere existence. Four consciousnesses exist only in the formless spheres. They are as follows:

Rūpeva rūpapākā vāruppapākā arūpisu;

Nava mahaggatā pākā, rūpārūpeva jāyare.

The form-sphere resultants arise only in the form sphere, and the formless-sphere resultants in the formless spheres. The nine sublime resultants arise only in the form and formless spheres respectively.

192. Kāmarūpabhavesveva aṭṭhārasa cittāni bhavanti.

192. Only in the desire-sphere and form-sphere existences do eighteen consciousnesses arise.

Taṃ [M 0.0040] yathā –

They are as follows:

Puññarūpāni pañceva, puññajaṃ sampaṭicchanaṃ;

Cakkhusotadvayaṃ puññapākaṃ santīraṇadvayaṃ.

The five form-sphere wholesome consciousnesses, the wholesome-resultant receiving consciousness, the pair of eye- and ear-consciousness that are wholesome-resultant, and the pair of investigating consciousnesses.

Puññapākaṃ hasituppādamanodhātukriyāpi ca;

Aṭṭhārasādimaggena, pañca rūpakriyāpi ca;

Kāmarūpabhavesveva, etāneva sadā siyuṃ.

The smile-producing consciousness and the functional mind-element; the five form-sphere functional consciousnesses, and the first path: these eighteen always exist only in the desire-sphere and form-sphere existences.

Dvecattālīsa cittāni, honti tīsu bhavesupi dvecattālīsa cittāni honti. Taṃ yathā –

Forty-two consciousnesses exist in the three existences. They are as follows:

Paṭighadvayavajjitāni[V 1.0034], apuññāni daseva ca;

Mahāpuññāni aṭṭheva, voṭṭhabbanakriyāni ca.

The ten unwholesome consciousnesses, excluding the two connected with aversion; the eight great wholesome consciousnesses; and the functional determining consciousness;

Puññāruppāni cattāri, āruppakiriyāni ca;

Kaniṭṭhamaggavajjāni, satta lokuttarāni ca;

Dvecattālīsa cittāni, honti tīsu bhavesupi.

the four formless wholesome consciousnesses and the four formless functional consciousnesses; and the seven supramundane consciousnesses, excluding the lowest path. These forty-two consciousnesses exist in the three existences.

193. Ṭhapetvā pana sabbesaṃ, catassopāyabhūmiyo catasso apāyabhūmiyo ṭhapetvā vajjetvā apāyato sesānaṃ sabbesaṃ puggalānaṃ chabbīsabhūmīsu terasa eva cittāni honti. Taṃ yathā –

193. But setting aside the four woeful planes: for all the remaining individuals in the twenty-six planes, there are just thirteen consciousnesses. They are as follows:

Catutthārūpāvacaraṃ, anāgāmiphalādayo;

Mahākriyā ca jāyanti, terasāpāyavajjitā.

The wholesome, resultant, and functional consciousnesses of the fourth formless sphere; the fruition of non-returning and the fruition of arahantship; and the eight great functional consciousnesses: these thirteen arise, being absent from the woeful planes.

Anāgāmiphalādayoti ādi-saddena hi arahattaphalāni gahitāni.

‘Fruition of non-returning and so on’: by the word ‘and so on,’ the fruition of arahantship is included.

194. Aparāni catassopi, ṭhapetvāruppabhūmiyo catasso arūpabhūmiyo ṭhapetvā sesāsu chabbīsabhūmīsu aparāni cha cittāni jāyanti. Taṃ yathā –

194. Furthermore, setting aside the four formless planes, six other consciousnesses arise in the remaining twenty-six planes. They are as follows:

Manodhātukriyañceva[M 0.0041], puññajaṃ sampaṭicchanaṃ;

Cakkhusotadvayaṃ puññapākaṃ santīraṇadvayaṃ;

Cheva cittāni jāyanti, tathā uparivajjite.

The functional mind-element, the wholesome-resultant receiving consciousness, the pair of eye- and ear-consciousness that are wholesome-resultant, and the pair of investigating consciousnesses: these six consciousnesses arise, thus being absent from the higher planes.

195. Suddhāvāsikadevānaṃ, ṭhapetvā pañca bhūmiyo pañca bhūmiyo ṭhapetvā pañcavīsatibhūmīsu pañca cittāni jāyanti. Taṃ yathā –

195. Setting aside the five planes of the Pure Abodes, five consciousnesses arise in the twenty-five planes. They are as follows:

Diṭṭhiyā sampayuttānaṃ, vicikicchāyutaṃ tathā;

Pañca sabbattha jāyanti, suddhāvāsavivajjite.

The four consciousnesses associated with wrong view, and that associated with doubt: these five arise everywhere except in the Pure Abodes.

196.

196.

Aparāni [V 1.0035] duve honti, pañcavīsatibhūmisu;

Ṭhapetvā nevasaññañca, catassopāyabhūmiyo.

There are two others, which arise in twenty-five planes, setting aside the plane of neither-perception-nor-non-perception and the four woeful planes.

Catassopāyabhūmiyo nevasaññānāsaññañca ṭhapetvāyeva pañcavīsatibhūmīsu aparāni duve cittāni honti. Taṃ yathā –

Setting aside the four woeful planes and the plane of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, two other consciousnesses arise in the twenty-five planes. They are as follows:

Ṭhapetvā nevasaññañca, catassopāyabhūmiyo;

Sesāsu tatiyāruppajavanaṃ jāyati dvayaṃ.

Setting aside the plane of neither-perception-nor-non-perception and the four woeful planes, in the remaining planes the pair of javanas of the third formless sphere arise.

197. Dvepi cittāni jāyanti, catuvīsatibhūmisu catassopāyabhūmiyo ākiñcaññañca nevasaññañca ṭhapetvā sesāsu catuvīsatibhūmīsu dvepi cittāni jāyanti. Taṃ yathā –

197. Two consciousnesses also arise in twenty-four planes. Setting aside the four woeful planes, the plane of nothingness, and the plane of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, two consciousnesses arise in the remaining twenty-four planes. They are as follows:

Catutthatatiyāruppaṃ, ṭhapetvāpāyabhūmiyo;

Sesāsu dutiyāruppa-javanaṃ jāyati dvayaṃ.

Setting aside the fourth and third formless planes and the woeful planes, in the remaining planes the pair of javanas of the second formless sphere arise.

198. Apāyabhūmiyo hitvā catasso apāyabhūmiyo tisso upari arūpabhūmiyo hitvā chaḍḍetvā sesāsu tevīsatibhūmīsu dveyeva pana cittāni honti. Taṃ yathā –

198. Having abandoned the four states of misery and the three higher formless realms, in the remaining twenty-three realms only two types of consciousness arise. They are:

Apāyabhūmiyo [M 0.0042] hitvā, tissocāruppabhūmiyo;

Sesāsu paṭhamāruppaṃ, javanadvayaṃ jāyati.

Having abandoned the woeful states and the three higher formless realms, in the remaining planes a pair of javanas of the first formless sphere arises.

199. Arūpe ca apāye ca aṭṭha bhūmiyo ṭhapetvā sesāsu bāvīsatibhūmīsu ekādasavidhaṃ cittaṃ hoti. Taṃ yathā –

199. Setting aside the eight planes—the formless planes and the woeful states—in the remaining twenty-two planes, eleven types of consciousness arise. They are:

Sabbaṃ rūpañca vipākaṃ, ṭhapetvā sitamānasaṃ;

Ekādaseva jāyati, apāyārūpavajjite.

Setting aside all form-sphere consciousness, resultant consciousness, and the smiling consciousness, eleven types arise in the planes devoid of the woeful states and the formless realms.

200. Suddhāvāse [V 1.0036] apāye ca nava bhūmiyo ṭhapetvā sesāsu ekavīsāsu bhūmīsu niccampi cattāro eva mānasā honti. Taṃ yathā –

200. Setting aside the nine planes—the Pure Abodes and the woeful states—in the remaining twenty-one planes, four types of consciousness always arise. They are:

Sotāpattiphalañceva, sakadāgāmiphalampi ca;

Sakadāgāmimaggo ca, ṭhapetvāpāyasuddhake;

Anāgāmimaggo ceva, ekavīsāsu honti hi.

The fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of the once-returner, the path of the once-returner, and the path of the non-returner—these indeed arise in the twenty-one planes, setting aside the woeful states and the Pure Abodes.

201. Ekaṃ sattarasasveva, cittaṃ jāyati bhūmisu suddhāvāsaapāyāruppabhūmiyo ṭhapetvā avasesāsu sattarasasu bhūmīsu ekaṃ cittaṃ jāyati. Taṃ yathā –

201. In just seventeen planes one consciousness arises. Setting aside the Pure Abodes, the woeful states, and the formless planes, in the remaining seventeen planes one type of consciousness arises. It is:

Suddhāvāse apāye ca, ṭhapetvāruppabhūmiyo;

Ādimaggo eko hoti, sattarasasu bhūmisu.

Setting aside the Pure Abodes, the woeful states, and the formless planes, the one initial path arises in seventeen planes.

202.

202.

Dvādaseva tu jāyante, ekādasasu bhūmisu;

Ṭhapetvā pana sabbāpi, bhūmiyo hi mahaggatā. –

But twelve types of consciousness arise in eleven planes, having indeed set aside all the sublime planes.

Ekūnavīsatibhūmiyo ṭhapetvā sesāsu ekādasasu bhūmīsu dvādasa cittāni jāyanti. Taṃ yathā –

Setting aside the nineteen planes, in the remaining eleven planes twelve types of consciousness arise. They are:

Domanassadvayāpuññapākā satta ca puññajaṃ;

Ghānādittayaṃ sesāsu, hitvā sabbā mahaggatā.

The two consciousnesses accompanied by displeasure, the seven unwholesome-resultants, and the three wholesome-resultant consciousnesses beginning with nose-consciousness: these arise in the remaining planes, having abandoned all sublime planes.

203. Kāmāvacaradevānaṃ [M 0.0043] vasena ca manussānaṃ vasena ca sattasu kāmāvacarabhūmīsu aṭṭha cittāni sabbadā jāyanti. Taṃ yathā –

203. In the seven sense-sphere planes, for the sense-sphere devas and for humans, eight types of consciousness always arise. They are:

Kāme devamanussānaṃ, mahāpākāni jāyare;

Sadā sattasu etāni, hitvā tevīsa bhūmiyo.

For the devas and humans in the sense-sphere, the great resultants arise. These always arise in the seven planes, having abandoned the twenty-three other planes.

204. Pañcamajjhānapākeko[V 1.0037], jāyate chasu bhūmisu eko pañcamajjhānavipāko vehapphalādīsu chasu bhūmīsu jāyati. Cattāri pana rūpavipākacittāni tīsu tīsu bhūmīsu jāyanti. Ayametthādhippāyo – eko paṭhamarūpavipāko brahmapārisajjabrahmapurohitamahābrahmānaṃ tīsu bhūmīsu jāyati, eko dutiyarūpavipāko, eko tatiyarūpavipāko ca parittābhāappamāṇābhāābhassarānaṃ tīsu bhūmīsu jāyati, eko catuttharūpavipāko parittasubhaappamāṇasubhasubhakiṇhānaṃ tīsu bhūmīsu jāyati.

204. The one resultant of the fifth jhāna arises in six planes. One fifth-jhāna resultant consciousness arises in the six planes beginning with Vehapphala. But the four form-sphere resultant consciousnesses arise in three planes each. This is the intended meaning: one first form-sphere resultant arises in the three planes of the Retinue of Brahmā, the Ministers of Brahmā, and the Great Brahmās. One second form-sphere resultant and one third form-sphere resultant arise in the three planes of Limited Radiance, Immeasurable Radiance, and Radiant Lustre. One fourth form-sphere resultant arises in the three planes of Limited Glory, Immeasurable Glory, and Refulgent Glory.

205. Cattāri pana cittāni, honti ekekabhūmisu arūpāvacaravipākānaṃ vasena cattāri pana cittāni ekekabhūmīsu ekekāsu bhūmīsu honti, iti evaṃ iminā mayā vuttappakārena sabbāsu bhūmīsu cittuppādaṃ paridīpaye paṇḍito katheyya.

205. Further, four types of consciousness arise one in each plane; that is, by way of the formless-sphere resultants, four types of consciousness arise one in each of the formless planes. Thus, in the manner I have stated, a wise person should explain and elucidate the arising of consciousness in all planes.

206-7. Kusalākusalā kāme kāme vīsati kusalākusalā, tesaṃ pākā ahetukā tesaṃ kusalākusalānaṃ ahetukā pañcadasa vipākā āvajjanadvayañca iti evaṃ iminā mayā vuttappakārena sattatiṃsa mānasā narakādīsu catūsu apāyesupi jāyare. Avasesāni dvipaññāsa cittāni kadācipi kismiñci kālepi nuppajjanti. Taṃ yathā –

206-7. In the sense-sphere there are twenty wholesome and unwholesome types of consciousness. Their results are rootless. Of those wholesome and unwholesome kammas, there are fifteen rootless resultants and two adverting consciousnesses. Thus, in the manner I have stated, thirty-seven mental states arise in the four woeful states beginning with hell. The remaining fifty-two types of consciousness never arise at any time. They are:

Pañcadasāni [M 0.0044] rūpe tu, arūpe dvādasīritā;

Aṭṭha lokuttarāneva, kāmapākā sahetukā.

Fifteen in the form sphere, and twelve are said to be in the formless; the eight supramundane, and the sense-sphere resultants with roots.

Aṭṭha mahākriyā ceva, hasituppādamānasaṃ;

Dvipaññāsāni cittāni, apāyesu na jāyare.

And the eight great functional consciousnesses, and the smile-producing consciousness: these fifty-two types of consciousness do not arise in the woeful states.

208. Kāme devamanussānaṃ kāmāvacare devamanussānaṃ mahaggatā nava pākā neva jāyanti, asīti hadayā mānasā sadā jāyanti. Taṃ yathā –

208. For devas and humans in the sense-sphere, the nine sublime resultants never arise; eighty types of consciousness arise. They are:

Dvādasākusalāneva, kusalānekavīsati;

Sattavīsati pākā ca, mahaggatavivajjitā.

The twelve unwholesome, twenty-one wholesome, and twenty-seven resultant types of consciousness, excluding the sublime resultants.

Kāme [V 1.0038] devamanussānaṃ, kriyacittāni vīsati;

Honti asīti cittāni, viññeyyāni vibhāvinā.

For devas and humans in the sense-sphere, there are twenty functional consciousnesses. Thus there are eighty types of consciousness, to be understood by the discerning one.

209-12. Kāme kāmāvacare aṭṭha mahāvipākā domanassadvayampi ca tathā ghānādiviññāṇattayaṃ kusalavipākaṃ apuññajā satta pākā. Natthi āruppapākā ca, rūpāvacarabhūmiyaṃ arūpapākā ca cattāro rūpāvacarabhūmiyaṃ natthi. Ayametthādhippāyo – rūpāvacarabhūmiyaṃ aṭṭha mahāvipākā kāmasugatisattānaṃ dvinnaṃ vipākacittattā na honti, jhānena vikkhambhitattā domanassadvayampi natthi, ghānajivhākāyapasādavirahitattā kusalavipākaṃ ghānādittayaṃ natthi, aniṭṭhārammaṇānaṃ abhāvato satta akusalavipākā ca natthi, arūpapākā ca natthi. Kasmā? Arūpānaṃ vipākacittattā. Imehi saha cittehi imehi catuvīsaticittehi saha tayo maggā phaladvayaṃ sotāpattimaggo sakadāgāmimaggo anāgāmimaggo ca sotāpattiphalasakadāgāmiphalāni ca cattāro diṭṭhisaṃyuttā vicikicchāsaṃyuttampi ca cattāro heṭṭhimā pākā ca suddhāvāse na labbhare na labbhanti. Ayametthādhippāyo – puthujjanasotāpannasakadāgāmipuggalānaṃ asādhāraṇattā suddho ca āvāso, atha vā [M 0.0045] ghorātikkamaṭṭhitattā anāgāmipuggalā suddhā nāma, caturoghatiṇṇattā khīṇāsavā suddhā nāma, tesaṃ suddhānaṃ dvinnaṃ uttamasattānaṃ āvāsotipi suddhāvāso, tasmiṃ.

209-12. In the sense-sphere realm are the eight great resultants, the two consciousnesses accompanied by displeasure, the three wholesome-resultant consciousnesses of smell, etc., and the seven unwholesome-resultant consciousnesses. And in the form-sphere realm, the four formless-sphere resultants do not arise. This is the intended meaning: in the form-sphere realm, the eight great resultants do not arise because they are the resultant consciousnesses of beings in the sense-sphere's happy destinations. Due to suppression by jhāna, the two consciousnesses accompanied by displeasure also do not arise. Because of the absence of the sense faculties of smell, taste, and body, the three wholesome-resultant consciousnesses of smell, etc., do not arise. Due to the absence of undesirable objects, the seven unwholesome resultants also do not arise. And the formless-sphere resultants do not arise. Why? Because they are the resultant consciousnesses of formless beings. Together with these twenty-four types of consciousness, the three paths—the path of stream-entry, the path of once-returning, and the path of non-returning—the two fruits—the fruit of stream-entry and the fruit of once-returning—the four consciousnesses associated with wrong view, the one associated with doubt, and the four lower form-sphere resultants are not found in the Pure Abodes. This is the intended meaning: because it is not common to worldlings, stream-enterers, and once-returners, the abode is pure. Or, because they are established in having overcome the dreadful, non-returners are called 'pure'; because they have crossed the four floods, the taintless ones are called 'pure'; the abode of these two supreme beings is also the 'Pure Abode.' In that abode, these are not found.

Ayametthādhippāyo – suddhāvāse pana sotāpattimaggasotāpattiphalasakadāgāmimaggasakadāgāmiphalaanāgāmimaggā na vijjanti. Kasmāti ce? Anāgāmiphalaṭṭhānaṃyeva tasmiṃ uppajjanato cattāro diṭṭhisaṃyuttā ca vicikicchāyuttañca pañca akusalacittānaṃ sotāpannena vināsitattā, iti tasmā kāraṇā na jāyanti. Cattāro heṭṭhimavipākā heṭṭhimānaṃ rūpabrahmānaṃ vipākacittattā natthi. Sesāni ekapaññāsa cittāni suddhāvāse pana labbhanti. Taṃ yathā –

This is the intended meaning: In the Pure Abodes, the path of stream-entry, the fruit of stream-entry, the path of once-returning, the fruit of once-returning, and the path of non-returning are not found. Why? Because one is reborn there established in the fruit of non-returning, and because the five unwholesome types of consciousness—the four associated with wrong view and the one associated with doubt—have been destroyed by the stream-enterer; for that reason they do not arise. The four lower resultant consciousnesses are not found because they are the resultant consciousnesses of the lower form-sphere brahmās. The remaining fifty-one types of consciousness, however, are found in the Pure Abodes. They are:

Diṭṭhiyā vippayuttāni, uddhaccasahagataṃ tathā;

Kāmapuññāni aṭṭha ca, rūpapuññāni pañca vā.

The unwholesome consciousnesses dissociated from wrong view, and likewise the one accompanied by restlessness; the eight sense-sphere wholesome consciousnesses, and the five form-sphere wholesome ones.

Arūpakusalāneva, maggo khīṇāsavassa ca;

Cakkhusotamanodhātu, puññajā tīraṇā duve.

The formless wholesome consciousnesses, and the path of the taintless one; the wholesome-resultant eye-element, ear-element, and mind-element, and the two investigating consciousnesses.

Pañcamajjhānapāko [V 1.0039] ca, anāgāmiphalādayo;

Suddhāvāsesu labbhanti, kriyacittāni vīsati.

The resultant of the fifth jhāna, and the fruits beginning with the non-returner's; these are obtained in the Pure Abodes, along with the twenty functional consciousnesses.

Rūpāvacarikā sabbe sabbāni rūpāvacarāni pañcadasa cittāni, kāmadhātuyā sabbe tevīsati vipākā.

All fifteen form-sphere consciousnesses are of the form sphere. In the sense-sphere, all twenty-three resultants are found.

213. Domanassādimaggo ca domanassadvayañca ādimaggo ca sotāpattimaggo ca, kriyā ca dve ahetukā pañcadvārāvajjanahasituppādāni kiriyāni cāti tecattālīsa cittāni arūpabhūmiyaṃ natthi. Pañca rūpāvacaravipākā rūpīnaṃ vipākacittattā natthi. Rūpajavanāni heṭṭhimajhānānaṃ virattattā natthi. Cakkhusotaviññāṇāni puññajāni pasādarahitattā natthi. Ghānādiviññāṇāni pakatiyāyeva natthi. Kusalavipākā manodhātu cakkhādiggahitapañcārammaṇattā arūpānaṃ dhammārammaṇattā natthi, asati cakkhādiviññāṇe sā ca puññajā manodhātu [M 0.0046] tāya ca asatiyā cakkhādiviññāṇampi natthiyeva. Kiriyāmanodhātupi pañcārammaṇattāyeva natthi, hasituppādopi rūpakāyābhāvā sitassābhāvā natthi, pubbeva diṭṭhasaccā ariyā rūpabhūmikā, tasmā ādimaggopi natthi.

213. The two consciousnesses accompanied by displeasure, the initial path which is the path of stream-entry, and the two rootless functional consciousnesses—five-door adverting and smile-producing—these forty-three types of consciousness do not exist in the formless realm. The five form-sphere resultant consciousnesses do not exist there, as they are the resultants for beings with form. The form-sphere javanas of the lower jhānas do not exist, due to detachment from them. The wholesome-resultant eye- and ear-consciousnesses do not exist due to the absence of the sense faculties. The consciousnesses of smell and so forth are naturally absent. The wholesome-resultant mind-element does not exist, for it takes one of the five sense-objects as its object, whereas formless beings have only mind-objects; and when eye-consciousness and the others are absent, that wholesome-resultant mind-element is also absent, and with its absence, eye-consciousness and the others are certainly absent. The functional mind-element also does not exist because it takes the five sense-objects as its object. The smile-producing consciousness does not exist due to the absence of a physical body and thus the absence of smiling. Since noble ones who attain the formless realm have already seen the truths, the initial path also does not exist there.

214. Evaṃ bhūmivaseneva, cittuppattiṃ vibhāvaye evaṃ iminā mayā vuttappakārena bhūmivasena cittuppattiṃ vibhāvaye dhīro katheyya. Tathā evaṃ ekādasannaṃ puggalānaṃ vasena cittuppattiṃ dhīro vibhāvaye katheyya.

214. Thus, according to the planes, one should clarify the arising of consciousness. In this manner that I have stated, a wise person should clarify and explain the arising of consciousness according to the planes. Likewise, a wise person should clarify and explain the arising of consciousness according to the eleven types of individuals.

215.

215.

Kusalākusalā kāme,

Tesaṃ pākā ahetukā;

Āvajjanadvayañcāti,

Sattatiṃseva mānasāti. –

The wholesome and unwholesome of the sense-sphere, their rootless results, and the two adverting consciousnesses—thus there are just thirty-seven mental states.

Ayaṃ vuttatthā.

This is the meaning of what was said.

216. Evaṃ catūsvapāyabhūmīsu manussabhūmiyañcāti pañcabhūmīsu ahetukassa sattassa jāyante [V 1.0040] uppajjanti. Dvepaññāsāvasesāni, na jāyanti kadācipi avasesāni dvepaññāsa cittāni kadācipi na jāyanti na uppajjanti, tāni sarūpato vuttāneva.

216. Thus, in the four woeful states and in the human plane—in these five planes—these thirty-seven consciousnesses arise for a rootless being. The remaining fifty-two never arise. The remaining fifty-two types of consciousness never arise, never occur; they have been stated in their own form.

217. Ahetukassa sattassa uppajjantehi sattatiṃsacittehi saha duhetukā, catumahāvipākā cāti cattālīsa cittāni tathā ekakaṃ duhetukassa sattassa jāyanti.

217. For a being with two roots, forty types of consciousness arise. These are the thirty-seven that arise for a rootless being, along with the four great resultants that are two-rooted.

218-23. Sabbe mahaggatā ceva sabbe sattavīsatividhā mahaggatā ceva sabbepi ca anāsavā sabbe aṭṭha lokuttarā ceva cattāro tihetukavipākā ca kāme hasituppādo sahetukamahākiriyā cāti nava kriyāpi ceti cattālīsaṃ tathā aṭṭha ca duhetuno sattassa na jāyanti.

The twenty-seven sublime consciousnesses, the eight supramundane consciousnesses, the four resultant consciousnesses with three roots, and the nine functional consciousnesses—the smile-producing consciousness and the great functional consciousnesses with roots—these forty-eight consciousnesses do not arise for a being with two roots.

Ayametthādhippāyo [M 0.0047] – duhetuno rūpārūpasamāpattiyā asamatthatāya sattavīsa mahaggatā na jāyanti, maggaphalaṃ adhigantuṃ asamatthatāya aṭṭha lokuttarā na jāyanti, tihetukavipākā tihetukānaṃ sattānaṃ vipākacittattā na jāyanti, nava kiriyāni khīṇāsavānaṃyeva uppajjamānattā na jāyantīti. Kāmāvacarasattassa, tihetupaṭisandhino puthujjanassa catupaññāsa mānasā jāyanti. Katamāni tāni? Duhetukassa vuttāni cattālīsa cittāni tathā ekañca kāmadhātuyaṃ cattāro ñāṇasampayuttavipākā rūpārūpesu nava puññāni cāti catupaññāsa mānasā jāyanti. Puthujjanassa tihetuno kāmasattassa pañcatiṃsa cittāni na jāyare na jāyanti. Taṃ yathā –

This is the meaning here: Because a being with two roots is incapable of the form and formless attainments, the twenty-seven sublime consciousnesses do not arise. Because they are incapable of realizing the path and fruition, the eight supramundane consciousnesses do not arise. The resultants with three roots do not arise because they are the resultant consciousnesses of beings with three roots. The nine functional consciousnesses do not arise because they arise only for those whose taints are destroyed. For a worldling with a three-rooted relinking in the sense sphere, fifty-four mental states arise. Which are they? The forty consciousnesses stated for a being with two roots, as well as the four resultant consciousnesses associated with knowledge in the sense sphere and the nine wholesome consciousnesses of the form and formless realms—thus fifty-four mental states arise. For a three-rooted worldling who is a sense-sphere being, thirty-five consciousnesses do not arise. They are as follows:

Āvajjanadvayaṃ hitvā, aṭṭhārasa kriyāpi ca;

Nava mahaggatā pākā, aṭṭha lokuttarāni ca.

The eighteen functional consciousnesses, excluding the two adverting ones; the nine sublime resultants; and the eight supramundane consciousnesses.

Kāmaputhujjanasseva, tihetupaṭisandhino;

Pañcatiṃseva cittāni, na jāyanti kadācipi.

For a sense-sphere worldling with a three-rooted relinking, these thirty-five consciousnesses never arise at any time.

Chadevesu manussesu cāti sattasu bhūmīsu jātassa sotāpannassa dehino sattassa paññāsa cittāni jāyanti. Iti vacanaṃ dhīro niddise katheyya. Taṃ yathā –

For a stream-enterer born in the seven planes of existence—that is, among humans and in the six sense-sphere heavens—for such a being, fifty consciousnesses arise. Thus the wise one should point out this statement. They are as follows:

Diṭṭhiyā [V 1.0041] vippayuttāni, domanassadvayampi ca;

Uddhaccasahitañceva, kāmapuññāni aṭṭha ca.

Those dissociated from wrong view, the two accompanied by displeasure, and the one accompanied by restlessness; and the eight sense-sphere wholesome consciousnesses.

Nava mahaggatapuññāni, āvajjanadvayampi ca;

Sabbe kāmavipākā ca, sotāpattiphalampi ca.

The nine sublime wholesome consciousnesses, and the two adverting consciousnesses; all the sense-sphere resultants, and the fruition of stream-entry.

Assa sotāpannassa navatiṃseva cittāni na uppajjanti. Iti vacanaṃ dhīro dīpaye deseyya. Taṃ yathā –

For this stream-enterer, thirty-nine consciousnesses do not arise. The wise one should explain and teach this statement. They are as follows:

Āvajjanadvayaṃ hitvā, aṭṭhārasa kriyāpi ca;

Nava mahaggatā pākā, satta lokuttarāni ca.

The eighteen functional consciousnesses, excluding the two adverting ones; the nine sublime resultants; and the seven other supramundane consciousnesses.

Diṭṭhiyā [M 0.0048] sampayuttāni, vicikicchāyutaṃ tathā;

Navatiṃsa na jāyanti, sotāpannassa dehino.

Those associated with wrong view, and likewise the one connected with doubt; thus thirty-nine do not arise for the being who is a stream-enterer.

224. Paṭhamaṃ phalaṃ ṭhapetvā sotāpannassa puggalassa vuttāni cittāni attano sakadāgāmino phalena sakadāgāmiphalena saha sakadāgāmipuggalassa siyuṃ.

224. Setting aside the first fruition, the consciousnesses spoken of for the stream-enterer, together with the fruition of once-returning, are those that would arise for a once-returner.

225. Sotāpannassa vuttāni, ṭhapetvā paṭighadvayaṃ dutiyañca phalaṃ sakadāgāmiphalañca hitvā attano anāgāmiphalena saha sotāpannassa sattassa vuttāni yāni aṭṭhacattālīsa cittāni atthi, tāni anāgāmissa sattassa jāyanti. Iti vacanaṃ dhīro viniddise.

225. Setting aside the two consciousnesses accompanied by aversion from those spoken of for a stream-enterer, and excluding the fruition of the once-returner, the forty-eight consciousnesses that remain, together with the non-returner's own fruition, arise for the being who is a non-returner. Thus the wise one should discern.

226. Kati cittāni jāyanti, kāme arahato pana kāme sattasu kāmabhūmīsu jātassa arahato khīṇāsavassa kati cittāni jāyanti? Cattāri ca cattārīsañca cittāni kāme sattasu kāmabhūmīsu jātassa arahato siyuṃ bhaveyyuṃ. Taṃ yathā –

226. How many consciousnesses arise for an Arahant in the sense sphere? For an Arahant born in the seven sense-sphere planes, one whose taints are destroyed, how many consciousnesses arise? Forty-four consciousnesses would arise for an Arahant born in the seven sense-sphere planes. They are as follows:

Tevīsa kāmapākāni, kriyacittāni vīsati;

Arahattaphaleneva, kāme arahato siyuṃ.

Twenty-three sense-sphere resultant consciousnesses, twenty functional consciousnesses, and the fruition of Arahantship—these arise for an Arahant in the sense sphere.

227. Maggaṭṭhānaṃ [V 1.0042] catunnampi tesaṃ puggalānaṃ sakaṃ sakaṃ maggacittaṃ siyā bhaveyya. Ekacittakkhaṇā hi te hi saccaṃ taṃ mayā vuttaṃ vacanaṃ. Te maggā ekacittakkhaṇā.

227. For each of the four individuals established in the path, their own respective path-consciousness would arise. For those paths are of a single mind-moment. Indeed, that statement spoken by me is true: those paths are of a single mind-moment.

228. Puthujjanassa tīsveva, paṭhamajjhānabhūmisu tīsu eva paṭhamajjhānabhūmīsu jātassa puthujjanassa brahmuno pañcatiṃsa eva cittāni jāyanti. Iti vacanaṃ dhīro viniddise uccāreyya. Taṃ yathā –

228. For a worldling born in the three first-jhāna planes, for such a brahmā, thirty-five consciousnesses arise. The wise one should discern and declare this statement. They are as follows:

Domanassadvayaṃ hitvā, apuññāni daseva ca;

Kāmapuññāni aṭṭheva, nava puññā mahaggatā.

Excluding the two consciousnesses accompanied by displeasure, there are the ten unwholesome consciousnesses; the eight sense-sphere wholesome consciousnesses; and the nine sublime wholesome consciousnesses.

Cakkhusotadvayaṃ [M 0.0049] puññapākaṃ santīraṇadvayaṃ;

Āvajjanadvayañceva, puññajaṃ sampaṭicchanaṃ;

Paṭhamajjhānapāko ca, pañcatiṃseva jāyare.

The wholesome-resultant eye- and ear-consciousness pair, the two investigating consciousnesses, the two adverting consciousnesses, the wholesome-resultant receiving consciousness, and the first-jhāna resultant—these thirty-five arise.

229-234. Ghānādīsu pasādesu pavattaṃ kusalavipākaṃ viññāṇattayaṃ satta apuññajā pākā aṭṭha mahāpākā tathā uparijhānabhūmīsu jātā pākā āruppā cattāro vipākāpi ca domanassadvayampi ca āvajjanadvayavajjā aṭṭhārasa kriyā ceva aṭṭha lokuttarāni ca etāni catupaññāsa cittāni paṭhamajjhānabhūmīsu tīsu nibbattassa puthujjanassa dehino sattassa na ca labbhare na labbhanti. Tāsu tīsu bhūmīsu nibbattassa puthujjanassa brahmuno vuttesu cittesu apuññapañcakaṃ hitvā tattha tīsu paṭhamajjhānabhūmīsu nibbattassa sotāpannassa brahmuno paṭhamaphalena saha ekatiṃsa cittāni jāyare jāyanti. Sakadāgāmino tattha tīsu paṭhamajjhānabhūmīsu jātassa sakadāgāmino brahmuno tesu cittesu paṭhamaṃ phalaṃ ṭhapetvā sakadāgāmiphalaṃ pakkhipitvā ekatiṃseva cittāni jāyare. Anāgāmissa tattheva tīsu paṭhamajjhānabhūmīsu eva jātassa anāgāmissa dutiyaṃ phalaṃ ṭhapetvā attano phalacittena saha ekatiṃseva cittāni jāyanti.

The triad of wholesome-resultant consciousness occurring in the sense faculties of smell, taste, and touch; the seven unwholesome-resultant cittas; the eight great resultants; the resultants born in the higher jhāna planes; the four formless resultants; the two cittas accompanied by displeasure; the eighteen functional cittas, excluding the two adverting cittas; and the eight supramundane cittas—these fifty-four cittas are not obtained by, do not arise for, a worldling reborn in the three first-jhāna planes. From the cittas that arise for a worldling brahmā reborn in those three planes, excluding the five unwholesome ones, thirty-one cittas arise for a stream-enterer brahmā reborn there, together with the first fruition. For a once-returner brahmā born in those same three first-jhāna planes, setting aside the first fruition and including the once-returner fruition, thirty-one cittas also arise. For a non-returner born in those very same three first-jhāna planes, setting aside the second fruition, thirty-one cittas also arise, together with their own fruition-citta.

235.

235.

Viññāṇaṃ cakkhusotānaṃ, puññajaṃ sampaṭicchanaṃ;

Santīraṇadvayañceva, kriyacittāni vīsati.
