Eye- and ear-consciousness, wholesome-resultant receiving consciousness, the two investigating cittas, and twenty functional cittas.

236-7. Arahattaphalaṃ [V 1.0043] paṭhamajjhānato sambhavo pāko sattavīsati cittāni arahantassa khīṇāsavassa jāyare. Puthujjanassa tīsveva tīsu eva dutiyajjhānabhūmīsu jātassa puthujjanassa brahmuno dutiyajjhānatatiyajjhānapākena saha chattiṃsa cittāni jāyanti. Taṃ yathā –

The fruition of Arahantship and the resultant arising from the first jhāna—with others, twenty-seven cittas arise for an Arahant whose taints are destroyed. For a worldling brahmā born in the three second-jhāna planes, thirty-six cittas arise, together with the second-jhāna and third-jhāna resultants. They are as follows:

Domanassadvayaṃ [M 0.0050] hitvā, apuññāni daseva ca;

Kāmapuññāni aṭṭheva, nava puññamahaggatā.

Excluding the two cittas accompanied by displeasure, there are the ten unwholesome cittas; the eight sense-sphere wholesome cittas; and the nine sublime wholesome cittas.

Cakkhusotadvayaṃ puññapākaṃ santīraṇadvayaṃ;

Āvajjanadvayañceva, puññajaṃ sampaṭicchanaṃ.

The wholesome-resultant eye- and ear-consciousness pair, the two investigating cittas; the two adverting cittas also, and the wholesome-resultant receiving consciousness.

Dutiyajjhānapākena, tatiyajjhānapākato;

Chattiṃseva ca cittāni, dutiyajjhānadehino.

With the second-jhāna resultant and the third-jhāna resultant, there are thirty-six cittas for a being of the second-jhāna plane.

238-241. Puthujjanassa vuttesu, hitvā vāpuññapañcakaṃ attano phalena saha bāttiṃsa cittāni sotāpannassa jāyanti. Sotāpannassa vuttesu, ṭhapetvā paṭhamaṃ phalaṃ sotāpannassa vuttesu paṭhamaṃ phalaṃ ṭhapetvā attano phalacittena saha bāttiṃsa cittāni, sakadāgāmissa vuttesu dutiyaṃ phalaṃ ṭhapetvā anāgāmiphalena saha bāttiṃseva cittāni assa anāgāmino bhavanti. Arahantassa tīsveva, aṭṭhavīsati attano tīsu eva dutiyajjhānabhūmīsu jātassa arahato attano phalena dutiyajjhānatatiyajjhānapākato pākehi saha aṭṭhavīsati cittāni honti. Taṃ yathā –

From the cittas spoken of for a worldling, by excluding the five unwholesome cittas, thirty-two cittas arise for a stream-enterer, together with their own fruition. From those spoken of for a stream-enterer, setting aside the first fruition, thirty-two cittas arise for a once-returner with their own fruition-citta. From those spoken of for a once-returner, setting aside the second fruition, thirty-two cittas arise for a non-returner with the non-returner's fruition. For an Arahant born in the three second-jhāna planes, twenty-eight cittas arise, together with their own fruition and the resultants of the second and third jhānas. They are as follows:

Viññāṇaṃ cakkhusotānaṃ, puññajaṃ sampaṭicchanaṃ;

Santīraṇadvayañceva, kriyacittāni vīsati.

Eye- and ear-consciousness, wholesome-resultant receiving consciousness, the two investigating cittas, and twenty functional cittas.

Arahattaphalaṃ pāko, dutiyajjhānasambhavo;

Tatiyajjhānapāko ca, aṭṭhavīsati mānasā.

The fruition of Arahantship, the resultant arising from the second jhāna, and the third-jhāna resultant—these with the previous make twenty-eight mental states.

242-6. Parittakasubhādīnaṃ, devānaṃ tīsu bhūmīsu catutthajjhānavipākena saha pañcatiṃseva cittāni [V 1.0044] jāyanti. Sotāpannassa tattheka-tiṃsa cittāni jāyaretattha tāsu tīsu parittakasubhādīnaṃ bhūmīsu sotāpannassa ca ekatiṃsa cittāni jāyare. Yathā evaṃ sakadāgāmino ekatiṃsa cittāni jāyare. Tathā anāgāmino ekatiṃsa jāyare. Tattheva [M 0.0051] tāsu tīsu bhūmīsu eva jātassa khīṇāsavassa sattavīsati mānasā honti, tathā evaṃ vehapphale vehapphalabhūmiyaṃ jātānaṃ puthujjanasekkhānaṃ pañcannaṃ sabbesaṃ puggalānaṃ mānasā honti. Pañcasu suddhāvāsikabhūmīsu jātassa anāgāmino sattassa ekatiṃseva cittāni honti. Iti vacanaṃ dhīro paridīpaye deseyya. Tattheva tāsu suddhāvāsabhūmīsu eva jātassa arahato sattavīsati mānasā honti. Evaṃ iminā mayā vuttappakārena rūpīsu pañcadasasu rūpibhūmīsu jātānaṃ sabbesaṃ puggalānaṃ cittāni vibhāvinā dhīrena viññeyyāni jānitabbāni.

For the devas of the planes of Limited Luster and so on, in those three planes, thirty-five cittas arise, together with the fourth-jhāna resultant. For a stream-enterer in those three planes, thirty-one cittas arise. Similarly, for a once-returner, thirty-one cittas arise. Likewise, for a non-returner, thirty-one arise. In those same three planes, for one whose taints are destroyed, an Arahant, born there, twenty-seven mental states arise. Likewise, in the Vehapphala plane, the mental states are the same for all five types of individuals born there—worldlings and trainees. For a non-returner born in the five Pure Abodes, thirty-one cittas arise. The wise one should explain and teach this statement. In those same Pure Abodes, for an Arahant born there, twenty-seven mental states arise. In this way, as explained by me, the cittas of all individuals born in the fifteen fine-material planes should be understood and known by the discerning wise one.

247. Catuvīsati cittāni, paṭhamāruppabhūmiyaṃ paṭhamaāruppabhūmiyaṃ jātassa puthujjanassa catuvīsati cittāni jāyanti. Iti vacanaṃ dhīro viniddise. Taṃ yathā –

247. For a worldling born in the first immaterial plane, twenty-four cittas arise. Thus should a wise one explain. They are as follows:

Domanassadvayaṃ hitvā, apuññāni daseva ca;

Kāmapuññāni aṭṭheva, āruppakusalāni ca;

Paṭhamāruppapāko ca, kriyāvoṭṭhabbanampi ca.

Having excluded the two [cittas] accompanied by displeasure, there are the ten unwholesome ones; the eight sense-sphere wholesome ones and the four immaterial wholesome ones; the resultant of the first immaterial [attainment] and the functional determining [consciousness] too.

248-251. Sotāpannassa tattheva, ṭhapetvāpuññapañcakaṃtattha tissaṃ paṭhamāruppabhūmiyaṃ eva sotāpannassa puggalassa apuññapañcakaṃ hitvā attano phalena saha vīsati cittāni honti. Tathā tattha tissaṃ paṭhamāruppabhūmiyaṃ sakadāgāmino, anāgāminopi ca puggalassa pubbaṃ pubbaṃ phalaṃ vinā vajjetvā attano phalena saha vīsati cittāni jāyanti. Khīṇāsavassa tattheva tattha tissaṃ paṭhamāruppabhūmiyaṃ eva jātassa khīṇāsavassa dasa pañca mānasā ca jāyanti. Taṃ yathā –

For a stream-enterer in that very first immaterial plane, having abandoned the five unwholesome cittas, there are twenty cittas together with their own fruition. Similarly, for a once-returner and a non-returner in that very first immaterial plane, excluding the preceding fruition, twenty cittas arise for each together with their own fruition. For an Arahant born right there in that very first immaterial plane, fifteen minds arise. They are as follows:

Mahākriyāni aṭṭheva, catvāruppakriyāni ca;

Arahattaphalaṃ pāko, voṭṭhabbañcāpi mānasaṃ.

The eight great functional [cittas] and the four immaterial functional [cittas]; the fruition of Arahantship, the resultant, and the determining mind too.

Dutiyāruppabhūmiyaṃ [M 0.0052] jātassa puthujjanassa sattassa tevīsati cittāni honti. Taṃ yathā –

For a worldling born in the second immaterial plane, there are twenty-three cittas. They are as follows:

Domanassadvayaṃ [V 1.0045] hitvā, apuññāni daseva ca;

Kāmapuññāni aṭṭheva, puññārūpūparī tayo;

Dutiyāruppapāko ca, voṭṭhabbañcāpi mānasaṃ.

Having excluded the two [cittas] with displeasure, there are the ten unwholesome ones; the eight sense-sphere wholesome ones, and the three higher immaterial wholesome ones; the resultant of the second immaterial [attainment], and the determining mind too.

Iti evaṃ iminā pakārena vatvā kathetvā dhīro paṇḍito vibhāvaye deseyya. Ettha etissaṃ dutiyāruppabhūmiyaṃ jātānaṃ tiṇṇannaṃ sekkhānampi ekūnavīsati cittāni honti. Taṃ yathā –

Thus, having spoken and explained in this manner, the wise and learned one should clarify and teach. Here, for the three trainees born in this second immaterial plane, there are also nineteen cittas. They are as follows:

Diṭṭhiyā vippayuttāni, uddhaccasahitaṃ tathā;

Kāmapuññāni aṭṭheva, puññārūpūparī tayo.

[The four unwholesome cittas] dissociated from wrong view, and likewise the one accompanied by restlessness; the eight sense-sphere wholesome ones, and the three higher immaterial wholesome ones.

Dutiyāruppapāko ca, voṭṭhabbañcāpi mānasaṃ;

Sakasakaphaleneva, cittānekūnavīsati.

And the resultant of the second immaterial [attainment], and the determining mind too; with one's own respective fruition, the cittas are nineteen.

252. Cuddaseva tu cittāni dutiyāruppabhūmiyaṃ jātassa khīṇāsavassa kiriyacittāni dvādasa eko pāko arahattaphalañcāti cuddaseva cittāni honti. Taṃ yathā –

252. Indeed, for an Arahant born in the second immaterial plane, there are fourteen cittas: twelve functional cittas, one resultant, and the fruition of Arahantship. Thus there are fourteen cittas. They are as follows:

Mahākriyāni aṭṭheva, kriyārūpūparī tayo;

Voṭṭhabbañca sako pāko, arahattaphalampi ca.

The eight great functional [cittas], and the three higher immaterial functional ones; the determining [consciousness], their own resultant, and the fruition of Arahantship too.

253. Puthujjanassa sattassa, tatiyāruppabhūmiyaṃ tatiyaarūpabhūmiyaṃ jātassa puthujjanassa sattassa bāvīsati cittāni bhavanti. Iti vacanaṃ dhīro pakāsaye. Taṃ yathā –

253. For a worldling born in the third immaterial plane, there are twenty-two cittas. Thus a wise one should declare. They are as follows:

Domanassadvayaṃ hitvā, apuññāni daseva ca;

Kāmapuññāni aṭṭheva, puññārūpūparī duve;

Tatiyāruppapāko ca, voṭṭhabbañcāpi mānasaṃ.

Having excluded the two [cittas] with displeasure, there are the ten unwholesome ones; the eight sense-sphere wholesome ones, and the two higher immaterial wholesome ones; the resultant of the third immaterial [attainment], and the determining mind too.

254-5. Aṭṭhāraseva cittāni, sotāpannassa puggalassa aṭṭhārasa eva cittāni jāyare. Taṃ yathā –

254-5. For a stream-enterer there are eighteen cittas; for the stream-entering person, eighteen cittas indeed arise. They are as follows:

Diṭṭhiyā [M 0.0053][V 1.0046] vippayuttāni, uddhaccasahitaṃ tathā;

Mahāpuññāni aṭṭheva, puññārūpūparī duve.

The four [unwholesome cittas] dissociated from wrong view, and likewise the one accompanied by restlessness; the eight great wholesome ones, and the two higher wholesome immaterial ones.

Aṭṭhāraseva pākena, sotāpattiphalena ca;

Voṭṭhabbañcāpi mānasaṃ, sotāpannassa jāyare.

With the resultant, the fruit of stream-entry, and the determining mind as well, eighteen [cittas] arise for the stream-enterer.

Sakadāgāmino paṭhamaṃ phalaṃ ṭhapetvā attano phalena tāni aṭṭhārasa cittāni honti. Sakadāgāmino vuttesu cittesu dutiyaṃ phalaṃ ṭhapetvā attano phalena saha aṭṭhārasa cittāni eva anāgāmissa jāyare.

For the once-returner, excluding the first fruit, there are those eighteen cittas together with his own fruit. For the non-returner, from among the cittas mentioned for the once-returner, excluding the second fruit, eighteen cittas likewise arise together with his own fruit.

256. Teraseva ca cittāni, tatiyāruppabhūmiyaṃ tatiyaarūpabhūmiyaṃ jātassa khīṇāsavassa teraseva cittāni jāyanti. Iti vacanaṃ dhīro viniddise. Taṃ yathā –

256. And for an Arahant born in the third immaterial plane, thirteen cittas arise. Thus should a wise one explain this statement. They are as follows:

Mahākriyāni aṭṭheva, kriyārūpūparī duve;

Arahattaphalaṃ pāko, voṭṭhabbañcāpi mānasaṃ.

The eight great functional [cittas], and the two higher immaterial functional ones; the fruit of Arahantship, the resultant, and the determining mind as well.

257. Ekavīsati cittāni, catutthāruppabhūmiyaṃ catutthaarūpabhūmiyaṃ jātassa puthujjanassa sattassa ekavīsati cittāni jāyanti. Iti idaṃ vacanaṃ dhīro viniddise. Taṃ yathā –

257. For an ordinary being born in the fourth immaterial plane, twenty-one cittas arise. Thus should a wise one explain this statement. They are as follows:

Domanassadvayaṃ hitvā, apuññāni daseva ca;

Kāmapuññāni aṭṭheva, voṭṭhabbañcāpi mānasaṃ;

Catutthāruppapuññañca, sapākenekavīsati.

Having excluded the two [cittas] with displeasure, there are the ten unwholesome ones; the eight sense-sphere wholesome ones, and the determining mind as well; the fourth immaterial wholesome [citta] with its resultant makes twenty-one.

258-260. Sotāpannassa sattassa, sattarasa cittāni dhīro pakāsaye. Taṃ yathā –

258-260. A wise one should declare seventeen cittas for a stream-entering being. They are as follows:

Diṭṭhiyā vippayuttāni, uddhaccasahitaṃ tathā;

Kāmapuññāni aṭṭheva, sotāpattiphalampi ca;

Catutthāruppapuññañca, sapāko voṭṭhabbampi ca.

The four [unwholesome cittas] dissociated from wrong view, and likewise the one accompanied by restlessness; the eight sense-sphere wholesome ones, and the fruit of stream-entry too; the fourth immaterial wholesome [citta] with its resultant, and the determining [consciousness] too.

Sakadāgāmino [V 1.0047] paṭhamaṃ phalaṃ ṭhapetvā tāni eva cittāni saphalena honti. Sakadāgāmino vuttesu cittesu dutiyaṃ [M 0.0054] phalaṃ ṭhapetvā attano phalena sattarasa mānasā anāgāmissa honti. Dvādaseva tu cittāni, catutthāruppabhūmiyaṃ jātassa arahantassa dvādasa eva cittāni jāyanti. Taṃ yathā –

For the once-returner, excluding the first fruit, there are those same cittas together with his own fruit. For the non-returner, from among the cittas mentioned for the once-returner, excluding the second fruit, there are seventeen minds together with his own fruit. Indeed, for an Arahant born in the fourth immaterial plane, twelve cittas arise. They are as follows:

Mahākriyāni aṭṭheva, voṭṭhabbañcāpi mānasaṃ;

Catutthañca kriyārūpaṃ, pāko arahato phalaṃ.

The eight great functional [cittas] and the determining mind as well; and the fourth immaterial functional [citta], its resultant, and the Arahant's fruit.

Iti evaṃ iminā mayā vuttappakārena puggalānaṃ vasena bhūmīsu cittappavattiṃ vidū dhīro vibhāvaye.

Thus, in the way described by me, a knowing and wise one should elucidate the occurrence of cittas in the planes according to the individuals.

261-2. Heṭṭhimānaṃ arūpīnaṃ, brahmānaṃ uparūpari jātā arūpakusalā ceva kiriyāpi ca uppajjanti. Uddhaṃ uddhaṃ bhāge jātānaṃ arūpīnaṃ brahmānaṃ heṭṭhimā heṭṭhimā āruppā heṭṭhābhāge jātā arūpāvacarā pana neva jāyanti. Kasmā kāraṇāti? Kira mayā sutaṃ, heṭṭhimajhānesu diṭṭhādīnavato diṭṭhadosabhāvato neva jāyanti.

261-2. For the lower immaterial brahmās, wholesome and functional immaterial [cittas] of the successively higher planes arise. But for immaterial brahmās born in successively higher planes, the lower immaterial [attainments] do not arise. For what reason? I have heard it said that they do not arise because of having seen the danger and fault in the lower jhānas.

263-5. Ṭhapetvā paṭhamaṃ maggaṃ sotāpattimaggaṃ ṭhapetvā kusalānuttarā tayo tayo anuttarā kusalā tayo maggā, kāmāvacarapuññāni aṭṭha, tathā dasa apuññāni cittāni, arūpapuññāni cattāri. Sabbe pākā anuttarā sabbāni lokuttaraphalāni, paṭhamāruppapāko ca nava kāmakiriyāpi ca, arūpāpi sabbā kiriyā, etāni pana tecattālīsa mānasā paṭhamāruppabhūmiyaṃ uppajjanti.

263-5. Excluding the first path, the three higher supramundane wholesome paths, the eight sense-sphere wholesome cittas, the ten unwholesome cittas, and the four immaterial wholesome cittas; all the supramundane resultants, the first immaterial resultant, the nine sense-sphere functional cittas, and all the immaterial functional cittas—these forty-three minds arise in the first immaterial plane.

266-7. Sabbo tevīsatikāmavipāko, sabbo pannarasavidho mahaggato rūpo cittuppādo, manodhātu kiriyāmanodhātu, domanassadvayampi ca ādimaggo ca tathā upari jātā tayo arūpapākā cāti chacattālīsa cittāni ettha etissaṃ paṭhamāruppabhūmiyaṃ natthi.

266-7. All twenty-three sense-sphere resultant cittas, all fifteen kinds of fine-material sphere cittas, the mind-element, the functional mind-element, the two [cittas] accompanied by displeasure, the initial path, and the three higher immaterial resultants—these forty-six cittas do not exist here in this first immaterial plane.

268-9. Vuttesu [M 0.0055] pana cittesu, paṭhamāruppabhūmiyaṃ vuttesu cittesu kusalapākakiriyāvasena paṭhamāruppattayaṃ ṭhapetvā attano pāko cāti cattālīsa cittāni dutiyāruppabhūmiyaṃ [V 1.0048] jāyanti. Evaṃ iminā mayā vuttappakārena sesadvaye paṭhamadutiyāruppato sesaākiñcaññāyatananevasaññānāsaññāyatanabhūmidvaye heṭṭhimaheṭṭhimaṃ kusalavipākakiriyāvasena heṭṭhābhāge jātaṃ arūpattayaṃ hitvā attano attano pākā evaṃ iminā mayā vuttappakārena paṇḍitena ñeyyā jānitabbā.

268-9. Now, from the cittas mentioned for the first immaterial plane, by excluding the triad of the first immaterial attainment—wholesome, resultant, and functional—forty cittas arise in the second immaterial plane. In the manner I have explained, for the remaining two planes—the plane of nothingness and the plane of neither-perception-nor-non-perception—it should be understood by the wise that the triads of the lower immaterial planes are respectively excluded.

270-3. Cattāro ca anāsavā, vipākā cattāri lokuttaraphalacittāni, sabbe sabbāni ca catūsu āruppabhūmīsu honti. Voṭṭhabbanena cittena saha kāme aṭṭha mahākiriyā, catasso arūpakiriyāpi cāti terasa eva kiriyā paṭhamāruppabhūmiyaṃ jātassa khīṇāsavassa jāyanti. Dutiyāruppabhūmiyaṃ jātassa khīṇāsavassa paṭhamāruppakiriyaṃ hitvā dvādasa eva kiriyā honti. Tatiyāruppabhūmiyaṃ jātassa khīṇāsavassa paṭhamadutiyāruppakiriyāni hitvā ekādasa kiriyā honti. Catutthāruppabhūmiyaṃ jātassa khīṇāsavassa paṭhamadutiyatatiyāruppakiriyāni hitvā daseva kiriyā ñeyyā jānitabbā.

270-3. The four taintless resultants—the four supramundane fruit-cittas—are all present in the four immaterial planes. Together with the determining citta, the eight great functional [cittas] of the sense-sphere and the four immaterial functional [cittas]—thus thirteen functional cittas arise for an Arahant born in the first immaterial plane. For an Arahant born in the second immaterial plane, excluding the first immaterial functional [citta], twelve functional cittas arise. For an Arahant born in the third immaterial plane, excluding the first and second immaterial functional [cittas], eleven functional cittas arise. For an Arahant born in the fourth immaterial plane, excluding the first, second, and third immaterial functional [cittas], ten functional cittas are to be known.

274.

274.

Arahato pana cittāni, honti ekūnavīsati;

Arahattaṃ kriyā sabbā, ṭhapetvāvajjanadvayaṃ.

But for an Arahant, there are nineteen cittas: the fruit of Arahantship and all functional [cittas], excluding the two adverting [cittas].

Āvajjanadvayaṃ ṭhapetvā sabbā kiriyā, arahattaphalañcāti ekūnavīsati cittāni arahato pana honti. Āvajjanadvayaṃ kiñcāpi khīṇāsavassa honti, evampi aññesaṃ puthujjanasekkhānampi hontiyeva. Ekūnavīsati cittāni khīṇāsavassa eva honti, na aññesanti ñāpanatthaṃ “āvajjanadvayaṃ ṭhapetvā”ti vuttaṃ.

Excluding the two adverting [cittas], all functional [cittas] and the fruit of Arahantship are the nineteen cittas that an Arahant has. Although the two adverting [cittas] occur for an Arahant, they also occur for other ordinary persons and trainees. To make it known that the nineteen cittas belong only to an Arahant and not to others, it was said, 'excluding the two adverting [cittas].'

275-6. Catunnaṃ [M 0.0056] phalaṭṭhānaṃ puggalānañca tihetukaputhujjane ca teraseva cittāni bhavanti. Iti vacanaṃ dhīro pakāsaye. Taṃ yathā – cattāro ñāṇasampayuttā mahāvipākāni, nava rūpārūpapākā ca ime teraseva cittāni bhavanti.

275-6. For the four persons established in the fruit and for the three-rooted worldling, there are just thirteen consciousnesses. Thus the wise should declare. That is: the four great resultants associated with knowledge and the nine form-sphere and formless-sphere resultants; these are the thirteen consciousnesses.

277-9. Catunnaṃ phalaṭṭhānaṃ puggalānañca duhetukaputhujjane ca ñāṇaparihīnāni cattāri vipākāni eva jāyare. Puthujjanānaṃ tiṇṇampi, catunnaṃ ariyadehinaṃ ariyagatānaṃ sattannaṃ puggalānaṃ [V 1.0049] sattaraseva cittāni bhavanti. Taṃ yathā – duve pañcaviññāṇāni, manodhātuttayasantīraṇāni, voṭṭhabbanañca ime sattarasa eva honti.

277-9. For the four persons established in the fruit and for two-rooted worldlings, only the four resultants devoid of knowledge arise. For the three kinds of worldlings and for the four noble persons—for these seven persons—there are just seventeen consciousnesses. That is: the ten five-sense consciousnesses, the mind-element-triad, the three investigating consciousnesses, and the determining consciousness; these are the seventeen.

280-5. Heṭṭhā tiṇṇaṃ phalaṭṭhānaṃ, tihetukaputhujjane catunnaṃ puggalānaṃ mahaggatāni eva kusalāni honti. Tiṇṇaṃ puthujjanānañca, ādito tiṇṇaṃ ariyānaṃ heṭṭhā ariyānaṃ teraseva cittāni uppajjanti. Iti vacanaṃ dhīro niddise. Aṭṭheva kāmapuññāni, apuññato akusalavasena diṭṭhihīnā cattāro cittuppādāpi, uddhaccasampayuttañcāti terasa cittāni honti. Heṭṭhā dvinnaṃ phalaṭṭhānaṃ sotāpannasakadāgāmipuggalānaṃ sabbaputhujjane ahetukaduhetukatihetukaputhujjane domanassayuttaṃ dvayameva cittaṃ jāyate. Tiṇṇaṃ puthujjanānañca pañca eva jāyare. Taṃ yathā –

280-5. For the four persons—the three lower fruit-attainers and the three-rooted worldling—only the sublime wholesome consciousnesses arise. For the three kinds of worldlings and for the three lower noble ones, just thirteen consciousnesses arise. Thus the wise should point out. They are: the eight sense-sphere wholesome consciousnesses, and from the unwholesome, the four consciousnesses devoid of wrong view and the one associated with restlessness; these are the thirteen consciousnesses. For the two lower fruit-attainers—the stream-enterer and the once-returner—and for all worldlings—the rootless, two-rooted, and three-rooted—only the pair of consciousnesses associated with displeasure arises. And for the three kinds of worldlings, just five arise. They are as follows:

Cattāri diṭṭhiyuttāni, vicikicchāyutampi ca;

Maggaṭṭhānaṃ catunnampi, maggacittaṃ sakaṃ sakaṃ.

The four associated with wrong view, and also the one associated with doubt. For the four persons established in the path, there is their own respective path consciousness.

Tesaṃ catunnaṃ maggaṭṭhānaṃ puggalānaṃ sakaṃ sakaṃ ekameva maggacittaṃ bhave bhaveyya. Iti evaṃ iminā mayā vuttappakārena dhīro paṇḍito vibhāvaye cittappavattiṃ pakāsaye.

For those four persons established in the path, in any given existence there would be only their own single path consciousness. Thus, in this way described by me, the wise and learned person should clarify and declare the process of consciousness.

286-9. Mayā bhavesu cittānaṃ, puggalānaṃ vasena ca. Bhavesu sabbabhavesu cittānaṃ, puggalānaṃ vasena ca cittappavatti bhikkhūnaṃ [M 0.0057] ābhidhammikabhikkhūnaṃ pāṭavatthāya chekabhāvāya mayā pakāsitā. Evaṃ sabbamidaṃ cittaṃ, bhūmipuggalabhedato evaṃ iminā mayā vuttappakārena bhūmipuggalabhedato idaṃ sabbaṃ cittaṃ bahudhāpi ca bahuppakārampi ca hoti. Iti gahaṇaṃ vibhāvinā viññātabbaṃ. Sakkā vuttānusārena mayā vuttassa anusārena bhedo cittabhedo vibhāvinā ñātuṃ vijānituṃ sakkā. Ganthavitthārabhītena mayā idaṃ cittappavattidīpakavacanaṃ saṃkhittaṃ, pubbāparaṃ viloketvā, cintetvā ca punappunaṃ atthaṃ upaparikkhitvā vibhāvinā gahetabbaṃ.

286-9. The process of consciousness in all existences, according to the persons, has been declared by me for the proficiency and skill of bhikkhus who are experts in the Abhidhamma. Thus, in this way described by me, according to the distinctions of planes and persons, all this consciousness becomes manifold and of many kinds. This should be understood by the discerning one. It is possible for the discerning one to know and understand the distinctions of consciousness in accordance with what has been said. Fearing the expansion of the text, this discourse illuminating the process of consciousness has been condensed by me. Having examined what comes before and after, having reflected again and again, and having investigated the meaning, it should be grasped by the discerning one.

290. Imañcābhidhammāvatāraṃ susāraṃ, varaṃ sattamohandhakārappadīpaṃ imañca abhidhammāvatārappakaraṇaṃ susāraṃ sundarasārabhūtaṃ varaṃ sattaandhakārasadise mohe padīpaṃ pajjotappadīpaṃ [V 1.0050] yo naro sādhukaṃ cinteti vācetipi, taṃ naraṃ rāgadosā ciraṃ cirakālaṃ nopayanti na upagacchanti.

290. This Abhidhammāvatāra, of excellent essence, the supreme lamp for the darkness of beings' delusion: whatever person carefully reflects on or recites this treatise—the Abhidhammāvatāra, which is of excellent and beautiful essence, supreme, a lamp, a shining lamp for the delusion that is like the darkness of beings—lust and hatred will not approach that person for a long, long time.

Iti abhidhammāvatāraṭīkāya

Thus in the Subcommentary to the Abhidhammāvatāra.

Bhūmipuggalacittuppattiniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Exposition on the Arising of Consciousness according to Planes and Persons is finished.

Pañcamo paricchedo.

The Fifth Chapter.

6. Chaṭṭho paricchedo

6. The Sixth Chapter.

Ārammaṇavibhāgavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Analysis of Objects.

291.

291.

Etesaṃ pana cittānaṃ, ārammaṇamito paraṃ;

Dassayissāmahaṃ tena, vinā natthi hi sambhavo.

Hereafter I will show the objects of these consciousnesses, for without an object, their arising is indeed impossible.

Ito paraṃ ito paricchedato paraṃ ahaṃ etesaṃ pana cittānaṃ ārammaṇaṃ dassayissāmi. Hi kasmā? Tena vinā taṃ ārammaṇaṃ vajjetvā cittānaṃ sambhavo natthi yasmā kāraṇā, tasmā kāraṇā dassayissāmi.

Hereafter, that is, after this chapter, I will show the objects of these consciousnesses. Indeed, why? Because without it—that is, apart from that object—there is no arising of consciousnesses; for that reason, I will show them.

292.

292.

Rūpaṃ [M 0.0058] saddaṃ gandhaṃ rasaṃ, phoṭṭhabbaṃ dhammameva ca;

Chadhā ārammaṇaṃ āhu, chaḷārammaṇakovidā.

Form, sound, smell, taste, tangible object, and the dhamma-object: those skilled in the six objects say that the object is sixfold.

Chaḷārammaṇesu chekā paṇḍitā ārammaṇaṃ chadhā chappakāraṃ āhu kathesuṃ.

The wise who are skilled in the six objects have said that the object is sixfold, of six kinds.

293. Tattha bhūte upādāya. Tattha tesu ārammaṇesu bhūte upādāya bhūte paṭicca vaṇṇo catusamuṭṭhito [V 1.0051] kammacittautuāhārasaṅkhātehi catūhi paccayehi samuṭṭhito nibbatto nidassanena saha pavatto paṭighena saha pavatto rūpārammaṇasaññito.

293. Therein, depending on the primary elements. Therein, among those objects, color, which depends on the primary elements, which is conditioned by the primary elements, arises from four sources—that is, it is arisen and produced from the four conditions called kamma, consciousness, temperature, and nutriment. Occurring with visibility and with resistance, it is designated as the form-object.

294. Duvidhopi samuddiṭṭho, saddo cittotusambhavo saddo duvidhopi muninā samuddiṭṭho cittotusambhavo, saviññāṇakasaddova cittasamuṭṭhito hoti. Kathaṃ? Vacībhedakacittena bhūtāya jātāya bhūmiyā pathavīdhātuyā vikāratā pathavīlakkhaṇabhāvato atithaddhalakkhaṇatā vikāratā nāma. Sā vacīviññatti viññāyatīti viññattiyā upādiṇṇaghaṭṭanassa kammajapathavīdhātuyā ghaṭṭanassa kāraṇaṃ cittajapathavīdhātuyā kammajapathavīdhātuyā ghaṭṭanañca saddo ca apubbaṃ acarimaṃ hoti.

294. Sound is pointed out as twofold: arisen from consciousness and temperature. Sound has been pointed out as twofold by the Sage: arisen from consciousness and temperature. Sound associated with a living being is that which arises from consciousness. How? By the consciousness that produces speech, there is an alteration of the earth element, which is the basis that has arisen. This alteration is the characteristic of extreme hardness, departing from the natural state of the earth element. That is verbal intimation. The striking of the consciousness-born earth element with the kamma-born earth element is the cause for the striking of the appropriated, kamma-born earth element; this striking and the sound arise simultaneously.

295. Aviññāṇakasaddo yo so aviññāṇakasaddo utusamuṭṭhito hoti. Ayaṃ duvidhopi saddo saddārammaṇataṃ gato saddārammaṇabhāvaṃ patto.

295. That sound which is not associated with a living being is arisen from temperature. This sound, of both kinds, becomes a sound-object, attaining the state of a sound-object.

296. Dharīyatīti gacchanto gacchanto janehi dharīyateti gandho. Gamu sappa gatimhi, dhara dhāraṇe. Sūcanato attano sādhāraṇassa pupphādino vatthussa pakāsanatopi vā gandho nāma. Gandha sūcane. Ayaṃ gandho catūhi samuṭṭhānaṃ etassāti catusamuṭṭhāno. Gandhārammaṇasammato.

296. It is called 'gandha' (smell) because it is borne by people as they go about. The root 'gam' is in the sense of going; 'dhara' is in the sense of bearing. Or it is called 'gandha' from 'indicating,' because it reveals its own basis, such as a flower. The root 'gandh' is in the sense of indicating. This smell has four sources of origin and is considered the smell-object.

297. Rasamānā [M 0.0059] rasantīti, rasoti parikittito janā rasamānā yaṃ dhammajātaṃ rasanti anubhavanti, iti yasmā kāraṇā, tasmā kāraṇā raso iti raso nāma paṇḍitehi parikittito, so raso catusambhūto rasārammaṇanāmako.

297. Because they savor it, it is called 'rasa' (taste). Because people, while savoring, taste and experience a certain phenomenon, for that reason it is declared by the wise by the name 'rasa.' That taste, arisen from four sources, is named the taste-object.

298. Phusīyatīti phoṭṭhabbaṃ yaṃ dhammajātaṃ janehi phusīyatīti tasmā phoṭṭhabbaṃ, pathavītejavāyavo. Taṃ phoṭṭhabbaṃ catusambhūtaṃ phoṭṭhabbārammaṇaṃ mataṃ.

298. Because it is touched, it is called a 'tangible.' Because a certain phenomenon is touched by people, it is therefore a tangible—this refers to the earth, fire, and air elements. That tangible, arisen from four sources, is considered the tangible-object.

299. Sabbaṃ nāmañca rūpañca, hitvā rūpādipañcakaṃ rūpādipañcakaṃ hitvā sabbaṃ nāmañca cittacetasikanibbānanāmañca rūpañca pañcapasādasukhumarūpañca lakkhaṇāni ca aniccadukkhaanattalakkhaṇāni ca paññatti ca dhammārammaṇasaññitaṃ.

299. Having excluded the pentad beginning with form, all mentality (consciousness, mental factors, and Nibbāna), and the rest of materiality (the five sensitivities and subtle matter), as well as characteristics (impermanence, suffering, and non-self), and concepts, are designated as the dhamma-object.

300. Chārammaṇāni [V 1.0052] labbhanti, kāmāvacarabhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacarabhūmiyaṃ chārammaṇāni labbhanti. Tīṇi rūpāvacare rūpasaddadhammārammaṇavasena labbhanti. Arūpe pana ekekaṃ dhammārammaṇaṃ labbhati.

300. Six objects are found in the sense-sphere plane. In the sense-sphere plane, six objects are found. In the form sphere, three are found, namely, the form, sound, and dhamma objects. In the formless sphere, however, only the single dhamma-object is found.

301-3. Khaṇavatthuparittattā, āpāthaṃ na vajanti ye ye rūpādayo pañca visayā khaṇavatthuparittattā pañcārammaṇānaṃ khaṇassa parittattā mandattā tesaṃ appāyukattā vatthuparittattā pañcārammaṇānaṃ atikhuddakavatthukattā āpāthaṃ pañcadvāresu pākaṭabhāvaṃ na vajanti, pañcapasādesu ghaṭṭanakiccaṃ na sādhenti, te rūpādayo pañca visayā dhammārammaṇaṃ honti. Iti yesaṃ ekaccānaṃ ācariyānaṃ mataṃ hoti. Kirāti anussavanatthe nipāto. Te paṭikkhipitabbāva te evaṃ vādino ekacce ācariyā paṭikkhipitabbā, mayā paṭisedhitabbā. Kasmā? Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ sotaviññāṇassa gocarabhūtaṃ saddaṃ na paṭianubhoti, sotaviññāṇaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa gocarabhūtaṃ [M 0.0060] rūpaṃ na paṭianubhoti. Iti aññamaññassa gocaraṃ neva paccanubhontānaṃ tesaṃ pañcannaṃ cakkhuviññāṇādīnaṃ viññāṇānaṃ tañca gocaraṃ manodhātumanoviññāṇadhātusaṅkhātaṃ javanaṃ pana paccanubhoti. Iti vacanassa bhagavatā vuttattā paṭikkhipitabbā. Rūpādayo pana visayā rūpādipañcārammaṇāni eva honti.

301-3. 'Because of the minuteness of their moment and basis, they do not come into range.' Those five objects beginning with form which, because of the minuteness of their moment and basis—that is, the weakness and short duration of the moment of the five objects, and the extreme smallness of the basis of the five objects—do not come into range, that is, do not become manifest at the five doors and do not accomplish the function of striking the five sensitivities, those five objects beginning with form become the dhamma-object. This, it is said, is the view of certain teachers. The particle 'kirā' is in the sense of hearsay. Those who hold such a view are to be refuted; they are to be rejected by me. Why? Because it was said by the Blessed One: 'Eye-consciousness does not experience sound, the object-domain of ear-consciousness; ear-consciousness does not experience form, the object-domain of eye-consciousness.' Thus, while those five consciousnesses beginning with eye-consciousness do not experience one another's object-domain, the impulsion, designated as mind-element and mind-consciousness-element, does experience that object-domain. Because this was stated by the Blessed One, they are to be refuted. Rather, the objects beginning with form are only the five objects beginning with form.

304-6. Dibbacakkhādiñāṇānaṃ, rūpādīneva gocarā tāni rūpādīni eva gocarā dibbacakkhādiñāṇānaṃ anāpāthagatānaṃ eva pākaṭabhāvaṃ appattāneva. Itipi vacanaṃ vuttaṃ na yujjati. Yaṃ dhammajātaṃ rūpārammaṇaṃ bhavantaṃ, taṃ dhammajātaṃ kathaṃ kena pakārena dhammārammaṇaṃ bhaveyya? Evaṃ sati rūpārammaṇassa dhammārammaṇatte sati etesaṃ rūpārammaṇadhammārammaṇānaṃ niyamopi kathaṃ bhave kena pakārena bhaveyya? Sabbaṃ ārammaṇaṃ etaṃ etaṃ sabbaṃ ārammaṇaṃ chabbidhaṃ chappakāraṃ bhagavatā samudīritaṃ. Taṃ parittattikādīnaṃ vasena bahuppakārehi mataṃ.

304-6. The objects of the divine eye and other knowledges are only forms and so on, even those that have not come into range and have not attained a state of manifestation. This statement is also untenable. How, in what way, could a phenomenon that is a form-object become a mental-object? If this were so, how, in what way, could there be a fixed distinction between these form-objects and mental-objects? All this object, this entire range of objects, has been declared by the Blessed One to be of six kinds. This is regarded in many ways by means of the triad of the limited, etc.

307. Sabbo kāmavipāko ca sabbo tevīsatikāmavipāko ca kriyāhetudvayampi ca manodhātuhasituppādavasena kiriyāhetudvayampi cāti pañcavīsati cittuppādā ekantaparittārammaṇā ekantakāmāvacarārammaṇā siyuṃ bhaveyyuṃ.

307. All sense-sphere resultant consciousness—that is, all twenty-three sense-sphere resultant consciousnesses—and also the two rootless functional consciousnesses, namely, the mind-element and the smile-producing consciousness: these twenty-five types of consciousness have exclusively limited objects and exclusively sense-sphere objects.

308-10. Iṭṭhādibhedā pañceva, rūpasaddādayo pana dvipañcannaṃ viññāṇānaṃ paṭipāṭiyā anukkamena gocarā honti. Rūpādipañcakaṃ sabbaṃ, manodhātuttayassa tu manodhātuttayassa pana sabbaṃ [V 1.0053] rūpādipañcakaṃ ārammaṇaṃ hoti, etesaṃ terasannaṃ pana cittānaṃ rūpakkhandhova gocaro ārammaṇaṃ hoti. Nārūpaṃ nāmaṃ ārammaṇaṃ na karonti. Na ca paññattiṃ paññattiṃ ārammaṇaṃ na karonti. Nātītaṃ atītaṃ ārammaṇaṃ na karonti[M 0.0061]. Na canāgataṃ anāgataṃ ārammaṇaṃ na karonti eva. Hi saccaṃ vattamāno gocaro etesaṃ dvipañcaviññāṇānaṃ, manodhātuttayassa cāti terasannaṃ cittānaṃ taṃ ārammaṇaṃ vattamānaṃ eva paccuppannaṃ eva.

308-10. The five kinds of objects distinguished as desirable, etc.—that is, forms, sounds, and so on—are the respective objects, in sequence, of the two sets of five consciousnesses. The entire pentad of form, etc., is the object of the triple mind-element. For these thirteen types of consciousness, only the form aggregate is the object. They do not take the non-material or name as their object. Nor do they take a concept as their object. They do not take the past as their object, nor do they take the future. Indeed, their object is strictly the present—for these two sets of five consciousnesses and the triple mind-element, that is, for these thirteen consciousnesses. That object is only the present.

311. Terasetāni cittāni, jāyante kāmadhātuyaṃ etāni terasa cittāni kāmadhātuyaṃ jāyanti, rūpāvacare puññajāni cakkhusotaviññāṇasampaṭicchanāni, kiriyāmanodhātu cāti cattāri cittāni jāyanti. Arūpisu arūpabhūmīsu neva kiñcipi ekampi cittaṃ neva jāyati.

311. These thirteen types of consciousness arise in the sense-sphere. These thirteen consciousnesses arise in the sense-sphere. In the form-sphere, four consciousnesses arise: the wholesome-resultant eye-consciousness and ear-consciousness, the receiving consciousness, and the functional mind-element. In the formless realms, not even a single one of these consciousnesses arises at all.

312-3. Mahāpākānamaṭṭhannaṃ aṭṭhannaṃ mahāvipākānaṃ pavattiyaṃ chasu dvāresu tadārammaṇakiccānaṃ rūpādichaparittāni gocarā. Santīraṇattayassapi pavattiyaṃ pañcadvāre santīraṇattayakiccassa, chadvāresu tadālambaṇakiccassa ca rūpādichaparittāni gocarā. Rūpādayo parittā cha, hasituppādagocarā hasituppādassa rūpādayo cha parittā gocarā honti. Pañcadvāre paṭuppannā pañcasu dvāresu ye gocarā paccuppannā, manodvāre tikālikā ye gocarā tikālikā tīsu kālesu niyuttā.

312-3. For the eight great resultants, when they occur at the six doors with the function of registration, their objects are the six kinds of limited objects, i.e., forms, etc. For the triple investigating consciousness, when it occurs at the five doors with the function of investigation and at the six doors with the function of registration, its objects are the six kinds of limited objects, i.e., forms, etc. The six limited objects, forms, etc., are the objects of the smile-producing consciousness. The six limited objects, forms, etc., are the objects of the smile-producing consciousness. At the five doors, the objects are present; at the mind door, the objects are related to the three times.

314-5. Dutiyāruppacittañca, catutthāruppamānasaṃ kusalavipākakiriyāvasena chabbidhaṃ cittaṃ mahaggatagocaraṃ niyataṃ niyatārammaṇaṃ hoti, taṃ chabbidhaṃ cittaṃ mahaggatagocaraṃ pubbe attanā adhigataākāsānañcāyatanaākiñcaññāyatanakusalārammaṇaṃ, tesu dve dutiyacatutthāruppapākā “yassa yassa kusalajhānassa yaṃ yaṃ ārammaṇaṃ gahetvā brahmaloke paṭisandhi hotī”ti vacanato sakasakakusalassa ārammaṇaṃ eva tesaṃ vipākānaṃ ārammaṇaṃ hoti. Nibbānārammaṇattā hi, ekantena anaññato aṭṭhānāsavacittānaṃ appamāṇova nibbānaṃ eva gocaraṃ ārammaṇaṃ hoti[M 0.0062]. Hi kasmā kāraṇā? Nibbānārammaṇattā, na aññato ārammaṇato.

314-5. The second formless consciousness and the fourth formless consciousness—these six types of consciousness, being threefold each as wholesome, resultant, and functional—have a sublime and fixed object. These six types of consciousness have as their sublime object the wholesome consciousness of the base of infinite space and the base of nothingness, which were previously attained by oneself. Among them, for the two resultants of the second and fourth formless states, the object of those resultants is the very object of their respective wholesome consciousness, according to the saying: 'For whichever wholesome jhāna, having taken whichever object, rebirth occurs in a brahma world.' For the eight taintless consciousnesses, because Nibbāna is their object, the immeasurable Nibbāna alone is their object and support, exclusively and not otherwise. For what reason? Because their object is Nibbāna, not any other object.

316-320. Cattāro ñāṇahīnā ca, kāmāvacarapuññato kāmāvacarakusalavasena cattāro ñāṇahīnā ca kriyato kiriyavasena cattāro ñāṇahīnā ca dvādasākusalāni ca te parittārammaṇā ceva mahaggatagocarā ca, te na vattabbā ca honti. Kasmā? Paññattārammaṇattā[V 1.0054]. Cattāro ñāṇasaṃyuttā, puññato kusalavasena cattāro ñāṇasampayuttā, kriyato kiriyavasena cattāro ñāṇasampayuttā ca tathā abhiññādvayañca kiriyāvoṭṭhabbanampi ca ekādasannaṃ etesaṃ cittānaṃ gocaro parittamahaggataappamāṇavasena tividho hoti. Ime ekādasa na vattabbāpi honti. Kasmā? Paññattārammaṇattā. Yāni vuttāvasesāni vuttato cittato sesāni yāni cittāni, tāni na vattabbārammaṇānīti vibhāvinā viññeyyāni.

316-320. The four wholesome sense-sphere consciousnesses dissociated from knowledge, the four functional consciousnesses dissociated from knowledge, and the twelve unwholesome consciousnesses: these have limited and sublime objects, and they are also 'not to be specified.' Why? Because they can take a concept as object. The four wholesome consciousnesses associated with knowledge, the four functional consciousnesses associated with knowledge, the two direct knowledges, and the functional determining consciousness: for these eleven consciousnesses, the object is threefold as limited, sublime, and immeasurable. These eleven are also 'not to be specified.' Why? Because they can take a concept as object. The remaining consciousnesses that have been mentioned should be understood by the discerning one as having an object that is 'not to be specified'.

Parittārammaṇattikaṃ samattaṃ.

The Triad on Limited Objects is completed.

321.

321.

Dutiyāruppacittañca, catutthāruppamānasaṃ;

Chabbidhaṃ pana ekantaatītārammaṇaṃ siyā.

The second formless consciousness and the fourth formless consciousness; these six types, however, may have an exclusively past object.

322-6. Viññāṇānaṃ dvipañcannaṃ dvinnaṃ pañcaviññāṇānaṃ, manodhātuttayassa ca terasannaṃ cittānaṃ gocarā rūpādayo pañca dhammā paccuppannāva, aṭṭha kāmamahāvipākā tadārammaṇakiccavasena atītānāgatapaccuppannagocarā, cutikiccavasena atītārammaṇā, paṭisandhibhavaṅgakiccavasena paccuppannātītārammaṇā. Somanassasantīraṇaṃ santīraṇakiccavasena paccuppannārammaṇaṃ. Tadārammaṇakiccavasena paccuppannānāgatātītārammaṇaṃ. Sesasantīraṇadvayaṃ santīraṇakiccavasena paccuppannārammaṇaṃ[M 0.0063], tadārammaṇakiccavasena paccuppannānāgatātītārammaṇaṃ, cutikiccavasena atītārammaṇaṃ, paṭisandhibhavaṅgakiccavasena paccuppannātītārammaṇaṃ. Hasituppādacittaṃ javanakiccavasena paccuppannātītānāgatagocaraṃ. Iti ete dvādasa mānasā pana siyātītārammaṇā atītārammaṇā siyuṃ. Paccuppannānāgatagocarā paccuppannārammaṇā anāgatārammaṇā siyuṃ. Kāme vīsati kusalākusalā kriyato kiriyavasena kāme nava mānasā, voṭṭhabbaṃ voṭṭhabbanakiccavasena paccuppannārammaṇaṃ, āvajjanakiccavasena tikālārammaṇaṃ. Mahākiriyamānasā javanakiccavasena tikālārammaṇā, sante paññattikāle navattabbārammaṇā. Dve abhiññāmānasāpi abhiññākiccavasena atītādigocarā siyuṃ. Ime mānasā paññattikālepi sante navattabbā bhavanti. Rūpārūpabhavesu mayā vuttato sesāni sabbāni cittāni atītārammaṇādinā atītārammaṇādivasena paṇḍitena na vattabbāni na kathitabbāni honti eva, paññattārammaṇāni eva hontīti attho.

322-6. For the thirteen consciousnesses—the two sets of five consciousnesses and the triple mind-element—their objects, the five sense objects such as form, are strictly present. The eight great sense-sphere resultant consciousnesses have past, future, and present objects when functioning as registration; past objects when functioning as death; and present or past objects when functioning as rebirth-linking and life-continuum. The investigating consciousness accompanied by joy has a present object when functioning as investigation, and objects of the three times when functioning as registration. The remaining two investigating consciousnesses have a present object when functioning as investigation; objects of the three times when functioning as registration; a past object when functioning as death; and present or past objects when functioning as rebirth-linking and life-continuum. The smile-producing consciousness has an object of the three times when functioning as impulsion. Thus these twelve consciousnesses may have past objects, or they may have present or future objects. The twenty wholesome and unwholesome sense-sphere consciousnesses and the nine functional sense-sphere consciousnesses: when functioning as determining, their object is present; when functioning as adverting, their object is of the three times. The great functional consciousnesses have an object of the three times when functioning as impulsion; when their object is a concept, it is 'not to be specified' as to time. The two direct-knowledge consciousnesses may have objects of the past, etc., when functioning as direct knowledge. These consciousnesses too, when their object is a concept, are 'not to be specified.' In the fine-material and formless existences, all remaining consciousnesses apart from those I have mentioned should not be specified by the wise as having past objects, etc.; the meaning is that they have only concept-objects.

327. Kāmato [V 1.0055] ca kriyā pañca kāmāvacaravasena pañca kiriyā, rūpato rūpāvacaravasena pañcamī kriyā abhiññācittaṃ, etesaṃ channaṃ cittānaṃ natthi kiñci ekampi agocaraṃ anārammaṇaṃ, sabbārammaṇanti attho. “Pañcamī kriyā”ti vacanaṃ abhiññācittavasena vuttaṃ. Suddhajhānassa pañcamarūpakiriyassa paññattārammaṇaṃ evāti veditabbaṃ.

327. The five functional consciousnesses of the sense-sphere, and from the form-sphere the fifth functional consciousness, which is the direct-knowledge consciousness: for these six consciousnesses, there is not a single one that is objectless or without a range; the meaning is that they can take any object. The phrase 'the fifth functional' is stated with reference to the direct-knowledge consciousness. It should be understood that the fifth form-sphere functional consciousness, the pure jhāna, has only a concept as its object.

328. Nibbānañca catubbidhaṃ phalaṃ, maggaṃ rūpañca arūpaṃ cittacetasikasaṅkhātaṃ nāmañca gocaraṃ kātuṃ yāni cittāni sakkonti, tāni cittāni me vada, ācariya, tāni mayhaṃ kathehi.

328. Those consciousnesses that are able to take as their object Nibbāna, the fourfold fruit, the path, form, the formless, and name (designated as consciousness and mental factors)—tell me of those consciousnesses, teacher, explain them to me.

329-30. Cattāro ñāṇasaṃyuttā, puññato puññavasena cattāro ñāṇasampayuttā, kriyato tathā kiriyavasena [M 0.0064] cattāro ñāṇasampayuttā, dve abhiññāmānasā, kiriyāvoṭṭhabbanampi cāti ekādasa cittāni nibbānañca phalañca maggañca rūpañca arūpaṃ nāmañca gocaraṃ kātuṃ sakkonti.

329-30. The four wholesome consciousnesses associated with knowledge, the four functional consciousnesses likewise associated with knowledge, the two direct-knowledge consciousnesses, and the functional determining consciousness: these eleven consciousnesses are able to take as their object Nibbāna, fruition, path, form, the formless, and name.

331-4. Cittesu pana sabbesu yāni cittāni arahattaphalaṃ arahattamaggaṃ gocaraṃ kātuṃ sakkonti, tāni kati cittāni me vada tāni mayhaṃ tvaṃ kathehi. Sabbesu pana cittesu, cha ca cittāni me suṇa, bho bhaddamukha, tvaṃ mayhaṃ vacanaṃ suṇohi, sabbesu pana cittesu cha cittāni arahattaphalaṃ arahattamaggaṃ gocaraṃ kātuṃ sakkonti. Cattāro ñāṇasaṃyuttā, kiriyā ca voṭṭhabbanampi ca kiriyābhiññāmano cāti cha ca cittāni gocaraṃ kātuṃ sakkonti. Puññato puññavasena cattāro ñāṇasampayuttā, puññato puññavasena abhiññācittañca arahattaphalaṃ maggaṃ gocaraṃ kātuṃ na sakkonti.

331–334. Among all consciousnesses, tell me, how many consciousnesses can take the fruition of arahantship and the path of arahantship as their object? Explain them to me. Among all consciousnesses, listen to my words, good sir: six types of consciousness can take the fruition of arahantship and the path of arahantship as their object. The four functional consciousnesses associated with knowledge, the determining consciousness, and the functional direct-knowledge consciousness—these six types of consciousness can take them as their object. The four wholesome consciousnesses associated with knowledge by way of merit, and the direct-knowledge consciousness by way of merit, cannot take the fruition of arahantship and the path as their object.

335-8. Arahato khīṇāsavassa maggacittaṃ phalamānasaṃ vā puthujjanā vā sekkhā vā vijānituṃ na sakkonti. Kasmā kāraṇā? Puthujjano sotāpannassa mānasaṃ na jānāti, sotāpanno sakadāgāmissa mānasaṃ na jānāti, sakadāgāmī anāgāmissa mānasaṃ na jānāti, anāgāmī arahantassa mānasaṃ na jānāti. Heṭṭhimo heṭṭhimo puggalo uparūpari ṭhitassa puggalassa mānasaṃ neva jānāti, uparūpari ṭhito puggalopi heṭṭhimassa heṭṭhimassa puggalassa mānasaṃ jānāti.

335–338. The path-consciousness of an Arahant whose taints are destroyed, or their fruition-consciousness, cannot be known by ordinary persons or trainees. For what reason? An ordinary person does not know the mind of a stream-enterer, a stream-enterer does not know the mind of a once-returner, a once-returner does not know the mind of a non-returner, and a non-returner does not know the mind of an Arahant. A lower individual does not know the mind of a higher individual, but a higher individual does know the mind of a lower individual.

339-342. Yo [V 1.0056] dhammo yassa dhammassa ārammaṇaṃ hoti, taṃ ārammaṇaṃ ekaṃ ekaṃ uddharitvā ito paraṃ pavakkhāmi. Kusalārammaṇaṃ kāme kāme aṭṭhavidhaṃ kusalaṃ aṭṭhavidhassa kāmāvacarakusalassa ārammaṇaṃ hoti. Kathaṃ[M 0.0065]? Pubbeva kataṃ aṭṭhavidhaṃ mahākusalaṃ pacchā somanassasahagatañāṇasampayuttacittadvayena vā somanassasahagatañāṇavippayuttacittadvayena vā upekkhāsahagatañāṇasampayuttadvayena vā upekkhāsahagatañāṇavippayuttadvayena vā anussaraṇakaālādīsu tassa aṭṭhavidhassa kusalassa javanakiccavasena ārammaṇaṃ hoti, vippaṭisārakālādīsu dvādasavidhassa akusalassa ārammaṇaṃ hoti, kusalassa abhiññāmānasassa ca kiriyassa abhiññāmānasassa ca ārammaṇaṃ hoti, ekādasavidhassa kāmāvacaravipākassa tadārammaṇavasena ārammaṇaṃ hoti. Tathā kāmakriyassāti javanakiccavasena hasanassa āvajjanakiccavasena voṭṭhabbanassa javanakiccavasena mahākiriyassa ārammaṇaṃ hoti, etesaṃ channaṃ rāsīnaṃ ārammaṇaṃ siyā bhaveyya. Rūpāvacarapuññāni pañca tato charāsito kāmavipākaṃ vajjetvā pañcannaṃ rāsīnaṃ ārammaṇāni honti. Tadā lobhamūlamohamūlavasena attanā paṭiladdhajhānānaṃ anussaraṇakāle tassa dasavidhassa akusalassa ārammaṇaṃ hoti, tihetukapaṭisandhino sattassa jhānato parihīnassa jhānaṃ paccavekkhato jhānārammaṇaṃ domanassayuttaṃ hoti, tadā tassa paṭighadvayassa ārammaṇaṃ hoti. Kāmakriyassāti ekantaparittārammaṇāni kiriyāmanodhātuhasanāni vajjetvā āvajjanakiccavasena voṭṭhabbanassa, javanakiccavasena mahākiriyassa ca ārammaṇaṃ hoti.

339–342. Whatever phenomenon serves as the object for another phenomenon, I will now explain, taking up each of those objects one by one. As to wholesome objects: the eightfold sense-sphere wholesome consciousness can be an object for the eightfold sense-sphere wholesome consciousness. How? Previously performed eightfold great wholesome kamma becomes the object for the subsequent two types of consciousness associated with knowledge accompanied by joy, or the two types of consciousness dissociated from knowledge accompanied by joy, or the two types of consciousness associated with knowledge accompanied by equanimity, or the two types of consciousness dissociated from knowledge accompanied by equanimity, during recollection, etc., functioning as the impulsion of that eightfold wholesome consciousness. During regret, etc., it becomes the object of the twelve types of unwholesome consciousness. It serves as the object for the wholesome direct-knowledge consciousness and the functional direct-knowledge consciousness. It is the object for the eleven sense-sphere resultant consciousnesses by way of registration. Similarly, for the sense-sphere functional consciousness, it serves as the object for the smiling consciousness in its function as impulsion, for the determining consciousness in its function as adverting, and for the great functional consciousness in its function as impulsion. It may be an object for these six groups. The five form-sphere wholesome consciousnesses, excluding the sense-sphere resultant consciousnesses from those six groups, serve as objects for five groups. When one recollects the jhānas one has attained, this recollection, being rooted in greed or delusion, becomes the object for the ten types of unwholesome consciousness. For a being with a triple-rooted rebirth-linking consciousness who has fallen from jhāna, reviewing the jhāna becomes an object accompanied by grief—then it serves as the object for the two types of consciousness rooted in aversion. As for sense-sphere functional consciousness, excluding the functional mind-element and the smiling consciousness, which have exclusively limited objects, it serves as the object for the determining consciousness in its function as adverting and for the great functional consciousness in its function as impulsion.

343. Āruppakusalañcāpi, tebhūmakusalassa ca mahākusalassa ca abhiññākiccavasena pañcamarūpakusalassa ca dutiyacatutthaarūpakusalassa ca tebhūmakakriyassāpi voṭṭhabbanassa mahākiriyassa ca abhiññākiccavasena pañcamarūpakiriyassa ca dutiyacatutthāruppakiriyassa ca ārammaṇaṃ hoti, dutiyāruppakiriyassa ca paṭhamāruppakiriyāya ārammaṇena [M 0.0066] bhavitabbaṃ, catutthāruppakiriyassa ca tatiyāruppakiriyāya ārammaṇena bhavitabbaṃ, evañca sati kathaṃ paṭhamāruppakusalaṃ dutiyāruppakiriyassa ārammaṇaṃ hoti, tatiyāruppakusalañca catutthāruppakiriyassa ārammaṇaṃ hotīti ce vattabbaṃ, yadā puthujjanayogī vā sekkho vā yogī rūpasamāpattiṃ samāpajjitvā tato vuṭṭhahitvā ākāsānañcāyatanasaṅkhātaṃ paṭhamāruppasamāpattiṃ samāpajjitvā vītarāgo hutvā attanā adhigatā samāpattiyo gahetvā puthujjanasekkhakāle attanā anadhigataṃ dutiyaṃ arūpasamāpattiṃ samāpajji, tadā khīṇāsavakāle [V 1.0057] samāpajjitaṃ dutiyaṃ arūpakiriyaṃ paṭhamāruppakusalaṃ ārammaṇaṃ karoti, evaṃ paṭhamāruppakusalaṃ dutiyāruppakiriyassa ārammaṇaṃ hoti.

343. Also, the immaterial wholesome consciousness becomes an object for: the wholesome consciousness of the three planes; the great wholesome consciousness; the fifth form-sphere wholesome consciousness in its function of direct knowledge; the second and fourth immaterial wholesome consciousnesses; and also for the functional consciousness of the three planes—that is, for the determining consciousness, the great functional consciousness, the fifth form-sphere functional consciousness in its function of direct knowledge, and the second and fourth immaterial functional consciousnesses. The second immaterial functional consciousness must have the first immaterial functional consciousness as its object, and the fourth immaterial functional consciousness must have the third immaterial functional consciousness as its object. This being so, if it is asked: 'How does the first immaterial wholesome consciousness become an object for the second immaterial functional consciousness, and the third immaterial wholesome consciousness for the fourth immaterial functional consciousness?'—it should be explained as follows: When an ordinary yogi or a trainee yogi attains a form attainment, emerges from it, and then attains the first immaterial attainment known as the base of infinite space, having become free from passion, he takes up the attainments he has himself realized and attains the second immaterial attainment, which he had not realized himself during the time he was an ordinary person or a trainee. Then, at the time of being one whose taints are destroyed, the second immaterial functional consciousness that is attained makes the first immaterial wholesome consciousness its object. Thus, the first immaterial wholesome consciousness becomes an object for the second immaterial functional consciousness.

Yadā yogī rūpasamāpattiyo samāpajjitvā tato vuṭṭhahitvā paṭhamāruppakusalaṃ dutiyāruppakusalaṃ tatiyāruppakusalañca samāpajjitvā khīṇāsavo hutvā attanā adhigatā samāpattiyo gahetvā attanā anadhigataṃ catutthaṃ arūpasamāpattiṃ samāpajji, tadā catutthāruppakiriyā tatiyāruppakusalaṃ ārammaṇaṃ karoti, evaṃ catutthāruppakiriyassa tatiyāruppakusalaṃ ārammaṇaṃ hoti, pacchā khīṇāsavakāle samāpajjitā rūpārūpasamāpattiyo honti. Yathā hoti, tathā eva akusalassapi ārammaṇaṃ hoti.

When a yogi, having attained the form attainments and emerged from them, and having attained the first, second, and third immaterial wholesome attainments, becomes one whose taints are destroyed, he takes up the attainments he has himself realized and attains the fourth immaterial attainment, which he had not realized himself. Then the fourth immaterial functional consciousness makes the third immaterial wholesome consciousness its object. Thus, the third immaterial wholesome consciousness becomes an object for the fourth immaterial functional consciousness. Subsequently, at the time of being one whose taints are destroyed, the form and immaterial attainments are entered upon. Just as this is so, so too does it become an object for the unwholesome.

344-7. Arūpāvacarapākānanti jātiniddhāraṇaṃ, catutthadutiyānaṃ arūpapākānampi ārammaṇaṃ hoti, “catutthadutiyāna”nti vattabbe tiyānaṃ-saddassa lopaṃ katvā “catutthadū”ti vuttaṃ, tadā dvinnaṃ arūpapākānaṃ paṭhamāruppatatiyāruppajavanāni ārammaṇāni honti, “yassa kusalassa jhānassa yaṃ ārammaṇaṃ gahetvā brahmaloke paṭisandhi hotī”ti vacanato sakasakakusalānaṃ ārammaṇabhūtāni [M 0.0067] ākāsānañcāyatanaākiñcaññāyatanāni tesaṃ dutiyacatutthāruppapākānaṃ ārammaṇāni honti, evaṃ arūpakusalaṃ imesaṃ aṭṭharāsīnaṃ ārammaṇapaccayo hoti. Apariyāpannapuññampi catubbidhalokuttarakusalampi kāmāvacarato kāmāvacaravasena kusalassa ñāṇasampayuttamahākusalassa ca kriyassa voṭṭhabbanassa, ñāṇasampayuttato kiriyassa ca rūpato rūpāvacaravasena pañcamassa rūpakusalassa ca pañcamassa rūpakiriyassa cāti catunnaṃ rāsīnaṃ ārammaṇaṃ sadā hoti, ayamettha adhippāyo – sekkhānaṃ ñāṇasampayuttamahākusalassa, voṭṭhabbanassa, pañcamassa rūpakusalassa ca tividhaṃ lokuttarapuññaṃ ārammaṇaṃ hoti. Khīṇāsavassa voṭṭhabbanassa, ñāṇasampayuttamahākiriyassa, pañcamassa rūpakiriyassa ca arahattapuññaṃ ārammaṇaṃ hoti. Yathā tathā eva sabbaṃ akusalaṃ kāmāvacarato kāmāvacaravasena kusalassa mahākusalassa, kriyassa hasanavoṭṭhabbanamahākiriyassa ca rūpāvacarato pana rūpāvacaravasena pañcamassa rūpakusalassa, pañcamassa rūpakiriyassa ca ārammaṇaṃ hoti, yathā tathā eva sabbassa akusalassa ca kāmāvacaravipākānaṃ tadārammaṇakiccavasena ekādasannañcāti channaṃ rāsīnaṃ ārammaṇaṃ bhagavatā īritaṃ.

344–347. 'Of the immaterial-sphere resultants' is a specification of the class. It is also an object for the second and fourth immaterial resultant consciousnesses. When 'second and fourth' should be said, having elided the word for 'third', 'second and fourth' is stated. Thus, for the two immaterial resultant consciousnesses, the javanas of the first and third immaterial attainments become the objects. According to the statement, 'Rebirth occurs in a Brahma world by taking as object a certain wholesome jhāna,' the base of infinite space and the base of nothingness, which serve as the objects for their respective wholesome states, are the objects of the second and fourth immaterial resultant consciousnesses. In this way, the immaterial wholesome consciousness becomes the object-condition for these eight groups. The supramundane merit, that is, the fourfold supramundane wholesome consciousness, is always an object for four groups: the great wholesome consciousness associated with knowledge; the functional consciousness (namely, the determining consciousness and the great functional consciousness associated with knowledge); the fifth form-sphere wholesome consciousness; and the fifth form-sphere functional consciousness. Herein, this is the meaning: for trainees, the three kinds of supramundane merit are an object for the great wholesome consciousness associated with knowledge, the determining consciousness, and the fifth form-sphere wholesome consciousness. For one whose taints are destroyed, the merit of arahantship is an object for the determining consciousness, the great functional consciousness associated with knowledge, and the fifth form-sphere functional consciousness. Similarly, all unwholesome consciousness is an object for: the great wholesome consciousness; the functional, namely smiling, determining, and great functional consciousnesses; and the fifth form-sphere wholesome and fifth form-sphere functional consciousnesses. Likewise, it has been declared by the Blessed One that for six groups, the object is all unwholesome consciousness and the eleven sense-sphere resultants in their function of registration.

348-352. Vipākārammaṇaṃ [V 1.0058] kāme sabbaṃ vipākārammaṇaṃ kāmāvacaratopi kāmāvacaravasenapi kusalassa mahākusalassa, kriyassa hasanavoṭṭhabbanamahākiriyassa ca rūpāvacarato ceva rūpāvacaravasena ca eva pañcamassa rūpakusalassa, pañcamassa rūpakiriyassa ca kāmāvacarapākānaṃ kāmāvacaravipākānaṃ ekādasannañca tatheva akusalassa ca channaṃ rāsīnaṃ ārammaṇaṃ hoti. Rūpe vipākārammaṇaṃ kāmāvacaratopi ca kāmāvacaravasenapi ca kusalassa mahākusalassa[M 0.0068], kriyassa ca voṭṭhabbanamahākiriyassa ca rūpāvacarato ceva rūpāvacaravasena ca eva kusalassa ca apuññassa cāti pañcannaṃ rāsīnaṃ gocaro hoti, arūpāvacarapākesu ayaṃ nayo bhagavatā mato. Vaṭṭe na pariyāpannā nappaviṭṭhāti apariyāpannā, tesaṃ puggalānaṃ pākāpi kāmato kāmāvacaravasena kusalassa ñāṇasampayuttamahākusalassa, kriyassa ca voṭṭhabbanañāṇasampayuttamahākiriyassa ca rūpatopi rūpāvacaravasenapi kusalassa pañcamassa rūpakusalassa, kriyassa ca pañcamassa rūpakiriyassa ca evaṃ ārammaṇaṃ hotīti. Etthāyamadhippāyo apariyāpannapuññe vuttanayeneva veditabbo.

348–352. Resultant consciousness as object in the sense-sphere: All sense-sphere resultant consciousness is an object for six groups: from the sense-sphere, for the wholesome, that is, the great wholesome consciousness, and for the functional, that is, the smile-producing, determining, and great functional consciousness; and from the form-sphere, for the fifth form-sphere wholesome consciousness and the fifth form-sphere functional consciousness; and also for the eleven sense-sphere resultants and likewise for the unwholesome. Resultant consciousness in the form-sphere is an object for five groups: from the sense-sphere, for the wholesome, that is, the great wholesome consciousness, and for the functional, that is, the determining and great functional consciousness; and from the form-sphere, for the wholesome and the unwholesome. This method is considered by the Blessed One for the immaterial-sphere resultants. 'Not included' means not included in the round, not entered into it. For those individuals, their resultants, too, are an object: from the sense-sphere, for the wholesome, that is, the great wholesome consciousness associated with knowledge, and for the functional, that is, the determining and the great functional consciousness associated with knowledge; and from the form-sphere, for the fifth form-sphere wholesome consciousness and the fifth form-sphere functional consciousness. Here, this meaning should be understood in the same way as explained for the supramundane merit.

353-6. Kāme idaṃ sabbakiriyacittaṃ kāmāvacaratopi ca kāmāvacaravasenapi ca kusalassa mahākusalassa, kriyassa ca hasanavoṭṭhabbanamahākiriyassa ca rūpāvacarato ceva rūpāvacaravasena ca eva kusalassa pañcamassa rūpakusalassa, kriyassa ca pañcamassa rūpakiriyassa ca ekādasakāmāvacarapākassa ca tatheva akusalassa ca etesaṃ channaṃ rāsīnaṃ ārammaṇaṃ hoti. Yaṃ kriyāmānasaṃ rūpe rūpāvacare yaṃ kiriyāmānasaṃ, kāmapākaṃ tato vinā tato rāsito kāmapākaṃ vinā vajjetvā pañcannaṃ pana rāsīnaṃ ārammaṇaṃ hoti. Kāmāvacarato kāmāvacaravasena kiriyassa voṭṭhabbanamahākiriyassa ārammaṇaṃ hoti, hasanaṃ ekantaparittārammaṇattā rūpakiriyaṃ ārammaṇaṃ na karoti. Kriyācittaṃ panāruppe arūpakiriyācittaṃ pana tesaṃ pañcannaṃ eva ca rāsīnaṃ āruppakriyassāpi paṭhamāruppakiriyaṃ dutiyāruppakiriyassa ārammaṇaṃ hoti, tatiyāruppakiriyaṃ catutthāruppakiriyassa ārammaṇaṃ hoti. Iti channaṃ rāsīnaṃ gocaro hotiyeva.

353–356. In the sense-sphere, all this functional consciousness is an object for these six groups: from the sense-sphere, for the wholesome, that is, the great wholesome consciousness, and for the functional, that is, the smile-producing, determining, and great functional consciousness; and from the form-sphere, for the fifth form-sphere wholesome consciousness and the fifth form-sphere functional consciousness; and for the eleven sense-sphere resultants and likewise for the unwholesome. Whatever functional mind is in the form-sphere, excluding the sense-sphere resultants from that group, it is an object for five groups. From the sense-sphere and by way of the sense-sphere, it is an object for the functional, that is, the determining and great functional consciousness. Smile-producing consciousness, because its object is exclusively limited, does not make the form-sphere functional consciousness its object. Functional consciousness, however, in the immaterial realm—the immaterial functional consciousness—is an object for those same five groups. Moreover, of the immaterial functional consciousness, the first is an object for the second, and the third is an object for the fourth. Thus, it is indeed the range of six groups.

357-8.

357-8.

Rūpaṃ [M 0.0069] catusamuṭṭhānaṃ, rūpārammaṇasaññitaṃ;

Kāmāvacarapuññassa, tatheva kusalassa ca;

Abhiññādvayacittassa, kāmapākakriyassa ca.

Form, arising from four sources and designated as the form-object, is for the sense-sphere meritorious consciousness, and likewise for the wholesome consciousness; for the consciousness of the two direct-knowledges, and for the sense-sphere resultant and functional consciousness.

Dvicakkhuviññāṇamanodhātudvayasantīraṇattayamahāpākassa [V 1.0059] ca kāmakiriyassa cāti ekādasavidhassa kāmakiriyassa ca channaṃ etesaṃ rāsīnaṃ ārammaṇapaccayo hoti.

For the two eye-consciousnesses, the two mind-elements, the three investigating consciousnesses, the great resultant consciousness, and the sense-sphere functional consciousness—that is, the eleven kinds of sense-sphere functional consciousness—for these six classes, the object condition obtains.

359-360. Nibbānārammaṇaṃ kāmarūpāvacarato kāmarūpāvacaravasena sekkhānaṃ ñāṇasampayuttamahākusalassa, rūpāvacaravasena pañcamassa rūpakusalassa ca kāmarūpakiriyassa ca khīṇāsavānaṃ voṭṭhabbanañāṇasampayuttamahākiriyassa ca pañcamarūpakiriyassa ca ubhayassāpi cittassa ārammaṇaṃ hoti. Apariyāpannato ceva lokuttaravasena ca eva phalassa, kusalassa ca etesaṃ channaṃ rāsīnaṃ ārammaṇapaccayo hoti.

Nibbāna as an object, in the context of the sense- and form-spheres, is an object for the knowledge-associated great wholesome consciousness of trainees, and for the fifth form-sphere wholesome consciousness. It is also an object for the functional consciousness of those whose taints are destroyed, including the determining, knowledge-associated great functional consciousness, and the fifth form-sphere functional consciousness; it is an object for both these types of consciousness. As unincluded and by way of the supramundane, it is an object for the fruition consciousness and the wholesome path consciousness. Thus, for these six classes, the object condition obtains.

361-2. Nānappakārakaṃ sabbaṃ, paññattārammaṇaṃ pana tebhūmakassa puññassa mahākusalassa, suddhajhānassa pañcavidhassa rūpakusalassa, paṭhamāruppatatiyāruppakusalassa ca tatheva akusalassa ca rūpārūpavipākassa sabbassa rūpavipākassa, paṭhamāruppatatiyāruppavipākassa ca tebhūmakakriyassa ca hasanavoṭṭhabbanamahākiriyassa sabbassa rūpakiriyassa, paṭhamāruppatatiyāruppakiriyassa cāti navannaṃ pana rāsīnaṃ ārammaṇapaccayo hoti.

However, any diverse conceptual object is an object for: the great wholesome consciousness, being merit of the three planes; the fivefold form-sphere wholesome consciousness of pure jhāna; the first and third formless-sphere wholesome consciousnesses, and similarly for the unwholesome consciousness; for all form-sphere resultant consciousness, and for the first and third formless-sphere resultant consciousnesses; and for the functional consciousness of the three planes—namely, the smile-producing, determining, and great functional consciousnesses; all form-sphere functional consciousness; and the first and third formless-sphere functional consciousnesses. Thus, for these nine classes, the object condition obtains.

363-4. Rūpārammaṇikā dve tu dve cittuppādā rūpārammaṇikā, dve dve saddādigocarā dve dve cittuppādā saddārammaṇādigocarā, tayo manodhātusaṅkhātā cittuppādā pañcārammaṇikā nāma matā bhagavatā. Idha imasmiṃ kāmāvacarādhikāre [M 0.0070] ekacattālīseva cittuppādā chaḷārammaṇikā matā. Ayaṃ kāmāvacaracittānaṃ ārammaṇakkamo.

Two consciousnesses have form as object; two each have sound and so on as objects; and three consciousnesses, designated as mind-element, are considered by the Blessed One to have five objects. Here, in this sense-sphere section, forty-one consciousnesses are considered to have six objects. This is the order of objects for sense-sphere consciousnesses.

365-9. Pañcābhiññā vivajjetvā, rūpārūpā anāsavā ime sabbe cittuppādā dhammārammaṇagocarā honti. Paṭhamāruppakusalaṃ dutiyāruppacetaso kusalassa ārammaṇaṃ hoti, dutiyāruppacetaso vipākassa ca ārammaṇaṃ hoti, dutiyāruppacetaso kiriyassa ca ārammaṇaṃ hoti. Dutiyāruppacetaso kiriyassa paṭhamāruppakusalārammaṇabhāve kāraṇaṃ heṭṭhā vuttameva. Paṭhamāruppapākoyaṃ, dutiyāruppacetaso kusalassa ca dutiyāruppacetaso vipākassa ca dutiyāruppacetaso kiriyassa ca ārammaṇaṃ na hoti. Hi kasmā? Tesaṃ dutiyāruppakusalavipākakiriyānaṃ paṭhamāruppakusalārammaṇattā. Paṭhamaṃ tu kriyācittaṃ paṭhamaṃ kiriyācittaṃ pana dutiyāruppacetaso puññassa ārammaṇaṃ na hoti. Dutiyāruppacetaso vipākassa ārammaṇaṃ na [V 1.0060] hoti. Rūpārūpabhavesu hi khīṇāsavā vipākacittāni cutivasena sakasakakusalānaṃ ārammaṇaṃ karonti. Paṭhamaṃ tu kriyācittaṃ pana dutiyāruppacetaso kiriyassa ārammaṇaṃ hoti. Iti evaṃ iminā mayā vuttappakārena cittānaṃ ārammaṇuppatti vibhāvinā dhīrena ñeyyā.

Except for the five higher knowledges, all these form-sphere, formless-sphere, and taintless consciousnesses have dhamma as their object-range. The first formless-sphere wholesome consciousness is an object for the second formless-sphere wholesome mind, for the resultant of the second formless-sphere mind, and for the functional of the second formless-sphere mind. Regarding the second formless-sphere functional mind having the first formless-sphere wholesome consciousness as its object, the reason is as stated below. This first formless-sphere resultant consciousness, however, is not an object for the wholesome, resultant, or functional of the second formless-sphere mind. Why? Because those—the wholesome, resultant, and functional of the second formless-sphere—have the first formless-sphere wholesome consciousness as their object. The first formless-sphere functional consciousness, however, is not an object for the meritorious consciousness of the second formless-sphere mind, nor is it an object for the resultant of the second formless-sphere mind. Indeed, in form-sphere and formless-sphere existences, the resultant consciousnesses of those whose taints are destroyed make their respective wholesome consciousnesses their object at the moment of death. The first formless-sphere functional consciousness, however, is an object for the functional of the second formless-sphere mind. Thus, in this manner, the arising of objects for the consciousnesses has been clearly explained by me, to be understood by the wise.

370-3. Puthujjanassa sekkhassa, arūpārammaṇaṃ dvidhā dvippakāraṃ kusalaṃ kusalassa dutiyāruppakusalassa ārammaṇaṃ hoti, taṃ paṭhamāruppakusalaṃ dutiyāruppavipākassa ārammaṇaṃ siyā bhaveyya. Khīṇāsavassa bhikkhussa, paṭhamāruppamānasaṃ ārammaṇaṃ tidhā tippakāraṃ hoti. Iti vacanaṃ mahesinā vuttaṃ. Kriyassāpi dutiyāruppakiriyassāpi paṭhamāruppakiriyā ārammaṇaṃ hoti. Kusalampi paṭhamāruppakusalampi dutiyāruppakiriyassa ca ārammaṇaṃ hoti. Kusalaṃ [M 0.0071] paṭhamāruppakusalaṃ dutiyāruppavipākassa ārammaṇaṃ hoti. Evaṃ iminā mayā vuttappakārena paṭhamāruppamānasaṃ ārammaṇaṃ tidhā hoti. Tatiyāruppacittampi catutthāruppacetaso kusalassa ārammaṇaṃ hoti, catutthāruppacetaso vipākassa ca taṃ ārammaṇaṃ hoti. Evameva yathā paṭhamāruppamānasaṃ ārammaṇaṃ dvidhā hoti, evameva tathā tatiyāruppacittaṃ ārammaṇaṃ dvidhā hoti. Yathā paṭhamāruppamānasaṃ ārammaṇaṃ tidhā hoti, evameva tathā tatiyāruppacittaṃ ārammaṇaṃ tidhā siyā.

For an ordinary person and a trainee, the first formless consciousness as an object is twofold: the wholesome consciousness is an object for the second formless-sphere wholesome consciousness, and that first formless-sphere wholesome consciousness may be an object for the second formless-sphere resultant consciousness. For a monk whose taints are destroyed, the first formless-sphere mind is an object in three ways. Thus, the great sage has spoken. For the functional consciousness of the second formless-sphere, the first formless-sphere functional consciousness is also an object. The first formless-sphere wholesome consciousness is also an object for the second formless-sphere functional consciousness. The first formless-sphere wholesome consciousness is an object for the second formless-sphere resultant consciousness. Thus, in the way I have described, the first formless-sphere mind is an object in three ways. The third formless-sphere consciousness is also an object for the wholesome consciousness of the fourth formless-sphere mind, and it is an object for the resultant consciousness of the fourth formless-sphere mind. Just as the first formless-sphere mind is an object in two ways, so too is the third formless-sphere consciousness an object in two ways. Just as the first formless-sphere mind is an object in three ways, so too may the third formless-sphere consciousness be an object in three ways.

374. Yaṃ yaṃ pana idhārabbha idha imasmiṃ adhikāre yaṃ yaṃ gocaraṃ ārabbha paṭicca ye ye cittuppādā jāyanti, so so gocaro tesañca tesañca cittuppādānaṃ ārammaṇapaccayo hoti.

374. Whatever object is taken up here in this section, dependent on whatever range is taken up, whatever consciousnesses arise, that very range serves as the object condition for those various consciousnesses.

375. Yo pana naro imassa abhidhammāvatārassa kira pāraṃ duttaraṃ idha imasmiṃ loke uttarati, so naro abhidhammamahaṇṇave pāraṃ duttaraṃ uttaraṃ uttarati eva.

375. The person who here in this world crosses the difficult-to-cross shore of this Abhidhammāvatāra, that person indeed crosses the further, difficult-to-cross shore of the great ocean of the Abhidhamma.

Iti abhidhammāvatāraṭīkāya

Thus, from the Abhidhammāvatāra Commentary.

Ārammaṇavibhāgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Division of Objects is concluded.

Chaṭṭho paricchedo.

The Sixth Chapter.

7. Sattamo paricchedo

7. The Seventh Chapter.

Vipākacittappavattiniddesavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Exposition on the Process of Resultant Consciousness.

376.

376.

Anantañāṇena [V 1.0061] niraṅgaṇena,

Guṇesinā kāruṇikena tena;

Vutte vipāke matipāṭavatthaṃ,

Vipākacittappabhavaṃ suṇātha.

By the Stainless One of infinite knowledge, by that virtuous and compassionate one; regarding the result he spoke, for the sake of keenness of intellect, listen to the arising of resultant consciousness.

Yena [M 0.0072] jinena anantañāṇena nikkilesena guṇesinā kāruṇikena tena jinena vutte vipākasmiṃ matipāṭavatthaṃ matichekabhāvatthāya vipākacittappabhavaṃ mayā bhaṇamānaṃ vipākacittappavattiṃ tumhe suṇātha.

By that Victor, possessed of infinite knowledge, free from defilements, virtuous, and compassionate—for the sake of keenness of intellect and intellectual skillfulness regarding the result spoken by him—listen to the process of resultant consciousness, its arising, as I speak it.

377. Ekūnatiṃsa kammāni, pākā dvattiṃsa bhagavatā dassitā, kammāni tīsu dvāresu dissare, vipākā chasu dvāresu dissanti.

377. Twenty-nine kammas were shown by the Blessed One, with thirty-two results. The kammas are seen in three doors, and the results are seen in six doors.

378-9. Kusalaṃ kāmalokasmiṃ kāmalokamhi kusalaṃ pavatte, paṭisandhiyañca taṃtaṃpaccayamāgamma taṃtaṃpaccayaṃ paṭicca. So so paccayo taṃtaṃpaccayo, “tatapaccayo”ti vattabbe niggahītāgamavasena “taṃtaṃpaccayo”ti vuttaṃ. Vicchākammadhārayasamāsoyaṃ. Vividhaṃ phalaṃ dadāti. Ekāya cetanāya ekā paṭisandhi bhagavatā pakāsitā. Nānākammehi nānā paṭisandhiyo ca bhavanti.

Wholesome kamma in the sense-sphere gives its results during the course of life and at rebirth-linking, depending on and conditioned by each particular condition. The term 'taṃtaṃpaccayo' (each particular condition) is used instead of the expected 'tatapaccayo' due to the insertion of a niggahita. This is a distributive karmadhāraya compound. It yields various fruits. The Blessed One has declared one rebirth-linking from one volition. And from diverse kammas, diverse rebirth-linkings come to be.

380-1. Tihetukaṃ tu yaṃ kammaṃ tihetukaṃ yaṃ kammaṃ pana kāmāvacarasaññitaṃ tihetukaṃ vipākaṃ duhetuñca vipākaṃ ahetuñca vipākaṃ deti. Duhetukaṃ tu yaṃ kammaṃ duhetukaṃ yaṃ kammaṃ pana, taṃ kammaṃ tihetukaṃ vipākaṃ na deti, attano vipākaṃ duhetuñca ahetuñca deti.

As for a three-rooted kamma pertaining to the sense-sphere, it yields three-rooted, two-rooted, and rootless results. As for a two-rooted kamma, however, it does not yield three-rooted results; it yields two-rooted and rootless results.

382-3. Tihetukena [V 1.0062] kammena, paṭisandhi tihetukā hoti, duhetukāpi paṭisandhi hoteva, ahetukā paṭisandhi neva hoti, ukkaṭṭhatihetukakammena tihetukā paṭisandhi, omakatihetukakammena duhetukā paṭisandhi hotīti adhippāyo. Duhetukena kammena duhetukā paṭisandhi, ahetukāpi paṭisandhi hoteva, tihetukā paṭisandhi neva hoti. Ukkaṭṭhaduhetukakammena duhetukā paṭisandhi, omakaduhetukakammena ahetukā paṭisandhi hotīti adhippāyo.

By three-rooted kamma, rebirth-linking is three-rooted; two-rooted rebirth-linking also occurs, but rootless rebirth-linking never occurs. By superior three-rooted kamma, rebirth-linking is three-rooted; by inferior three-rooted kamma, rebirth-linking is two-rooted—this is the meaning. By two-rooted kamma, rebirth-linking is two-rooted; rootless rebirth-linking also occurs, but three-rooted rebirth-linking never occurs. By superior two-rooted kamma, rebirth-linking is two-rooted; by inferior two-rooted kamma, rebirth-linking is rootless—this is the meaning.

384. Asaṅkhārakammaṃ [M 0.0073] asaṅkhāravipākaṃ deti, sasaṅkhāravipākampi deti, sasaṅkhārakammaṃ sasaṅkhāraphalaṃ, tathā asaṅkhāraphalaṃ deti.

384. Unprompted kamma yields unprompted results, and it can also yield prompted results. Prompted kamma yields prompted results, and likewise, it can yield unprompted results.

385. Ekāya cetanāyettha ettha etāsu cetanāsu ekāya kusalāya cetanāya soḷasavidhā vipākacittāni bhavanti. Iti vacanaṃ jino pakāsaye.

385. With a single volition, here, among these volitions, through one wholesome volition, sixteen types of resultant consciousness arise. Thus, the Conqueror declared.

386-92. Vedanāparivattanaṃ ārammaṇena hoteva, tadārammaṇacittampi javanena niyāmitaṃ, somanassayutte kusale javane javite tadārammaṇampi somanassayuttameva hotīti attho. Upekkhāyuttakusalepi eseva nayo. Kāmāvacaracittena kusalenādinā paṭhamena kusalena tulyena vipākacittena. Tatiyāvisesanaṃ. Yena sattena gahitā paṭisandhi ce yadi, iṭṭhe balavārammaṇe manāpe atimahantārammaṇe tassa sattassa cakkhussa cakkhupasādassa āpāthaṃ pākaṭabhāvaṃ āgate sati manodhātuyā tāya bhavaṅgasmiṃ āvaṭṭite bhavaṅgasote chindite sati cakkhuviññāṇakādīsu vīthicittesu jātesu paṭhamaṃ kusalaṃ kāmamānasaṃ javanaṃ hutvā jāyate. Sattakkhattuvārāni javitvāna paṭhame mahākusale gate tadeva taṃ eva iṭṭhaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā teneva paṭhamamahākusalena sadisaṃ tadārammaṇavipākacittaṃ. Sandhiyā tulyato paṭisandhiyā tulyabhāvena mūlabhavaṅganti mūlabhavaṅgaṃ nāma bhagavatā pavuccate. Tañca tadārammaṇacittaṃ santīraṇaṃ somanassayuttaṃ santīraṇaṃ dassanaṃ sampaṭicchanaṃ ettha etasmiṃ vīthicitte gaṇanūpagacittāni gaṇanaṃ upagatāni cittāni cattāri eva bhavanti.

386-92. The change of feeling certainly occurs based on the object, and that registering consciousness is also determined by the impulsion.
