When a wholesome impulsion associated with joy has occurred, the registering consciousness is also associated with joy—this is the meaning. The same principle applies to wholesome consciousness associated with equanimity. The resultant consciousness is similar to the first wholesome sense-sphere consciousness, and so on. This is the third distinction: For whichever being rebirth-linking is grasped, if a desirable, strong, pleasing, extremely great object comes into the range of that being’s eye sensitivity, then when the mind-element has turned towards the life-continuum, and the life-continuum stream has been interrupted, among the process-consciousnesses beginning with eye-consciousness that have arisen, the first wholesome sense-sphere impulsion arises. After that first great wholesome impulsion has impulsed seven times and passed, taking that same desirable object, the registering resultant consciousness similar to that first great wholesome impulsion arises. Due to similarity with the rebirth-linking, it is called 'root life-continuum' by the Blessed One. And that registering consciousness is investigating, the investigating being associated with joy, seeing, receiving—here, in this process of consciousness, the consciousnesses that enter into the calculation are only four.

393-4. Yadā hi dutiyaṃ cittaṃ, kusalaṃ javanaṃ yadā yasmiṃ kāle tasseva somanassatihetuno puggalassa dutiyaṃ [M 0.0074] kusalaṃ cittaṃ javanaṃ hoti, tadā tasmiṃ kāle tena javanena tulyavipākaṃ tadārammaṇaṃ. Tassa sandhiyā asamānattā tassa tadārammaṇacittassa sandhiyā asamānattā [V 1.0063] dve nāmāni assa vipākacittassa anena vipākacittena labbhare labbhanti, “āgantukabhavaṅga”nti nāmaṃ “tadārammaṇaka”nti ca nāmaṃ iti dve nāmāni labbhanti.

393-94. When, for a person whose cause is joy, a second wholesome consciousness arises as the impulsion, then at that time, the registering consciousness, with a result similar to that impulsion, arises. Due to dissimilarity in connection with the linking consciousness, two names can be obtained for this resultant consciousness: "adventitious life-continuum" and "registering consciousness"—thus, two names are obtained.

395-6. Yadā tasseva puggalassa tatiyaṃ puññaṃ javanaṃ hoti, tadā tena javanena sadisaṃ tatiyaṃ pākaṃ tadārammaṇikaṃ siyā. Idaṃ vipākacittaṃ āgantukabhavaṅganti āgantubhavaṅgaṃ nāma bhagavatā vuccate, purimāni ca pañca vipākacittāni iminā pana tatiyavipākena pana saddhiṃ cha cittāni honti.

395-6. When the third wholesome impulsion occurs for that same individual, then a third resultant, similar to that impulsion, may be a registration of that object. This resultant consciousness is called "adventitious life-continuum" by the Blessed One. And the previous five resultant consciousnesses, together with this third resultant, become six consciousnesses.

397-8. Yadā catutthaṃ kusalaṃ javanaṃ hoti, tadā tena javanena tulyaṃ catutthavipākaṃ tadārammaṇabhāvaṃ vaje gaccheyya. Catutthavipākaṃ āgantukabhavaṅgaṃ tadārammaṇanāmakaṃ hoti, purimāni cha pākāni iminā saha catutthapākena satta cittāni honti.

397-8. When the fourth wholesome impulsion occurs, then, by that impulsion, the fourth resultant, similar to that impulsion, may function as tadārammaṇa. The fourth resultant is called adventitious life-continuum tadārammaṇa. The previous six resultants, together with this fourth resultant, become seven consciousnesses.

399-403. Yadā yasmiṃ kāle tasmiṃ cakkhudvāre iṭṭhamajjhattārammaṇaṃ pana tathā āpāthaṃ āgacchati ca, tadā vuttanayena āvajjanadassanasampaṭicchanacittesu jātesu idha imasmiṃ majjhattārammaṇe ārammaṇavasena vedanā parivattati, tasmā upekkhāsahagataṃ santīraṇaṃ mano hoti. Upekkhāsahagatesu eva catūsupi javanesu javitesu tehi javanehi tulyāni cattāri vipākacittāni jāyare. Accantaṃ ekantena vedanāya upekkhāvedanāya purimehi somanassasahagatehi cittehi asamānattā cattāri cittāni nāmato piṭṭhibhavaṅgāni nāma honti, piṭṭhibhavaṅgāni somanassavipākānaṃ pacchābhāge bhavaṅgānīti attho. Imāni [M 0.0075] upekkhāsahagatāni pañca vipākāni purimehi sattahi vipākehi saddhiṃ dvādasa vipākāni bhavanti. Iti vacanaṃ dhīro viniddise.

399-403. When, at any time, a neutral object, neither desirable nor undesirable, similarly comes to the range of the eye-door, then, as described previously, after the adverting, seeing, and receiving consciousnesses have arisen, here in this neutral object, the feeling changes in accordance with the object. Therefore, the investigating mind is accompanied by equanimity. When four impulsions accompanied by equanimity have impulsed, four resultant consciousnesses similar to those impulsions arise. Because these four consciousnesses are entirely and absolutely dissimilar in feeling (being equanimous feeling) from the previous joy-accompanied consciousnesses, they are called "posterior life-continuum" by name—meaning they are life-continuum in the phase after the joy-accompanied resultants. These five equanimous resultants, together with the previous seven resultants, make twelve resultants. Thus, the wise should understand.

404-6. Yathā cakkhudvāre dvādasa vipākāni honti, tathā evaṃ sotādīsu dvāresupi dvādasa pākāni honti. Iti vacanaṃ dhīro niddise, ime mayā vuttā vipākā samasaṭṭhi bhavanti. Evaṃ iminā mayā vuttappakārena ekāya cetanāya kamme āyūhite pavattite samasaṭṭhi vipākāni uppajjanti, imasmiṃ vacane saṃsayo natthi. Gahitāggahaṇenettha ettha etesu vipākesu gahitānaṃ vipākānaṃ aggahaṇena cakkhudvāre dvādasa pākā, sotaviññāṇakādīni cattāri cāti soḷasa pākāni honti.

404-6. Just as there are twelve resultants in the eye-door, so too there are twelve resultants in the ear-door and other doors. Thus the wise should understand this saying: "These resultants that I have spoken of are sixty-six in total." Thus, in this manner explained by me, sixty-six resultants arise from a single volition when kamma is accumulated and performed. There is no doubt in this statement. Here, by the principle of inclusion and exclusion, sixteen resultant consciousnesses are counted: twelve at the eye-door, and the four beginning with ear-consciousness.

407-11. Ekena [V 1.0064] tihetukakusalena asaṅkhārikena kammena āyūhite yathā, evameva sasaṅkhāratihetukakusalenāpi asaṅkhārasasaṅkhāraupekkhāsahagatehipi kusalehi kamme āyūhite pavattite tesaṃ tiṇṇaṃ kusalānaṃ vipākehi tīhipi dinnāya paṭisandhiyā eseva nayo paṇḍitena jānitabbo. Idha imasmiṃ upekkhāsahagatadvaye iṭṭhamajjhattagocarassa vasena vipākacittappavattiṃ paṭhamaṃ dassetvā dassetabbātha pacchā tu, iṭṭhasmiṃ gocare idha atha pacchā mayā vuttacittappavattito pacchākāle pana idha imasmiṃ iṭṭhagocare ekekasmiṃ pana dvādasa dvādasa pākā paṇḍitena dassetabbā. Gahitāggahaṇenettha ettha etesu vipākesu gahitānaṃ vipākānaṃ aggahaṇena soḷasa pākacittāni honti. Pubbe kāle mayā vuttanayeneva sabbaṃ vacanaṃ asesato asesabhāvena paṇḍitena ñeyyaṃ.

407-11. Just as kamma is accumulated and set in motion by a single unprompted three-rooted wholesome kamma, so too is it when kamma is accumulated and set in motion by prompted three-rooted wholesome kamma, and by wholesome kamma accompanied by equanimity, whether unprompted or prompted. For these three wholesome kammas, regarding the rebirth-linking given by their three results, this same method should be understood by the wise. Here, in these two types of equanimity, after first showing the arising of resultant consciousness based on the object being desirable or neutral, then, later, in the case of a desirable object, after the consciousness process previously stated by me, in the subsequent phase, for each door, twelve resultant consciousnesses should be shown by the wise. Here, by the principle of inclusion and exclusion, sixteen resultant consciousnesses are counted. All this statement should be fully understood by the wise, without omission, just as explained by me previously.

412-4. Tihetukena kammena, paṭisandhi tihetukā bhavati, iti ayaṃ vāro ettāvatā ettakena vacanena mayā [M 0.0076] vutto. Ekaṃ kammaṃ ekasmiṃ bhave ekaṃ paṭisandhiṃ janeti, tato paṭisandhito aparaṃ aññaṃ dutiyaṃ paṭisandhiṃ na janeti, pavattiyaṃ anekāni vipākāni sañjaneti. Hi saccaṃ “ekaṃ kamma”ntiādikaṃ vacanaṃ. Ekasmā bījā ekato bījato ekaṃ aṅkuraṃ jāyati, assa bījassa bahūni phalāni hetuppavattito salilādihetuppattiyā honti.

412-4. By a three-rooted kamma, rebirth-linking is three-rooted. Thus far, this section has been stated by me with these words. One kamma produces one rebirth-linking in one becoming; after that rebirth-linking, it does not produce another, a second rebirth-linking, but in the course of existence, it produces many results. Indeed, the statement 'one kamma' and so forth is true. From one seed, one sprout arises from that single seed. But from that seed, many fruits come into being due to the arising of causes, such as water and other conditions.

415-21. Duhetukena kammena, paṭisandhi duhetukā hoti, iti vacanaṃ ayaṃ vāro anupubbena anupaṭipāṭiyā āgato. Idha imasmiṃ adhikāre duhetukena puññena somanassayuttena asaṅkhārikena cittena kamme āyūhite pana duhetukena somanassayuttakusalena tulyena pākena yena sattena gahitā paṭisandhi ce, iṭṭhe ārammaṇe tassa sattassa cakkhudvāre āpāthaṃ āgate somanassayutte ñāṇahīne kusalamānase tasmiṃ duhetuke sattakkhattuṃ javitvāna gate taṃ eva ārammaṇaṃ katvā tadanantaraṃ tassa javanassa anantaraṃ taṃsarikkhakaṃ tena javanena sadisaṃ ekantaṃ asaṅkhārikamānasaṃ jāyati. Tanti taṃ cittaṃ mūlabhavaṅganti mūlabhavaṅgaṃ nāma tadārammaṇamiccapi tadārammaṇaṃ nāma ubhayampi nāmaṃ tasseva nāmaṃ tassa cittassa eva nāmaṃ. Iti evaṃ iminā pakārena bhagavatā paridīpitaṃ. Duhetuke sasaṅkhāre kusale javane javitepi ca taṃsamaṃ tena cittena sadisaṃ āgantukasaṅkhātaṃ tadārammaṇamānasaṃ hoti.

415-21. 'By a two-rooted kamma, rebirth-linking is two-rooted'—this section has come in due sequence and order. Here, in this context, when a kamma is performed by a two-rooted, unprompted, wholesome consciousness accompanied by joy, and if rebirth-linking is taken by a being through a two-rooted wholesome resultant consciousness accompanied by joy, similar to that kamma—then, when a desirable object comes into the range of the eye-door of that being, a wholesome mind-consciousness, accompanied by joy and devoid of knowledge, having run as impulsion seven times in that two-rooted being and then ceased, taking that very object, immediately after that impulsion, a mind-consciousness similar to that impulsion, entirely unprompted, arises. That consciousness is the root life-continuum (mūlabhavaṅga). The root life-continuum is also called the registering consciousness (tadārammaṇa); both are names for that very consciousness. Thus has it been explained by the Blessed One. Even when a prompted, wholesome impulsion has run in a two-rooted being, a registering mind-consciousness similar to that consciousness arises, which is known as the 'visiting' one.

422-9. Tatheva ca tathā eva ca iṭṭhamajjhattagocare duhetūnaṃ dvinnaṃ upekkhāyuttānaṃ javanānaṃ [V 1.0065] anantaraṃ tādisāni tehi javanehi sadisāni dve tadārammaṇamānasāni jāyante, tesaṃ tadārammaṇamānasānaṃ “piṭṭhibhavaṅga”nti nāmaṃ, “āgantukabhavaṅga”nti ca nāmaṃ hoti. Santīraṇadvayañceva dassanaṃ [M 0.0077] sampaṭicchanaṃ imāni dve bhavaṅgāni cāti aṭṭha vipākā cakkhudvāre honti. Evaṃ iminā mayā vuttappakārena pañcasu dvāresupi ca aṭṭha aṭṭha vipāke katvā pavattiyaṃ cattālīsa vipākāni bhavanti. Gahitāggahaṇenettha, cakkhudvāre panaṭṭha ca ettha etesu vipākesu gahitānaṃ vipākānaṃ aggahaṇena cakkhudvāre aṭṭha ca vipākā sotaghānādinā vipākena saddhiṃ dvādasa eva vipākāni bhavanti. Ekāya cetanāyevaṃ evaṃ iminā mayā vuttappakārena ekāya cetanāya kamme āyūhite pavattite pana sati dvādaseva vipākāni bhavanti. Iti vacanaṃ vijitakusalayuddhasaṅgāmena pakāsitaṃ desitaṃ. Duhetukattayenāpi, sesena sadisena tu mayā vuttato duhetuto sesena duhetukattayenāpi sadisena pākena ādinnasandhino gahitapaṭisandhikassa sattassa evaṃ nayo mato kathito niraṅgaṇena. Duhetukena kammena duhetukā paṭisandhi hoti. Iti ayaṃ vāro ca ettāvatā ettakena vacanena mayā vutto.

422-9. Likewise, in the sphere of desirable-neutral objects, immediately after the two two-rooted impulsions accompanied by equanimity, two registering mind-consciousnesses similar to those impulsions arise. These registering mind-consciousnesses are named 'back-bhavaṅga' and 'visiting-bhavaṅga.' The two investigating consciousnesses, seeing, and receiving, along with these two bhavaṅgas—thus there are eight resultants in the eye-door. In this manner I have described, by taking eight resultants in each of the five sense-doors, there are forty resultants in the course of existence. Here, by the method of inclusion and exclusion: there are eight resultants in the eye-door; then, by not recounting those already included, together with the resultants of the ear, nose, and so on, there are just twelve resultants. When a kamma is performed and set in motion by a single volition, there are just twelve resultants. This has been declared and taught by the one victorious in the war and battle of the wholesome. For a being who has taken rebirth-linking with a resultant similar to the remaining triad of two-rooted kammas, this method is likewise considered and has been taught by the Stainless One. 'A two-rooted kamma produces a two-rooted rebirth-linking'—thus this section has been stated by me with this much said.

430-8. Duhetukena kammena ahetukā paṭisandhi hoti, iti ayaṃ vāro anupubbena paṭipāṭiyā āgato. Tesu catūsupi duhetukesu kusalesu cittesu aññatareneva hetukena kamme āyūhite pavattite sati tasseva duhetukassa kusalajavanassa pākabhūtāya upekkhāsahagatāhetukāya manoviññāṇadhātuyā ādinnapaṭisandhino sattassa sā paṭisandhi kammasadisā nāma na vattabbā paṇḍitehi. Hi saccaṃ “paṭisandhi na vattabbā”tiādikaṃ vacanaṃ. Kammaṃ duhetukaṃ hoti, paṭisandhi ahetukā hoti. Tassa dehino sattassa vuḍḍhimupetassa vuḍḍhiṃ upagatassa cakkhudvāre pana iṭṭhamajjhattagocare āpāthamāgate sati duhetukānaṃ catunnaṃ puññānaṃ yassa kassaci [M 0.0078] javanassa avasānamhi idaṃ ahetukaṃ mano tadārammaṇabhāvena jāyati. Ettha etasmiṃ vacane saṃsayo sandeho natthi, taṃ ahetukacittaṃ mūlabhavaṅgañca tadārammaṇameva ca hoti. Cakkhuviññāṇakādīsupi vīthicittesu jātesu upekkhāsahagataṃyeva santīraṇampi ca hoti. Tesu ekaṃ ṭhapetvāna, gahitāggahaṇenidha tesu dvīsu santīraṇatadārammaṇakiccesu vipākesu ekaṃ santīraṇakiccaṃ tadārammaṇakiccaṃ taṃ cittaṃ ṭhapetvā gahitānaṃ vipākānaṃ aggahaṇena idha iṭṭhamajjhattārammaṇe gaṇanūpagacittāni tīṇiyeva bhavanti.

430-8. 'By a two-rooted kamma, rebirth-linking is rootless'—this section has come in due sequence and order. Among those four two-rooted wholesome consciousnesses, when a kamma is performed and set in motion by any one of them, for a being whose rebirth-linking is taken by the rootless mind-consciousness-element accompanied by equanimity—which is the resultant of that very two-rooted wholesome impulsion—the wise say that such a rebirth-linking is not to be called similar to the kamma. Indeed, this statement is true. The kamma is two-rooted, but the rebirth-linking is rootless. For that being, having reached maturity, when a desirable-neutral object comes into the range of the eye-door, at the end of the impulsion of any one of those four wholesome two-rooted types, this rootless mind arises with the function of registering. In this statement, there is no doubt; that rootless consciousness is both the root life-continuum and the registering consciousness. Even when eye-consciousness and other process-consciousnesses arise, the investigating-consciousness accompanied by equanimity also occurs. Here, by the method of inclusion and exclusion: among the two resultant functions of investigating and registering, setting aside one of them, and by not recounting resultants already included, in the case of a desirable-neutral object, the consciousnesses to be counted are only three.

439-41. Iṭṭhe ārammaṇe cakkhu-dvāre āpāthamāgate tadā santīraṇañceva somanassayuttaṃyeva [V 1.0066] hoti, tadārammaṇamānasañca somanassayuttaṃyeva hoti, tesu santīraṇatadārammaṇakiccesu vipākesu ekekaṃ santīraṇakiccaṃ, tadārammaṇakiccaṃ vā cittaṃ gahetvā purimāni ca tīṇi cattāri eva vipākāni bhavanti. Evaṃ iminā mayā vuttappakārena pañcasu dvāresupi cattāri cattāri vipākacittānīti pavattiyaṃ vipākāni vīsati cittāni honti.

439-41. When a desirable object comes into the range of the eye-door, the investigating-consciousness is accompanied by joy, and the registering mind-consciousness is also accompanied by joy. Counting the types of resultants: taking the consciousnesses that perform the functions of investigating and registering, along with the preceding ones, there are four types of resultants. Thus, in the manner I have explained, with four resultant consciousnesses in each of the five sense-doors, there are twenty resultant consciousnesses in the course of existence.

442-8. Cakkhudvāre tu cattāri, gahitāggahaṇenidha gahitānaṃ vipākānaṃ aggahaṇena cakkhudvāre pana cattāri vipākāni idha imasmiṃ iṭṭhārammaṇe sotaghānādinā vipākena saddhiṃ ahetukaṃ aṭṭhakaṃ hoti eva. Ahetukapaṭisandhissa sattassa duhetukaṃ, tihetukaṃ vā tadārammaṇaṃ na bhave na bhaveyya, duhetupaṭisandhino sattassa tihetukaṃ tadārammaṇaṃ na bhave. Jātā sugatiyaṃ yena, pākena paṭisandhi tu sugatiyaṃ yena pākena paṭisandhi jātā, tena vipākena tulyampi, hīnaṃ vā tesaṃ tadārammaṇaṃ bhaveyya. Manussalokaṃ sandhāya, vuttañcāhetukaṭṭhakaṃ sugatiyaṃ ahetukaṭṭhakañca manussalokañca sandhāya paṭicca kāraṇaṃ [M 0.0079] katvā mayā vuttaṃ. Catūsupi apāyesu pana apeto ayo patiṭṭhā etehīti apāyo, tesu. Pavatte ahetukaṃ aṭṭhakaṃ āpāyikehi labbhati. Thero nerayikānaṃ tu, dhammaṃ deseti vassati thiro thirakāradhammo yasmiṃ atthīti thero, dutiyaaggasāvakabhūto iddhimā moggallānatthero nerayikānaṃ niraye jātānaṃ sattānaṃ dhammaṃ deseti vassati, “ucchaṅge maṃ nisīditvā”tiādīsu viya devaṃ vassāpetīti attho. Gandhaṃ vāyuñca māpeti yadā, tadā pana tesaṃ nerayikānaṃ sattānaṃ tehi nerayikasattehi theraṃ disvā, dhammañca sutvā, gandhañca ghāyitvā jalaṃ udakañca pivataṃ pivantānaṃ muduṃ vāyuñca tehi phusataṃ phusantānaṃ tesaṃ nerayikasattānaṃ cakkhuviññāṇakādīni pañcapi puññajāni eva kusalavipākāni eva santīraṇadvayaṃ puññajaṃ eva kusalavipākaṃ eva puññajā eva ekā manodhātu iti aṭṭhakaṃ hoti.

442-8. At the eye-door, there are four. Here, by the method of inclusion and exclusion, there are four resultants at the eye-door. In the case of a desirable object, together with the resultants of the ear, nose, and so on, this indeed makes up the rootless eightfold group. For a being with a rootless rebirth-linking, a two-rooted or three-rooted registering consciousness would not arise. For a being with a two-rooted rebirth-linking, a three-rooted registering consciousness would not arise. For one born in a happy destiny, by whatever resultant rebirth-linking has occurred, their registering consciousness may be equal to or inferior to that resultant. The rootless eightfold group in the happy destinies has been taught by me with reference to the human world. As for the four woeful states (apāya)—so called because welfare (ayo) has departed (apeto) from them—in those realms, during the course of existence, the rootless eightfold group is obtained by the beings there. The Elder (thero)—so called because he possesses steadfast (thira) qualities—preaches the Dhamma to the hell-beings, raining it down. The venerable Moggallāna, the second chief disciple, endowed with psychic powers, teaches the Dhamma to beings born in hell. When he creates a fragrance and a breeze, then for those hell-beings—upon seeing the Elder, hearing the Dhamma, smelling the fragrance, drinking the water, and feeling the gentle breeze—the five sense-consciousnesses, the two investigating consciousnesses, and the one mind-element, all being wholesome resultants born of merit, arise. This makes the eightfold group.

449-50. Ayaṃ tāva kathā “cakkhuviññāṇakādīni puññajānevā”tiādikā ayaṃ kathā iṭṭhaiṭṭhamajjhattagocare kāmāvacare puññānaṃ javanānaṃ vasena mayā vuttā. Tadārammaṇacetaso tadārammaṇacittassa yaṃ niyamattaṃ “tadārammaṇamānasaṃ javanena niyāmita”ntiādivacanena mayā vuttaṃ, taṃ niyamattaṃ kusalaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Somanassayutte kāmāvacarakusale javite tadārammaṇampi somanassayuttameva hoti, upekkhāyutte kāmāvacarakusale javite tadārammaṇampi upekkhāyuttameva [V 1.0067] hoti, netaṃ akusale upekkhāyutte vicikicchādike akusale javane pana javite somanassayuttampi tadārammaṇaṃ hotīti adhippāyo. Itipi vacanaṃ ācariyena dīpitaṃ.

449-50. Thus far, this discussion concerning 'eye-consciousness and so forth being born of merit,' etc., has been stated by me in regard to desirable and desirable-neutral objects in the sense-sphere, on the basis of wholesome impulsions. The determination of the registering consciousness, which I stated with the words 'the registering consciousness is determined by the impulsion,' and so forth—that determination was stated in reference to the wholesome. When a sense-sphere wholesome impulsion associated with joy has run, its registering consciousness is also associated with joy; when a sense-sphere wholesome impulsion associated with equanimity has run, its registering consciousness is also associated with equanimity. This does not apply to the unwholesome; for when an unwholesome impulsion associated with equanimity, such as doubt, has run, a registering consciousness associated with joy can also arise. This is the intended meaning. Thus, this statement has been explained by the teacher.

451-7. Idha imasmiṃ adhippāye akusalacittesu somanassayuttesu catūsupi iṭṭhe ārammaṇe tesu cittesu [M 0.0080] javitesu somanassayuttā ahetumanoviññāṇadhātu tadanantaraṃ tesaṃ akusalajavanānaṃ anantaraṃ tadārammaṇabhāvena jāyati. Upekkhāyuttesu chasu akusalacittesu iṭṭhamajjhatte gocare javitesu puññajā upekkhāsahagatā ahetumanoviññāṇadhātu eva tadanantaraṃ vā tesaṃ upekkhāsahagatānaṃ channaṃ akusalajavanānaṃ anantaraṃ tadārammaṇabhāvena jāyati. Iṭṭhārammaṇayogasmiṃ buddharūpādiiṭṭhārammaṇayogasmiṃ kaṅkhato “buddho nu kho, no buddho”ti kaṅkhantassa sattassa uddhatassa vā sattassa tadārammaṇamānasaṃ somanassayuttaṃ ahetukaṃ vipākaṃ hoti piṭṭhibhavaṅgaṃ. Somanassayute citte, javane javite pana somanassayuttā eva pañca tadārammaṇamānasā paṇḍitena gavesitabbā. Upekkhāsahagate citte javane pana javite sati upekkhāsahagatā cha ca tadārammaṇamānasā paṇḍitena gavesitabbā.

451-7. Here, in this context, among the four unwholesome consciousnesses accompanied by joy, when they have run as impulsions with a desirable object, the rootless mind-consciousness element accompanied by joy arises immediately after them as the registering consciousness. Among the six unwholesome consciousnesses accompanied by equanimity, when they have run as impulsions with a desirable or neutral object, only the rootless mind-consciousness element accompanied by equanimity, born of merit, arises immediately after them as the registering consciousness. In connection with a desirable object, such as the form of the Buddha, for a being who is doubting—doubting, 'Is this the Buddha or not?'—or for a restless being, the registering consciousness, accompanied by joy, rootless, and resultant, becomes the subsequent life-continuum. When the impulsion consciousness is accompanied by joy, five registering consciousnesses accompanied by joy should be sought by the wise. When the impulsion consciousness is accompanied by equanimity, six registering consciousnesses accompanied by equanimity should be sought by the wise.

458-63. Tihetusomanassena, ādinnapaṭisandhino sattassa jhānato parihīnassa vippaṭisārino taṃ jhānaṃ paccavekkhato paccavekkhantassa domanassayuttaṃ cittaṃ hoti. Tassa domanassassa anantaraṃ kiṃ mānasaṃ jāyate, tvaṃ domanassayuttajavanassa anantaramānasaṃ brūhi kathehi. Paṭṭhāne paṭisiddhā hi domanassassānantaraṃ somanassassa uppatti paṭṭhāne paṭisiddhā paṭṭhānappakaraṇe bhagavatā nivāritā, assa somanassassa vā anantaraṃ domanassassa uppatti paṭṭhāne paṭṭhānappakaraṇe paṭisiddhā bhagavatā nivāritā. Mahaggataṃ panārabbha mahaggataṃ paṭicca javane javitepi ca tadārammaṇamānasaṃ tattheva tasmiṃ paṭṭhāne eva paṭisiddhaṃ bhagavatā nivāritaṃ. Tasmā kāraṇā bhavaṅgapāto vā tadārammaṇameva vā na hoti. Kiṃ nu kātabbaṃ tesaṃ bhavaṅgatadārammaṇānaṃ abhāve kāraṇaṃ yaṃ kātabbaṃ, amhehi taṃ [M 0.0081] kāraṇaṃ kiṃ nu pucchāma, taṃ tadatthaṃ ābhidhammikabhāvena ābhidhammika taṃ kāraṇaṃ vada vadāhi. Upekkhāsahagatāhetumanoviññāṇadhātu puññāpuññavipākā tadārammaṇikā siyā bhaveyya.

458-63. For a being who has taken rebirth with three roots and joy, who has fallen from jhāna and is regretful, when he reflects on that jhāna, a consciousness associated with displeasure arises. Immediately after that displeasure, what consciousness arises? Explain the consciousness that arises immediately after the impulsion accompanied by displeasure. In the Paṭṭhāna, the arising of joy immediately after displeasure is indeed prohibited; it is prevented by the Blessed One in the Paṭṭhāna treatise. Likewise, the arising of displeasure immediately after joy is prohibited in the Paṭṭhāna treatise by the Blessed One. Moreover, when an impulsion has run taking a sublime object as its support, the registering consciousness is also prohibited right there in that Paṭṭhāna by the Blessed One. Therefore, there is neither a lapse into the life-continuum nor a registering consciousness. In the absence of that life-continuum and registering consciousness, what is to be done? What is the reason for what is to be done? We ask, what is that reason? O Abhidhammika, for this purpose, speak, declare that reason in an Abhidhammic manner. The rootless mind-consciousness element accompanied by equanimity, the resultant of wholesome or unwholesome kamma, could be the registering consciousness.

464-7. Imassa tadārammaṇassa āvajjanaṃ kiṃ natthi? Taṃ tadārammaṇamānasaṃ kathaṃ kena pakārena jāyate? Bhavaṅgaāvajjanānaṃ cittānaṃ kiṃ āvajjanamattaṃ? Maggassa anantarassa ca phalassāpi kiṃ āvajjanaṃ natthi? Nirodhā ca nirodhato vuṭṭhahantassa bhikkhuno phalacittassa vāti [V 1.0068] mayā sutaṃ, evaṃ iminā mayā vuttappakārena āvajjanaṃ natthi. Vinā āvajjanenāpi, hotu jāyatu mānasaṃ cittaṃ āvajjanena vinā āvajjanaṃ vajjetvā hotu jāyatu, kimassārammaṇaṃ assa tadārammaṇamānasassa kiṃ ārammaṇaṃ, paṇḍita, tvaṃ ārammaṇaṃ yadi jānāsi, taṃ ārammaṇaṃ brūhi mayhaṃ kathehi. Vinā ārammaṇenetaṃ etaṃ mānasaṃ ārammaṇena vinā ārammaṇaṃ vajjetvā na jāyati. Hi saccaṃ “vinā ārammaṇeneta”ntiādikaṃ vacanaṃ, tadārammaṇamānasaṃ yadā domanassayuttaṃ javanaṃ mahaggatārammaṇaṃ javati, tadā tasmiṃyeva javanacittakkhaṇe parittesu kāmāvacarārammaṇesu yaṃ kiñci parittārammaṇaṃ ārabbha paṭicca jāyati.

464-7. Is there no adverting for this registering consciousness? How and by what means does that registering consciousness arise? For the consciousnesses of the life-continuum and adverting, is there only adverting? For the fruit consciousness immediately following the path, is there no adverting? And I have heard that for the fruit consciousness of a monk emerging from cessation, there is no adverting. Thus, in the way I have described, there is no adverting. Even without adverting, let the consciousness arise. Let the consciousness arise without adverting, setting adverting aside. What is its object? What is the object of that registering consciousness? O wise one, if you know the object, tell me that object, explain it to me. Without an object, this consciousness does not arise; setting an object aside, it does not arise. Indeed, the statement 'without an object...' is true. When the impulsion accompanied by displeasure runs on a sublime object, then at that very moment of the impulsion consciousness, the registering consciousness arises taking as its support some sense-sphere object among the sense-sphere objects.

468-73. Utubījaniyāmo ca utuniyāmo bījaniyāmo ca kammadhammaniyāmatā ca kammaniyāmatā ca sīlādipāramīdhammaniyāmatā ca cittassa niyāmo cāti pañca niyāmatā paṇḍitena ñeyyā. Tattha tesu pañcasu niyāmesu sabbesaṃ pana rukkhānaṃ ekappahārena phalapupphādidhāraṇaṃ utu, ayaṃ utuniyāmatā. Tesaṃ tesaṃ tu bījānaṃ, taṃtaṃtulyaphalubbhavo tesaṃ tesaṃ bījānaṃ pana tehi tehi bījehi tulyānampi sassānaṃ phalānaṃ uppatti, ayaṃ bījaniyāmatā[M 0.0082]. Matthake nāḷikerassa nāḷikeraphalassa matthake chiddattaṃ chiddabhāvo, ayaṃ bījajo bījato jāto niyāmo. Tihetukakammaṃ tihetukañca vipākaṃ duhetukañca vipākaṃ ahetukañca vipākaṃ yato yaṃ kammaṃ deti, ayaṃ kammaniyāmatā. Bodhisattassa jātiyaṃ jinaṅkurassa jātikkhaṇe medanīkampanādikaṃ anekavisesattaṃ, ayaṃ sīlādipāramīdhammaniyāmatā. Tena gocarena pasādasmiṃ ghaṭṭite sati idha imasmiṃ cittavīthiyaṃ āvajjanādīnaṃ cittānaṃ uppatti, ayaṃ cittaniyāmatā.

468-73. The five determinacies should be known by the wise: the determinacy of seasons, the determinacy of seeds, the determinacy of kamma, the determinacy of the norm of virtues and perfections, and the determinacy of consciousness. Among these five determinacies: that all trees bear fruit, flowers, and so forth at the same time is due to the season; this is the determinacy of seasons. The production of a corresponding fruit from each respective seed, that is, the arising of fruits and crops similar to those respective seeds from those seeds; this is the determinacy of seeds. The hollowness at the top of a coconut is a determination born of the seed. That a three-rooted kamma gives a three-rooted resultant, a two-rooted resultant, and a rootless resultant; this is the determinacy of kamma. At the birth of the Bodhisatta, at the moment of the arising of the embryo of the Victor, the shaking of the earth and other various extraordinary phenomena occur; this is the determinacy of the norm of virtues and perfections. When a sense object has impinged upon a sense faculty, the arising of consciousnesses such as adverting in this cognitive process; this is the determinacy of consciousness.

474. Yo puggalo dhīro dhīrasampanno guṇasampanno vikkhittapāpo mohandhakārāpagamaṃ andhakāramanissāya avijjānissaraṇaṃ yadicche sace iccheyya, so dhīro imaṃ abhidhammāvatārappakaraṇaṃ andhajjanānaṃ andhasadisabālajanānaṃ hadayandhakāraṃ viddhaṃsanaṃ andhakārasannissitassa yassa hadayassa viddhaṃsanakaraṃ jalantaṃ dīpaṃ jalamānaṃ dīpaṃ. Payattoti pakārena yatati vīriyaṃ karotīti payatto, satataṃ sabbadā sikkhetha sajjhāyanadhāraṇacintanavasena sikkheyya.

474. Whatever wise person, endowed with wisdom and virtues, whose evils are dispelled, should desire the removal of the darkness of delusion and the escape from ignorance without relying on darkness, that wise person should constantly and always train by means of this treatise, the Abhidhammāvatāra—a blazing lamp, a burning lamp, which dispels the darkness in the hearts of blind people, of foolish people who are like the blind, and which destroys the heart that is dependent on darkness. 'Diligent' (payatto) means one who strives, who makes effort in a proper manner; he should train through study, recitation, retention, and reflection.

Iti abhidhammāvatāraṭīkāya

Thus ends the Abhidhammāvatāra Commentary.

Vipākacittappavattiniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Arising of Resultant Consciousness is concluded.

Sattamo paricchedo.

The Seventh Chapter.

8. Aṭṭhamo paricchedo

8. The Eighth Chapter.

Pakiṇṇakaniddesavaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Miscellaneous Exposition.

475.

475.

Idāni [V 1.0069] pana sabbesaṃ, etesaṃ mānasaṃ mayā;

Pāṭavatthāya bhikkhūnaṃ, kathīyati pakiṇṇakaṃ.

Now, however, having all these matters in mind, the miscellaneous section is spoken by me for the mastery of the monks.

Idāni pana kāle etesaṃ tihetukadvihetukaahetukānaṃ sabbesaṃ puggalānaṃ pakiṇṇakaṃ mānasaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭavatthāya [M 0.0083] bhikkhūnaṃ chekabhāvatthāya mayā kathīyate uccate.

Now, at this time, a miscellaneous exposition of the mental states of all these individuals—those with three roots, two roots, and no roots—is spoken and declared by me for the monks' proficiency, for the monks' skillfulness.

476-85. Panthamakkaṭako uṇṇanābhi panthamakkaṭako nāma pañcasu disāsu tassa suttaṃ pasāretvā jālamajjhe nipajjati. Paṭhamāya disāyettha ettha etāsu disāsu paṭhamāya disāya pasārite sutte pāṇakena paṭaṅgena vā makkhikāya vā ghaṭṭite sati sā uṇṇanābhi kiñci calitvā phandanaṃ katvā nipannaṭṭhānato suttānusārena suttaṃ anusāretvā tassa pāṇakassa yūsaṃ yūsasaṅkhātaṃ soṇitaṃ pivati. Punāgantvā tattheva tasmiṃ jālamajjheyeva yathāsukhaṃ nipajjati, yathā paṭhamāya disāya calanādikaṃ kiriyaṃ karoti, evameva dutiyādīsu catūsu disāsu calanādikaṃ kiriyaṃ karoti, evaṃ pañcasu disāsu suttaṃ viya pañca pasādā paṇḍitena daṭṭhabbā, majjhe makkaṭako viya ca cittaṃ pana paṇḍitena daṭṭhabbaṃ. Pāṇakādīhi khuddakatiracchānehi tassa saṅghaṭṭanā viya ārammaṇe pana pasādānaṃ saṅghaṭṭanā paṇḍitena daṭṭhabbā. Jālamajjhe nipannāya uṇṇanābhiyā taṃ calanaṃ viya pasāde ghaṭṭetīti pasādaghaṭṭanaṃ, kiṃ taṃ? Ārammaṇaṃ. Tattha tissaṃ vīthiyaṃ pasādaghaṭṭanaṃ ārammaṇaṃ gahetvā manodhātukiriyācittaṃ bhavaṅgaṃ āvaṭṭetīti bhavaṅgāvaṭṭanaṃ mataṃ bhagavatā. Tassa panthamakkaṭakassa suttānusāraṃva suttaṃ anugamanaṃ viya vīthicittappavattanaṃ paṇḍitena daṭṭhabbaṃ. Sīse pana vijjhitvā assa makkaṭassa yūsapānaṃ viya javanassa cittassa ārammaṇesu pavattanaṃ paṇḍitena daṭṭhabbaṃ. Puna āgantvā suttajālamajjhe nipajjanaṃ yathā vatthuṃyeva hadayavatthuṃ eva nissāya cittassa parivattanaṃ paṇḍitena daṭṭhabbaṃ.

476-85. The spider at the crossroads, a spider named Uṇṇanābhi, spreads its thread in five directions and lies in the middle of the web. When the thread spread in the first direction is touched by a small creature, a moth, or a fly, that spider moves slightly, quivers, and then, following the thread from where it was lying, drinks the juice of that creature, which is the blood so designated. Returning again, it lies comfortably right there in the middle of the web. Just as it performs the action of moving and so forth in the first direction, so too does it perform such actions in the remaining four directions. Thus, the threads in the five directions should be seen by the wise as the five sense faculties, and the spider in the middle should be seen by the wise as the mind. The striking by small creatures and the like should be seen by the wise as the striking of the sense faculties by their objects. The striking on a sense faculty is like that movement of the spider lying in the middle of the web. What is that striking? The object. There, in that cognitive process, taking the object that strikes the sense faculty, the functional mind-element consciousness turns the life-continuum; this is considered the turning of the life-continuum by the Blessed One. The following of the thread by that spider at the crossroads should be seen by the wise as the proceeding of the cognitive process consciousnesses. The piercing of the head and the drinking of juice by that spider should be seen by the wise as the proceeding of the javana-consciousness towards its objects. The returning again to lie in the middle of the web should be seen by the wise as the turning back of the mind, which is dependent on the heart-base as its physical basis.

486-93. Idaṃ [V 1.0070] tu pana opammaṃ, atthaṃ dīpeti kiṃ tu hi idaṃ opammaṃ kaṃ atthaṃ dīpeti pakāseti? Paṭhamaṃ pasāde ārammaṇena [M 0.0084] ghaṭṭite sati pasādavatthuto pasādo vatthu nissayo etassāti pasādavatthu, cittaṃ, tato pasādavatthuto, paṭhamaṃ eva vatthusannissitaṃ bhavaṅgasaṅkhātaṃ mano jāyati, itipi attho tena opammena dīpito. Ekekārammaṇaṃ dvīsu dvīsu dvāresu sabbaso sabbappakārena pana āpāthaṃ āgacchati, ayamatthopi tena opammena dīpito “dvīsu dvīsu dvāresū”ti, ekaṃ rūpārammaṇaṃ ekasmiṃyeva khaṇe cakkhudvāre, manodvāre cāti dvīsu dvāresu āpāthaṃ āgacchatīti attho. Sotadvārādīsupi eseva nayo ñeyyo. Rūpaṃ cakkhupasādamhi ghaṭṭetvā taṅkhaṇe pana tassa khaṇe pana tathā manodvāre pana āpāthaṃ āgacchati, bhavaṅgacalanassa paccayo hotīti attho. Na saṃsayo etasmiṃ vacane saṃsayo natthi. Yathā khago yathā sakuṇo. Hi saccaṃ mayā vuttaṃ vacanaṃ. Rukkhagge rukkhakoṭiyaṃ nilīyantova sākhino sākhaṃ ghaṭṭeti, tassa chāyā bhūmiyaṃ pathaviyaṃ pharati paṭihaññati. Idhāti nipāto. Sākhāya sakuṇena ghaṭṭanaṃ bhūmiyaṃ chāyāpharaṇāpi ca apubbaṃ acarimaṃ ekakkhaṇasmiṃyeva jāyare jāyanti. Evameva pana rūpassa, pasādassa ca ghaṭṭanaṃ, tatheva atthato atthavasena bhavaṅgacalanassāpi paccayattena paccayabhāvena manodvāre āpāthaṃ āgamanaṃ apubbaṃ acarimaṃ ekakkhaṇeyeva hoti.

486-93. But this simile—what meaning does it illustrate and reveal? First, when an object strikes the sensitivity, the mind, which is called the life-continuum, arises initially, dependent on the physical basis of the sensitivity. This meaning too is illustrated by that simile. Each object, in every way, comes into range in two doors each; this meaning too is illustrated by that simile, by the phrase “in two doors each.” For example, a single visible form appears at one moment in the eye-door and also in the mind-door—this is the meaning. The same method should be understood for the ear-door and others. When a form strikes the eye-sensitivity, at that very moment it also appears in the mind-door, becoming a condition for the vibration of the life-continuum—this is the meaning. There is no doubt in this statement; there is no doubt. Just as a bird, just as a fowl—indeed, the word spoken by me is true. While alighting on a treetop, on a branch of a tree, it touches a branch, and its shadow spreads and falls upon the ground. Here, the bird's touching of the branch and the spreading of its shadow on the ground occur simultaneously, not one before or after the other, in a single moment. In the same way, the striking of the form against the sensitivity, and likewise, in that sense, its appearance in the mind-door as a condition for the vibration of the life-continuum—both happen simultaneously, not one before or after the other, in a single moment.

494-7. Tato paraṃ bhavaṅgasotaṃ chinditvā cakkhudvāre cakkhupasāde yathākkamaṃ āvajjane samuppanne, dassane samuppanne, sampaṭicchane samuppanne, santīraṇe samuppanne, tathā voṭṭhabbane ca samuppanne kusalaṃ javanacittaṃ javati, tathā akusalameva cittaṃ javati. Sotadvārādīsupi saddādīnaṃ ārammaṇānaṃ ghaṭṭane eseva nayo avisesena viññunā viññeyyo. Etassa atthassa dīpane dovārikopamādīni vacanāni [M 0.0085] uddharitvā tato pakaraṇato nīharitvā ettha etasmiṃ vīthiyādhikāre viññunā dassetabbāni.

494-7. Then, having cut off the stream of the life-continuum, at the eye-door, on the eye-sensitivity, in due order, when adverting has arisen, seeing has arisen, receiving has arisen, investigating has arisen, and likewise determining has arisen, a wholesome impulsion-consciousness impels, or an unwholesome consciousness impels. At the ear-door and so on, when sounds and other objects impinge, this same method should be understood by the wise without distinction. To clarify this meaning, the sayings concerning the simile of the gatekeeper and so on should be extracted from the treatise and then, in this section on the cognitive process, they should be presented by the wise.

498-9. Asambhedena cakkhussāti tassāpi cakkhu asambhinnaṃ hoti. Jīvitā niruddhampi pittena vā semhena vā ruhirena vā palibuddhaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa paccayo bhavituṃ asakkontaṃ sambhinnaṃ nāma, sakkontaṃ asambhinnaṃ nāma hoti. Tena cakkhupasādassa asambhinnena rūpāpāthagamanena ālokasannissayenāpi. Tena tividhena paccayena samanakkārahetunā pañcadvārāvajjanapaccayena saha pavattanena. Etehi pana catūhi paccayehi saṃ ekato inti pavattantīti [V 1.0071] sametā, sametehi sahagatehi samāgamaṃ ekībhāvaṃ āgatehi, taṃ cakkhuviññāṇaṃ cakkhupasādanissitaṃ viññāṇaṃ sampayuttehi cetasikehi saha jāyate.

498-9. 'By the unimpaired eye' means that the eye faculty is unimpaired. That which is obstructed by bile, phlegm, or blood, and thus unable to serve as a condition for eye-consciousness, is called 'impaired'; that from which life has ceased is also unable and is thus called 'impaired'. That which is able to serve as a condition is called 'unimpaired.' Thus, by the unimpaired eye-sensitivity, by a form coming into range, by the support of light, and by the cause of proper attention—by these four conditions, which are assembled, concurrent, and have come to association and unity, that eye-consciousness, the consciousness dependent on the eye-sensitivity, arises together with its associated mental factors.

500-1. Asambhedena sotassa sotapasādassa asambhinnena saddāpāthagamena ca saddassa āpāthagamanena ca. Ākāsanissayenāpi pihitakaṇṇacchiddassa sotaviññāṇaṃ nuppajjati. Tena tividhena paccayena. Samanakkārahetunā pañcadvārāvajjanapaccayena saha pavattena. Etehi pana catūhi paccayehi sametehi sahagatehi samāgamaṃ ekībhāvaṃ āgatehi taṃ sotaviññāṇaṃ sampayuttehi saha jāyati.

500-1. By the unimpaired ear-sensitivity, by a sound coming into range, and by the support of space—for ear-consciousness does not arise for one whose ear-hole is blocked; and by the cause of proper attention—by these four conditions, which are assembled, concurrent, and have come to association and unity, that ear-consciousness arises together with its associated factors.

502-3. Asambhedena ghānassa ghānapasādassa asambhinnena gandhāpāthagamena ca gandhassa āpāthagamanena ca. Vāyosannissayenāpīti ghānabilamhi pavisantena vāyunāti attho. Tena tividhena paccayena. Samanakkārahetunā pañcadvārāvajjanapaccayena saha pavattena. Etehi pana catūhi paccayehi sametehi sahagatehi samāgamaṃ ekībhāvaṃ [M 0.0086] āgatehi taṃ ghānaviññāṇaṃ sampayuttehi saha jāyati.

502-3. By the unimpaired nose-sensitivity, by a smell coming into range, and by the support of air—meaning the air entering the nasal cavity; and by the cause of proper attention—by these four conditions, which are assembled, concurrent, and have come to association and unity, that nose-consciousness arises together with its associated mental factors.

504-5. Asambhedena jivhāya jivhāya asambhinnena rasāpāthagamena ca rasassa āpāthagamanena ca. Āposannissayenāpīti jivhātemanaṃ āpaṃ laddhā ca uppajjati, tena vinā sukkhakhādanīye jivhāya sāyitepi jivhāviññāṇaṃ nuppajjatīti attho. Tena tividhena paccayena. Samanakkārahetunā pañcadvārāvajjanapaccayena saha pavattena. Etehi pana catūhi paccayehi sametehi sahagatehi samāgamaṃ ekībhāvaṃ āgatehi taṃ jivhāviññāṇaṃ sampayuttehi saha jāyati.

504-5. 'By the unimpaired tongue' means by the tongue being unimpaired, and by the coming of taste into range. 'Also by dependence on the water element' means that it arises having obtained tongue-moistening water; without that, even when a dry edible is tasted by the tongue, tongue-consciousness does not arise. By these three conditions, and together with the cause of proper attention, which occurs as the five-door adverting condition—by these four conditions, which are assembled, co-existent, and have come to a state of union and oneness, that tongue-consciousness arises together with its associated factors.

506-7. Kāyapasādassa asambhedena phoṭṭhabbassa āpāthagamanena ca. Pathavīnissayenāpīti tena vinā kāyadvārampīti bahiddhā mahābhūtārammaṇaṃ ajjhattikaṃ kāyapasādaṃ ghaṭṭetvā pasādapaccayesu mahābhūtesu paṭihaññati. Tena tividhena paccayena. Samanakkārahetunā pañcadvārāvajjanapaccayena saha pavattena. Etehi pana catūhi paccayehi sametehi sahagatehi samāgamaṃ ekībhāvaṃ āgatehi taṃ kāyaviññāṇaṃ sampayuttehi saha jāyati.

506-7. By the unimpaired body-sensitivity and by the coming of a tangible object into range. Also by dependence on the earth element: without it, at the body-door, the external great elements as object, upon striking the internal body-sensitivity, are repelled by the great elements that are the conditions for the sensitivity. By these three conditions, and together with the cause of proper attention, which occurs as the five-door adverting condition—by these four conditions, which are assembled, co-existent, and have come to a state of union and oneness, that body-consciousness arises together with its associated factors.

508-9. Asambhedā [V 1.0072] manassāpīti mananti bhavaṅgacittaṃ. Taṃ niruddhampi āvajjanacittassa paccayo bhavituṃ asamatthaṃ mandatamagatameva vattamānampi sambhinnaṃ nāma hoti. Āvajjanassa paccayo bhavituṃ samatthaṃ asambhinnaṃ nāma. Manassa asambhedena dhammassa āpāthagamanena ca vatthusannissayena hadayavatthusannissayena. Tena tividhena paccayena. Samanakkārahetunā manodvārāvajjanena saha pavattena. Etehi pana catūhi paccayehi sametehi sahagatehi samāgamaṃ [M 0.0087] ekībhāvaṃ āgatehi taṃ manoviññāṇaṃ taṃ manoviññāṇasaṅkhātaṃ javanacittaṃ sampayuttehi saha jāyate.

508-9. 'Also by the unimpaired mind': here, 'mind' means the life-continuum consciousness. That which, even when it has ceased, is unable to be a condition for the adverting consciousness, or that which, even while occurring, has reached a very weak state, is called 'impaired'. That which is able to be a condition for adverting is called 'unimpaired'. By the unimpairedness of the mind, by the coming of a mental object into range, and by dependence on the base—that is, dependence on the heart-base. By these three conditions, and due to the cause of proper attention, which occurs together with mind-door adverting—by these four conditions, which are assembled, co-existent, and have come to a state of union and oneness, that mind-consciousness—that impulsion-consciousness designated as mind-consciousness—arises together with its associated factors.

510-11. Mano bhavaṅgacittaṃ nāma vibhāvinā veditabbaṃ. Āvajjanakriyācittaṃ āvajjanakiriyācittadvayaṃ samanakkāro nāma vibhāvinā saññitaṃ. Vatthusannissayena iti ayaṃ pāṭho sabbattha sabbesu bhavesu na gacchati. Pañcahi khandhehi vokāro vokiṇṇoti pañcavokāro, pañcavokārabhavaṃ sandhāya kāraṇaṃ katvā “vatthusannissayenā”ti ayaṃ pāṭho pana kathito mayā, pañcavokārabhavo nāma kāmarūpabhavo, arūpabhavo catuvokārabhavo nāma, asaññībhavo ekavokārabhavo nāma. Ayaṃ pāṭho catuvokāraarūpabhavaṃ sandhāya na kathitoti attho. Vatthussa rūpattā arūpabhave kathaṃ vatthusannissayo bhaveyyāti attho.

510-11. The mind known as the life-continuum consciousness should be understood by one who discerns. The adverting-functional consciousness—the two adverting-functional consciousnesses—is designated as 'proper attention' by one who discerns. The passage 'by dependence on a base' does not apply everywhere in all states of existence. 'Five-aggregate existence' means that existence is mingled with the five aggregates. It is with reference to five-aggregate existence, making it the reason, that this passage 'by dependence on the base' was stated by me. Five-aggregate existence refers to the sense-sphere and form-sphere existences; the formless existence is called four-aggregate existence, and the non-percipient existence is called one-aggregate existence. The meaning is that this passage was not stated with reference to the four-aggregate formless existence. The meaning is: since the base is material form, how could there be dependence on a base in the formless existence?

512-4. Paṭisandhādicittāni, sabbānekūnavīsati honti, kāmāvacaresu dasa, rūpesu pañca, arūpīsu cattāri, sabbāni paṭisandhicittāni ekūnavīsati honti. Kammaṃ nāma kusalākusalacetanā. Kammanimittaṃ nāma rūpāni pañcārammaṇāni paññatti ca mahaggatacittañca. Tathā gatinimittakaṃ nāma kapparukkhādayo, akusalapakkhe rūpādiārammaṇabhūtā lohakumbhādayo ca. Iti evaṃ iminā mayā vuttappakārena tesaṃ paṭisandhādicittānaṃ ārammaṇaṃ tividhaṃ bhagavatā udīritaṃ. Kāmāvacarasandhīnaṃ parittārammaṇaṃ kāmāvacarārammaṇaṃ bhagavatā mataṃ. Paccuppannaṃ rūpādipañcārammaṇaṃ, gatinimittaṃ pañcārammaṇañca paccuppannañca hoti. Atītaṃ vā kammaṃ kusalākusalacetanā atītāyeva, na paccuppannā. Anāgataṃ ārammaṇaṃ natthi.

512-4. The rebirth-linking consciousnesses and others are nineteen in total: ten in the sense sphere, five in the form sphere, and four in the formless sphere. All rebirth-linking consciousnesses are nineteen. Kamma means wholesome and unwholesome volition. The kamma-sign means forms, the five sense objects, a concept, and exalted consciousness. Similarly, the destiny-sign means things like wishing-trees, and on the unwholesome side, things like iron pots which have become objects such as form. Thus, in this manner, the object of those rebirth-linking consciousnesses and others is threefold, as declared by the Blessed One. For rebirth-linkings in the sense sphere, a limited, sense-sphere object is held by the Blessed One. The five sense-objects beginning with form can be a present object; the destiny-sign is also a five-sense object and is present. Past kamma, that is, wholesome or unwholesome volition, is only past, not present. There is no future object.

515-26. Aṭṭheva ca mahāvipākā, tīṇi santīraṇāni cāti ekādasavidhaṃ cittaṃ tadārammaṇasaññitaṃ. Ekādasavidhe citte [M 0.0088] tadārammaṇasaññite puññavipākāni kusalavipākā dasa [V 1.0073] honti, apuññajaṃ akusalavipākaṃ pana ekaṃ hoti. Mahāvipākā rūpārūpabhavadvaye na jāyanti, kāmarūpabhave santīraṇattayaṃ hoti. Yāni tadārammaṇacittāni satthunā jinena vuttāni, tesu tadārammaṇacittesu ekampi tadārammaṇacittaṃ rūpārūpabhavadvaye tadārammaṇaṃ hutvā kadācipi nappavattati. Kasmā kāraṇā? Tattha tasmiṃ rūpārūpabhavadvaye “tadārammaṇaṃ na hotī”ti vacanaṃ codako bhaveyya, bījassābhāvato pana na hotīti parihāro. Akāmāvacarārammaṇe akāmāvacaradhamme idaṃ tadārammaṇamānasaṃ neva anubandhati. Hi kasmā kāraṇā? Parittārammaṇattā ca ekantena avassaṃ tadārammaṇamānasassa kāmāvacarārammaṇattā ca tathā aparicitattā ca sabbadā nānubandhati. Tañhi yathā pitaraṃ vā pitusadisaṃ vā ñātiṃ anubandhantopi taruṇadārako gharadvārantaravīthicatukkādimhi pariciteyeva dese anubandhati, na araññaṃ vā yuddhabhūmiṃ vā gacchati, evaṃ kāmāvacare dhamme anubandhantampi mahaggatalokuttaradhammamārabbha pavattamāne dhamme nānubandhati. Yasmā cassa sabbo kāmāvacarapāko ca kiriyāmanodhātu kiriyāahetukamanoviññāṇadhātu somanassasahagatā ime dhammā parittārammaṇāti evaṃ accantaṃ parittameva ārammaṇaṃ vuttaṃ, tasmā cetaṃ mahaggatalokuttarārammaṇe kāmāvacaradhammepi nānubandhatīti veditabbaṃ.

515-26. The eight great resultants and the three investigating consciousnesses—these eleven types of consciousness are designated as registering. Among these eleven types of registering consciousness, ten are wholesome resultants, and one is an unwholesome resultant. The great resultants do not arise in the two existences of form and formlessness; the three investigating consciousnesses occur in the sense-sphere and form existences. Of the registering consciousnesses taught by the Teacher, the Victor, not even a single registering consciousness ever occurs as a registering consciousness in the two existences of form and formlessness. For what reason? If an objector were to ask why 'registering does not occur there' in those two existences of form and formlessness, the refutation is: because of the absence of a seed. This registering mind never pursues a non-sense-sphere object, that is, a non-sense-sphere phenomenon. Why is that? Because its object is limited, because the registering mind absolutely and invariably has a sense-sphere object, and also because of unfamiliarity, it never pursues them. For just as a young child, though following their father or a father-like relative, follows only in familiar places like the doorway of the house, the street, or the crossroads, and does not go into the forest or to a battlefield; so too, though it pursues sense-sphere phenomena, it does not pursue phenomena that arise in connection with exalted and supramundane phenomena. And since for this consciousness, all sense-sphere resultants, the functional mind-element, and the functional, rootless mind-consciousness-element accompanied by joy—these phenomena are said to have an extremely limited object, thus their object is said to be entirely limited. Therefore, it should be understood that it does not pursue even a sense-sphere phenomenon that has an exalted or supramundane object.

527-32. Kiṃ tena yuttivādena, vuttaṃ aṭṭhakathāsu hi “janakaṃ tena tulya”ntiādikena tena, yuttiyā vādo yuttivādo, “janakaṃ tena tulya”ntiādikāya yuttikathāya kiṃ payojanaṃ vuttaṃ? Aṭṭhakathāsu hi saccaṃ “kiṃ tena yuttivādenā”ti vacanaṃ, “atthakathāsū”ti vattabbe samāse hi ttha-ssa ṭṭha-kāraṃ katvā “aṭṭhakathāsū”ti vuttaṃ[M 0.0089]. Kāmāvacare dhamme paṭicca tadārammaṇabhāvadīpakaṃ vacanaṃ ācariyena vuttaṃ. Tadārammaṇacittāni, ekādasapi sabbaso sabbappakārenapi tadārammaṇacittāni nāmagottaṃ panārabbha tissādikaṃ nāmapaññattiṃ paṭicca kaccāyanagottakassapagottādikaṃ gottapaññattiṃ paṭicca javane javitepi ca tadārammaṇaṃ na gaṇhanti, rūpārūpabhavesu vā tadārammaṇaṃ na gaṇhanti. Yadā paññattimārabbha, javane javitepi vā yadā mayā vuttāya paññattiyā sesapaññattiṃ paṭicca javane javitepi vā tadārammaṇaṃ na labbhate ācariyena, tathā dukkhaaniccaanattalakkhaṇārammaṇikāya vipassanāya tadārammaṇaṃ na labbhate ācariyena. Tadārammaṇā na labbhanti, micchattaniyatesupi micchatte micchāsabhāve “natthi dinna”ntyādivasena niyatāni cattāri diṭṭhiyuttajavanāni micchattaniyatāni, micchattaniyatesupi tadārammaṇaṃ na labbhate ācariyena, lokuttaradhamme ārabbha [V 1.0074] javane gatepi tadārammaṇaṃ na labbhate ācariyena. Tathā mahaggate dhamme ārabbha javane javitepi tadārammaṇaṃ na labbhate ācariyena, paṭisambhidāñāṇaṃ ārabbha javane javitepi tadārammaṇaṃ na labbhate ācariyena. Manodvārepi sabbesaṃ javanānaṃ anantaraṃ anupubbato tadārammaṇacittāni bhavanti.

527-32. What is the use of that discourse by reasoning? For in the commentaries it is said, 'The producer is equal to that,' and so on. A discourse by reasoning is a 'yuttivāda.' What purpose is served by stating such reasoning as 'The producer is equal to that'? Indeed, in the commentaries, the statement 'What is the use of that discourse by reasoning?' is true. When it should be said 'atthakathāsū,' in the compound, the letters 'ttha' are made into 'ṭṭha,' hence it is said 'aṭṭhakathāsū.' The teacher has stated a passage illuminating the nature of the registering object with respect to sense-sphere phenomena. The registering consciousnesses—even all eleven types in every way—do not take a registering object even when the impulsion has run, whether with respect to a name-concept like 'Tissa' and so on, or a lineage-concept like 'Kaccāyana lineage' or 'Kassapa lineage.' Nor do they take a registering object in the form and formless existences. When, having taken a concept as object, even when the impulsion has run, or when, dependent on a concept other than that stated by me, even when the impulsion has run, a registering object is not obtained by the teacher. Similarly, in insight meditation with the characteristics of suffering, impermanence, and non-self as objects, a registering object is not obtained by the teacher. Registering objects are not obtained even in the case of those fixed in wrongness. In wrongness, in the state of wrongness, the four impulsions associated with wrong view, which are fixed by statements like 'there is no giving,' are fixed in wrongness. Even for those fixed in wrongness, a registering object is not obtained by the teacher. Even when the impulsion has proceeded with a supramundane phenomenon as its object, a registering object is not obtained by the teacher. Similarly, when the impulsion has run with an exalted phenomenon as its object, a registering object is not obtained by the teacher. Even when the impulsion has run with the knowledge of analytical insight as its object, a registering object is not obtained by the teacher. At the mind-door as well, immediately after all impulsions, registering consciousnesses arise in sequence.

533-4. Manodvāre ārammaṇaghaṭṭanā na vijjati. Bhavaṅgato cetaso vīthicittassa vuṭṭhānaṃ kathaṃ kena pakārena hoti? Manodvārepi ghaṭṭanāya vinā ghaṭṭanaṃ vajjetvā āpāthaṃ āgacchanteva yasmā kāraṇā, tasmā vīthicittānaṃ sambhavo hoti.

533-4. At the mind-door, there is no impact of the object. How, and in what manner, does the arising of process-consciousness from the life-continuum mind occur? Since, even at the mind-door, objects come into range without impact, for that reason the arising of process-consciousnesses occurs.

535-6. Dvādasāpuññacittānaṃ dvādasaakusalacittānaṃ vipākā sattasattati pāpapākā dvādasapāpacittānaṃ vipākā [M 0.0090] caturāsīti pavattiyaṃ honti. Ekassa somanassayuttadiṭṭhisampayuttākusalassa cakkhusotaghānajivhākāyaviññāṇāni, sampaṭicchanaṃ, upekkhāyuttasantīraṇāni cāti satta akusalapākā honti. Tathā sesānaṃ ekādasannaṃ akusalānampi satta vipākā honti. Ekādasavidhānaṃ tu, hitvā uddhaccamānasaṃ uddhaccamānasaṃ hitvā ekādasavidhānaṃ paṭisandhiyo ekādasavidhā ceva bhavanti.

535-6. For the twelve demeritorious consciousnesses, the twelve unwholesome consciousnesses, the results are seventy-seven; the evil results, the results of the twelve evil consciousnesses, are eighty-four in the course of existence. For one unwholesome consciousness associated with joy and accompanied by wrong view, the seven unwholesome results are: eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, receiving consciousness, and investigating consciousness accompanied by equanimity. Similarly, for the remaining eleven unwholesome consciousnesses, there are also seven results. As for the eleven types, however, excluding the mind accompanied by restlessness, the rebirth-linkings are of eleven kinds.

537-8. Kriyacittesu sabbesu yaṃ āvajjanadvayaṃ javanaṃ na ca hoti, taṃ āvajjanadvayaṃ karaṇamattattā kiriyāmattattā vātapupphasamaṃ vātapupphena sadisaṃ mataṃ bhagavatā. Ayametthādhippāyo – khīṇāsave uppannakāle vā taṃ āvajjanadvayaṃ kiriyacittaṃ bhavituṃ yuttaṃ. Sabbesu puthujjanesu uppannakāle kathaṃ kiriyā hotīti ce? Karaṇamattattā aphaladāyakaṃ vātapupphaṃ viya aphaladāyakaṃ kiriyacittaṃ bhavituṃ yuttihāro kiriyā pana hoti. Yaṃ sabbaṃ kiriyacittaṃ kiccasādhanato javanakiccasādhanavasena javanattaṃ javanabhāvaṃ pattaṃ chinnamūlassa rukkhassa pupphaṃ aphalaṃ hoti yathā, evaṃ chinnāvijjātaṇhāmūlassa vītarāgassa taṃ sabbaṃ kiriyacittaṃ aphalaṃ vipākavirahitaṃ siyā bhaveyya.

537-8. Among all functional consciousnesses, those two advertings that are not impulsions are, because of being mere actions, mere functions, considered by the Blessed One to be like a wind-flower. The meaning here is this: when arising in one whose taints are destroyed, it is fitting for those two advertings to be functional consciousness. If it is asked how they can be functional when arising in all ordinary beings, the answer is: because they are mere actions, fruitless like a wind-flower, it is a reasonable inference that they are fruitless functional consciousnesses; yet, the function does occur. Whatever functional consciousness, by accomplishing its task, has attained the nature of impulsion by way of accomplishing the function of impulsion—just as the flower of a tree whose roots are cut is fruitless, so too for one free from passion, whose roots of ignorance and craving are cut, all that functional consciousness would be fruitless, devoid of result.

539-40. Paṭicca pana etasmā, phalametīti paccayo ekaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca etasmā dhammato phalaṃ eti pavattati tasmā paccayo, yo dhammo yassa dhammassa ṭhitiyā uppattiyāpi upakāro [V 1.0075] nāma hoti, so dhammo tassa dhammassa paccayoti paccayo nāma paṇḍitena pavuccate. Sambhavo pabhavo hetu kāraṇaṃ paccayo mato bhagavatā. Idaṃ vacanaṃ aññattha dīpanavacanaṃ.

539-40. Dependent on this, a result comes forth; therefore, it is a condition (paccaya). A result arises and proceeds from this phenomenon, dependent on a phenomenon; therefore, it is a condition. Whatever phenomenon is helpful for the stability or arising of another phenomenon, that phenomenon is called a condition of that phenomenon by the wise. Origination, source, cause, and reason: a condition is regarded as such by the Blessed One. This statement is an explanatory statement found elsewhere.

541. Lobhādi pana yo dhammo, mūlaṭṭhenupakārako yo lobhādi pana dhammo mūlabhāvena phaladhammassa [M 0.0091] upakārako, so lobhādidhammo phaladhammassa hetūti hetu nāma vibhāvinā viññātabbo.

541. Moreover, any phenomenon such as greed which assists as a root, or any phenomenon such as greed which assists the resultant phenomenon by being its root—that phenomenon of greed, etc., is to be understood by the discerning as a 'cause' (hetu).

542. Lobho doso ca moho ca tathā alobhādayo tayo hetū, te cha eva hetuyo honti, jātito jātivasena kusalajātiakusalajātiabyākatajātivasena navadhā navahi koṭṭhāsehi siyuṃ.

542. Greed, hatred, and delusion, as well as the three—non-greed, non-hatred, and non-delusion—are the roots. These are indeed the six roots. By way of their class—that is, by way of the wholesome class, the unwholesome class, and the indeterminate class—they would be ninefold, in nine categories.

543-4. Dhammānaṃ kusalādīnaṃ, kusalādittasādhako yo dhammo kusalādīnaṃ dhammānaṃ kusalādittasādhako kusalādibhāvasādhako, so dhammo mūlaṭṭho nāma. Evaṃ vacanaṃ eke ekacce ācariyā vadanti. Evaṃ sante kusalākusalādīnaṃ dhammānaṃ kusalādittasādhakavasena mūlaṭṭhe sante taṃsamuṭṭhānarūpīsu tehi cittehi samuṭṭhānarūpesu tehi cittehi samuṭṭhitesu cittajarūpesu hetūnaṃ lobhādihetūnaṃ hetupaccayatā kadācipi neva sampajjati. Ayametthādhippāyo – yadi cittesu rūpāni samuṭṭhāpentesu te lobhādayopi cittānaṃ sampayuttacittānaṃ ekuppādattā ca rūpāni samuṭṭhāpentiyeva. Tadā tesaṃ mate tesaṃ cittajarūpānaṃ kusalādittaṃ siyā. Na ca kadāci rūpāni kusalādināmakāni dissanti yasmā, tasmā cittajarūpānaṃ kusalādibhāvañāpanatthaṃ tesaṃ cittajarūpānaṃ te lobhādayo hetupaccayā na honti, iti vacanaṃ vattabbaṃ siyā. Evañca sati cittajarūpāni nāma kadācipi viyuttāni caranti, tasmā kusalādittasādhako mūlaṭṭho na hoti.

543-4. Of states such as wholesome states, the state that establishes the wholesome nature of wholesome states, etc.—that state is called the root-condition. Thus, some teachers say. If this is so, then when states such as wholesome and unwholesome states exist as root-conditions establishing the quality of wholesome, etc., the root-conditionality of roots such as greed and other roots never occurs with regard to the mind-produced material forms arising from those consciousnesses. The meaning here is this: if, when consciousnesses produce material forms, then greed and other roots, being associated with those consciousnesses and arising simultaneously with them, also produce material forms. In that case, according to their view, the mind-produced material forms would have the quality of wholesome, etc. But since material forms are never observed to be called wholesome, etc., it would have to be said that greed and other roots are not root conditions for those mind-produced material forms in order to make known their quality of being wholesome, etc. And if this is so, then mind-produced material forms would sometimes proceed dissociated; therefore, that which establishes the quality of being wholesome, etc., is not the root-condition.

545-6. Hi saccaṃ “evaṃ sante tu hetūna”ntiādikaṃ vacanaṃ. Te lobhādayo hetū tesaṃ rūpānaṃ kusalāditaṃ kusalādibhāvaṃ na sādhenti na nipphādenti. Te hetū tesaṃ [M 0.0092] pana rūpānaṃ paccayā na ca na hontiyeva, tasmā kāraṇā kusalādīnaṃ dhammānaṃ kusalādittasādhako yo dhammo, so dhammo mūlaṭṭhoti mūlasabhāvo nāma samayaññunā samayavijānanasīlena viññunā gantabbo jānitabbo.

545-6. Indeed, the statement beginning 'but in that case, the roots' is true. Those roots, greed and the others, do not establish or accomplish the wholesome or unwholesome nature of those material forms. However, those roots are indeed conditions for those material forms. Therefore, the phenomenon that establishes the wholesome nature of wholesome states, etc., is the root-condition, or the nature of a root, and this should be understood by a wise person who discerns the proper context.

547. Suppatiṭṭhitabhāvassa[V 1.0076], sādhanenupakārako suppatiṭṭhitabhāvaṃ sādhanena upakārako yo attho, so attho hetūnaṃ lobhādīnaṃ mūlaṭṭho mūlasabhāvo iti ca gahaṇaṃ vibhāvinā viññātabbaṃ.

547. The meaning that assists by establishing the state of being well-established—that meaning is to be understood by the discerning as the root-condition, the nature of a root, for the roots such as greed and so forth.

548-9. Kusalākusalā hetū kusalā hetū, akusalā hetū, kriyāhetū sabbaso sabbappakārena sabbe kiriyāhetuyo ca sampayuttānaṃ pañcavokārabhūmiyaṃ sampayuttānaṃ dhammānaṃ aññamaññapaccayabhāvena hetupaccayataṃ yātā gatā. Taṃsamuṭṭhānānaṃ cittajarūpānañca hetupaccayataṃ yātā gatā, ete hetū catuvokārabhūmiyaṃ sampayuttānaṃ eva dhammānaṃ hetupaccayataṃ yātā gatā.

548-9. Wholesome and unwholesome roots—that is, wholesome roots, unwholesome roots, and functional roots—and all functional roots, in every way, have become a root-condition by way of mutual condition to their associated states in the five-constituent existence. They have also become a root-condition to the mind-produced material forms arising from them. These roots have become a root-condition only to their associated states in the four-constituent existence.

550-1. Kāme vipākahetūpi attanā sampayuttānaṃ hetupaccayataṃ yātā, paṭisandhikkhaṇepi kaṭattārūpajātānaṃ kammajarūpānaṃ hetupaccayataṃ yātā, tasmā paṭisandhicittuppādakkhaṇeyeva kammajarūpānaṃ uppādo hoti, yasmā kāraṇā pavattiyaṃ cittajānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayataṃ gatā.

550-1. Resultant roots in the sense-sphere have become a root-condition to their associated states. At the moment of rebirth-linking, they have become a root-condition to kamma-born material forms. Therefore, the arising of kamma-born material forms occurs precisely at the moment of the arising of the rebirth-linking consciousness, for which reason they have also become a root-condition to mind-produced material forms in the course of existence.

552-5. Rūpe vipākahetū kāmāvacarabhūmiyaṃ hetuyo viya hetupaccayā honti, pañcavokāre lokuttaravipākahetavo cittajānaṃ rūpānañca sampayuttānañca pañcavokārabhūmiyaṃ hetupaccayā honti. Catuvokāre lokuttaravipākajā hetavo sampayuttānaṃ eva catuvokārabhūmiyaṃ hetupaccayā bhavanti. Itare catuvokāre arūpabhave vipākajā hetavo sampayuttānaṃ eva sabhūmiyaṃ attano [M 0.0093] bhūmiyaṃ arūpabhūmiyaṃ hetupaccayā honti. Hetuttho hetūnaṃ attho hetuyo ceva hetupaccayo ceva hetupaccayasambhavo hetupaccayuppatti, evameva evaṃ iminā pakārena. Sañjāto sukhahetu yassāti sañjātasukhahetu, tena viññeyyo.

552-5. Resultant roots in the fine-material sphere are a root-condition just like the roots in the sense-sphere existence. In the five-constituent existence, supramundane resultant roots are a root-condition for mind-produced material forms and their associated states. In the four-constituent existence, supramundane resultant roots are a root-condition only for their associated states in the four-constituent existence. In the other four-constituent existence, namely, in the formless existence, resultant roots are a root-condition only for their associated states in their own realm, the formless realm. The meaning of 'root' is the meaning of roots: the roots themselves, the root-condition, and the arising conditioned by the root—in this way, thus, by this manner. The term 'sañjātasukhahetu' (whose cause of happiness has arisen) should be understood by that.

556-8. Chando cittañca vīriyaṃ vīmaṃsā cāti catudhādhipatī lokādhipatinā satthunā vuttā. Chandaṃ jeṭṭhakaṃ katvā cittassa uppattikālasmiṃ yo chando, so chandādhipati nāma, chandaṃ dhuraṃ katvā samādhikaraṇacittassa eseva nayo sesesupi ca tīsu mayā vuttato chandādhipatito sesesupi ca adhipatīsu. Yo dhammo jeṭṭhaṭṭhena upakārako, so dhammo adhipatīti adhipati nāma bhagavatā niddiṭṭho.

556-8. Desire, consciousness, energy, and investigation—these four dominances were taught by the Teacher, the Lord of the World. Taking desire as the foremost, the desire at the moment of the mind's arising is called the dominance of desire. This same method applies to the mind that causes concentration by making desire the yoke, and likewise to the remaining three dominances, as explained by me regarding the dominance of desire. Whatever phenomenon is helpful by way of being foremost, that phenomenon is called a dominance, as pointed out by the Blessed One.

559.

559.

Sumatimativibodhanaṃ [V 1.0077] vicittaṃ,

Kumatimatindhanapāvakaṃ padhānaṃ;

Imamatimadhuraṃ avedi yo yo,

Jinavacanaṃ sakalaṃ avedi so so.

The awakening of good understanding, variegated,

The fire that consumes the fuel of wrong understanding, the foremost text;

Whoever understands this exceedingly sweet text,

That person understands all the words of the Conqueror.

Yo yo jano imaṃ abhidhammāvatāraṃ sumatimativibodhanaṃ sumatīnaṃ sundaramatīnaṃ paṇḍitānaṃ matiyā vibodhanakaraṃ vicittaṃ kumatīnaṃ kucchitamatīnaṃ bālānaṃ matiindhane padhānaṃ pāvakaṃ atimadhurakaraṃ avedi jāni, so so jano sakalaṃ jinavacanaṃ avedi jāni.

Whatever person knows this Abhidhammāvatāra, which causes the awakening of the understanding of the wise, of those with fine understanding, and of the learned; which is variegated; a foremost fire for the fuel of the understanding of those with wrong understanding, corrupt understanding, and fools; and which is exceedingly sweet—that person knows all the words of the Conqueror.

Iti abhidhammāvatāraṭīkāya

Thus in the Subcommentary on the Abhidhammāvatāra.

Pakiṇṇakaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Exposition of the Miscellaneous Section is completed.

Aṭṭhamo paricchedo.

The Eighth Chapter.

9. Navamo paricchedo

9. The Ninth Chapter.

Puññavipākapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Exposition of the Condition for the Result of Merit

560-2.

560-2.

Bāttiṃsapākacittāni[M 0.0094], lokikāneva yāni hi;

Etesaṃ pākacittānaṃ, paṭisandhipavattisu.

Thirty-two resultant consciousnesses, which are indeed mundane;

Of these resultant consciousnesses, in rebirth-linking and the course of existence.

Yāni lokikāni eva bāttiṃsa pākacittāni honti, etesaṃ pākacittānaṃ puññāpuññādisaṅkhārā bhavādīsu yonigativiññāṇaṭṭhitisattāvāsesu paṭisandhipavattīsu yathā yena pakārena paccayā honti eva, imesaṃ vipākacittānaṃ tepi saṅkhārā bhavādīsu yonigativiññāṇaṭṭhitisattāvāsesu paṭisandhipavattīsu tathā tena pakārena vibhāvinā paṇḍitena viññātabbā. Tayo bhavā catasso ca yoniyo kāmabhavarūpabhavaarūpabhavavasena tayo bhavā, aṇḍajajalābujasaṃsedajaopapātikayonivasena catasso ca yoniyo, nirayagatitiracchānagatipetagatimanussagatidevagativasena [V 1.0078] gatipañcakaṃ, sandhisaññāya paṭisandhisaññāya nānattā nānābhāvato, kāyassāpi ca rūpakāyassāpi ca nānattā nānābhāvato kāmasugatiyo, nānā attā sabhāvo etassāti nānattā, nānatto rūpakāyo etesanti nānattakāyā, nānā sabhāvo etassāti nānattā, nānattāyeva saññā nānattasaññā, sā etesaṃ atthīti nānattasaññī nāma, paṭhamajjhānabhūmi ca caturāpāyabhūmiyo ca nānattakāyaekattasaññī nāma, dutiyajjhānabhūmi ekattakāyanānattasaññī nāma, tatiyajjhānabhūmivehapphalabhūmisuddhāvāsabhūmiyo ekattakāyaekattasaññī nāma, heṭṭhā ṭhitā rūpehi saddhiṃ sattaviññāṇaṭṭhitiyo, tiṭṭhanti viññāṇāni etthāti ṭhitiyo, viññāṇānaṃ ṭhitiyo viññāṇaṭṭhitiyo, viññāṇassa abhāvato asaññībhūmi na gayhate, catutthāruppabhūmi ca [M 0.0095] paṭuviññāṇābhāvato na gayhate. Sattāvāsavasena asaññībhūmiṃ, catutthāruppabhūmiñca pana gahetvā te sattāvāsā nava eva honti.

Just as the formations of merit, demerit, and so on, are conditions in whatever manner for the thirty-two mundane resultant consciousnesses during rebirth-linking and the course of existence—in existences, modes of birth, destinations, stations of consciousness, and abodes of beings—so in that same manner should those formations be understood by the discerning wise person as conditions for these resultant consciousnesses. There are three existences and four modes of birth. The three existences are the sense-sphere existence, the fine-material existence, and the formless existence. The four modes of birth are egg-born, womb-born, moisture-born, and spontaneously born. The five destinations are the hell destination, the animal destination, the ghost destination, the human destination, and the deva destination. Due to the diversity of perception at linking and perception at rebirth-linking, and also due to the diversity of the body and the material body, there are the happy sense-sphere destinies. “Diverse is the individual nature of this”—therefore, it is diverse (nānattā). “Diverse is the material body of these”—therefore, they are of diverse bodies (nānattakāyā). “Diverse is the individual nature of this”—therefore, it is diverse (nānattā). “Diverse indeed is the perception”—therefore, it is diverse perception (nānattasaññā); one who has that is called “one with diverse perception” (nānattasaññī). The first jhāna plane and the four woeful planes are called “of diverse bodies and uniform perception” (nānattakāyaekattasaññī). The second jhāna plane is called “of uniform body and diverse perception” (ekattakāyanānattasaññī). The third jhāna plane, the Vehapphala plane, and the Pure Abodes are called “of uniform body and uniform perception” (ekattakāyaekattasaññī). The seven stations of consciousness are situated below, together with material form. “Consciousnesses abide here”—therefore, they are stations (ṭhitiyo), that is, stations of consciousness. The non-percipient plane is not included due to the absence of consciousness. The fourth formless plane is also not included due to the absence of distinct consciousness. But, taking the non-percipient plane and the fourth formless plane by way of abodes of beings, those abodes of beings are nine in number.

563-8. Kāme puññābhisaṅkhārasaññitā aṭṭha cetanā pūrenti attano kārakaṃ pūrenti ca, ajjhāsayaṃ pujjañca bhavaṃ nibbattentīti puññāni, abhisaṅkharonti vipākaṃ, kammajarūpañcāti abhisaṅkhārā, puññāni eva abhisaṅkhārā puññābhisaṅkhārā, teyeva saññitā puññābhisaṅkhārasaññitā, kāme puññābhisaṅkhārasaññitā aṭṭha cetanā. Navannaṃ pākacittānaṃ upekkhāyuttāhetukamahāvipākavasena navannaṃ pākacittānaṃ kāmasugatiyaṃ pana nānā vattamānacetanākhaṇato paraṃ khaṇaṃ etassāti nānākhaṇaṃ, taṃ eva nānakkhaṇikaṃ, tameva kammaṃ nānakkhaṇikakammaṃ, vattamānacetanāto parā atītacetanāti attho. Balavā nissayapaccayo upanissayapaccayo, balavattho cettha upa-saddo, balavapaccayoti attho, nānakkhaṇikakammapaccayavasena balavapaccayavasena cāti attho. Dvedhā dvīhi pakārehi tesaṃ paṭisandhiyaṃ paccayā bhavanti, tā aṭṭha kāmāvacaramahākusalacetanā upekkhāsahitāhetumanoviññāṇadhātuyā vinā upekkhāsahagatāhetumanoviññāṇadhātuṃ vajjetvā parittapākānaṃ cakkhusotaghānajivhākāyasampaṭicchanasomanassayuttāhetukakusalavipākānaṃ dvedhā nānakkhaṇikakammūpanissayapaccayehi pavattiyaṃ paccayā honti. Tāyeva cetanā tā eva aṭṭha kāmāvacaramahākusalacetanā rūpabhave pañcannaṃ pākacittānaṃ kusalavipākacittānaṃ cakkhusotasampaṭicchanasomanassayuttaupekkhāyuttasantīraṇānaṃ dvedhā nānakkhaṇikakammūpanissayapaccayehi pavattiyaṃ paccayā honti. Aṭṭhannaṃ tu parittānaṃ, kāme duggatiyaṃ tathā aṭṭhannaṃ parittānaṃ kusalavipākānaṃ cakkhusotaghānajivhākāyasampaṭicchanānaṃ, dvinnaṃ [M 0.0096] santīraṇānañca pavatte pavattikkhaṇe [V 1.0079] paccayā honti, paṭisandhiyaṃ paṭisandhikkhaṇe pana paccayā na honti. Vuttappakārāva kāme sugatiyaṃ yathāvuttappakārāva aṭṭha kāmāvacaramahākusalacetanā kāmasugatiyaṃ tathā soḷasannaṃ kusalavipākānaṃ pavatte pavattikkhaṇe dvedhā nānakkhaṇikakammūpanissayapaccayehi paccayā honti, pavatte pavattikkhaṇe sattannaṃ kusalavipākānaṃ paccayā honti. Paṭisandhiyaṃ paṭisandhikkhaṇe navannaṃ kusalavipākacittānaṃ paccayā honti.

In the sense-sphere, eight volitions designated as meritorious formations fulfill their own agent and intention, and give rise to a worthy existence—thus, they are merits. They form the result and kamma-born matter—thus, they are formations. Merits themselves are meritorious formations. Designated as such, they are 'designated as meritorious formations.' In the sense-sphere, eight volitions are designated as meritorious formations. For the nine resultant consciousnesses, by way of the great rootless resultant consciousnesses accompanied by equanimity, in the sense-sphere happy destinies, a moment subsequent to the moment of a present volition is a 'different moment'; that itself is 'of a different moment'. That very kamma is 'different-moment kamma'. The meaning is: a past volition, which is other than the present volition. The strong dependence condition is the decisive support condition. Here, the prefix 'upa-' signifies strength; thus, it means a strong condition. It is explained as being by way of the different-moment kamma condition and by way of the strong condition. In two ways, in two modes, these serve as conditions for rebirth-linking. Those eight great wholesome volitions of the sense-sphere, excluding the rootless mind-consciousness-element accompanied by equanimity, serve as conditions in two ways—by different-moment kamma and decisive support conditions—during the course of life for the limited resultants: eye-, ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-consciousness, receiving consciousness, and the joy-associated rootless wholesome resultant consciousnesses. Those same volitions, those same eight great wholesome volitions of the sense-sphere, in the fine-material existence, serve as conditions in two ways—by different-moment kamma and decisive support conditions—during the course of life for the five resultant consciousnesses, namely, the wholesome resultant eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, receiving consciousness, and the joy-associated and equanimity-associated investigating consciousnesses. But for the eight limited wholesome resultants in the sense-sphere woeful states—namely, eye-, ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-consciousness, receiving consciousness, and the two investigating consciousnesses—they serve as conditions during the course of life, at the moment of occurrence, but not at the moment of rebirth-linking. As previously described, in the sense-sphere happy destinies, those eight great wholesome volitions of the sense-sphere serve as conditions in two ways—by different-moment kamma and decisive support conditions—for sixteen wholesome resultant consciousnesses during the course of life, at the moment of occurrence. During the course of life, at the moment of occurrence, they serve as conditions for seven wholesome resultants. At the moment of rebirth-linking, they serve as conditions for nine wholesome resultant consciousnesses.

569-74. Rūpe puññābhisaṅkhārā, rūpāvacarabhūmiyaṃ pañcannaṃ pākacittānaṃ paṭisandhiyaṃ paṭisandhikkhaṇe paccayā hontimāpuññasaṅkhārā, kāme duggatiyaṃ dvidhā ime apuññābhisaṅkhārā, imā kusalapaṭipakkhā uddhaccavajjā ekādasa cetanā kāmaduggatiyaṃ ekassa paṭisandhiviññāṇassa paṭisandhiyaṃ paṭisandhikkhaṇe dvidhā nānakkhaṇikakammūpanissayapaccayehi paccayā honti. Dvādasa akusalacetanā pavatte pavattikkhaṇe eva channaṃ cakkhusotaghānajivhākāyasampaṭicchanānaṃ akusalavipākānaṃ paccayā honti, paṭisandhiyaṃ paṭisandhikkhaṇe paccayā no honti. Sattannampi bhavanteva pavatte pavattikkhaṇe paṭisandhiyaṃ paṭisandhikkhaṇe akusalavipākāni sattannaṃ cakkhusotaghānajivhākāyasampaṭicchanasantīraṇānaṃ paccayā bhavanti. Kāme sugatiyaṃ tesaṃ, sattannampi tatheva ca dvādasākusalacetanā kāme sugatiyaṃ tatheva ca tesaṃ sattannaṃ akusalavipākānaṃ pavatte pavattikkhaṇe paccayā honti, paṭisandhiyaṃ paṭisandhikkhaṇe paccayā na honti. Viññāṇānaṃ catunnampi, tesaṃ rūpabhave tathā tāyeva dvādasākusalacetanā rūpabhave tesaṃ catunnaṃ akusalavipākānaṃ cakkhusotasampaṭicchanasantīraṇasaṅkhātānaṃ viññāṇānaṃ tathā pavatte pavattikkhaṇe paccayā honti, paṭisandhiyaṃ paṭisandhikkhaṇe [M 0.0097] paccayā na honti. So ca kāmabhaveniṭṭharūpādiupaladdhiyaṃ so ca apuññābhisaṅkhāro kāmabhave aniṭṭharūpādiupaladdhiyaṃ amanāparūpādīni ārammaṇāni upaladdhiyaṃ tesaṃ catunnaṃ apuññajānaṃ viññāṇānaṃ paccayo hoti. Hi saccaṃ “so ca kāmabhaveniṭṭha-rūpādiupaladdhiya”ntiādikaṃ vacanaṃ. Aniṭṭharūpādayo nāma visayā brahmaloke na vijjare na vijjanti.
