Meritorious formations in the form realm are conditions, at the moment of rebirth-linking, for the five resultant consciousnesses. These demeritorious formations are twofold in the sense-sphere woeful states. These eleven volitions, excluding restlessness, which are the antithesis of wholesome states, are conditions for a single rebirth-linking consciousness in the woeful states at the moment of rebirth-linking, by way of different-moment kamma and decisive support conditions. The twelve unwholesome volitions are conditions during the course of life, at the moment of occurrence, for the six unwholesome resultant consciousnesses, namely, eye-, ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-consciousness, and receiving-consciousness; they are not conditions at the moment of rebirth-linking. The twelve unwholesome volitions are conditions for all seven unwholesome resultants—namely, eye-, ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-consciousness, receiving-consciousness, and investigating-consciousness—in existence, both during the course of life and at rebirth-linking. In the sense-sphere happy destinies, these same twelve unwholesome volitions are likewise conditions for those seven unwholesome resultant consciousnesses during the course of life, at the moment of occurrence, but not at the moment of rebirth-linking. In the form realm, for the four unwholesome resultant consciousnesses—namely, eye-, ear-, receiving-, and investigating-consciousness—these same twelve unwholesome volitions are likewise conditions during the course of life, at the moment of occurrence, but not at the moment of rebirth-linking. And that demeritorious formation is a condition for those four consciousnesses born of demerit when disagreeable forms and so on are experienced in the sense-sphere existence. Indeed, the statement 'and that in the sense-sphere existence, upon the experience of a disagreeable form, etc.' is true, for objects such as disagreeable forms do not exist in the Brahma-world.

575-6. Tathevāneñjasaṅkhāro na iñjati na phandati na calatīti āneñjaṃ, āneñjañca taṃ saṅkhāro cāti āneñjasaṅkhāro, tathā eva āneñjasaṅkhāro arūpāvacarabhūmiyaṃ catunnaṃ pākacittānaṃ pavatte pavattikkhaṇe paṭisandhiyaṃ paṭisandhikkhaṇe paccayo hoti. Bhavesvete bhavesu ete vuttappakārā paccayā vuttappakārena paṭisandhipavattīsu yathā ca yena yena ca pakārena [V 1.0080] nānakkhaṇikakammūpanissayapaccayehi paccayā honti, tena paccayā tathā tena tena pakārena vibhāvinā vijānantena paṇḍitena ñeyyā.

Similarly, the imperturbable formation. It does not shake, tremble, or waver, thus it is called 'imperturbable'. That is imperturbable and it is a formation, hence it is called the 'imperturbable formation'. In the same way, the imperturbable formation serves as a condition for the four resultant consciousnesses in the formless realm, both during the course of life, at the moment of occurrence, and at the moment of rebirth-linking. In these existences, these conditions, in the manner described for rebirth-linking and the course of life, should be understood by the wise and discerning person according to the various ways they function as conditions by different-moment kamma and decisive support.

577. Eseva ca nayo ñeyyo, yoniādīsu yonigativiññāṇaṭṭhitisattāvāsesu eseva ca nayo bhavesu mayā vutto eva nayo paṇḍitena ñeyyo. Tatridaṃ tatra bhavesu ādito paṭṭhāya vuttaṃ idaṃ vacanaṃ mukhamattanidassanaṃ upāyamattadīpanaṃ hoti.

577. This same method should be understood regarding the modes of birth and so on—namely, the modes of birth, destinations, stations of consciousness, and abodes of beings. This is the very method I have explained regarding the realms of existence, and it is this method that should be understood by the wise. In this regard, what has been said about those realms of existence from the beginning is merely an indication of the entry-point, a mere illustration of the means.

578-81. Avisesena puññābhi-saṅkhāro dvibhavesupi kāmapuññābhisaṅkhāravasena, rūpapuññābhisaṅkhāravasena ca puññābhisaṅkhāro avisesena samānabhāvena dvīsu bhavesu kāmarūpabhavesu paṭisandhiṃ datvā so saṅkhāro sabbapākaṃ janeti nibbatteti. Tathā catūsu viññeyyo, aṇḍajādīsu yonisu dvibhavesu puññābhisaṅkhāro viya tathā catūsu aṇḍajādīsu so puññābhisaṅkhāro paṇḍitena ñeyyo. “Aṇḍajādīsū”ti [M 0.0098] vacanaṃ padumapaccekabuddhānaṃ manussattaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Bahudevamanussānaṃ vasena dvīsu gatīsu eva ca tathā so puññābhisaṅkhāro paṇḍitena ñeyyo. Tathā nānattakāyādi-viññāṇānaṃ ṭhitīsupi nānattakāyanānattasaññīnānattakaāyaekattasaññī ekattakāyanānattasaññī ekattakāyaekattasaññīnaṃ vasena catūsu viññāṇaṭṭhitīsu so puññābhisaṅkhāro paṇḍitena ñeyyo. Nānattakāyanānattasaññīnānattakāyaekattasaññīekattakāyanānattasaññīekattakāyaekattasaññīnaṃ vasena vuttappakārasmiṃ catubbidhe sattāvāse tathā so puññābhisaṅkhāro paṇḍitena ñeyyo. Evaṃ iminā mayā vuttappakārena puññābhisaṅkhāro bhavādīsu bhavayonigativiññāṇaṭṭhitisattāvāsesu yathārahaṃ soḷasannaṃ kāmakusalapākānaṃ, pañcannaṃ rūpapākānañcāti ekavīsatipākānaṃ dvidhā nānakkhaṇikakammūpanissayapaccayena paccayo hoti.

578-81. The meritorious volitional formation, without distinction, in two existences—by way of the meritorious volitional formation of the sense-sphere and by way of the meritorious volitional formation of the form-sphere—this meritorious volitional formation, without distinction and with an equal nature in the two existences, the sense-sphere and form-sphere existences, having given rebirth-linking, that formation generates and produces all resultants. Similarly, it should be understood in the four wombs, beginning with the egg-born. Just as the meritorious volitional formation in two existences, so too in the four beginning with the egg-born, that meritorious volitional formation should be known by the wise. The statement 'in the egg-born and others' is said with reference to the human state of the lotus-born Paccekabuddhas. By way of many gods and humans, in the two destinations, so too that meritorious volitional formation should be known by the wise. Likewise, in the stations of consciousness of those with diverse bodies and diverse perceptions, diverse bodies and unified perception, a unified body and diverse perceptions, and a unified body and unified perception, by way of these four stations of consciousness, that meritorious volitional formation should be known by the wise. In the fourfold abodes of beings described by way of those with diverse bodies and diverse perceptions, diverse bodies and unified perception, a unified body and diverse perceptions, and a unified body and unified perception, so too that meritorious volitional formation should be known by the wise. Thus, in the manner explained by me, the meritorious volitional formation, in existences, births, destinations, stations of consciousness, and abodes of beings, appropriately becomes a condition in two ways for the sixteen resultant states of sense-sphere wholesome kamma and the five resultant states of form-sphere kamma, totaling twenty-one resultants, through the different-moment kamma-decisive-support condition.

582-3. Kāme apuññasaṅkhāro kāmabhave aṇḍajajalābujasaṃsedajaopapātikayonivasena aṇḍajādīsu yonīsu nirayagatipetagatitiracchānagativasena tīsu gatīsu nānattakāyaekattasaññīvasena ekissā viññāṇaṭṭhitiyā nānattakāyaekattasaññīvasena ca ekasmiṃ pana sattāvāse dvidhā nānakkhaṇikakammūpanissayapaccayehi pavatte pavattikkhaṇe paṭisandhiyaṃ paṭisandhikkhaṇe so apuññābhisaṅkhāro paccayo hoti.

582-3. The demeritorious volitional formation in the sense-sphere becomes a condition in the sense-sphere existence; in the wombs beginning with the egg-born, by way of the egg-born, womb-born, moisture-born, and spontaneously born; in the three destinations, by way of the hell, ghost, and animal destinations; in one station of consciousness, by way of beings with diverse bodies and unified perception; and in one abode of beings, by way of beings with diverse bodies and unified perception. That demeritorious volitional formation becomes a condition in two ways by the different-moment kamma-decisive-support conditions: during the course of existence, at the moment of continuity, and at rebirth-linking, at the moment of rebirth-linking.

584-6. Tathevāneñjasaṅkhāro [V 1.0081] tathā eva āneñjasaṅkhāro, ekārūpabhave ekasmiṃ arūpabhave ekissā opapātikayoniyā ceva ekissā devagatiyāpi ca ākāsānañcāyatanabhūmi viññāṇañcāyatanabhūmi ākiñcaññāyatanabhūmivasena tīsu eva cittaṭṭhitīsu catunnaṃ arūpabhūmīnaṃ vasena catubbidhe sattāvāse catunnaṃ arūpapākacittānaṃ dvedhā [M 0.0099] nānakkhaṇikakammopanissayapaccayehi so āneñjābhisaṅkhāro paccayo hoti. Paṭisandhipavattīnaṃ, vasenevaṃ bhavādīsu evaṃ iminā mayā vuttappakārena paṭisandhipavattīnaṃ vasena bhavādīsu yathā ye saṅkhārā esaṃ pākacittānaṃ paccayā honti, tathā te saṅkhārā evaṃ iminā mayā vuttappakārena paṇḍitena vijānitabbā.

584-6. Similarly, the imperturbable volitional formation, in one formless existence, in one spontaneous birth, and also in one divine destination; by way of the base of the sphere of infinite space, the base of the sphere of infinite consciousness, and the base of the sphere of nothingness, in the three stations of consciousness; by way of the four formless planes, in the fourfold abodes of beings; for the four formless resultant consciousnesses, that imperturbable volitional formation becomes a condition in two ways through the different-moment kamma-decisive-support conditions. Thus, by way of rebirth-linking and continuity, in existences and so on, in the manner I have explained, as certain volitional formations are conditions for these resultant consciousnesses, so should those volitional formations be understood by the wise in the manner I have explained.

587-90. Na rūpārūpadhammānaṃ, saṅkanti pana vijjati rūpadhammānaṃ, cittacetasikasaṅkhātānaṃ nāmadhammānañca saṅkanti pana saṅkamanaṃ pana na vijjati. Saṅkantibhāve asati atītabhavato idha imasmiṃ bhave rūpadhammānaṃ saṅkamanabhāve asati paṭisandhicittaṃ kathaṃ kena pakārena siyā bhaveyya? Natthi cittassa saṅkanti, atītabhavato idha imasmiṃ bhave cittassa saṅkanti saṅkamanaṃ natthi, tato atītabhavato atītaṃ hetuṃ vinā vajjetvā idha imasmiṃ bhave cittassa pātubhāvo na vijjati. Suladdhapaccayaṃ rūpārūpamattaṃ suṭṭhu laddhapaccayaṃ rūpanāmamattaṃ jāyati. Evaṃ iminā mayā vuttappakārena paccayaṃ labhitvā uppajjamānaṃ rūpārūpamattaṃ rūpanāmamattaṃ jāyati. Evaṃ iminā mayā vuttappakārena paccayaṃ labhitvā uppajjamānaṃ rūpārūpamattaṃ bhavantaraṃ aññabhavaṃ paṭisandhiṃ upeti upagacchati. Iti vacanaṃ samaññāya lokiyavohārena pavuccate, satto vā natthi, satto jīvoti vevacanaṃ, attā vāpi na vijjati.

587-90. There is no transition of material and immaterial phenomena. Indeed, there is no transition or movement of material phenomena, nor of mental phenomena, which are designated as consciousness and mental factors. In the absence of transition, there being no movement of material phenomena from a past existence to this existence here, how, in what way, could rebirth-linking consciousness arise? There is no transition of consciousness; from a past existence to this existence here, there is no transition or movement of consciousness. Therefore, without a past cause from a past existence, the manifestation of consciousness here in this existence does not occur. Mere materiality and mentality, having well-obtained their conditions, are born. Thus, in the manner I have explained, having obtained the conditions, the arising mere materiality and mentality are born. Thus, in the manner I have explained, having obtained the conditions, the arising mere materiality and mentality reaches another existence, another becoming, and attains rebirth-linking. This statement is spoken by convention, by worldly usage: there is no being—'being' is a synonym for 'living soul'—nor is any self to be found.

591-9. Tassidaṃ pākaṭaṃ katvā, paṭisandhikkamaṃ pana tassa sattassa idaṃ paṭisandhikkamaṃ sudubbudhaṃ atidubbijānaṃ pākaṭaṃ katvā ahaṃ dassayissāmi, tametaṃ paṭisandhikkamaṃ sādhu sādhukaṃ nibodhatha, sādhu sādhukaṃ manasi karotha, vividhesu ārammaṇesu lobhavasena cittaṃ anāmetvā vajiramañjūsāya anagghamaṇiratanaṃ pakkhipanto viya citte ṭhapetvāti attho. Atītasmiṃ bhave tassa, āsannamaraṇassa hiito [M 0.0100] bhavato atītasmiṃ bhave āsannamaraṇassa tassa sarīrasmiṃ ātape pakkhittaṃ haritaṃ tālapaṇṇaṃ viya sussamāne sati cakkhundriyādike indriye naṭṭhe hadayavatthumattasmiṃ ṭhite kāyappasādike viññāṇe tasmiṃ khaṇe vatthusannissitaṃ hadayavatthunissitaṃ. “Citta”nti vacanaṃ bhavaṅgamanodvārāvajjanajavanaṃ sandhāya vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Pubbānusevitanti [V 1.0082] ito kālā pubbakāle tena pana anusevitaṃ anuciṇṇaṃ puññaṃ kammaṃ vā apuññaṃ eva vā kammaṃ kammanimittaṃ gatinimittaṃ vā kammaphalena dvāresu paccupaṭṭhitaṃ ālambitvā manodvārāvajjanajavanavasena sevitacittaṃ pavattati. Evaṃ iminā mayā vuttappakārena pavattamānaṃ taṃ viññāṇaṃ taṃ javanacittaṃ laddhapaccayaṃ laddhārammaṇapaccayaṃ. Avijjāya paṭicchannādīnave visayeti akusalajavane javite tassa javanassa avijjāya appaṭicchannadose tasmiṃ kammādike ārammaṇe kusalajavane javite tato cittavīthito pubbabhāge pavattāya avijjāya paṭicchannadose tasmiṃ kammādike ārammaṇe. Taṇhāti akusalajavanena sahajo lobho, akusalajavane vā javite tato vīthicittato pubbabhāge pavatto lobho taṇhā. Nametīti aññaṃ ārammaṇaṃ aggāhāpetvā daḷhaggāhavasena taṃ eva kammanimittagatinimittasaṅkhātaṃ ārammaṇaṃ gaṇhāpetīti attho. Sahajā saṅkhārā pana tassa cittassa sahajā ekato jātā cetanā pana tasmiṃ yevārammaṇe khipanti pavattanti. Imasmiṃ paccuppannabhave ekasantativasā pavattāya taṇhāya namīyamānaṃ taṃ viññāṇaṃ orimā tīramhā rajjukaṃ ālambitvā mātikātikkamo puriso viya etaṃ purimaṃ nissayabhūtaṃ hadayavatthuṃ jahati chaḍḍeti, cuticittaṃ uppajjitvā nirujjhatīti attho. Aparaṃ kammasambhūtaṃ nissayaṃ aparaṃ aññakammato sambhūtaṃ nissayabhūtaṃ hadayavatthuṃ labhitvā vā alabhitvāpi vā ārammaṇādīhi [M 0.0101] paccayehi taṃ paṭisandhisaṅkhātaṃ mānasaṃ pavattati. “Labhitvā”ti vacanaṃ kāmarūpabhavaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. “Alabhitvā”ti vacanaṃ arūpabhavaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Ettha etesu cittesu purimaṃ “jahatī”ti vacanena vuttañceva cittaṃ, cuticittaṃ pacchimaṃ “ārammaṇādīhi paccayehi pavattatī”ti vacanena vuttañceva cittaṃ paṭisandhicittaṃ paṇḍitena veditabbaṃ.

591-9. Having made this clear, I will now reveal the process of rebirth-linking for that being—a process extremely difficult to comprehend and to know. Understand this process of rebirth-linking well, take it to heart well. The meaning is: just as one places a priceless gem into a jeweled casket, so too should you establish this in the mind, without letting it incline toward various objects due to greed. In a past existence, for that being nearing death, as the body dries up like a green palm leaf placed in the sun, when the faculties such as the eye-faculty have ceased and only the heart-base remains, at that moment consciousness dependent on a physical base, dependent on the heart-base, arises. It should be understood that the word 'mind' (citta) is said with reference to the life-continuum, mind-door adverting, and impulsion. 'Previously practiced' means that in a time prior to this, the mind that was practiced by him continues by way of mind-door adverting and impulsion, taking as its object a meritorious or demeritorious kamma, a kamma-sign, or a destiny-sign, presented at the doors by the result of kamma. Thus, proceeding in the manner I have explained, that consciousness, that impulsion-mind, has obtained its condition, has obtained its object-condition. Regarding 'in an object whose faults are concealed by ignorance': when an unwholesome impulsion has arisen, it is in relation to a kamma-object whose fault is not concealed by the ignorance of that impulsion; when a wholesome impulsion has arisen, it is in relation to a kamma-object whose fault is concealed by ignorance that occurred in the preceding part of the thought-process. Craving (taṇhā) is the greed that is co-nascent with unwholesome impulsion, or it is the greed that occurred in the preceding part of the thought-process when an unwholesome impulsion arose. 'It inclines' means that, not allowing it to grasp another object, it causes it to grasp that very object known as the kamma-sign or destiny-sign, by way of a firm grasp. The co-nascent formations are the volitions born together with that mind, which propel it in that very object. In this present existence, that consciousness, being inclined by craving that proceeds in a single continuity, abandons this former support, the heart-base, like a man crossing a watercourse by holding onto a rope from the near bank. The meaning is that the death-consciousness arises and ceases. Then, having obtained another kamma-produced support—another heart-base produced from other kamma—or even without having obtained it, that mind, called rebirth-linking, proceeds by means of its object and other conditions. The word 'having obtained' is said with reference to the sense-sphere and form-sphere existences. The word 'without having obtained' is said with reference to the formless existence. Here, among these minds, the wise should understand that the former mind, spoken of by the word 'abandons,' is the death-consciousness, and the latter mind, spoken of by the phrase 'proceeds by means of its object and other conditions,' is the rebirth-linking consciousness.

600-6. Tadetaṃ taṃ etaṃ paṭisandhicittaṃ purimā bhavato idha imasmiṃ pacchimabhave nāpi āgataṃ, kammādiñca hetuṃ vinā vajjetvā paṭisandhicittaṃ pātubhūtaṃ na ceva taṃ ettha etasmiṃ vacane etassa paṭisandhicittassa purimā bhavato idha imasmiṃ paccuppannabhave anāgamane atītabhavahetūhi atītabhave kammādipaccayehi etassa paṭisandhicittassa sambhave. Paṭighosadīpamuddādī, bhavantettha nidassanā ettha etasmiṃ tassa paṭisandhicittassa atītabhavato anāgamane atītabhave hetūhi sambhave paṭighosadīpamuddādiatthanidassanā upamā bhavanti. Aññatra aññasmiṃ paṭighosādīnaṃ atthānaṃ pavattiṭṭhāne āgantvā saddādihetukā saddādayo paccayā honti yathā. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – imasmiṃ ṭhāne janehi pavattāpitā saddadīpamuddādayo atthā [V 1.0083] pabbatantarādīsu aññesu ṭhānesu pavattānaṃ paṭighosadīpamuddādīnaṃ atthānaṃ hetukā honti. Tesu saddādīsu paccayesu santesu ye te paṭighosādayo honti, asantesu na honti yathā, evameva ca viññāṇaṃ atītabhavato paccuppannabhavaviññāṇavasena pavattaṃ viññāṇaṃ vibhāvinā veditabbaṃ. Santānabandhato santānabandhavasena ekatā atītabhavapaccuppannabhavaviññāṇavasena pavattassa viññāṇassa ekībhāvo natthi, nānatāpi tassa viññāṇassa nānābhāvopi paccekabhāvo api. Sati santānabandhe tu, ekantenekatā siyā santānabandhe sati ekantena tassa [M 0.0102] viññāṇassa ekatā ekībhāvo siyā bhaveyya, khīrasabhāvato paggharaṇasabhāvato khīrato sambhūtaṃ ghanasabhāvaṃ kadācipi kismiñcipi kāle na bhaveyya, sabbadā paggharaṇasabhāvakhīrameva bhaveyyāti attho. Athāpi aparo nayopi sā ekantanānatā tassa viññāṇassa so ekantanānābhāvo yadi bhaveyya, khīrasāmiko so puggalo dadhisāmi na bhaveyya. Khīrakāle khīrassa issarabhūto sāmiko paggharaṇasabhāvaṃ jahitvā dadhissa uppajjamānakāle tassa dadhissa issaro na bhaveyya, tato khīrasāmiko añño puggalo tassa dadhissa anissaro asāmiko bhaveyyāti attho. Yasmā kāraṇā ettha etasmiṃ paṭisandhikkamavinicchaye ekantaekatāpi vā ekantanānatāpi vā samayaññunā viññunā na ceva upagantabbā.

600-6. That very rebirth-linking consciousness has not come here from the previous existence to this present existence. Nor has the rebirth-linking consciousness appeared without a cause such as kamma. And here, in this statement, the arising of this rebirth-linking consciousness in this present existence is not due to its coming here from the previous existence; rather, it arises due to causes from the past existence, such as kamma. Examples like an echo, a lamp, or a seal are given here as illustrations. In this context, the examples of an echo, a lamp, or a seal serve to show that the arising of this rebirth-linking consciousness is due to causes from the past existence, even though it has not come here from that past existence. Just as sounds and other phenomena arise elsewhere due to causes like sound, so too, here, the sounds, lights, seals, and the like initiated by people in this place become the causes for the echoes, lights, and seals produced in other places, such as in a distant mountain range. When those conditions like sound are present, those echoes and lights occur; when they are absent, they do not. In the same way, consciousness should be understood by one who discerns it as consciousness that proceeds from a past existence by way of a present-existence consciousness. From the perspective of the continuity of the stream, there is neither absolute oneness nor absolute difference in the consciousness that arises in the past and present existences. If there were absolute oneness due to the continuity of the stream, then that consciousness would have absolute unity, just as milk, by its fluid nature, would never become solid at any time but would always remain milk. And if there were absolute difference in that consciousness, then the owner of the milk would not be the owner of the curd. At the time of the milk, the owner is the lord of the milk, but when, having abandoned its fluid nature, it becomes curd, he would no longer be its lord. The meaning is that the owner of the milk, being a different person, would then not be the lord or owner of that curd. For this reason, in this analysis of the process of rebirth-linking, neither absolute oneness nor absolute difference should be accepted by a wise person who understands the doctrine.

607-10. Evaṃ iminā mayā vuttappakārena asaṅkantipātubhāve saṅkantipātubhāvarahite bhave sati imasmiṃ manussattabhāve khandhādisamatā abhisambhūtā ye khandhā honti, etesaṃ idha imasmiṃ manussattabhāve niruddhattā idha imasmiṃ manussattabhāve janehi katassa tassa kammassa phalahetuno phalassa paccayabhūtassa parattha parasmiṃ loke āgamato ceva evaṃ aññassa sattassa aññato kammato hi tato sattato aññena sattena katato aññato ceva kammato taṃ phalaṃ siyā bhaveyya, “aññassa sattassā”ti vacanena titthiyasattassapi kammaṃ aññassa ca phalaṃ dadeyyāti attho, tasmā kāraṇā etaṃ sabbaṃ eva ca tumhehi vuttavidhānaṃ na sundaraṃ. Etthāhāti etasmiṃ ṭhāne ṭhatvā codako āha – nanu evaṃ “asaṅkantipātubhāve bhave satī”tiādikaṃ vacanaṃ niyatīti? Vuccate – santāne yaṃ phalaṃ etaṃ ekasmiṃ [M 0.0103] santāne pavattamānaṃ yaṃ etaṃ phalaṃ aññassa sattassa na hoti, aññato kammato na ca hoti, bījānaṃ abhisaṅkhāro etassatthassa “ekasmiṃ santāne”tiādikassa etassa atthassa sādhako nipphādako hoti.

607-10. Thus, in this way, when existence is without transference and manifestation, and when the aggregates and so forth have reached equilibrium in this human state, then because of the cessation of these aggregates here in this human state, and because the result of that kamma done by people here—which is the causal condition for the result—would come to another world, it would follow that the result from one being's action would come to be for another being, due to a different action from another being. The statement 'for another being' means that even the action of a sectarian could give a result to another. Therefore, for this reason, all that has been stated by you is not sound. Here, the objector, standing in this position, says: 'Surely, the statement “when existence is without transference and manifestation,” and so forth, is deterministic?' It is replied: The result that is in a continuum does not belong to another being, nor does it arise from another's action. The conditioning of seeds is what proves and establishes this meaning of 'in one continuum,' and so forth.

611-5. Ekasmiṃ [V 1.0084] pana santāne, vattamānaṃ phalaṃ pana aññassa sattassāpi vā na hoti, taṃ phalaṃ aññato kammato na hoti. Bījānaṃ abhisaṅkhāro etassatthassa “ekasmiṃ pana santāne”tiādikassa etassa atthassa sādhako nipphādako hoti, bījānaṃ abhisaṅkhāre madhuādinā vatthunā janehi kate tassa bījassa santāne paṭhamaṃ laddhapaccayo paṭhamaṃ laddhamadhuādipaccayo tassa bījassa phalaṃ kālantare madhuādinā bījābhisaṅkharaṇato aññasmiṃ kāle madhuro hoti. Hi saccaṃ “bījānaṃ abhisaṅkhāre”tiādikaṃ vacanaṃ. Tāni hi tāni eva paṭhamaṃ madhuādinā janehi ropitāni bījāni abhisaṅkharaṇato kālantare madhurabhāvaṃ phalampi vā phalaṭṭhaṃ vā na pāpuṇanti. Evaṃ iminā pakārena idaṃ mayā vuttaṃ “ekasmiṃ pana santāne”tiādikaṃ vacanaṃ paṇḍitena ñeyyaṃ. Api ca aparo nayo. Bālakāle taruṇakāle tena taruṇena payuttena vijjāsipposadhādinā kammenāpi tassa vuddhakālasmiṃ phaladānasīlena ayaṃ “ekasmiṃ pana santāne”tiādiko attho paṇḍitena dīpetabbo.

611-5. However, the result occurring in one continuum does not belong to another being, nor does that result arise from another’s action. The conditioning of seeds proves and establishes the meaning of 'in one continuum,' and so forth. When people condition seeds with substances like honey, the fruit of that seed, having first received that condition in the seed's continuum—having first received the condition of honey and so forth—becomes sweet at a later time due to this conditioning. Indeed, the statement 'the conditioning of seeds,' and so forth, is true. For those very seeds, first planted by people with honey and so forth, do not attain sweetness in their fruit or the state of bearing fruit at a later time without such conditioning. In this way, this statement I have made, 'in one continuum,' and so forth, should be understood by the wise. Moreover, there is another method. By the nature of kamma performed by a young person in their youth—with knowledge, skill, medicine, and so forth—to give its fruit in their old age, this meaning of 'in one continuum,' and so forth, should be elucidated by the wise.

616-20. Codako punāha – evaṃ santepi taṃ kammaṃ evaṃ iminā mayā vuttappakārena kamme santepi saṃvijjamānepi taṃ kammaṃ etasmiṃyeva khaṇe vijjamānampi vā phalassa paccayo hoti. Atha vāvijjamānakaṃ paccayo na bhaveyya. Etasmiṃyeva khaṇe avijjamānakaṃ kammaṃ vā phalassa paccayo hoti. Sace yadi vijjamānaṃ phalassa paccayo hoti, tappavattikkhaṇe pana [M 0.0104] tassa kammassa pavattikkhaṇe tassa kammassa vijjamānakāle pana hetunā kammeneva saddhiṃ pākena bhavitabbaṃ. Atha vā aparo nayo. Vijjamānaṃ niruddhaṃ kammaṃ vipākassa paccayo yadi bhaveyya, pavattikkhaṇato tassa kammassa pavattikkhaṇato pubbe vā kāle, tassa kammassa pavattikkhaṇato pacchā vā avijjamānakāleti attho. Niccaphalaṃ siyāti sabbadā kammapaccayavirahitaṃ phalaṃ siyāti attho. Ācariyena vuccate – “lobhaṃ, bhikkhave, pajahatha, sotāpattipaṭilābhāya ahameva pāṭibhogo”tiādīsu pāṭhesu pāṭibhogo viya kammaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Sotāpattiphalaṃ viya kammato sambhūtaṃ phalaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Kaṭattāyeva janehi kaṭattāyeva taṃ kammaṃ phalassa paccayo hoti, assa vijjamānattaṃ na ca hoti, tassa avijjamānassa kammassa vijjamānatā vā na ca neva hoti.

616-20. The questioner said further: 'Even so, with kamma being as I have described, does that kamma, while existing at that very moment, become a condition for the fruit? Or would a non-existent one not be a condition? Or does a kamma that is non-existent at that very moment become a condition for the fruit? If an existing kamma is a condition for the fruit, then at the moment of its occurrence, at the time that kamma exists, the result must be present together with the cause, the kamma itself. Or, another way: if a ceased kamma were a condition for the result—meaning at a time before its occurrence or after its occurrence, when it is non-existent—then the fruit would be permanent, meaning the fruit would exist always, without the condition of kamma.' The teacher replies: In passages such as, 'Monks, abandon greed; I myself am the guarantor for the attainment of stream-entry,' kamma should be seen as the guarantor. The fruit that arises from kamma should be seen as the attainment of stream-entry. Simply because it has been done, that kamma becomes a condition for the fruit. Its existence is not present, nor is there any existence for that kamma which is non-existent.

621. Abhidhammāvatāroyaṃ abhidhammāvatāro ayaṃ paramatthappakāsano bhūtatthadīpano sotūnaṃ puggalānaṃ [V 1.0085] pītibuddhivivaḍḍhano paṇḍitehi vividhesu ārammaṇesu cittaṃ anāmetvā sakkaccena manasikārena sotabbo.

621. This is the Abhidhammāvatāra, this Abhidhammāvatāra, which reveals the ultimate truth, illuminates the true meaning, and increases the joy and wisdom of its listeners. It should be listened to by the wise with careful attention, without diverting their minds to various objects.

Iti abhidhammāvatāraṭīkāya

Here ends the Sub-commentary on the Abhidhammāvatāra.

Puññavipākapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the exposition of the condition of meritorious result is completed.

Navamo paricchedo.

The Ninth Chapter.

10. Dasamo paricchedo

10. The Tenth Chapter.

Rūpavibhāgavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Analysis of Form.

622. Vuttamādimhi yaṃ rūpaṃ, cittajānamanantaraṃ yaṃ rūpaṃ cittacetasikānaṃ anantaraṃ ādimhi pakaraṇādimhi “cittaṃ cetasikaṃ [M 0.0105] rūpa”ntiādinā vacanena ācariyena vuttaṃ, ito paraṃ idāni tassa rūpassa vibhāvanaṃ samāsena saṅkhepena karissaṃ.

622. That form which was mentioned at the beginning—that is, the form immediately following mind-born phenomena, the form immediately following mind and mental factors—was stated by the teacher at the beginning of the treatise with the words, 'mind, mental factors, form,' and so on. Hereafter, I will now provide a brief and concise explanation of that form.

623. Yaṃ ruppatīti rūpanti yaṃ dhammajātaṃ ruppati sītādinā viruddhapaccayena vikāramāpajjati. Tathā rūpayatīti rūpaṃ yaṃ dhammajātaṃ vaṇṇavikāramāpajjamānaṃ hadayaṅgatabhāvaṃ ajjhāsayaṃ pakāseti, iti tasmā rūpaṃ, kiṃ taṃ? Vaṇṇāyatanaṃ. Rūpārūpabhavātīto, surūpo rūpamabrvi bhagavā rūpārūpabhavaatīto surūpo rūpaṃ abrvi kathesi.

623. 'It is afflicted,' thus it is form—whatever phenomenon is afflicted, undergoing alteration due to opposing conditions such as cold. Likewise, 'it manifests,' thus it is form—whatever phenomenon, while undergoing a change of appearance, reveals its state and underlying disposition. Therefore, it is form. What is that? The sense-sphere of forms. The Blessed One, of beautiful form and gone beyond the form and formless existences, declared form.

625-6. Mahābhūtenāti mahanto bhūto uppatti etassāti mahābhūto, tena. Vañcakattā mahābhūtasamāti vā.

625-6. By 'the great element' is meant: it has a great and manifest arising, thus it is a 'great element'; by that. Or, because of its deceptiveness, it is like a great element.

630. Nirupādānamānasoti upādānavirahitacitto.

630. 'Having a mind without fuel' means having a mind devoid of clinging.

633. Tassa [V 1.0086] sampattīti tassa kiccassa sampatti.

633. 'His accomplishment' means the accomplishment of that task.

634. Upabrūhanarasāti vaḍḍhanakiccā.

634. 'Having the function of augmenting' means having the task of increasing.

637. Āsayānusaye ñāṇanti ettha āsayo nāma

637. Regarding 'knowledge of inclinations and latent tendencies,' herein 'inclination' means:

Sassatucchedadiṭṭhī ca, khantī saccānulomikaṃ;

Yathābhūtañca yaṃ ñāṇaṃ, etaṃ āsayasadditaṃ.

The views of eternalism and annihilationism, patience that is in conformity with the truth, and that knowledge of things as they have come to be—this is termed 'inclination'.

Atthīti kho, kaccāna, ayameko anto, anto kho, kaccāna, atthi iti ayaṃ eko anto koṭṭhāso, ayaṃ sassatadiṭṭhi. Natthīti kho, kaccāna, ayaṃ dutiyo anto, ayaṃ ucchedadiṭṭhi. Khantī saccānulomikanti catunnaṃ saccānaṃ anulomikañāṇaṃ, saṅkhārupekkhāñāṇanti attho. Yathābhūtañca yaṃ ñāṇanti sappaccayanāmarūpadassanaṃ ñāṇaṃ. Etaṃ āsayasadditanti [M 0.0106] etaṃ āsayaṃ iti kathitaṃ. Evaṃ vuttappakārena āsaye ñāṇaṃ nāma. Anusayo nāma diṭṭhānusayādayo anusayā satta. Indriyānaṃ paropareti pare adhikabhāvena opare ca tikkhānubhāvena ayaṃ satto tikkhasaddhindriyo mudusaddhindriyo hīnasaddhindriyoti attho. Samādhindriyādīsupi eseva nayo. Iti sattānaṃ indriyānaṃ paraopare ñāṇaṃ.

'It exists,' Kaccāna, this is one extreme. 'It exists,' Kaccāna, this is one extreme, one part; this is the eternalist view. 'It does not exist,' Kaccāna, this is the second extreme; this is the annihilationist view. 'Patience in conformity with the truth' means knowledge that conforms to the four truths; the meaning is the knowledge of equanimity towards formations. 'And that knowledge of things as they have come to be' means the knowledge that sees name-and-form with its conditions. 'This is termed inclination' means this is called inclination. In this way, it is named knowledge of inclination. 'Latent tendency' refers to the seven latent tendencies, beginning with the latent tendency of views. 'The superiority and inferiority of the faculties' means that by their varying degrees of sharpness one knows: 'This being has a sharp faith faculty, a dull faith faculty, or an inferior faith faculty.' The same method applies to the faculty of concentration and the others. Thus, it is knowledge of the superiority and inferiority of the faculties of beings.

638. Sabbaññutā ñāṇanti tihetukakāmāvacarakriyācatukkaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

638. 'The knowledge of omniscience' should be understood as the fourfold functional sense-sphere consciousness rooted in three causes.

641. Akkhikūṭehi matthaluṅgena paricchinno antato.

641. Bounded within by the eye sockets and the brain.

645. Bhāvasambhavasaṇṭhānāti itthipumasambhavabhūtavaṇṇāyatanaṃ.

645. The characteristic of the arising of sex is the visual-object base that is the basis for the arising of female and male.

647. Ete dasa catusamuṭṭhānā sambhārā catūhi paccayehi cattālīsa bhavanti.

647. These ten constituents, arising from four sources, become forty through four conditions.

652. Niviṭṭheti patiṭṭhite.

652. `Niviṭṭhe` means established.

658. Ubbiadhikānaṃ [V 1.0087] pathavīadhikānaṃ.

658. `Ubbiadhikānaṃ` means for whom the earth element is pre-eminent.

660-2. Visese satīti nissayabhūtānaṃ catunnaṃ visese sati, sabbaso sabbesaṃ visesaparikappanaṃ pahāya eva kammavisesena pasādānaṃ visesatā ñeyyā.

When there is a distinction means: when there is a distinction in the four which are the basis. Having completely abandoned all conceptualization of distinction for everything, the distinctiveness of the sensitive faculties should be understood to be solely due to the distinction in kamma.

663. Saddīyatīti uccārīyate. Rasantīti assādenti.

663. `Saddīyati` means it is uttered. `Rasanti` means they savor.

668. Paratoti paṭhamakappato aparabhāge paṭisandhiyaṃ bhāvadvayaṃ samuṭṭhātīti viññeyyaṃ. “Pavattepi samuṭṭhāyā”tiādikaṃ soṇakumārādayo sandhāya vuttaṃ.

668. `Parato` means: in the part subsequent to the first aeon, it should be understood that the two sexes arise at rebirth-linking. The phrase beginning with, 'Also arises in the course of existence,' was spoken with reference to Soṇa Kumāra and others.

672. Na taṃ byañjanakāraṇanti taṃ indriyadvayaṃ byañjanassa kāraṇaṃ na siyā. Tassāti byañjanassa.

672. `Na taṃ byañjanakāraṇan` means: that pair of faculties would not be the cause of the sign. `Tassā` means: of the sign.

674. Ubbāhananti [M 0.0107] nīharaṇaṃ.

674. `Ubbāhanaṃ` means taking out.

676-7. Annapānādikaṃ vatthu yaṃ kammajaṃ aggiṃ harati, kevalaṃ ekaṃ hutvā taṃ annapānādikaṃ vatthu jīvitaṃ pana pāletuṃ na ca sakkoti. Ekato jīvitaṃ pāletuñca sakkonti.

The matter of food and drink, etc., carries the kamma-born heat. That matter of food and drink, etc., being merely single, cannot, however, sustain life. Together, they can sustain life.

Kāyena rūpakāyena attano bhāvaṃ viññāpentānaṃ bhāvo kāyaggahaṇānusārena kāyaggahaṇassa anucintanena gahitāya vāyodhātuvikārasaṅkhātāya etāya dhammajātiyā paṇḍitehi viññāyate. Itipi tasmā kāyaviññatti.

The state of those who make known their own state by means of the body—the material body—is understood by the wise through this kind of phenomenon, which is reckoned as an alteration of the wind element and is grasped in accordance with the grasping of the body or by reflecting upon the grasping of the body. For this reason, it is also bodily intimation.

681. Ekāvajjanavīthiyaṃ heṭṭhā chahi cittehi vāyodhātusamuṭṭhitaṃ upatthambhaṃ labhitvā.

681. In a single advertence process, having obtained support arisen from the wind element generated by the six preceding consciousnesses.

684. Saha saddena vāti saddena saheva.

684. It blows with sound, that is, together with sound.

690-1. Etāsaṃ pana lahutādīnaṃ tissannaṃ pavattiyaṃ nidassanaṃ kamato ārogyaṃ lahutā[V 1.0088], madditaṃ dhammaṃ mudutā, dhantahemaṃ kammaññatā hoti. Lahutādittayaṃ pana kammaṃ kātuṃ na sakkoti, āhārādittayaṃyeva lahutādittayaṃ karoti yasmā, tato taṃ tijaṃ nāma.

Now, as an illustration of the occurrence of these three—lightness, etc.—in order: health is lightness, softened matter is softness, and refined gold is workability. However, the triad of lightness, etc., cannot perform an action; since it is the triad of nutriment, etc., that produces the triad of lightness, etc., it is therefore called 'born of three sources'.

693. Vuttamākāranānattāti ettha ākāranānattā nāma ācayākāraanubandhatākāravasena vuttaṃ. Veneyyānaṃ vasena vāti eke veneyyā ācayavasena jātirūpaṃ jānanti, eke anubandhatāvasena jānanti. Iti veneyyānaṃ jānanavasena jātirūpaṃ dvidhā vuttaṃ.

693. `Vuttamākāranānattā` means: here, the diversity of modes is spoken of in terms of the mode of accumulation and the mode of continuity. Or, `veneyyānaṃ vasena` means: some trainees understand arising-form in terms of accumulation, while others understand it in terms of continuity. Thus, arising-form is spoken of in two ways according to the understanding of the trainees.

694. Sabhāvānapagame attano sabhāvassa anapagame sati.

694. `Sabhāvānapagame` means: when there is no departure from one's own nature.

Te [M 0.0108] middharūpavādācariyā paṭikkhipitabbā. Kathaṃ? Addhā munisi sambuddho, natthi nīvaraṇā tavāti yo tvaṃ addhā ekantena muni asi sambuddho asi nīvaraṇā dhammā tava tuyhaṃ natthi, iti vacane sace middhaṃ nīvaraṇaṃ rūpe paviṭṭhaṃ siyā. Bhagavatā rūpakāyassa vijjamānattā “natthi nīvaraṇā tavā”ti vacanaṃ vattabbaṃ siyā. Thinamiddhanīvaraṇaṃ avijjānīvaraṇena saha nīvaraṇañceva hoti, nīvaraṇasampayuttañca hoti. Iti sampayuttavacanato sampayuttassa rūpassa abhāvato tampi na vattabbaṃ siyā. Na purejātapaccayāti aññamaññapaccayāti attho. Sace thinamiddhaṃ rūpaṃ siyā, kathaṃ arūpepi aññamaññaṃ siyā, na siyāti attho. Arūpepi kāmacchandanīvaraṇaṃ paṭicca thinamiddhanīvaraṇaṃ uppajjati. Iti vacanena ca na middharūpaṃ siyā, arūpe kathaṃ siyāti attho. Arūpameva middhaṃ iti paṭikkhipitabbā. Arūpepi etassa middhassa uppattiyā sādhakavacanato niṭṭhaṃ ettha ca avagantabbaṃ “arūpa”nti viññunā.

Those teachers who hold the view that torpor is material should be rejected. How? In the statement, 'Surely you are a sage, a fully enlightened one; there are no hindrances for you,' if torpor, a hindrance, were included in material form, then because the Blessed One's material body exists, the statement 'there are no hindrances for you' could not be said. The hindrance of sloth and torpor, along with the hindrance of ignorance, is both a hindrance and is associated with hindrances. Thus, because of the statement about association, and because there is no associated material form, that also should not be said. 'Not by way of pre-nascent condition' means 'by way of mutual condition.' If sloth and torpor were material, how could there be mutuality even in the immaterial? There could not be, is the meaning. Even in the immaterial, the hindrance of sloth and torpor arises in dependence on the hindrance of sensual desire. And by this statement, torpor could not be material; how could it be in the immaterial, is the meaning. It should be rejected that torpor is material; torpor is indeed immaterial. And because of the statement establishing the arising of this torpor even in the immaterial, the conclusion here should be understood by the wise as 'it is immaterial'.

705-6. Kammena vīsati rūpāti aṭṭhindriyavatthuaṭṭhāvinibbhogasantatūpacayākāsā kammajā. Cetasā viññattidvayasaddalahutādittayaavinibbhogasantatūpacayākāsā cittajā. Utunā saddalahutādittayaavinibbhogasantatūpacayākāsā utujā. Āhārato lahutādittayaavinibbhogasantatūpacayākāsā āhārajā.

The twenty material phenomena produced by kamma are: the eight faculties, the heart-base, the eight inseparable phenomena, continuity, growth, and space are kamma-born. Those produced by consciousness are: the two intimations, sound, the triad of lightness, etc., the eight inseparable phenomena, continuity, growth, and space are consciousness-born. Those produced by temperature are: sound, the triad of lightness, etc., the eight inseparable phenomena, continuity, growth, and space are temperature-born. Those produced by nutriment are: the triad of lightness, etc., the eight inseparable phenomena, continuity, growth, and space are nutriment-born.

707-17. Jāyeyyuṃ yadi tānipīti tāni jaratāaniccatārūpā yadi jāyeyyuṃ, evaṃ sante tu tesaṃ jaratāaniccatā bhedā siyuṃ. Hi saccaṃ vacanaṃ pāko na paccati, bhedo vā na [V 1.0089] ca bhijjati yasmā, tasmā tesaṃ pākabhedā siyunti, taṃ vacanaṃ natthi. Etaṃ jaratāaniccatādvayaṃ jātassa nipphannarūpassa pākabhedattā na jāyati. Siyā kassaci buddhetthāti ettha jaratāaniccatāvinicchayādhikāre kassaci janassa buddhi ñāṇaṃ yadi siyā, “rūpassūpacayo”ti vacanena “jāti [M 0.0109] jāyatī”ti vacanaṃ dīpitaṃ yathā, evaṃ tathā pākopi paccatu, bhedopi paribhijjatu, evaṃ buddhi siyā. Jāti na ceva jāyate. Iti iminā pakārena vibhāvinā ñeyyā. Jāti jāyamānassa nipphannarūpassa nibbatti nāma pakāsitā. Tattha yassa siyā tattha vacane yassa janassa buddhi siyā. Yesaṃ nipphannarūpadhammānaṃ jāti atthi, sā jāti abhinibbattisammutiṃ tappaccayattavohāraṃ tesaṃ nipphannarūpadhammānaṃ paccayaṭṭhena laddhavohāraṃ kammajādikaṃ vohāraṃ labhateva yathā, tathā tesaṃ nipphannarūpadhammānaṃ te pākabhedā abhinibbattisammutiṃ nāma tappaccayattavohāraṃ labhanti, iti buddhi siyā. Tassa janassa evaṃ vattabbaṃ – idaṃ santatūpacayadvayaṃ kammādisambhavaṃ hoti yathā, evaṃ pākabhedā taṃ kammādisambhavavohāraṃ kadācipi na labhanti. Hi saccaṃ vacanaṃ kasmā kāraṇā janakānaṃ kammādipaccayānaṃ ānubhāvasaṅkhāte khaṇuppāde tesaṃ pākabhedānaṃ abhāvato na labhanti. Vuttappakārena khaṇuppāde jātiparamparābhāvato sā jāti labbhate, tasmā kāraṇā jāti eva abhinibbattisammutiṃ paccayattavohāraṃ labhati, itaraṃ jaratāaniccatādvayaṃ pana na labhati. Taṃ jaratāaniccatādvayaṃ jiyyati iti bhijjati iti vā na vattabbaṃ hoti. Kasmā? Kammādipaccayānaṃ ānubhāvakkhaṇe tassa jaratāaniccatādvayassa paccayānaṃ abhāvato.

If those also were to arise means: if those material phenomena of aging and impermanence were to arise, then their aging and impermanence would be further disintegrations. Indeed, since ripening does not ripen and disintegration does not disintegrate, the statement, 'therefore their ripening and disintegration would occur,' is not found. This pair, aging and impermanence, does not arise, for it is the ripening and disintegration of an already arisen, produced material phenomenon. If someone here were to have the idea: 'Just as the statement "birth arises" is clarified by the statement "the accumulation of matter," so too let ripening ripen and let disintegration disintegrate'—such might be their idea. Birth itself does not undergo arising. Thus it should be known by one who discerns. Birth is declared to be the production of a produced material phenomenon that is in the process of arising. Therein, if someone were to have the idea: 'Just as for those produced material phenomena that have birth, that birth obtains the conventional designation of origination and the convention of being dependent on its conditions, so too for those produced material phenomena, their ripening and disintegration obtain the conventional designation of origination and dependence on conditions'—such might be their idea. To that person it should be said: Just as this pair, continuity and accumulation, arises from kamma and other causes, ripening and disintegration never obtain that conventional usage of 'arising from kamma, etc.' Indeed, why? Because at the moment of arising, which is reckoned as the power of the generating conditions such as kamma, those ripening and disintegration are absent. In the manner described, at the moment of arising, that birth is obtained because there is no succession of births. Therefore, only birth obtains the conventional designation of origination and dependence on conditions, but the other pair, aging and impermanence, does not. That pair, aging and impermanence, should not be said to 'age' or 'disintegrate.' Why? Because at the moment of the power of the conditions like kamma, the conditions for that pair, aging and impermanence, are absent.

718-23. Aniccaṃ saṅkhatañcetaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ aniccasaṅkhātaṃ itipi vacanassa bhagavatā vuttattā jaratāaniccatādvayaṃ jāyati, evaṃ iti tvaṃ ce maññasi, evaṃ “jāyati evā”ti vacanaṃ bhagavatā na vattabbaṃ. Hi kasmā kāraṇā? “Aniccaṃ saṅkhatañcetaṃ, jarāmaraṇamiccapī”tivuttabhāvādinā ākāradesanāpariyāyena lesena bhagavatā aniccānaṃ nipphannarūpadhammānaṃ jarāmaraṇasaṅkhātaṃ sabhāvato jarāmaraṇaṃ aniccaṃ saṅkhatañcāpi [M 0.0110] cittajānaṃ vikārattā viññattiyo “cittajā”ti vuttā viya, tathā evaṃ bhagavatā vuttaṃ. Yadi evaṃ atthe sati etaṃ ruppanalakkhaṇattayaṃ ajātattā ca sabbathā sabbākārena khaṃpupphaṃva natthi, asaṅkhataṃ nibbānaṃ viya niccaṃvāti ca codako vadeyya, natthi niccanti idaṃ ubhayavacanaṃ no bhagavatā vattabbaṃ. Kasmā? Nissayadhammānaṃ āyattabhāvena pavattito pathaviyādīnaṃ nissayānaṃ bhāve sati tassa lakkhaṇattayassa bhāvato, tasmā khaṃpupphaṃva taṃ lakkhaṇattayaṃ na natthi, atthīti attho. Pathavīādīnaṃ [V 1.0090] abhāve taṃ lakkhaṇattayaṃ na ca labbhati yasmā, tasmā nibbānaṃ viya, tathā niccaṃ na.

718-23. If you think that because the Blessed One said, 'This aging and death is impermanent and conditioned, reckoned as impermanent,' the pair of aging and impermanence arises, then the Blessed One should not have said, 'it arises indeed.' For what reason? Because the Blessed One, by way of teaching the mode, by implication, stated that for impermanent, produced material phenomena, aging and death, reckoned as such, are by nature impermanent and conditioned—just as intimations are called 'mind-born' because they are modifications of what is born of mind. If, this being the meaning, the questioner were to say that this triad of characteristics of affliction, being unarisen, is entirely nonexistent in every way—like a flower in the sky—and is permanent like the unconditioned Nibbāna, then these two statements, 'it is nonexistent' and 'it is permanent,' should not have been said by the Blessed One. Why? Because it proceeds in dependence upon supporting phenomena; because when supporting phenomena like the earth element and so on exist, this triad of characteristics exists. Therefore, this triad of characteristics is not nonexistent like a flower in the sky; it does exist. This is the meaning. And since this triad of characteristics is not found in the absence of the earth element and so on, therefore, it is not permanent like Nibbāna.

724-5. Paricchedādayo anipphannā. Tesameva ca rūpānaṃ tesameva nipphannarūpadhammānaṃ vikārattā nipphannā ceva saṅkhatā sesavasena vuttānaṃ pabhedakatoti dassanato. Sesaṃ uttānatthameva.

724-5. Boundaries and the like are unproduced. And because they are modifications of those same material phenomena, that is, of those same produced material phenomena, they are both produced and conditioned. It should be said that they serve to differentiate the rest. The remainder is clear in meaning.

767.

767.

Gantuṃ panicche piṭakebhidhamme,

Yo dhammasenāpatinā samattaṃ;

Hitatthinā tena ca bhikkhunāyaṃ,

Sakkacca sammā pana sikkhitabbo.

Whoever wishes to penetrate the Abhidhamma Piṭaka, that which was completed by the General of the Dhamma, that monk, desiring his welfare, should diligently and rightly learn this.

Yo bhikkhu abhidhamme piṭake dhammasenāpatinā samattaṃ sabhāvaṃ gantuṃ pāpuṇituṃ iccheyya, tena ca bhikkhunā hitatthinā sakkaccaṃ ādarena sammā tīraṇacintanasajjhāyanehi ayaṃ abhidhammāvatāro sikkhitabbo.

The monk who wishes to fully understand and attain the complete nature of reality in the Abhidhamma Piṭaka, as set forth by the General of the Dhamma, should, for his own welfare, diligently and with respect learn this Introduction to the Abhidhamma with proper investigation, reflection, and recitation.

Iti abhidhammāvatāraṭīkāya

Thus in the Subcommentary to the Abhidhammāvatāra.

Rūpavibhāgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Analysis of Form is completed.

Dasamo paricchedo.

The Tenth Chapter.

11. Ekādasamo paricchedo

11. The Eleventh Chapter.

Nibbānaniddesavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Exposition of Nibbāna.

769. Bhavābhavaṃ [M 0.0111] vinanatoti khuddakaṃ, mahantaṃ bhavaṃ sibbanato. Sabbūpadhipaṭinissaggoti sabbehi saṅkhārūpadhikilesūpadhikhandhūpadhīhi paṭinissajjanaṃ. Accutirasaṃ acutisampattikaṃ. Nibbānaṃ puṭṭhenāti sugatena nibbānaṃ puṭṭhena sāriputtattherena. Ubhinnaṃ suttānanti dhammasenāpativuttānaṃ [V 1.0091] dvinnaṃ suttānanti attho. Khayassa upanissayattāti khayassa balavakāraṇattā. Puthūnaṃ dhammānaṃ appamattakkhaṇe rāgādikkhayamattaṃ nibbānaṃ bhaveyya. Sabbe bālaputhujjanā samadhigatanibbānā sacchikatanirodhā bhaveyyuṃ. Kiñca bhiyyo kiṃ uttari kāraṇañca atthīti attho. Rāgādīnaṃ saṅkhatattā tesaṃ saṅkhatānaṃ nibbānaṃ saṅkhatalakkhaṇaṃ bhaveyya. Kiṃ panetthāti etesu khaṇesu kiṃ pana khaṇe tvaṃ vadesi. Khīṇesvevāti bhavādīsu khīṇesu eva. Niruttaroti nipphannahāro.

769. `Bhavābhavaṃ vinanato` means the unweaving of small and great existence. `Vāna` is derived from `sibbanato`, the stitching together of great existence. `Sabbūpadhipaṭinissaggo` means the relinquishment of all substrates: the substrate of formations, the substrate of defilements, and the substrate of the aggregates. `Accutirasaṃ` means having the quality of the deathless. `Nibbānaṃ puṭṭhenāti` means by the Venerable Sāriputta, who was asked about Nibbāna by the Sugata. `Ubhinnaṃ suttānanti` means the two suttas spoken by the General of the Dhamma. `Khayassa upanissayattāti` means because it is a strong condition for destruction. If Nibbāna were merely the destruction of lust and so on at a slight moment for various phenomena, then all foolish worldlings would have attained Nibbāna and realized cessation. `Kiñca bhiyyo` means what more, what further reason is there? `Rāgādīnaṃ saṅkhatattā...` means since lust and so on are conditioned, their Nibbāna (i.e., their destruction) would have the characteristic of the conditioned. `Kiṃ panetthāti` means what then here, in these moments, of what moment do you speak? `Khīṇesvevāti` means when existences and so on are exhausted. `Niruttaroti` means one for whom sustenance is finished.

771. Assaddhoti bāhirasaddhāya virahito. Vantāsoti vantā vamitā āsā taṇhā yenāti vantāso.

771. `Assaddho` means devoid of external faith. `Vantāso` means one by whom hope (`āsā`), that is, craving (`taṇhā`), has been vomited (`vantā`) and spewed out (`vamitā`); hence, he is called `vantāso`.

Nissaraṇiyāti nissaraṇe niyuttā. Yadidaṃ nekkhammaṃ yaṃ idaṃ kāmānaṃ etaṃ nissaraṇaṃ nirodho, tassa kiñcibhūtassa saṅkhatassa paṭiccasamuppannadhammajātassa nirodho nissaraṇanti, evaṃ iminā pakārena vuttassa tassa nissaraṇanāmakassa abhāvappattidosato nissaraṇanāmakānaṃ paṭhamajjhānaākāsānañcāyatanānampi abhāvo bhaveyya. Atthi nissaraṇanti atthi nibbānaṃ. Uppādādīnanti uppādaṭṭhitibhaṅgānaṃ. Papañcābhāvatoti taṇhāmānadiṭṭhīnaṃ abhāvato.

`Nissaraṇiya` means that which is directed to liberation. That is, renunciation is the liberation from sensual pleasures, their cessation. The cessation of whatever has come to be, is conditioned, of the nature of dependently arisen phenomena, is called liberation. Thus, due to the fault of the non-existence of that which is called 'liberation' spoken of in this way, there would also be the non-existence of the first jhāna and the base of infinite space, which are also called 'liberation.' There is liberation—there is Nibbāna. 'Of arising, etc.' means of arising, persisting, and dissolving. 'Absence of proliferation' means the absence of craving, conceit, and views.

772. Apalokitanti adassanadhammaṃ.

772. `Apalokita` means having the nature of not being seen.

774. Abyāpajjhanti nidukkhaṃ. Akkharanti akharaṃ.

774. `Abyāpajjha` means without suffering. `Akkhara` means imperishable.

777. Saddhābuddhikaraṃ [M 0.0112] tathāgatamate jinavacane sammohaviddhaṃsanaṃ paññāsambhavaṃ paññākāraṇaṃ sampasādanakaraṃ. Atthabyañjanasālinanti atthabyañjanasāravantaṃ sumadhuraṃ sāraññu jinasāsanasāraññū vimhāpanaṃ accherakaraṃ imaṃ evaṃ vuttappakāraṃ abhidhammāvatāraṃ yo jānāti, so jano gambhīre nipuṇe nipuṇañāṇagocare abhidhammapiṭake padaṃ niṭṭhaṃ uttamasanniṭṭhānaṃ yāti pāpuṇāti.

777. Inspiring faith and wisdom in the teaching of the Tathāgata, the speech of the Victor; a destroyer of delusion, a source of wisdom, a cause of wisdom, a producer of serenity; possessing the essence of meaning and phrasing; sweet and essential; for one who discerns the essence, who understands the essence of the Victor’s teaching, it is astonishing and marvelous. Whoever knows this Introduction to the Abhidhamma, of the kind thus described, that person attains a firm footing, the ultimate conclusion, the highest certainty, in the profound, subtle Abhidhamma Piṭaka, the domain of subtle knowledge.

Iti abhidhammāvatāraṭīkāya

Thus in the Subcommentary to the Abhidhammāvatāra.

Nibbānaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Exposition of Nibbāna is completed.

Ekādasamo paricchedo.

The Eleventh Chapter.

12. Dvādasamo paricchedo

12. The Twelfth Chapter.

Paññattiniddesavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Exposition of Designations.

Saṅkhāyatīti [V 1.0092] saṅkhā, kathīyatīti attho. Kinti kiṃ iti kathīyati. “Aha”nti “mama”nti kathīyati.

`Saṅkhāyatīti saṅkhā` means it is designated, hence it is a designation; the meaning is 'it is spoken.' `Kinti` means 'how is it spoken?' It is spoken of as 'I' and 'mine'.

Tajjāpaññattīti tassa cakkhusotādikassa anurūpavasena jātā paññattīti attho.

`Tajjāpaññatti` means a designation that arises in conformity with that, namely, the eye, ear, and so forth.

Ekassavāti ekassa nāmadhammassa “accho”ti nāmaṃ gahetvā bahūnaṃ nāmadhammānaṃ “accho”ti nāmaṃ gahetvā. Samūhamevāti nāmadhammānaṃ samūhaṃ eva.

`Ekassavā` means taking the name 'bear' for a single mental phenomenon, or taking the name 'bear' for many mental phenomena. `Samūhameva` means simply a group of mental phenomena.

Gahito pubbe saṅketo etenāti gahitapubbasaṅketaṃ. Kiṃ taṃ? Manodvārāvajjanajavanaviññāṇaṃ. Tena gahitāya paññattiyā viññāyati “sattā”ti “kammajā”ti kathīyati.

A convention was previously grasped by this, hence it is called `gahitapubbasaṅketaṃ` (that by which a previous convention was grasped). What is that? The mind-door adverting and impulsion consciousness. By that grasped designation, it is understood as 'beings' and is spoken of as 'kamma-born.'

Itthī [M 0.0113] ca puriso ca itthipurisā, te ādayo yesaṃ te itthipurisādayo, tesaṃ.

`Itthī ca puriso ca` becomes `itthipurisā` (woman and man). Those things of which these are the beginning are `itthipurisādayo` (woman, man, and so on). `Tesaṃ` means 'of those'.

778. Tatiyā koṭīti tatiyo koṭṭhāso.

778. The third category is the third part.

Iti abhidhammāvatāraṭīkāya

Thus in the Subcommentary to the Abhidhammāvatāra.

Paññattiniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Exposition of Designations is completed.

Dvādasamo paricchedo.

The Twelfth Chapter.

13. Terasamo paricchedo

13. The Thirteenth Chapter.

Kārakapaṭivedhavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Penetration of the Agent

Vedakassāti [V 1.0093] sukhadukkhavedakassa. Tadāyattavuttīnanti tesaṃ āyattā paṭibaddhā yesaṃ vipākānaṃ te tadāyattavuttino, tesaṃ. Atra imasmiṃ ṭhāne ācariyena parihāro vuccate. Kutoyaṃ tava tatthānurodhoti tattha tasmiṃ aññassa attakārakassa abhāvepi sattusaṅkhātassa attano bhāvepi ayaṃ tava anurodho anunayo kuto kena kāraṇena idha imasmiṃ asati kattari kusalādīnaṃ atthibhāve kammavirodho kuto kena kāraṇena. Athāpīti aparo nayopi. Kiñcetthāti ettha etissaṃ codanāyaṃ kiñci vattabbaṃ atthi, avasiṭṭhaṃ tāva brūhi, aparisamattā te codanā. Tassāti attano. Kārakavedakattābhāvoti kārakavedakattassa abhāvo siyā.

Vedakassa means of the experiencer of pleasure and pain. "Those dependent on them" means those whose lives are dependent on those results, those whose lives are bound to the results of actions. Here, in this instance, the teacher speaks of a safeguard. "How is this your adherence there?"—in that situation, even in the absence of another doer and with the existence of a self conceived as an entity, how does this adherence, this compliance of yours, come about? "From what cause?"—here, in this case, in the absence of a doer, when wholesome actions and so on exist, how does opposition to kamma arise? "Moreover"—there is another way. "Is there anything further here?"—in regard to this challenge, is there anything further to be said? "Speak the remainder first"—your challenge is incomplete. "Of that one"—of oneself. "The absence of being a doer and an experiencer"—there would be the absence of being a doer and an experiencer.

Atha na bhavatīti attano anāse cetanāpi anāso yadi na bhavati. Paṭiññā hīnāti “cetanāya anañño attā”ti paṭiññā hīnā. Vuttappakāratoti “attano anāse cetanāya nāso na bhavati”iti vuttappakārato[M 0.0114]. Viparītanti “attano anāse cetanāya anāso”iti viparītaggahaṇaṃ siyā. Attā nassatu, cetanā tiṭṭhatu, atha pana evaṃ na bhavatīti attā nassatu, cetanā tiṭṭhatu, evaṃ gahaṇaṃ pana na bhavati. Anaññattapakkhaṃ pariccaja pariccajāhi “cetanāya anañño attā”ti. Paṭiññā hīnā yassa so paṭiññāhīno.

"Then, if it does not occur" means: if, when the self is not destroyed, volition is nevertheless destroyed. "The assertion is undermined" means: the assertion "the self is not other than volition" is undermined. "As stated" means: from the manner stated, "when the self is not destroyed, there is no destruction of volition." "The opposite" means: it would be taking the opposite, thus: "when the self is not destroyed, there is non-destruction of volition." "Let the self perish, let volition remain—but this does not happen" means: let the self perish, let volition remain—such a taking, however, does not occur. Abandon, abandon the position of non-otherness—that "the self is not other than volition." He whose assertion is undermined is one whose assertion is undermined.

Ubhinnaṃ cetanattānaṃ ekadesatā ekadesabhāvo natthi. Evañca satīti evaṃ ubhinnaṃ ekadesassa abhāve sati ko doso iti tvaṃ ce vadeyyāsi. Yaṃ pana tayā vuttaṃ yathā rūparasagandhādīnaṃ ekadese vattamānānampi lakkhaṇato aññattanti yaṃ vacanaṃ pana tayā vuttaṃ, taṃ vacanaṃ ayuttaṃ, nānurūpanti attho. Tava paṭiññā hīnāti “ekadese vattamānānaṃ cetanattānaṃ lakkhaṇato aññatta”nti paṭiññā hīnā.

There is no state of being in the same part, no partial nature, for both volition and self. "And this being so" means: if you were to say, "This being so, since they are not in the same part, what is the fault?" But as for that statement of yours—that "even though forms, tastes, smells, etc., exist in the same part, they are different in characteristic"—that statement of yours is improper and not suitable. "Your assertion is undermined" means: the assertion "volition and self, while existing in the same part, are different in characteristic" is undermined.

Evañca satīti etaṃ cetanāya aññabhāve sati ko doso iti ce bhavaṃ vadeyya. “Acetano [V 1.0094] attā”ti vacanaṃ, pubbe vuttadosatoti “pākāratarupāsāṇatiṇasadiso siyā”ti pubbe vuttadosato.

"And if this is so" means: if you were to say, "What is the fault in this, when there is a state of otherness from volition?" The statement "the self is without volition" is flawed, because of the fault previously stated, that "it would be like a wall, a tree, a rock, or grass."

780. Atthi sattopapātikoti opapātikā sattā atthi.

780. "There are spontaneously born beings" means: there are beings who are born spontaneously.

781. Bhārādānanti bhāraggahaṇaṃ. Bhāranikkhepananti bhāroropanaṃ.

781. "Taking up the burden" means the acceptance of the burden. "Laying down the burden" means the relinquishment of the burden.

783. Ekassa puggalassa aṭṭhisañcayo aṭṭhisamūho ekena kappena pabbatasamo rāsi siyā.

783. The accumulation of bones of a single person, a collection of bones, could in one aeon become a heap equal to a mountain.

785. Bho māra, tvaṃ satto iti paccesi, kaṃ saddahasi, “satto”ti gahaṇaṃ te tava diṭṭhigataṃ, suddhasaṅkhārapuñjo ayaṃ, idha loke satto na upalabbhati.

785. O Māra, you believe "it is a being." Whom do you trust? This taking of 'a being' is your wrong view. This is a heap of pure formations; no being is found here in this world.

787. Yo [M 0.0115] bhikkhu imaṃ ganthaṃ accantaṃ satatampi cinteti, tassa bhikkhuno paramā paññā vepulaṃ vipulabhāvaṃ gacchati.

787. For the monk who constantly and thoroughly contemplates this text, for that monk, supreme wisdom attains to abundance, to a state of profusion.

788. Yo bhikkhu imaṃ abhidhammāvatāraṃ atimatikaraṃ uttamaṃ abhiññāṇakaraṃ vimativināsakaraṃ kaṅkhacchedakaraṃ piyakkaraṃ pemakaraṃ sadā paṭhati, suṇāti, tassa bhikkhuno mati idha sāsane ṭhite vikasati paṭiphullati.

788. The monk who always recites and listens to this Abhidhammāvatāra, which causes one to transcend, is supreme, brings higher knowledge, destroys doubt, cuts off uncertainty, is endearing and beloved—for that monk, wisdom, established in this Teaching, develops and blossoms.

Iti abhidhammāvatāraṭīkāya

Thus in the Abhidhammāvatāra Subcommentary.

Kārakapaṭivedhavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Penetration of the Agent is concluded.

Terasamo paricchedo.

The Thirteenth Chapter.

14. Cuddasamo paricchedo

14. The Fourteenth Chapter.

Rūpāvacarasamādhibhāvanāniddesavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Exposition on the Development of Form-Sphere Concentration

789-93. Hitānayanti [V 1.0095] hitāvahaṃ. Mānasañca sugatanti suṭṭhu pavattamānasañca. Madhurā atthavaṇṇanā etassāti madhuratthavaṇṇanaṃ. Uttaraṃ tu manussānaṃ, dhammato ñāṇadassananti manussānaṃ lokiyadhammato uttaribhūtañāṇadassanalokuttaraṃ. Saṅkassarasamācāreti saṅkāya kaṅkhāya saritabbasamācāre. Acchiddaṃ akkhaṇḍaṃ akammāsaṃ. Atthakāmenāti attano hitakāmena.

789-93. "They bring benefit" means: they are beneficial. "And a mind well-gone" means: a mind that proceeds well. "For which there is a sweet explanation of the meaning" means: having a sweet explanation of the meaning. "But superior to humans, the knowledge and vision according to the Dhamma" means: the supramundane, that is, the knowledge and vision that has surpassed the worldly states of humans. "In conduct to be remembered with doubt" means: in conduct to be remembered with doubt and uncertainty. Unbroken, unimpaired, unspotted. "By one who desires the good" means: by one who desires his own welfare.

797. Duvidhalakkhaṇaṃ cārittavārittalakkhaṇaṃ.

797. It has a twofold characteristic: the characteristic of performance and the characteristic of avoidance.

805. Tesaṃ caritānaṃ vomissakanayā.

805. For those temperaments, by a mixed method.

807. Savaṇṇakasiṇāti nīlapītaodātalohitavaṇṇakasiṇā.

807. "The color kasiṇas" means: the blue, yellow, white, and red color kasiṇas.

808. Taṃ [M 0.0116] ekakaṃ ānāpānaṃ assāsapassāso.

808. That single one, mindfulness of breathing, is the in-breath and the out-breath.

809-10. Maraṇūpasamāyuttā satīti maraṇānussati upasamānussati. Āhāranissitasaññāti āhāre paṭikūlasaññā. Dhātuvavatthānanti catudhātuvavatthānaṃ.

809-10. "Mindfulness connected with death and peace" means: the recollection of death and the recollection of peace. "Perception dependent on nutriment" means: the perception of repulsiveness in nutriment. "Analysis of the elements" means: the analysis of the four elements.

811-2. Anukūlā ime sabba-caritānanti vaṇṇitāti yaṃ kammaṭṭhānaṃ saddhācaritassa anukūlaṃ, tameva paññācaritassa anukūlanti adhippāyo. Idaṃ sabbaṃ pana vacanaṃ ekantavipaccanīkabhāvato ekantapaṭipakkhabhāvato atisappāyato vuttaṃ, iti vibhāvinā ñeyyaṃ.

811-12. "These are suitable for all temperaments"—thus it is praised. The meaning is that the same meditation subject that is suitable for one of a faith temperament is also suitable for one of a wisdom temperament. But all this is said because it is entirely unopposed, entirely without a contrary, and extremely suitable; this should be understood by a discerning person.

835. Vipassanābhavasampatti-sukhānaṃ paccayā siyuṃ vipassanāsampattisukhānaṃ bhavasampattisukhānaṃ paccayā siyuṃ.

835. "They may be conditions for the happiness of the accomplishment of insight and existence" means: they may be conditions for the happiness of the accomplishment of insight and the happiness of the accomplishment of existence.

838. Sammaṭṭhānaṃ [V 1.0096] manobhunoti manobhuhadayo tassa hadayassa sammaṭṭhānaṃ.

838. "The proper support of the mind-born" means: the mind-born is the heart; it is the proper support of that heart.

844. Pattukāmena dhīmatā kasiṇaṃ kattabbaṃ.

844. A wise person desiring attainment should prepare the kasiṇa.

845. Saṃhārimanti ito cito ca haritabbakasiṇaṃ. Tatraṭṭhakanti tasmiṃ ṭhāne ṭhitaṃ ito cito ca anāharitabbaṃ kasiṇaṃ.

845. "Portable" means a kasiṇa that can be carried from here and there. "Fixed" means a kasiṇa that is established in that place and cannot be carried from here and there.

849. Vivaṭṭaṃ pana micchatāti nibbānaṃ icchantena vidatthicaturaṅgulaṃ vaṭṭaṃ kātuṃ taṃ kasiṇaṃ vaṭṭati.

849. "But one who desires the rolling back" means: for one who desires Nibbāna, it is proper to make that kasiṇa a circle with a diameter of a span and four finger-breadths.

851-2. Hatthapāsappamāṇasmiṃ, tamhā kasiṇamaṇḍalāti tato kasiṇamaṇḍalato hatthapāsappamāṇasmiṃ padese vidatthicaturaṅgule ucce. Parimukhaṃ satinti kammaṭṭhānābhimukhaṃ satiṃ.

851-52. "At a distance of an arm’s length from that kasiṇa circle" means: in a place at a distance of an arm’s length from that kasiṇa circle, and a span and four finger-breadths high. "Mindfulness in front" means: mindfulness directed towards the meditation subject.

853-4. Nekkhammanti jhānaṃ. Khemato daṭṭhuṃ disvā ahaṃ imāya paṭipattiyā addhā ekantena pavivekasukhassa nibbānasukhassa bhāgī assaṃ bhaveyyaṃ.

853-54. "Renunciation" means jhāna. "Having seen it as security" means: having seen it thus, one reflects: ‘Through this practice, I will surely and certainly become a partaker of the bliss of seclusion and the bliss of Nibbāna.’

856. So [M 0.0117] kasiṇassa vaṇṇo tena yoginā na pekkhitabbo, kasiṇassa lakkhaṇaṃ na pekkhitabbaṃ ussadassa vasena vaṇṇaṃ amuñcitvā.

856. The color of the kasiṇa should not be attended to by that yogi, nor should its characteristic. While not abandoning the color, one should not attend to it by way of its prominence.

860. Evaṃ iminā vuttappakārena ekaggacetaso ekaggacittassa yogino nimīletvā āvajjantassa yathā yena pakārena kammaṭṭhānaṃ hoti ummīlite kālepi, tathā tena pakārena taṃ kammaṭṭhānaṃ āpāthaṃ yāti ce yadi āgacchati, uggahameva uggahanimittaṃ.

860. Thus, in the way described, if for a yogi of one-pointed mind who is adverting with his eyes closed, the meditation subject comes into focus in just the same way as it does when his eyes are open, then it is the learning sign.

864. Pādānaṃ dhovane papañcaparihāratthaṃ. Ekatalikāti ekatalamattā.

864. The washing of the feet is for the purpose of avoiding proliferation. Single-soled means having just a single sole.

865. Taṃ saṃhārimaṃ kasiṇamādāya.

865. Taking up that portable kasiṇa.

866. Samannāharitabbanti [V 1.0097] kammaṭṭhānaṃ sumanena āharitabbaṃ, manasikātabbanti attho. Takkāhaṭanti vitakkena āhaṭaṃ phusitaṃ kare kareyya.

866. To be brought to mind means the meditation subject should be brought up with a good mind; the meaning is, it should be attended to. Brought by thought means he should make it be brought and contacted by initial thought.

868. Tanti taṃ nimittaṃ.

868. That means that sign.

871-4. Imassāti paṭibhāganimittassa. Purimassāti uggahanimittassa. Ko pana ayaṃ viseso? Thavikā nīharitaṃ ādāsamaṇḍalaṃ majjitaṃ viya. Toyade kāḷameghe setabalākā viya. Tadā taṃ uggahanimittaṃ padāletvāva niggataṃ paṭibhāganimittaṃ. Tato uggahanimittato. Tanti taṃ paṭibhāganimittaṃ. Saṇṭhānavantañca vaṇṇavantañca na ca upaṭṭhākāramattaṃ. Paññajanti paññāya jātaṃ.

871-74. Of this means: of the counterpart sign. Of the former means: of the learning sign. What, then, is this difference? It is like a polished mirror disk taken from its case; like a line of white cranes against a dark rain cloud. Then, having shattered the learning sign, the counterpart sign emerges. From that: from the learning sign. That means: that counterpart sign. It has both form and color and is not a mere appearance. Wisdom-born means: born of wisdom.

877-8. Upacārakkhaṇe tassāti tassa samādhino upacārakkhaṇe. Nīvaraṇappahānena samādhino paṭilābhakkhaṇe pana aṅgānaṃ vitakkādīnaṃ pātubhāvena iti dvīhi ākārehi.

877-78. At its moment of access means: at the moment of access of that concentration. But at the moment of attaining concentration through the abandoning of the hindrances, and through the manifestation of the factors such as initial thought—thus in two ways.

879. Dvinnaṃ [M 0.0118] samādhīnanti upacārappanāsamādhīnaṃ.

879. Of the two concentrations means: of access concentration and absorption concentration.

882. Cakkavattiyagabbhova ratanaṃ viya assa anena sudullabhaṃ.

882. Like a jewel in the womb of the chief consort of a wheel-turning monarch, it is extremely difficult to obtain.

884. Ayanti paṭisandhisanthāro.

884. This means the process of relinking.

891-2. Samataṃ vīriyassevāti vīriyasamabhāvaṃ. Layaṃ līnabhāvaṃ īsakampi yantaṃ gacchantaṃ mānasaṃ āvajjanacittaṃ.

891-92. The balance of energy itself means the state of balanced energy. Sluggishness: the state of being sluggish. The mind that is going, moving even slightly, is the adverting mind.

895-9. Bhavaṅgaṃ pana pacchijja ucchinditvā tadeva pathavīkasiṇaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā yogino manodvāramhi jāyati. Tatoti āvajjanato tatrevārammaṇe tasmiṃ pathavīkasiṇasaṅkhāte ārammaṇe tassa yogino javanāni cattāri vā pañca vā jāyante. Avasāne ekaṃ javanamānasaṃ rūpāvacarikaṃ hoti, tasmiṃ rūpāvacarike vitakkādayo aṅgā. Aññehi aññesaṃ cittānaṃ aññehi vitakkādīhi balavatarā honti. Tāni appanābhāvaṃ appattāni appanācetaso [V 1.0098] parikammopacārato parikammabhāvato parikammānīti vuccante, upacārabhāvato upacārānīti ca vuccante. Tāni javanāni appanāyānulomattā anulomāni eva ca vuccanti. Ettha anulomakesu yaṃ sabbantimaṃ javanaṃ, taṃ gotrabhūti pavuccati.

895-99. But having cut off the life-continuum, having made that same earth kasiṇa the object, it arises in the yogi’s mind-door. From that means: from adverting. In that same object, in the object called the earth kasiṇa, four or five impulsions arise for that yogi. At the end, one impulsion-mind becomes of the fine-material sphere; in that fine-material consciousness, the factors, initial thought and so on, are stronger than those of other minds. Those preceding impulsions, not having reached the state of absorption, are called 'preliminary' from being in a state of preparation for the absorption mind, and they are called 'access' from being in a state of access. Those impulsions are also called 'conformity' because they conform to absorption. Here, among the conformity impulsions, the very last impulsion is called 'change-of-lineage.'

901. Gotrabhu diṭṭhanti gotrabhu nāma uddiṭṭhaṃ.

901. Gotrabhū is seen means: it is designated by the name ‘gotrabhū.’

904-5. Purimehi javanehi yaṃ āsevanaṃ, taṃ balavapaccayaṃ laddhā labhitvā chaṭṭhaṃ javanaṃ, sattamaṃ vā javanaṃ appeti. Iti vacanaṃ pavuccati, ettha vāde godatto nāma ābhidhammiko ācariyo āha. Chinnataṭe mukhaṃ yassa chinnataṭamukho.

904-05. The repetition by the preceding impulsions, having gained a strong condition, brings the sixth or seventh impulsion to absorption. This statement is said. Here, in this debate, the Abhidhamma teacher named Godatta said: He whose mouth is at a broken bank is a `chinnataṭamukho` (one with a mouth at a broken bank).

908. Paccavekkhaṇā [M 0.0119] hetu yassa āvajjanassāti paccavekkhaṇahetukaṃ.

908. `Paccavekkhaṇahetukaṃ` means: the adverting for which reviewing is the cause.

911-2. Kāmacchandassa nānāvisaye paluddhassa. Cetaso ekasmiṃ visaye samādhānena samādhi.

911-12. Of sensual desire, which is ensnared in various objects. Concentration is the placing of the mind on a single object.

915. Sayañca atisantato sukhaṃ avūpasantasabhāvassa uddhaccakukkuccadvayassa paṭipakkhato vuttaṃ.

915. And oneself being extremely peaceful: this refers to happiness, which is spoken of as the opposite of the pair, restlessness and remorse, which have an unpacified nature.

917. Pañcaṅgavippayuttanti pañcanīvaraṇavippayuttaṃ. Pañcaṅgasaṃyutanti vitakkādīhi yuttaṃ.

917. Disassociated from five factors means disassociated from the five hindrances. Associated with five factors means associated with initial thought and so on.

920-1. Vepullanti kammaṭṭhānassa vipulabhāvaṃ. Tañca paṭibhāganimittaṃ upacāraṃ vicāretvā vaḍḍhetuṃ vaṭṭati.

920-21. Abundance means the extensive state of the meditation subject. And it is proper to develop that counterpart sign after investigating the access concentration.

928-31. Pamādayoginoti pamādavasena yogisampannassa kāmasahagatā saññāmanakkārā manasikārā ce caranti, tassa yogino taṃ jhānaṃ hānabhāgiyaṃ hoti. Sati santiṭṭhate tasmiṃ, santā tadanudhammatā tasmiṃ paṭhamajjhāne tadanudhammatā tassa paṭhamajjhānassa anurūpā sati nikanti santā saṃvijjamānā santiṭṭhate santiṭṭhati, taṃ jhānaṃ mandassa yogino ṭhitibhāgiyaṃ hoti, ṭhitiṃ bhajati. Visesabhāgiyaṃ hoti, visesaṃ dutiyādibhāvanaṃ pāpuṇātīti attho. Nibbidāsaṃyutā [V 1.0099] saññā, manakkārāti nibbidāvipassanāsaṃyuttā saññāmanakkārā. Nibbedhabhāgiyanti lokuttarabhāgiyaṃ, lokuttaramaggabhāgiyanti attho.

928-31. Of a negligent yogi means: if for a yogi endowed with attainment, through negligence, perceptions and mental advertings accompanied by sensual pleasure occur, that jhāna of that yogi is conducive to decline. When mindfulness is established in him, and the states conforming to it are present in that first jhāna—that is, when mindfulness conforming to that first jhāna, along with delight, is present and established—then that jhāna of a dull yogi is conducive to stability; it partakes of stability. It is conducive to distinction; the meaning is that it attains the distinction of developing the second jhāna and so on. Perceptions and mental advertings connected with disenchantment means: perceptions and mental advertings connected with disenchantment and insight. Conducive to penetration means: conducive to the supramundane; the meaning is, conducive to the supramundane path.

933. Ayaṃ samāpatti āsannākusalārayo āsannākusalārikā yasmā takkacārānaṃ thūlattā ca, tasmā kāraṇā ayaṃ samāpatti aṅgadubbalā.

933. Because this attainment has unwholesome states as a nearby enemy, and because of the grossness of initial and sustained thought, for that reason this attainment is weak in its factors.

935. Nikantinti taṇhaṃ. Pariyādāyāti sosāpetvā.

935. Delight means craving. Having exhausted means having caused to dry up.

936. Vidhināti [M 0.0120] pubbe vuttavidhinā. Satassāti satisampannassa.

936. By the method means: by the method stated previously. Of the mindful one means: of one endowed with mindfulness.

938. Nimittaṃ tu tadeva cāti tameva paṭhamanimittaṃ “pathavī pathavī”iti evaṃ manasā karontassa.

938. But the sign is just that means: for one who attends with the mind thus, ‘earth, earth,’ it is that very same first sign.

943. Sampasādananti saddhā. Majjhattanti tatramajjhattatā.

943. Confidence means faith. Equanimity means equanimity towards that.

944. Duvaṅgahīnanti vitakkavicārahīnaṃ.

944. Devoid of two factors means devoid of initial and sustained thought.

948. Pīti nāma cetaso cittassa uppilāpanaṃ uppilāpitattaṃ yato yasmā kāraṇā.

948. Rapture, by name, is the floating up and the state of having floated up of the mind, for which reason.

961-2. Āsannapītidosāti pītiyeva dosā. Ettha etasmiṃ tatiyajjhāne yadeva yaṃ eva sukhaṃ iti evaṃ sukhaṃ cetaso ābhogo manasikāro. Evaṃ iminā pakārena sukhassa thūlattā ayaṃ samāpatti aṅgadubbalā hoti.

961-62. The fault of proximity to rapture means: rapture itself is the fault. Here, in this third jhāna, whatever happiness there is, that happiness is the mind’s bending, its advertence. In this way, because of the grossness of happiness, this attainment is weak in its factors.

974-5. Sukhaṃ upekkhāya āsevanaṃ pana na hoti yasmā upekkhāya āsevanaṃ pana na hoti, yasmā upekkhāsahagatāni javanāni javanti, tasmā catutthajjhānaṃ upekkhāsahagataṃ samudīritaṃ.

974-75. However, there is no repetition of happiness by equanimity. Because impulsions accompanied by equanimity run, the fourth jhāna is therefore said to be accompanied by equanimity.

976. Dutiyajjhānaṃ dvidhā dvīhi koṭṭhāsehi ṭhitaṃ.

976. The second jhāna is established in two parts.

979. Ayaṃ [V 1.0100] abhidhammāvatāro sumadhuravarataravacano kaṃ nu janaṃ neva rañjayati, atinisitavisado buddhippacāro yassa so atinisitavisadabuddhippacāro, so tena janena vedanīyo jānitabbo.

979. This Introduction to the Abhidhamma, with its supremely sweet and excellent words—what person would it not delight? It is to be known and understood by one whose intellectual process is exceedingly sharp and clear.

Iti abhidhammāvatāraṭīkāya

Thus in the commentary on the Abhidhammāvatāra:

Rūpāvacarasamādhibhāvanāniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the exposition on the development of form-sphere concentration is concluded.

Cuddasamo paricchedo.

The Fourteenth Chapter.

15. Pannarasamo paricchedo

15. The Fifteenth Chapter.

Arūpāvacarasamādhibhāvanāniddesavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Exposition on the Development of Formless-Sphere Concentration

982-3. Rūpe [M 0.0121] kho vijjamānasminti rūpakāye vijjamāne daṇḍādānādayo daṇḍaggahaṇādayo. Iti rūpe rūpakāye ādīnavaṃ disvā.

982-3. 'When form exists': when the physical body exists, there is the taking up of sticks, etc., the grasping of sticks, etc. Thus: 'having seen the danger in form,' in the physical body.

984. Sūkarābhihatova sāti sūkaraṃ anubandhito sā sunakho viya.

984. 'Like one struck by a pig': like a dog that, though struck by a pig, follows it.

985. Vasīti yogī.

985. 'One with mastery': a yogi.

988-990. Phuṭṭhokāsañca tena tanti tena cittena phuṭṭhaṃ tamokāsaṃ “ananto ākāso”iti ca manasā karonto eva ugghāṭeti. Iti vacanaṃ vuccate, ayamañño nayo, “ākāso” iti manasā karonto taṃ kasiṇaṃ na saṃvelleti.

988-990. 'And the space touched by that': the space touched by that mind. And by mentally attending, 'Space is infinite,' he removes it. This is the phrase that is stated. This is another method: by mentally attending, 'Space,' he does not roll up that kasiṇa.

998. Rūpāvacarajjhānameva paccatthikaṃ rūpāvacarajjhānapaccatthikaṃ.

998. The form-sphere jhāna itself is the adversary; an adversary to the form-sphere jhāna.

1004. Ākāsaphuṭaviññāṇeti [V 1.0101] phuṭameva viññāṇaṃ phuṭaviññāṇaṃ, tasmiṃ ākāsārammaṇe phuṭaviññāṇe.

1004. 'In consciousness touched by space': consciousness that is touched is 'touched-consciousness'; in that touched-consciousness which has space as its object.

1005-6. Ayaṃ ākāso ananto iti evaṃ taṃ ākāsameva pharitvā pavattaṃ viññāṇaṃ viññāṇañca iti vacanaṃ vuccate. Viññāṇaṃ anantaṃ nāma na hoti, anantārammaṇattā “viññāṇaṃ ananta”nti vuccate, taṃ viññāṇaṃ manakkāravasena api anantaṃ paridīpitaṃ.

1005-6. 'And consciousness': this phrase refers to the consciousness that proceeds having pervaded that very space with the thought, 'This space is infinite.'
