Consciousness is not infinite by nature, but because its object is infinite it is called 'infinite consciousness.' That consciousness is also described as infinite by way of the mental attention.

1010. Paṭhamāruppaviññāṇassa abhāvo tassa eva paṭhamāruppassa suññato suññabhāvato.

1010. The absence of the consciousness of the first formless attainment is due to the emptiness, the void nature, of that very first formless attainment.

1013. Sati [M 0.0122] tiṭṭhati bhiyyo balavā sati tiṭṭhati.

1013. Mindfulness is established; a strong mindfulness is established all the more.

1015. Abhāvake natthibhāve.

1015. 'In the absence': in the state of non-existence.

1017-8. Dutiyāruppacakkhunāti cakkhunā dutiyāruppaṃ “natthi natthī”tiādinā ākārena parikammavasena manakkāre. Tassāpagamamattañca tassa paṭhamāruppassa apagamamattañca.

1017-8. 'With the eye of the second formless attainment': in the mental attention, by way of preliminary work, on the second formless attainment with the eye of wisdom, in the mode of 'there is not, there is not,' etc. 'And its mere passing away': and the mere passing away of that first formless attainment.

1029. Yā nāma ayaṃ samāpatti abhāvamattampi gocaraṃ katvā ṭhassati, ayaṃ samāpatti vata ekantena aho santāti padissati.

1029. Whatever attainment will stand having made even mere absence its object, this attainment, indeed, is seen as being utterly peaceful.

1033. Yāya saññāya nevasaññī, nāsaññī ca hoti, kevalaṃ ekantena atha kho sā saññā edisī na hoti.

1033. By whatever perception one becomes one with neither perception nor non-perception, yet that perception is not absolutely and entirely of such a nature.

1035-7. Paṭusaññāya kiccassa neva karaṇato ayaṃ samāpatti “nevasaññā”ti niddiṭṭhāti catutthaāruppato sambhavā pavattā tejodhātu sukhodake dahanakiccaṃ kātuṃ na sakkoti yathā, sā saṅkhāradhammānaṃ avasesattā.

1035-7. Because it does not perform the function of gross perception, this attainment is designated 'neither-perception.' Just as the fire element, having arisen and proceeding from the fourth formless attainment, is unable to perform the function of burning in pleasant water, so it is with this perception because of the residual nature of conditioned phenomena.

1040. Pāsādatalañca [V 1.0102] sāṭikā ca.

1040. And the palace terrace and the robe.

1041. Yo pana bhikkhu imaṃ rūpārūpajjhānasamāpattividhānaṃ sārataraṃ jānāti, so rūpārūpajjhānasamāpattipurekkho sekkho bhavaṃ kāmabhavaṃ abhibhuyya abhibhavitvā rūpārūpaṃ yāti pāpuṇāti.

1041. But whatever bhikkhu knows this method for the form and formless jhāna-attainments to be more essential, that trainee, placing the form and formless jhāna-attainments foremost, having overcome and mastered sensual existence, goes to and arrives at the form and formless realms.

Iti abhidhammāvatāraṭīkāya

Thus in the commentary on the Abhidhammāvatāra:

Arūpāvacarasamādhibhāvanāniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the exposition on the development of formless-sphere concentration is concluded.

Pannarasamo paricchedo.

The Fifteenth Chapter.

16. Soḷasamo paricchedo

16. The Sixteenth Chapter.

Abhiññāniddesavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Exposition on the Higher Knowledges

1045. Satāti [M 0.0123] satisampannena. Anuyoganti vīriyaṃ.

1045. 'By one who is mindful': by one endowed with mindfulness. 'Application': energy.

1047. Yogāvacarabhikkhunā nibbattitāsu abhiññāsu assa yogāvacarassa bhikkhuno samādhibhāvanā niṭṭhaṃ pariyosānaṃ gatā siyā.

1047. When the higher knowledges have been generated by a meditating bhikkhu, for that meditating bhikkhu the development of concentration may be said to have reached its culmination and conclusion.

1050. Danteti dante ṭhite. Acaleti acale ṭhite.

1050. 'Tamed': established in the tamed. 'Unshaken': established in the unshaken.

1052-4. Abhiññāya pādakaṃ kāraṇaṃ abhiññāpādakaṃ yogī sataṃ vāpi sahassaṃ vāpi yadi sace icchati, abhiññāpādakaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajjitvā tato abhiññāpādakajhānato vuṭṭhāya vuṭṭhahitvā “sataṃ homi, sataṃ homi” iti evaṃ kāmāvacaraparikammamānasaṃ katvā abhiññāya pādakaṃ kāraṇabhūtaṃ jhānaṃ punādhiṭṭhāti puna āpajjitvā tato jhānato vuṭṭhāya puna adhiṭṭhāti[V 1.0103], sahādhiṭṭhānena cetasā adhiṭṭhānasaṅkhātena catutthajjhānacittena saha so yogī sataṃ hoti. Iddhividhañāṇaṃ.

1052-4. 'The basis for higher knowledge': a cause that is the basis for higher knowledge. If a yogi wishes for a hundred or a thousand, having attained the jhāna that is the basis for higher knowledge and then emerged from it, he should perform the sense-sphere preliminary mental work, thinking, 'May I become a hundred! May I become a hundred!' Then he should again enter the jhāna that is the cause and basis for higher knowledge, emerge from it, and make a determination. Simultaneous with the determination-consciousness, that is, with the fourth jhāna consciousness called 'determination,' that yogi becomes a hundred. This is the knowledge of the kinds of spiritual power.

1067-8. Eso adhigatābhiñño yogī pādakārammaṇena catutthajjhānassa paṭibhāganimittasaṅkhātena ārammaṇena phuṭṭhe okāse gate pavatte pana sadde suṇāti. Dibbasotañāṇaṃ.

1067-8. This yogi who has attained the higher knowledges hears sounds that arise and occur in the space pervaded by the basic object, namely, the object called the counterpart sign of the fourth jhāna. This is the knowledge of the divine ear.

1069. Parassa cittaṃ pariyati paricchijjatīti cetopariyaṃ, tameva mānasaṃ cetopariyamānasaṃ.

1069. 'It encompasses and defines another's mind,' thus it is 'mind-encompassing' (cetopariya). 'Mind-encompassing mind' (cetopariyamānasaṃ) is that very mind.

1070. Hadayaṃ pana nissāyāti hadayavatthuṃ nissāya pavattamānalohitaṃ, hadayakose pavattaṃ ruhiranti attho.

1070. 'Depending on the heart': this means the blood that flows depending on the heart-basis; the meaning is the blood that flows in the chamber of the heart.

1075. Kāmāvacaracittañcāti [M 0.0124] kāmāvacarasattānaṃ kāmāvacaracittañca. Rūpārūpesu rūpabhavārūpabhavesu sattānaṃ mānasañca. Kiṃ bhūtaṃ? Sarāgādippabhedakaṃ mānasaṃ sabbaṃ cetopariyañāṇaṃ jānāti. Cetopariyañāṇaṃ.

1075. 'And the sense-sphere mind': the sense-sphere mind of sense-sphere beings. 'In the form and formless': the mind of beings in the form and formless existences. Of what kind? The knowledge of encompassing mind knows all mind with its distinctions, such as mind with lust, etc. This is the knowledge of encompassing mind.

1077-82. Nisajjā sabbapacchimāti sabbesaṃ iriyāpathānaṃ pacchā jātā nisajjā bhikkhunā āvajjitabbā. Tato pabhuti tato sabbapacchimato nisajjāto pabhuti taṃ sabbaṃ pacchimanisajjaṃ ādiṃ katvā paṭilomakkamā paṭilomakkamena sabbaṃ attanā kataṃ āvajjitabbaṃ. Asmiṃ bhave yāva yattakaṃ kālaṃ sandhi paṭisandhi hoti, tāva tattakaṃ kālaṃ kataṃ kiriyaṃ tena bhikkhunā āvajjitabbaṃ. Purimasmiṃ bhavepi cutikkhaṇepi nibbattaṃ nāmarūpañca sādhukaṃ āvajjitabbaṃ. Cutikkhaṇe nibbatte tasmiṃ nāmarūpe evaṃ bhikkhunā āvajjitabbe yadā tadeva tameva nāmarūpaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā cutikkhaṇe manodvāre manakkāro manodvārāvajjanacittaṃ uppajjati. Pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇaṃ.

1077-82. 'The final sitting': the sitting that occurred last of all the postures should be adverted to by the bhikkhu. 'From then on': from that final sitting onwards, taking that final sitting as the starting point, everything done by oneself should be adverted to in reverse order. For as long as there is a connection, a rebirth-linking, in this existence, for that long the deeds done should be adverted to by that bhikkhu. In the previous existence too, the name-and-form that arose at the moment of death should be well adverted to. When that name-and-form that arose at the moment of death is being adverted to by the bhikkhu, then, taking that very name-and-form as object, a mental advertence—the mind-door-adverting consciousness—arises at the mind door. This is the knowledge of the recollection of past lives.

1086-96. Abhiññāpādakaṃ kasiṇārammaṇaṃ jhānaṃ abhinīhārakkhamaṃ katvā imesu tīsu kasiṇesu katapuññehi. Tasmā tamitaraṃ vāpīti ālokakasiṇaṃ vā itaraṃ vāpi kasiṇadvayaṃ yathākkamaṃ [V 1.0104] uppādetvā upacārabhūmiyaṃyeva ṭhatvā taṃ ālokakasiṇaṃ ṭhapetabbaṃ. Appanaṃ paṇḍito na uppādeyya, sace uppādeti, taṃ ālokakasiṇaṃ pādakajjhānanissitaṃ pādakajjhānassa ārammaṇaṃ hoti. Vaḍḍhitassa jhānassa antogadhaṃ rūpaṃ tena yoginā passitabbaṃ bhave bhaveyya. Taṃ rūpaṃ passato passantassa tassa yogino parikammassa vāro atikkamati, tāvade tasmiṃyeva khaṇe ālokopi tassa yogino ālokopi khippaṃ antaradhāyati. Tasmiṃ āloke antarahite [M 0.0125] rūpagataṃ rūpaṃ na dissati. Divasampi nisīditvā passato rūpadassanaṃ hoti.

1086-96. By those who have made merit in regard to these three kasiṇas, the jhāna with a kasiṇa as its object, which is the basis for higher knowledge, should be made capable of being directed. Therefore, 'that or another': having generated the light kasiṇa or the other two kasiṇas in sequence and established oneself in the access sphere itself, that light kasiṇa should be maintained. A wise person should not generate absorption. If he does, that light kasiṇa, being dependent on the basic jhāna, becomes the object of the basic jhāna. The form included within the extended jhāna should be seen by that yogi. While that yogi is seeing that form, the time for preliminary work passes, and at that very moment the light quickly disappears for that yogi. When that light has disappeared, the form pertaining to the object is not seen. But for one who sits seeing even for a whole day, the vision of form occurs.

1100-1. Taṃcittasaṃyutanti tena catutthajjhānena yuttaṃ cittaṃ. Anāgataṃsañāṇassa parikammaṃ, yathākammūpagassa ñāṇassa ca parikammaṃ. Dibbacakkhuñāṇaṃ.

1100-1. 'Connected with that mind': the mind connected with that fourth jhāna. This is the preliminary work for the knowledge of the future and for the knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings according to their kamma. This is the knowledge of the divine eye.

1103. Yo bhikkhu idha imasmiṃ sāsane imaṃ pana ganthaṃ suṇāti, citte karoti ca, so bhikkhu anena tarena iminā ganthena taritvā abhidhammamahaṇṇavapāraṃ yāti pāpuṇāti, jānātīti attho.

1103. Whatever bhikkhu here in this Dispensation hears this text and gives it his attention, that bhikkhu, having crossed over by means of this text as a raft, goes to and reaches the far shore of the great ocean of the Abhidhamma. The meaning is: he knows.

Iti abhidhammāvatāraṭīkāya

Thus in the Subcommentary on the Abhidhammāvatāra.

Abhiññāniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the exposition on the higher knowledges is concluded.

Soḷasamo paricchedo.

The Sixteenth Chapter.

17. Sattarasamo paricchedo

17. The Seventeenth Chapter.

Abhiññārammaṇaniddesavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Exposition on the Objects of Direct Knowledge.

1104. Anāgataṃsañāṇañcāti na āgato anāgato, na tāva sampattoti attho, anāgate aṃsā koṭṭhāsā tesaṃ ñāṇaṃ anāgataṃsañāṇaṃ. Yaṃ yaṃ kammaṃ yathākammaṃ, taṃ upagacchati jānātīti yathākammupagaṃ, vipākacetanājānanakañāṇaṃ.

1104. And as to 'the knowledge of the future portions' (anāgataṃsañāṇa): anāgata means 'not come,' that is, not yet arrived. The knowledge of the portions (aṃsā) or parts (koṭṭhāsā) in the future is anāgataṃsañāṇa. 'Knowledge of how beings fare according to their kamma' (yathākammupagaṃ) is so called because it knows how one fares according to whatever kamma one has done; it is the knowledge that knows resultant volitions.

1107-9. Tattha [V 1.0105] tesu ārammaṇattikesu. Cittasannissitaṃ katvāti taṃ kāyaṃ cittaṃ sannissitaṃ karitvā tameva kāyacittacetasikavasena mahaggate cittasmiṃ samāropeti ñāṇaṃ iddhividhañāṇaṃ, tato kāyārammaṇato kāyassa parittattā kāmāvacarattā parittārammaṇaṃ ñāṇaṃ siyā.

1107-9. Herein, among those three kinds of objects. 'Having made it dependent on the mind' means having made that body dependent on the mind, the knowledge of the kinds of psychic power imposes that very body upon the sublime mind by way of body, mind, and mental factors. Then, since the body is its object, and because the body is limited and belongs to the sense sphere, the knowledge would have a limited object.

1110-3. Dissamānena [M 0.0126] kāyena, gantukāmo yadā bhave yo yogī dissamānena kāyena gantukāmo yadā bhaveyya, so yogī tadā cittaṃ kāyasannissitaṃ katvā rūpakāye sannissitaṃ katvā taṃ pādakajjhānacittaṃ kāyavasena kāye āropeti, tadā jhānārammaṇato taṃ ñāṇaṃ mahaggatagocaraṃ hoti, yaṃ ñāṇaṃ yadā anāgatañca dhammajātaṃ, atītañca dhammajātaṃ visayaṃ ārammaṇaṃ karoti, tadā taṃ ñāṇaṃ atītārammaṇaṃ hoti, tadā anāgatārammaṇaṃ ārammaṇakaraṇakāle anāgatagocaraṃ hoti. Dissamānena kāyena tassa bhikkhuno gamane pana sati tassa yogino ñāṇassa gocaro paccuppanno nāma hoti, iti viniddise.

1110-3. When a yogi with a visible body wishes to go—if a yogi with a visible body should wish to go—that yogi then, having made the mind dependent on the body, having made it dependent on the form-body, imposes that mind of the basic jhāna upon the body by way of the body. Then, since the jhāna is its object, that knowledge comes to have a sublime domain. When that knowledge takes the class of past phenomena as its object, it has a past object. When it takes the class of future phenomena as its object, at the time of doing so its domain becomes the future. But when that bhikkhu is actually going with a visible body, the domain of that yogi's knowledge is called the present. Thus it should be explained.

1114. Kāyaṃ cittassa vasena citte āropeti, cittaṃ kāyassa vasena kāye āropeti, iti pariṇāmanakālasmiṃ tassa yogino ñāṇaṃ ajjhattārammaṇaṃ siyā. Sampavattati sattasūti parittamahaggataatītaanāgatapaccuppannaajjhattabahiddhārammaṇasaṅkhātesu sattasu ārammaṇesu sampavattati.

1114. One imposes the body upon the mind by the power of the mind, and one imposes the mind upon the body by the power of the body; thus, at the time of transformation, that yogi's knowledge would have an internal object. 'It proceeds in seven' means it proceeds in the seven objects reckoned as limited, sublime, past, future, present, internal, and external.

1120. Jānane majjhimānanti mahaggatānaṃ jānane.

1120. 'In knowing the middle ones' means in knowing the sublime states.

1122. Etassa cetopariyañāṇassa maggārammaṇatā pariyāyena eva matā ñātā.

1122. That this knowledge of others' minds has the path as its object is to be understood only in a figurative sense.

1126-7. Tattha tikkhaṇasampattaṃ, paccuppannaṃ khaṇādikaṃ.

1126-7. Herein, the present, which is the moment and so on, is endowed with the three moments.

Tattha tesu paccuppannesu yaṃ paccuppannaṃ khaṇādikaṃ tikkhaṇasampattaṃ uppādaṭṭhitibhaṅgakkhaṇasampattaṃ khaṇādikaṃ khaṇāyeva taṃ khaṇāvayavaṃ paccuppannaṃ nāma. Ekadvesantativārapariyāpannanti ekacittadvicittavīthivārapariyāpannaṃ santatipaccuppannaṃ nāma. Paccuppannanti pacchimanti addhāpaccuppannanti attho.

Herein, among those kinds of present, that present which is the moment, etc., endowed with the three moments—that is, endowed with the moments of arising, presence, and dissolution—is just the moment. That constituent moment is called the 'momentary present.' 'Included in the course of one or two continuities' means included in the course of a cognitive process of one or two mind-moments; this is called the 'continuity present.' 'Present means the last' means the 'duration present'.

1131-2. Yena [M 0.0127][V 1.0106] āvajjanacittena dhamme āvajjati, yena cetasā jānāti, tesaṃ dvinnaṃ āvajjanajavanacittānaṃ sahaṭṭhānassa abhāvā taṃ “khaṇādikattayaṃ paccuppanna”ntiādikaṃ “ekassa cittamekena, avassaṃ pana vijjhati”iti pariyosānaṃ vacanaṃ na yujjati. Āvajjanajavanānaṃ nānārammaṇabhāvaṃ pattito āpajjanato ca na yujjati. Aniṭṭhe pana ṭhāne tesaṃ āvajjanajavanānaṃ ekārammaṇabhāve anicchite tasmiṃ ṭhāne na yujjati, aññasmiṃ pana ṭhāne maggavīthiyaṃ āvajjanaparikammajavanānaṃ kasiṇādikaṃ ārammaṇaṃ hoti, gotrabhulokuttaracittānañca nibbānaṃ ārammaṇaṃ hoti, ettha ārammaṇajavanānaṃ ekārammaṇatā anicchatā.

With the adverting mind one adverts to phenomena, and with a consciousness one knows. Since for these two—the adverting and impulsion minds—there is no co-existence, the statement beginning, 'The triad of moments, etc., is the present,' and ending, 'one mind certainly penetrates another,' is not tenable. It is not tenable because the adverting and impulsion minds have come to have different objects and because of their arising. However, in an undesirable instance, it is not tenable when it is not desired for those adverting and impulsion minds to have a single object. But in another instance, in the cognitive process of the path, the object of the adverting, preparation, and impulsion minds is a kasiṇa, etc., while for the change-of-lineage and supramundane minds, the object is Nibbāna. Here, it is not desired that the adverting and impulsion minds have a single object.

1134-41. “Ekabbhavaparicchinnaṃ, paccuppannanti pacchima”nti vatvā puna aññena pariyāyena taṃ paccuppannaṃ dassetuṃ idaṃ addhākhyaṃ addhānāma paccuppannaṃ javanavārato dīpetabbaṃ. Iti vacanaṃ niddiṭṭhaṃ. Yadā iddhimā yogī parassa cittaṃ ñātuṃ āvajjati, tassa āvajjanamano paccuppannakhaṇavhayaṃ paccuppannaṃ manodvārāvajjanacittaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā tena cittena saddhiṃ nirujjhati, tesu niruddhesu tassa yogino cattāri, pañca vā javanāni jāyanti. Etesaṃ catunnaṃ, pañcannaṃ javanānaṃ yaṃ pacchimaṃ cittaṃ iddhicittamudīritaṃ. Iddhicittato sesāni kāmāvacaracittāni. Etesaṃ kāmāvacare iddhijavanānaṃ tadeva ca paracittaṃ ārammaṇaṃ hoti yasmā, tasmā sabbāni tāni javanāni ekārammaṇataṃ yanti, tesaṃ javanānaṃ nānārammaṇatā addhāvasā na bhaveyya, paccuppannārammaṇato tesaṃ javanānaṃ ekārammaṇabhāvepi iddhimānasameva ca parassa cittaṃ jānāti. Itarāni kāmāvacarāni pana cittāni parassa cittaṃ na jānanti. Yathā cakkhudvāre tu viññāṇanti cakkhuviññāṇaṃ rūpaṃ passati, tathā itaraṃ cittaṃ na passati.

Having said: 'Limited to a single existence, the present is the last,' then to show that present moment in another way, this duration-present, so-called, should be explained from the perspective of the impulsion process. Thus the statement has been set forth. When a yogi with psychic power adverts in order to know another's mind, his adverting mind takes as its object the other's present mind-door-adverting consciousness, called the 'present moment,' and ceases together with that mind. When these have ceased, four or five impulsions arise in that yogi. Among these four or five impulsions, the last mind is called the mind of psychic power. The remaining minds are sense-sphere minds. Since for these sense-sphere impulsions of psychic power the object is that very mind of the other person, therefore all those impulsions proceed with a single object. There would be no diversity of objects for those impulsions on account of the duration. Although those impulsions have a single object because the object is present, still it is only the mind of the one with psychic power that knows the other's mind. The other sense-sphere minds, however, do not know the other's mind. Just as at the eye-door, the eye-consciousness sees a form but another mind does not, so too here.

1161. Anāgataṃsañāṇassāti [M 0.0128] anāgataṃsañāṇassa anāgataṃ dhammaṃ agocaraṃ, gocaraṃ na hotiyevāti attho.

1161. 'Of the knowledge of the future portions' means: for the knowledge of the future portions, a future phenomenon is not its domain; that is, it is not its domain at all—this is the meaning.

1169. Vividhatthāni vaṇṇapadāni yasmiṃ so vividhatthavaṇṇapado, taṃ madhuratthamatinīharaṃ uttamaṃ sotujanassa hadayaṃ pītikaraṃ sacetano ko nāma manujo na suṇeyya.

1169. That in which there are words of varied meaning and beautiful syllables, that which conveys the sweet essence of thought, supreme, delighting the hearts of listeners—what mindful person would not listen to it?

Iti abhidhammāvatāraṭīkāya

Thus in the Subcommentary to the Abhidhammāvatāra.

Abhiññārammaṇaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Exposition on the Objects of Direct Knowledge is completed.

Sattarasamo paricchedo.

The Seventeenth Chapter.

18. Aṭṭhārasamo paricchedo

18. The Eighteenth Chapter.

Diṭṭhivisuddhiniddesavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Exposition of the Purification of View.

1175. Yā [V 1.0107] sañjānanamattaṃva, saññā nīlādito panāti sā saññā nīlādivasena sañjānanamattaṃva karoti. Lakkhaṇappaṭivedhanti aniccādilakkhaṇapaṭibujjhanaṃ.

1175. As for the statement, 'Perception is but the mere act of perceiving blue and so forth,' this means that perception merely performs the function of perceiving by way of blue and so forth. 'The penetration of characteristics' means the awakening to characteristics such as impermanence and so on.

1177. Taṃ viññāṇaṃ ussakkitvā uddhaṃ sakkaṃ katvā satte maggaṃ pāpetuṃ na sakkoti.

1177. That consciousness, having striven and made an effort upwards, is unable to lead beings to attain the path.

1178-9. Sabbesaṃ pana dhammānaṃ sabhāvapaṭivedhanaṃ aviparītavasena paṭibujjhanaṃ paññāya lakkhaṇaṃ.

However, the characteristic of wisdom is the penetration of the intrinsic nature of all phenomena, an awakening to them in an undistorted way.

1180. Samādhi āsannakāraṇaṃ etāyāti samādhāsannakāraṇā.

1180. As to the phrase 'having concentration as its proximate cause': this is because concentration is the proximate cause of this wisdom.

1181. Lakkhaṇenekadhāti sabbadhammaṃ paṭibujjhanalakkhaṇena paññāva ekadhā vuttā.

1181. As to the phrase 'onefold by characteristic': wisdom itself is said to be onefold by its characteristic of awakening to all phenomena.

1183. Bhūripaññenāti [M 0.0129] bhūte atthe aviparīte atthe ramatīti bhūri, bhūri paññā etassāti bhūripañño, tena.

1183. As to 'by one with extensive wisdom': 'bhūri' is so-called because one delights in the true meaning, in the undistorted meaning. 'Bhūripañño' is one who has extensive wisdom. 'Tena' means by him.

1186-91. Tīsu atthadhammaniruttīsu ca ñāṇesu atthadhammaniruttīsu jātesu ñāṇesu ca ñāṇaṃ. Yaṃ kiñci paccayuppannaṃ phalaṃ dhammajātaṃ. Bhāsitatthoti pāḷiyā attho. Ete pañca dhammā atthasaññitā atthanāmakā. Phalanibbattako hetūti jananako paccayo. Bhāsitanti pāḷi. Dhammasaññitāti dhammanāmakā. Sabhāvaniruttīti aviparītavohāro. Pariyattīti sikkhanaṃ. Savanādhigamehi pubbayogena pubbe pavattanāya.

Knowledge concerning the three knowledges—of meaning, Dhamma, and language—and the knowledge that arises from them. 'Whatever conditionally arisen fruit' is a kind of phenomenon. 'The meaning of what is spoken' is the meaning of the Pāli text. These five phenomena are designated as 'meaning' and are named 'meaning.' 'The cause that produces the fruit' is the generative condition. 'What is spoken' is the Pāli text. 'Designated as Dhamma' means named 'Dhamma.' 'Natural language' is undistorted expression. 'Learning' is studying. 'Through hearing and attainment': by prior application, because of its previous occurrence.

1192. Bhūmibhūtesūti vipassanāya bhūmibhūtesu.

1192. As to 'in what has become the ground': this means in what has become the ground for insight.

1194. Jananāditoti [V 1.0108] jātiādito bhītena paññā bhāvetabbā.

1194. As to 'from birth and so on': wisdom should be developed by one who is afraid of birth and so on.

1203. Ekāsītiyā cittenāti lokuttaracittavajjitena vipassanābhūmibhūtena ekāsītiyā cittena.

1203. As to 'with eighty-one kinds of consciousness': this means with the eighty-one kinds of consciousness that have become the ground for insight, excluding supramundane consciousness.

1208. Sattasammohaghātatthanti sattoti sammohassa vināsitatthaṃ.

1208. As to 'for the purpose of destroying the delusion of beings': the word 'satta' (being) is used in the sense of destroying delusion.

1211. Nirīhakanti īhavirahitaṃ byāpāravirahitaṃ, dārurajjusamāyoge.

1211. As to 'without striving': this means devoid of longing, devoid of effort, as in the joining of wood and rope.

1215. Ubho bhijjanti paccayāti aññamaññapaccayakāraṇā.

1215. As to 'both break down due to conditions': this is because they are mutually conditioned.

1225. Antadvayanti kāmasukhallikānuyogaattakilamathānuyogadvayaṃ. Bhāvayeti diṭṭhivisuddhiṃ vaḍḍheyya.

1225. As to 'the two extremes': this means the pair of extremes, namely, addiction to sensual pleasures and addiction to self-mortification. As to 'one should develop': this means one should increase the purification of view.

Iti abhidhammāvatāraṭīkāya

Thus in the Subcommentary to the Abhidhammāvatāra.

Diṭṭhivisuddhiniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Exposition of the Purification of View is completed.

Aṭṭhārasamo paricchedo.

The Eighteenth Chapter.

19. Ekūnavīsatimo paricchedo

19. The Nineteenth Chapter.

Kaṅkhāvitaraṇavisuddhiniddesavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Exposition of the Purification by Overcoming Doubt.

1231. Iccevamādibāttiṃsakoṭṭhāsānaṃ [M 0.0130] paccayassa hetupaccaye tāva yogī manasā pariggaṇhāti.

1231. Thus the yogi first mentally comprehends the condition for the thirty-two parts beginning in this way, in terms of the root condition.

1233. Hetvaṅkurassa bījaṃ tu bījaṃ aṅkurassa hetujanakaṃ, pathavādayo aṅkurassa paccayā.

1233. The seed is the cause of the sprout, and the seed is the generative cause of the sprout; the earth element and so on are supporting conditions for the sprout.

1234. Pañca [V 1.0109] dhammāti avijjātaṇhupādānakammāhārā hetupaccayā dhammā.

1234. As to 'the five phenomena': ignorance, craving, clinging, kamma, and nutriment are phenomena that are causal conditions.

1235. Kammaṃ puttassa janako pitā viya nāmarūpassa janakaṃ.

1235. Kamma is the generator of name-and-form, just as a father is the generator of a son.

1238. Paccayāti paccayena.

1238. As to 'paccayā': this means 'by means of a condition.'

1240. Yā sāti yā sā kaṅkhā. Pubbante pubbakoṭṭhāse.

1240. As to 'that which': this means that which is doubt. 'In the past end': this means in the former part.

1241. Sabbathā sabbakoṭṭhāsato anavasesāva tassa yogino sā kaṅkhā pahiyyati nāsīyate.

1241. In every way, from every part, without remainder, that doubt of the yogi is abandoned and destroyed.

1243. Atthasādhikāti kusalapakkhe dānādiatthasādhikā, akusalapakkhe pāṇātipātādiatthasādhikā.

1243. As to 'accomplishing a purpose': on the wholesome side, it accomplishes the purpose of giving and so forth; on the unwholesome side, it accomplishes the purpose of killing living beings and so forth.

Taṃ vipākanti upaghātakakammassa taṃ vipākaṃ uppannaṃ nāma hoti. Evaṃ eko yogī kammavipākavasena nāmarūpassa paccayapariggahaṃ karoti.

As to 'that result': that result of destructive kamma is said to have arisen. Thus a yogi undertakes the comprehension of the conditions for name-and-form by way of kamma and its result.

1246. Hetuphalassa sambandhavasenāti hetuphalasambandhavasena idaṃ nāmarūpaṃ kevalaṃ ekantena pavattati, iti sammā aviparītākārena saṃ anupassati.

1246. As to 'by way of the connection between cause and result': this means that by way of the connection between cause and result this name-and-form proceeds purely and exclusively; thus one rightly and in an undistorted manner thoroughly contemplates it.

1247. Pākappavattito [M 0.0131] uddhaṃ pākapaṭivedakaṃ na passati na jāniyate.

1247. Beyond the occurrence of the result, an experiencer of the result is not seen or known.

1250-1. Appavatti nāma na dissati, upapannaṃ dissati. Titthiyā etamatthaṃ anaññāya ajānitvā asayaṃvasī sattasaññanti “satto”ti saññaṃ gahetvāna sassataucchedadassino aññamaññaṃ virodhino hutvā dvāsaṭṭhidiṭṭhiṃ gaṇhanti.

1250-1. 'Non-occurrence is not seen; what has arisen is seen.' Not understanding this meaning, the sectarians, who are not self-controlled and perceive a being, take up the perception 'a being.' Then, holding views of eternalism and annihilationism and becoming opposed to one another, they adopt the sixty-two views.

1254. Ubhoti ubho kammavipākā aññamaññato suññā. Na ca kammaṃ vinā phalanti kammaṃ vinā phalaṃ na ca hoti.

1254. As to 'both': both kamma and its result are empty of each other. As to 'and no fruit without kamma': this means that without kamma there is no fruit.

1255. Sambhārehīti [V 1.0110] sūriyādisambhārehi.

1255. As to 'with the components': this means with components such as the sun and so on.

1257. Suññaṃ taṃ nāmarūpadhammaṃ.

1257. That phenomenon of name-and-form is empty.

1258. Hetusambhārapaccayāti hetunā ca sambhārapaccayehi ca.

1258. As to 'by the cause-and-component-conditions': this means by the cause and by the component conditions.

Iti abhidhammāvatāraṭīkāya

Thus in the Subcommentary to the Abhidhammāvatāra.

Kaṅkhāvitaraṇavisuddhiniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Exposition of the Purification by Overcoming Doubt is completed.

Ekūnavīsatimo paricchedo.

The Nineteenth Chapter.

20. Vīsatimo paricchedo

20. The Twentieth Chapter.

Maggāmaggañāṇadassanavisuddhiniddesavaṇṇanā

The Description of the Exposition on the Purification of Knowledge and Vision of the Path and Not-Path.

1264. Paccuppannassa dhammassāti paccuppannassa nāmarūpadhammassa.

1264. As to 'of the present phenomenon': this means of the present phenomenon of name-and-form.

1266-8. Uppajjato uppajjantassa nāmarūpadhammassa rāsito nicayato āgamanañca natthi. Disāgamananti disāya gamanaṃ[M 0.0132]. Niruddhassāpi nāmarūpadhammassa ekasmiṃ ṭhāne nicayoti ca natthi.

1266-8. For the name-and-form phenomenon as it arises, there is no coming from a heap or an accumulation. 'Coming from a direction' means going from a direction. And for the name-and-form phenomenon that has ceased, there is no accumulation in any one place.

1270-1. Avijjāsamudayā rūpasamudayo, avijjānirodhā rūpanirodho. Taṇhāsamudayā rūpasamudayo, taṇhānirodhā rūpanirodho. Kammasamudayā rūpasamudayo, kammanirodhā rūpanirodho. Āhāranirodhā rūpanirodho. Dhammeti saṅkhāradhamme.

1270-1. From the arising of ignorance, form arises; with the cessation of ignorance, form ceases. From the arising of craving, form arises; with the cessation of craving, form ceases. From the arising of kamma, form arises; with the cessation of kamma, form ceases. With the cessation of nutriment, form ceases. As to 'phenomena': this means conditioned phenomena.

1280. Sampattapaṭivedhassāti sampattalokuttarasaṅkhātamaggaphalassa sotāpannādipuggalassa. Vippaṭipannassāti paṭipattiyaṃ appaṭipannassa, viruddhavasena paṭipannassa vā.

1280. As to 'of one who has attained penetration': this means of a person, such as a stream-enterer, who has attained the path and fruit designated as supramundane. As to 'of one who has gone astray': this means of one who has not entered upon the practice, or who has entered upon it in a contrary way.

1286. Kāyacittānīti [V 1.0111] kāyāti vedanāsaññāsaṅkhārā. Cittanti viññāṇaṃ.

1286. As to 'body and mind': 'body' means feeling, perception, and volitional formations. As to 'mind': this means consciousness.

1290. Yato yato paccayādito. Yaṃ amataṃ nibbānaṃ vijānataṃ vijānantānaṃ pītipāmojjaṃ, tehi labhitabbaṃ amataṃ, amataṃ viya pītipāmojjaṃ vā.

1290. From whatever cause, and so on. For those who know that which is the deathless, Nibbāna, there is joy and gladness. Or it means: by them the deathless is to be obtained, or joy and gladness like the deathless.

1293. Appatteti attani maggaphalasmiṃ appatte. Pattasaññīti maggaphale ahaṃ patto asmi iti saññito hoti.

1293. As to 'not having attained': this means not having attained the path and fruit in oneself. As to 'one who perceives attainment': this means one has the perception, 'I have attained the path and fruit.'

1297. Sāravedinoti sārajānanasīlā. Tanti taṃ maggāmaggañāṇadassanaṃ. Idaṃ ñāṇaṃ maggāmaggañāṇadassananti maggāmaggañāṇadassanaṃ nāma.

1297. As to 'those who experience the essence': this means those whose nature it is to know the essence. As to 'that': this means that knowledge and vision of the path and not-path. As to 'this knowledge is the knowledge and vision of the path and not-path': this means it is so named.

Iti abhidhammāvatāraṭīkāya

Thus in the Subcommentary to the Abhidhammāvatāra.

Maggāmaggañāṇadassanavisuddhiniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Description of the Exposition on the Purification of Knowledge and Vision of the Path and Not-Path is finished.

Vīsatimo paricchedo.

The Twentieth Chapter.

21. Ekavīsatimo paricchedo

21. The Twenty-First Chapter.

Paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhiniddesavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Exposition on the Purification of Knowledge and Vision of the Path.

1299. Upallesavimuttaṃ [M 0.0133] suvisadaṃ ñāṇanti aṭṭhavidhañāṇaṃ sandhāyāha.

1299. 'Knowledge utterly pure, freed from stain'—this is said in reference to the eight kinds of knowledge.

1302. Saccānulomañāṇanti ayameva pavuccati.

1302. This itself is called 'knowledge in conformity with the truths.'

1306. Ayaṃ sikhāpattā vipassanā eva saccānulomañāṇaṃ nāma pavuccati.

1306. This very insight that has reached its climax is called 'knowledge in conformity with the truths.'

1309. Bhavaṅgānantaraṃ saṅkhāru-pekkhāgatanayenāti bhavaṅgānantaraṃ saṅkhārupekkhāsaṅkhātena ñāṇena katanayena.

1309. 'Immediately after the life-continuum, by the method pertaining to equanimity towards formations' means: by the method accomplished through the knowledge known as equanimity towards formations, immediately after the life-continuum.

1314-6. Bodhipakkhiyadhammānaṃ[V 1.0112], uddhañca anulomatoti uddhaṃ vattamānānaṃ bodhipakkhiyadhammānaṃ anulomato, idaṃ anulomañāṇaṃ vuṭṭhānagāminiyā pariyosānaṃ nāma bhāsitaṃ mahesinā kathitaṃ. Saccānulomañāṇaṃ āhacca uppannā, sabbappakārena gotrabhupariyosānaṃ.

1314-6. 'Of the aids to enlightenment, and in conformity with what is higher': this means in conformity with the aids to enlightenment that are proceeding upwards. This conformity knowledge has been spoken of and declared by the Great Seer to be the culmination of the insight leading to emergence. Having arisen in dependence on the knowledge in conformity with the truths, it culminates in every way in change-of-lineage.

1318. Tatthāti vipassanāya.

1318. 'Therein' means in insight.

Iti abhidhammāvatāraṭīkāya

Thus in the Subcommentary to the Abhidhammāvatāra.

Paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhiniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Exposition on the Purification of Knowledge and Vision of the Path is finished.

Ekavīsatimo paricchedo.

The Twenty-First Chapter.

22. Dvāvīsatimo paricchedo

22. The Twenty-Second Chapter.

Ñāṇadassanavisuddhiniddesavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Exposition on the Purification of Knowledge and Vision.

1319-22. Āvajjanassa hitaṃ āvajjaniyaṃ, taṃ ṭhānaṃ etassāti āvajjaniyaṭhānaṃ, gotrabhūti attho. Taṃ gotrabhucittaṃ [M 0.0134] maggacittassa āvajjaniyaṭhānattā. Paṭipadāñāṇadassanaṃ kudācanaṃ na ca bhajati, tatheva ñāṇadassanavisuddhiṃ kudācanaṃ na bhajateva. Ubhinnaṃ ñāṇānaṃ antarā ekaṃ abbohārikaṃ vohāre niyuttanti vohārikaṃ, na vohārikaṃ abbohārikaṃ. Vipassanāya sotasmiṃ vipassanāya sote patitattā vipassanā nāma voharitabbā. Tato nibbānato.

1319-22. 'Beneficial for adverting' is āvajjaniya. 'That is its state' becomes āvajjaniyaṭhāna, the state for adverting, which means change-of-lineage. This is because that change-of-lineage consciousness is the state of adverting for the path consciousness. The knowledge and vision of the path never partakes of it, just as the purification of knowledge and vision never partakes of it. Between the two knowledges, one is non-conventional. That which is employed in convention is conventional; what is not conventional is non-conventional. Because it has fallen into the stream of insight, it should be designated by the name 'insight.' 'From that' means from Nibbāna.

1325. Sūraṃ tikkhaṃ vipassananti gotrabhucittaṃ sandhāyāha.

1325. 'Heroic, sharp insight'—this is said in reference to the change-of-lineage consciousness.

1326-9. Visaṅkhāranti saṅkhārehi vigataṃ. Paṭhamāvajjanañcevāti paṭhamāvajjanaṃ viya. Paṭhamābhogatāpi cāti paṭhamamanasikārā viya. Maggassa anantarādīhi paccayehi. Tassāti maggassa. Sikhāpattāya tāya vipassanāya muddhamhi matthake. Anāvattanti anivattaṃ.

1326-9. 'The unconditioned' means gone beyond formations. 'And just like the first adverting' means: like the first adverting. 'And also the first turning towards' means: like the first attention. By means of the path's conditions, such as the proximity condition. 'Of that' means: of the path. At the head, at the summit of that insight that has reached its climax. 'Not returning' means: unreturning.

1330-3. Ekena [V 1.0113] āvajjanena ekissāyeva vīthiyā. Anulomagotrabhucetasanti anulomagotrabhucittānaṃ nānārammaṇatā vuttā. Taṃ gotrabhucittaṃ anāvajjanampi maggassa āvajjanaṭṭhāne ṭhatvā. Saññaṃ datvā viyāti “ahaṃ nibbānaṃ ārammaṇaṃ karomi, tvampi tamevārammaṇaṃ karohi” iti saññaṃ datvā viyāti adhippāyo. Saññitanti saññaṃ. Kadācipi anibbiddhapubbaṃ maggo esa eso maggo pubbe anibbiddhapubbo.

1330-3. With one adverting in a single cognitive process. 'Of the conformity and change-of-lineage consciousnesses': by this the diversity of objects for the conformity and change-of-lineage cittas is stated. That change-of-lineage citta, though not itself an adverting, stands in the place of adverting for the path. 'As if giving a sign': the intention is 'as if giving the sign: “I am taking Nibbāna as my object; you too should take that same object.”' 'Signalled' means a sign. This path has never been penetrated before; this path was previously unpenetrated.

1336. Ujjhatīti chindati.

1336. 'It abandons' means it cuts off.

1338. Anekesaṃ ānisaṃsānaṃ dāyakena ādimaggena saṃyuttaṃ. Paṭhamamaggañāṇaṃ.

1338. Connected with the first path, the giver of many benefits. This is the knowledge of the first path.

1341. Ekassāsevanaṃ [M 0.0135] natthi ekassa cittuppādassa āsevanapaccayo natthi, tasmā kāraṇā dve cittuppādā anulomakā. Tehīti cittuppādehi āsevanapaccayaṃ laddhā labhitvā tatiyaṃ cittaṃ gotrabhu hoti.

1341. There is no repetition of a single moment; for a single arising of consciousness there is no repetition condition. For that reason, two arisings of consciousness are conformity moments. 'By them' means: having obtained the repetition condition from those arisings of consciousness, the third citta becomes change-of-lineage.

1345-7. Maggapekkhanahetu yassa āvajjanamanaso, taṃ maggapekkhanahetukaṃ. Tasmiṃ niruddheti tasmiṃ āvajjanacitte niruddhe maggassa paccavekkhaṇasaññitāni satta javanāni paṭipāṭiyā jāyante. Paccavekkhaṇañāṇāni ekūnavīsati honti.

1345-7. Because its adverting mind looks towards the path, it has looking towards the path as its cause. 'When that has ceased' means: when that adverting citta has ceased, seven impulsion moments designated as 'reviewing of the path' arise in sequence. There are nineteen reviewing knowledges.

1351. Tato tadā vipassanāvīthiṃ otarati. Dutiyamaggañāṇaṃ.

1351. Then, at that time, he enters the cognitive process of insight. This is the knowledge of the second path.

1361. Mūlaghātanti mūlaghātanaṃ. Tatiyamaggañāṇaṃ.

1361. 'Destroying the root' means the destruction of the root. This is the knowledge of the third path.

1363. Anāvattisabhāvatoti anivattato. Catutthamaggañāṇaṃ.

1363. 'Because of its nature of non-returning' means because it does not return. This is the knowledge of the fourth path.

Iti abhidhammāvatāraṭīkāya

Thus in the Subcommentary to the Abhidhammāvatāra.

Ñāṇadassanavisuddhiniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Exposition on the Purification of Knowledge and Vision is finished.

Dvāvīsatimo paricchedo.

The Twenty-Second Chapter.

23. Tevīsatimo paricchedo

23. The Twenty-Third Chapter.

Kilesapahānaniddesavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Exposition on the Abandoning of Defilements.

1375. Idha [V 1.0114] pana imasmiṃ panādhikāre kāraṇūpacārena lābhādikāraṇassa vohārena, lābho ādi vatthu yassa anunayassāti lābhādivatthuko, tassa.

1375. Here, however, in this section, by way of causal metaphor and by the designation 'cause of gain, etc.,' the explanation is: that persuasion which has gain, etc., as its object is 'having gain, etc., as its object.' Of that.

Sukhumāti kāmarāgapaṭighā sukhumā.

'Subtle' means that sensual lust and aversion are subtle.

1376. Yena [M 0.0136] yena paṭhamamaggādiñāṇena yo yo saṃyojanādiko pahātabbo dhammo ghātaṃ vināsaṃ yāti, so so dhammo tena tena asesena ñāṇena evaṃ sādhu mayā sandassito.

1376. By whatever knowledge, such as that of the first path, whatever state to be abandoned, such as the fetters, is destroyed and annihilated, that very state has been well shown by me as being thus destroyed by that very knowledge without remainder.

1383. Pariññābhisamayenāti paricchinditvā jānanena. Dukkhaṃ abhisametīti dukkhaṃ paṭivijjhati.

1383. 'By breakthrough with full understanding' means by knowing after having defined it. 'One makes a breakthrough to suffering' means one penetrates suffering.

1394. Yo yogī imaṃ viditvā hitabhāvanaṃ vanaṃ vanetabbaṃ viditvā jānitvā ve ekantena sukhasaṃhitaṃ hitaṃ upeti, cittassa tamaṃ anuttamaṃ hīnaṃ vidhūya vināsetvā aviggahakampadaṃ padaṃ aviggahakaṃ sarīrarahitaṃ padaṃ paṭipajjitabbaṃ ñātabbaṃ padaṃ nibbānaṃ upeti pāpuṇāti ca.

1394. Whatever yogi, having understood this, and having known well that the beneficial should be cultivated and the jungle of defilements abandoned, certainly attains welfare connected with happiness. Having dispelled and destroyed the inferior darkness of the mind, one approaches and attains the unsurpassed state, the state free from conflict and trembling, the bodiless state, the state to be realized and known—Nibbāna.

Iti abhidhammāvatāraṭīkāya

Thus in the Subcommentary to the Abhidhammāvatāra.

Kilesapahānaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the exposition of the abandoning of defilements is concluded.

Tevīsatimo paricchedo.

The Twenty-Third Chapter.

24. Catuvīsatimo paricchedo

24. The Twenty-Fourth Chapter.

Paccayaniddesavaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Exposition of Conditions.

1395. Rūpaṃ [V 1.0115] rūpassāti rūpaṃ rūpassa. Arūpassa nāmassa.

1395. 'Material form for material form' means material form for material form. 'For the immaterial' means for name.

1396. Missakassāti nāmarūpamissakassāti attho.

1396. 'For the mixed' means 'for the mixture of name-and-form.'

1397. Tipañca cāti pannarasa ca.

1397. 'And three times five' means 'and fifteen'.

1399. Ekoti [M 0.0137] kammapaccayo. Dvekālikoti atītapaccuppannakālavasena dvīsu kālesu niyutto. Dassitoti bhagavatā desito.

1399. 'One' means the kamma-condition. 'Relating to two times' means applicable in two times, by way of the past and the present. 'Shown' means taught by the Blessed One.

Iti abhidhammāvatāraṭīkāya

Thus in the Subcommentary to the Abhidhammāvatāra.

Paccayaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the exposition of conditions is concluded.

Catuvīsatimo paricchedo.

The Twenty-Fourth Chapter.

Nigamanakathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Concluding Discourse.

1401. Sumatimativicārabodhanoti sumatīnaṃ sundarapaññānaṃ kavīnaṃ matiyā vicārassa bodhano. Vimativimohavināsanoti vimatīnaṃ bālānaṃ vimohassa vināsano. Kumatimatimahātamonāsoti kumatīnaṃ bālānaṃ mahātamasannibhāya matiyā nāsako. Paṭumatibhāsakaroti paṭūnaṃ paṇḍitānaṃ tikkhapaññāya obhāsakaro.

1401. 'An awakener of the investigation of the minds of the wise' means it awakens the investigation of the mind of the wise, that is, of poets possessing beautiful wisdom. 'A destroyer of the delusion of the perplexed' means it destroys the delusion of the perplexed, that is, of the foolish. 'A dispeller of the great darkness of wrong views' means it is a destroyer of the thought of the foolish, which is like a great darkness. 'An illuminator for the astute' means it illuminates the sharp wisdom of the astute, that is, of the learned.

1402. Sumatināmako bhikkhu asamānato asadisāya pūjāya mama āyācito yato yasmā [V 1.0116] kāraṇā, tato tasmā kāraṇā ayaṃ abhidhammāvatāro. Padāto padāti koṭṭhāsato koṭṭhāsato. Hitavibhāvanā bhāvanāti hitappakāsanāya bhāvanāya mayā racito. Atha vā ahaṃ sumatinā bhikkhunā asamānato mānato āyācito yato yasmā, tato tasmā.

1402. Because the monk named Sumati requested me with unequal and incomparable reverence, for that reason this Abhidhammāvatāra was composed. 'From word to word' means from section to section. 'For the cultivation that reveals benefits' means it was composed by me for the cultivation that illuminates what is beneficial. Or else: because I was requested by the monk Sumati with unequal esteem, for that reason...

1405. Tividhā byappathānañhi gatiyoti byappathānaṃ vacanānaṃ atthaganthayuttivasena tividhā gatiyo.

1405. 'For the courses of expression are threefold' means that the courses of expressions, that is, of words, are threefold by way of meaning, text, and connection.

1406. Nikāyantaraladdhīhīti aññasmiṃ nikāye laddhīhi. Vācanāmagganissitoti vacanappabandhanissito.

1406. 'By the tenets of other schools' means by the tenets in another Nikāya. 'Based on the path of recitation' means based on the textual tradition.

1410. Asaṃkiṇṇakulākuleti [M 0.0138] asammissakulehi ākiṇṇe. Supasannasitodaketi madhurasītodake.

1410. 'Crowded with unmixed families' means crowded with families that are not intermingled. 'With very clear, cool water' means with sweet, cool water.

1411. Saṅkaṭeti sambādhe.

1411. 'In a narrow place' means in a confined space.

1412. Kelāsasikharākārapāsādapaṭimaṇḍiteti rajatapabbatamatthakanibhehi pāsādehi alaṅkate.

1412. 'Adorned with palaces shaped like the peaks of Kelāsa' means adorned with palaces resembling the summits of the silver mountain.

1413. Vividhākāracārupākāragopureti vividhasaṇṭhānamanuññapākāradvārakoṭṭhake.

1413. 'With charming ramparts and gateways of various forms' means having delightful ramparts, gateways, and gate-chambers of diverse shapes.

1414. Sallekhāti sallekhavutti. Sākhalyeti sakhilabhāve. Satāti satisampannena.

1414. 'Austerity' means an austere way of life. 'With friendliness' means in a state of gentleness. 'By a mindful one' means by one endowed with mindfulness.

1415. Vassavalāhakā devāti vassavalāhakabhūtā devā amarā.

1415. 'The rain-cloud devas' means the deathless devas who have become rain-clouds.

Nigamanakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Concluding Discourse is concluded.

Abhidhammāvatārapurāṇaṭīkā niṭṭhitā.

The Old Subcommentary to the Abhidhammāvatāra is concluded.

Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa

Homage to the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One.

Abhidhammāvatāra-abhinavaṭīkā

The New Subcommentary to the Abhidhammāvatāra

(Paṭhamo bhāgo)

(First Part)

Ganthārambhakathā

Introduction to the Text

(Ka) visuddhakaruṇāñāṇaṃ[M 1.0139][V 1.0117], buddhaṃ sambuddhapūjitaṃ;

Dhammaṃ saddhammasambhūtaṃ, vande saṃghaṃ niraṅgaṇaṃ.

(Ka) I pay homage to the Buddha, who possesses pure compassion and knowledge, who is honored by the Perfectly Enlightened Ones; to the Dhamma, born from the true Dhamma; and to the Sangha, which is stainless.

(Kha) sāriputtaṃ mahātheraṃ, pariyattivisāradaṃ;

Namāmi santavuttiṃ me, guruṃ gāravabhājanaṃ.

(Kha) I bow to the great elder Sāriputta, expert in the scriptures, and to my teacher, of peaceful conduct, worthy of reverence.

(Ga) vandantena mayā evaṃ,

Yā laddhā puññasampadā;

Hitvā tassānubhāvena,

Antarāye asesato.

(Ga) By the power of that accomplishment of merit obtained by me thus paying homage, having overcome all obstacles without remainder,

(Gha) mahāvihāravāsīnaṃ[V 1.0118], therānaṃ thirasīlinaṃ;

Vaṃsālaṅkārabhūtena, bhūtānuggahakārinā.

(Gha) By the one who is an ornament to the lineage of the elders of steadfast virtue dwelling in the Mahāvihāra, one who acts for the welfare of beings,

(Ṅa) therena buddhadattena, racitaṃ yaṃ manoramaṃ;

Piṭake abhidhammasmiṃ, otārupāyabhāvato.

(Ṅa) Which delightful [treatise] was composed by the elder Buddhadatta, on account of its being a means of entry into the Abhidhamma Piṭaka,

(Ca) abhidhammāvatāroti, laddhanāmena vissutaṃ;

Nānānipuṇagambhīranayaṃ pakaraṇuttamaṃ.

(Ca) That supreme treatise, renowned by the name it has received, 'Abhidhammāvatāra,' possessing various, subtle, and profound methods,

(Cha) atthasaṃvaṇṇanaṃ tassa, ārabhissaṃ yathābalaṃ;

Pāmojjajananatthāya, ābhidhammikabhikkhunanti.

(Cha) I shall begin its explanation of the meaning according to my ability, for the purpose of generating joy in the monks who are students of Abhidhamma.

Ganthārambhakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Introduction

1. Paramanipuṇavicittanayasamannāgataṃ [M 1.0140] sakasamayasamayantaragahanaviggāhaṇasamatthaṃ suvimalavipulapaññāveyyattiyajananaṃ pakaraṇamidamārabhantoyamācariyo paṭhamaṃ tāva ratanattayappaṇāmakaraṇena antarāyanivāraṇañceva paññāpāṭavañca pattheti. Ratanattayappaṇāmo hi atthato paṇāmakiriyābhinipphādikā kusalacetanā. Sā ca vandaneyyavandakānaṃ khettajjhāsayasampadāhi diṭṭhadhammavedanīyabhūtā yathāladdhasampattinimittakassa kammassa anubalappadānavasena tannibbattitavipākasantatiyā antarāyakarāni upapīḷakaupacchedakakammāni paṭibāhitvā tannidānānaṃ yathādhippetasiddhivibandhakānaṃ rogādiantarāyānamappavattiṃ sādheti, rāgādimalavikkhālanena ca cittasantānaṃ parisodhetvā tannissitāya paññāya yathādhippetasiddhisampādakaṃ tikkhavisadabhāvamāvahati. Kiñci āciṇṇametaṃ paṇḍitānaṃ, yadidaṃ ganthasamārambhe ratanattayappaṇāmakaraṇaṃ, tasmā sappurisācārānurakkhaṇatthañca ādimhi ratanattayavandanā āraddhāti evamādinā aññānipi bahūni payojanāni niddhāretabbāni. Tāni pana tattha tattha bahudhā vitthāritānīti taṃ papañcaparissamaṃ ṭhapetvā yathānuppattameva tāva vaṇṇayissāma.

1. This teacher, in commencing this treatise—which is endowed with extremely subtle and varied methods, capable of grappling with the dense thickets of his own and other doctrines, and a generator of very pure and vast wisdom and competence—first, by making an obeisance to the Triple Gem, seeks both the warding off of obstacles and sharpness of wisdom. For the obeisance to the Triple Gem is, in essence, the wholesome volition that accomplishes the act of paying homage. And that volition, through the excellence of the field of merit and the disposition of those who are worthy of homage and those who pay homage, becomes experienceable in this very life. By giving support to the kamma that is the sign of a fortune already obtained, for the continuity of the result produced by it, it wards off obstructive, oppressive, and destructive kammas that are obstacles to that continuity and thus brings about the non-occurrence of obstacles such as illness that are based on them and that hinder the achievement of the desired goal. And by washing away the stains of lust and so on, it purifies the mental continuum and brings about a sharp and clear state for the wisdom based on it, which accomplishes the achievement of the desired goal. Moreover, it is a custom of the wise to make an obeisance to the Triple Gem at the start of a book. Therefore, it should be inferred that the homage to the Triple Gem was begun at the start also for the sake of preserving the conduct of good people, and that there are many other such purposes. But since these have been explained at length in many places, setting aside that laborious proliferation, we shall for now explain the text just as it occurs in sequence.

Ettha ca ratanattayappaṇāmaṃ kattukāmo tathāgatamūlakattā sesaratanānaṃ paṭhamaṃ tāva tathāgatassa [V 1.0119] thomanāpubbaṅgamaṃ paṇāmamārabhanto āha “anantakaruṇāpañña”ntiādi. Thomanāpubbaṅgamena hi paṇāmena satthu guṇātisayayogo, tato cassa anuttaravandanīyabhāvo, tena ca attano vandanāya khettaṅgatabhāvo, khettaṅgatāya ca vandanāya yathādhippetanipphattiyā hetubhāvo ca dassito hoti.

Here, wishing to pay homage to the Triple Gem, and since the Tathāgata is the root of the remaining gems, he first begins the homage to the Tathāgata, preceded by praise, saying, “of boundless compassion and wisdom,” and so on. For by homage preceded by praise, the Teacher's connection with superior qualities is shown; from that, his state of being supremely worthy of veneration; through that, one's own homage's state of having become a proper field; and through the homage having become a proper field, its being a cause for the accomplishment of the desired aim is also shown.

Tattha [M 1.0141] vanditvāti pubbakālakiriyāniddeso. Tassa pana osānagāthāyaṃ “pavakkhāmī”ti iminā aparakālakiriyāvacanena saha sambandho. Buddhanti vandanakiriyāya kammaniddeso. “Anantakaruṇāpañña”ntiādikaṃ pana tabbisesanaṃ. Tattha kiratīti karuṇā, paradukkhaṃ vikkhipati apanetīti attho. Kirīyati dukkhitesu pasārīyatīti vā karuṇā. Atha vā karotīti karuṇā, paradukkhe sati sādhūnaṃ kampanaṃ hadayakhedaṃ janayatīti attho. Kiṇātīti vā karuṇā, parassa dukkhaṃ paccayavekallakaraṇato hiṃsatīti attho. Pajānātīti paññā, yathāsabhāvaṃ pakārehi paṭivijjhatīti attho. Karuṇā ca paññā ca karuṇāpaññā, natthi etāsaṃ antoti anantā, anantā karuṇāpaññā etassāti anantakaruṇāpañño, taṃ anantakaruṇāpaññaṃ.

There, 'having paid homage' is an indication of a past action. It is connected with the word indicating a future action, 'I will proclaim,' in the concluding verse. 'Buddha' is the indication of the object of the action of homage. But 'of boundless compassion and wisdom,' etc., is its qualifier. There, 'it acts' (kirati), thus it is compassion (karuṇā); the meaning is that it scatters and removes the suffering of others. Or, 'it is spread' (kirīyati) towards those who are suffering, thus it is compassion. Or else, 'it makes' (karoti), thus it is compassion; the meaning is that when others suffer, it generates a trembling, a pain of heart, in good people. Or, 'it injures' (kiṇāti), thus it is compassion; the meaning is that it harms the suffering of another by causing a lack of its supporting conditions. 'It knows' (pajānāti), thus it is wisdom (paññā); the meaning is that it penetrates things in various ways according to their intrinsic nature. Compassion and wisdom are 'compassion-and-wisdom' (karuṇāpaññā). There is no end (anta) to them, thus they are 'endless' (anantā). He for whom compassion and wisdom are endless is 'one of endless compassion and wisdom' (anantakaruṇāpañño). To him, 'the one of endless compassion and wisdom' (anantakaruṇāpaññaṃ).

Ettha ca uppādavayantatāvasena ceva santatipariyosānavasena ca satipi bhagavato karuṇāpaññānaṃ sapariyantabhāve anantārammaṇesu pavattanato anantatā veditabbā. Sammāsambuddhassa hi sabbasattānaṃ dukkhāpanayanākārappavattā anaññasādhāraṇā mahākaruṇā kañci sattaṃ avajjetvā sabbesu sattesu niravasesena pavattati, tathā sabbadhammasabhāvabodhanasamatthā sabbaññutaññāṇasaṅkhātā paññāpi sakalañeyyadhammesu anavasesato pavattati, tasmā anantārammaṇappavattakaruṇāñāṇavantatāya anantakaruṇāpañño bhagavā. Karuṇāpaññāggahaṇena cettha bhagavato sabbalokiyalokuttaraguṇasampatti dassitā hoti. Tathā hi karuṇāggahaṇena lokiyesu mahaggatabhāvappattāsādhāraṇaguṇadīpanato sakalalokiyaguṇasampatti dassitā, paññāggahaṇena sabbaññutaññāṇapadaṭṭhānamaggañāṇadīpanato sabbalokuttaraguṇasampatti dassitāti.

Here, although the Blessed One's compassion and wisdom have a limit in the sense of their arising and passing away and the end of their continuity, their infinity is to be understood from their operating on infinite objects. For the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One's great compassion, which is unique and operates to remove the suffering of all beings, extends to all beings without exception, omitting none. Similarly, his wisdom, called the knowledge of omniscience, which is capable of understanding the true nature of all phenomena, extends to all knowable things without remainder. Therefore, the Blessed One has infinite compassion and wisdom because he possesses compassion and knowledge that operate with infinite objects. And here, by the inclusion of compassion and wisdom, the Blessed One's accomplishment in all worldly and supramundane qualities is shown. For by the inclusion of compassion, which illuminates the extraordinary qualities that have reached the sublime state among worldly things, the entire accomplishment in worldly qualities is shown; and by the inclusion of wisdom, which illuminates the path knowledge that is the proximate cause of the knowledge of omniscience, the entire accomplishment in supramundane qualities is shown.

Apica [M 1.0142] sabbabuddhaguṇānaṃ karuṇā ādi, paññā pariyosānaṃ. Mahākaruṇāsañcoditamānaso hi bhagavā saṃsārapaṅkato sattānaṃ samuddharaṇatthāya katābhinīhāro anupubbena pāramiyo pūretvā anuttarasammāsambodhiyā adhigamena sakalabuddhaguṇe paṭilabhi. Iti [V 1.0120] sakalabuddhaguṇānaṃ tannidānabhāvato karuṇā sabbabuddhaguṇānamādi, sabbaññutaññāṇapadaṭṭhānassa pana maggañāṇassa paṭilabhanato uttarikaraṇīyābhāvato paññā pariyosānaṃ. Ādipariyosānadassanena ca sakalabuddhaguṇā nayato dassitā honti. Nayaggāho eva hi sabbabuddhaguṇānaṃ dassanupāyo, itarathā tādisassa sabbaññubuddhassapi vacanapathātītaṃ tathāgataguṇaṃ anupadaṃ vaṇṇento ko nāma pariyosānamāharituṃ sakkuṇeyyāti.

Moreover, of all the Buddha's qualities, compassion is the beginning and wisdom is the culmination. For the Blessed One, his mind stirred by great compassion, made the aspiration to rescue beings from the mire of saṃsāra. Having gradually fulfilled the perfections, by attaining unsurpassed perfect self-enlightenment he acquired all the Buddha's qualities. Thus, because it is their source, compassion is the beginning of all the Buddha's qualities; and since, with the attainment of the path knowledge—the proximate cause of the knowledge of omniscience—there is nothing further to be done, wisdom is the culmination. By showing the beginning and the end, all the Buddha's qualities are shown by way of a method. For grasping the method is indeed the means to see all the Buddha's qualities; otherwise, who indeed could bring to a conclusion a description of the Tathāgata's qualities, which transcend the range of speech even for such an omniscient Buddha, if one were to describe them quality by quality?

Evaṃ karuṇāpaññāmukhena saṅkhepato sakalabuddhaguṇehi bhagavantaṃ thometvāpi puna attano buddhaguṇasaṃkittane atittābhāvena ceva paresañca pasādabāhullajananatthaṃ tadantogadhepi visiṭṭhaguṇe padhānabhāvena nīharitvā dassento āha “tathāgata”ntiādi. Tattha “tathāgata”nti tathā āgatatādīhi aṭṭhahi kāraṇehi tathāgataṃ. Vuttañhetaṃ (dī. ni. aṭṭha. 1.7; ma. ni. aṭṭha. 1.12; bu. vaṃ. aṭṭha. 1.2 nidānakathā; a. ni. aṭṭha. 1.1.170) –

Having thus briefly praised the Blessed One for all the Buddha's qualities by way of compassion and wisdom, yet still not being satisfied with his own summary of the Buddha's qualities and wishing to generate abundant confidence in others, he draws out as primary even the distinguished qualities included within them and shows them, saying: 'Tathāgata,' etc. Herein, he is the Tathāgata for eight reasons, beginning with 'thus come.' For it has been said:

“Aṭṭhahi kāraṇehi bhagavā tathāgato, tathā āgatoti tathāgato, tathā gatoti tathāgato, tathalakkhaṇaṃ āgatoti tathāgato, tathadhamme yāthāvato abhisambuddhoti tathāgato, tathadassitāya tathāgato, tathavāditāya tathāgato, tathākāritāya tathāgato, abhibhavanaṭṭhena tathāgato”ti.

The Blessed One is the Tathāgata for eight reasons: because he has come thus, because he has gone thus, because he has attained to the true characteristic, because he has perfectly self-enlightened to true phenomena as they really are, because of seeing thus, because of speaking thus, because of doing thus, and in the sense of overcoming.

“Kathaṃ [M 1.0143] bhagavā tathā āgatoti tathāgato? Yathā sabbalokahitāya ussukkamāpannā purimakā sammāsambuddhā āgatā, kiṃ vuttaṃ hoti? Manussattādiaṭṭhaṅgasamannāgatena yena abhinīhārena te bhagavanto āgatā, teneva ca abhinīhārena ayampi bhagavā āgato, yathā ca te bhagavanto samatiṃsa pāramiyo pūretvā pañcamahāpariccāgādīni sampādetvā āgatā, yathā ca te sattatiṃsa bodhipakkhiyadhamme bhāvetvā brūhetvā āgatā, tathā ayampi bhagavā āgatoti evaṃ tāva tathā āgato”ti tathāgato. (1)

How is the Blessed One 'Thus Come' (Tathā Āgata), the Tathāgata? Just as the previous Perfectly Self-Enlightened Ones came, having undertaken the endeavor for the welfare of the entire world—what is meant? With whatever aspiration, endowed with the eight factors beginning with human existence, those Blessed Ones came, with that same aspiration this Blessed One has also come. And just as those Blessed Ones came having fulfilled the thirty perfections and accomplished the five great relinquishments and so on, and just as they came having developed and cultivated the thirty-seven requisites of enlightenment, so too has this Blessed One come. Thus, in this way, he is 'Thus Come,' the Tathāgata. (1)

“Kathaṃ tathā gatoti tathāgato? Yathā sampatijātā te bhagavanto sattapadavītihārena gatā, yathā vā te samathavipassanāmaggehi taṃ taṃ akusalapakkhaṃ vidhamitvā gatā, tathā ayampi bhagavā gato, evaṃ tathā gatoti tathāgato. (2)

How is he 'Thus Gone' (Tathā Gata), the Tathāgata? Just as those Blessed Ones, immediately upon birth, went with a stride of seven steps, or just as they went having demolished the various unwholesome sides by means of the paths of serenity and insight, so too has this Blessed One gone. Thus, he is 'Thus Gone,' the Tathāgata. (2)

“Kathaṃ [V 1.0121] tathalakkhaṇaṃ āgatoti tathāgato? Yasmā tesaṃ tesaṃ dhammānaṃ yaṃ sabhāvasarasalakkhaṇaṃ tathaṃ avitathaṃ, tañcesa tathalakkhaṇaṃ āgato yāthāvato adhigato, tasmā tathalakkhaṇaṃ āgatoti tathāgato gamanatthānaṃ bujjhanatthasambhavato. Tathā hi vadanti ‘ye gatiatthā, te bujjhanatthā. Ye bujjhanatthā, te gatiatthā’ti. (3)

How is he 'One Who Has Come to the True Characteristic' (Tathalakkhaṇam-āgata), the Tathāgata? Because for each and every phenomenon, whatever is its true, unerring characteristic—its own nature and essence—he has come to and realized that true characteristic as it really is. Therefore, he is 'One Who Has Come to the True Characteristic,' the Tathāgata, because the meaning of 'going' can be the meaning of 'awakening.' For it is said: 'Whatever are the meanings of going, they are the meanings of awakening. Whatever are the meanings of awakening, they are the meanings of going.' (3)

“Kathaṃ tathadhamme yāthāvato abhisambuddhoti tathāgato? Yasmā ‘idaṃ dukkhanti, bhikkhave, tathametaṃ avitathameta’ntiādivacanato (saṃ. ni. 5.1090) ‘avijjāya saṅkhārānaṃ [M 1.0144] paccayaṭṭho saṅkhārānaṃ avijjāpaccayasambhūtasamudāgataṭṭho tatho avitatho anaññatho’tiādivacanato ca tathadhammasaṅkhāte saccapaṭiccasamuppāde yāthāvato āgato abhisambuddho, tasmā tathadhamme yāthāvato abhisambuddhoti tathāgato. (4)

How is he 'One Perfectly Self-Enlightened to True Phenomena as They Really Are,' the Tathāgata? Because, based on statements such as, 'Bhikkhus, this is suffering—this is true, this is not untrue,' and on statements such as, 'The conditionality of formations by ignorance... is true, not untrue, not otherwise,' he has perfectly self-enlightened as they really are to the truths and dependent origination, which are designated as true phenomena. Therefore, he is 'One Perfectly Self-Enlightened to True Phenomena as They Really Are,' the Tathāgata. (4)

“Kathaṃ tathadassitāya tathāgato? Yasmā aparimāṇāsu lokadhātūsu aparimāṇānaṃ sattānaṃ chadvāraggahite ārammaṇe aviparītameva passati jānāti, ñatvā ca panevaṃ ‘katamaṃ taṃ rūpāyatanaṃ, yaṃ catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāyā’tiādinā (dha. sa. 616 ādayo) tathamesa aviparītaṃ vibhajati dasseti, tasmā tathaṃ āgacchati passati jānāti, taṃ vā āgamayati dassetīti tathāgatoti evaṃ tathadassitāya tathāgato. (5)

How is he the Tathāgata because of 'seeing thus' (tathadassitā)? Because in immeasurable world-systems, in regard to immeasurable beings, he sees and knows without distortion the object grasped through the six doors. And having known this, he analyzes and shows it truly and without distortion, as in the passage beginning: 'What is that form base which is derived from the four great elements?' Therefore, because he comes to, sees, and knows the truth (tathaṃ), or because he makes it known (āgamayati) and shows it, he is the Tathāgata. Thus he is the Tathāgata because of 'seeing thus.' (5)

“Kathaṃ tathavāditāya tathāgato? Yasmā esa abhisambodhito yāva parinibbānā rāgamadādinimmathanavasena ekasadisameva dhammaṃ tathaṃ avitathaṃ bhāsati, tasmā tathaṃ gadati, tatho aviparīto āgadovacanametassāti vā da-kārassa ta-kāraṃ katvā tathāgatoti vuttoti evaṃ tathavāditāya tathāgato. (6)

How is he the Tathāgata because of 'speaking thus' (tathavāditā)? Because from his perfect enlightenment until his final Nibbāna, by way of crushing passion, intoxication, and so on, he speaks a Dhamma that is uniform, true, and unerring. Therefore, he speaks what is true (tathaṃ gadati); or, his utterance (āgada) is true (tatho) and undistorted, and he is called 'Tathāgata' by changing the letter 'd' to 't'. Thus he is the Tathāgata because of 'speaking thus.' (6)

“Kathaṃ tathākāritāya tathāgato? Bhagavā hi ‘yathā vādī tathā kārī’ti (a. ni. 4.23; cūḷani. posālamāṇavapucchāniddesa 83) vacanato attano vācāya anurūpameva karoti, tasmā yathā vācā, tathā kāyopi gato pavatto imassāti tathāgatoti evaṃ tathākāritāya tathāgato. (7)

How is he the Tathāgata because of 'doing thus' (tathākāritā)? Because the Blessed One acts in conformity with his own speech, according to the saying, 'As he speaks, so he does.' Therefore, as is his speech, so too his bodily action has gone (gato) and proceeded. Thus he is the Tathāgata. In this way, he is the Tathāgata because of 'doing thus.' (7)

“Kathaṃ [M 1.0145] abhibhavanaṭṭhena tathāgato? Yasmā panesa anupamāya sakalalokiyalokuttaraguṇasampadāya [V 1.0122] samannāgatattā sadevakaṃ lokaṃ abhibhuyya pavattati, tasmā abhibhavanaṭṭhena tathāgatoti vuccatī”ti.

How is he the Tathāgata by way of overcoming? Because, endowed with an unsurpassed accomplishment of all worldly and supramundane qualities, he prevails, having overcome the world with its devas. Therefore, he is called the Tathāgata by way of overcoming.

Tatrevaṃ padasiddhi veditabbā – agado viyāti agado, desanāvilāso ceva puññussayo ca. Tena hesa mahānubhāvo bhisakko viya dibbāgadena sappe sabbaparappavādino, sadevakañca lokaṃ abhibhavati. Iti sabbalokābhibhavane tatho aviparīto yathāvutto agado etassāti da-kārassa ta-kāraṃ katvā tathāgatoti vuccatīti ayamettha saṅkhepo. Vitthāro pana dīghāgamasaṃvaṇṇanādīsu gahetabbo. Āha cettha –

Here the derivation of the word should be understood thus: `agado viyāti agado`—like a remedy, he is a remedy (`agada`), which is a graceful exposition of the teaching and an abundance of merit. By means of this, this one of great power, like a physician with a divine remedy, overcomes all poisonous snakes—that is, all holders of other views—and he overcomes the world with its devas. Thus, in overcoming the entire world, his remedy (`agada`) is true (`tatho`) and undistorted, as stated; he is called 'Tathāgata' by changing the letter 'd' to 't'. This is the summary here. The detailed explanation, however, should be taken from the commentaries on the Long Discourses and other texts. And it was said here:

“Yatheva lokamhi vipassiādayo,

Sabbaññubhāvaṃ munayo idhāgatā;

Tathā ayaṃ sakyamunīpi āgato,

Tathāgato vuccati tena cakkhumā. (dī. ni. aṭṭha. 1.7; ma. ni. aṭṭha. 1.12; a. ni. aṭṭha. 1.1.170; bu. vaṃ. aṭṭha. 1.2 nidānakathā);

Just as in the world the sages Vipassī and others came here to the state of omniscience, so too has this Sakyan Sage come; for that reason the One with Vision is called Tathāgata.

“Pahāya kāmādimale yathā gatā,

Samādhiñāṇehi vipassiādayo;

Mahesino sakyamunī jutindharo,

Tathā gato tena tathāgato mato.

Having abandoned stains such as sensual pleasures, as the great seers Vipassī and others went by means of concentration and knowledge, so too the great seer, the radiant Sakyan Sage, has gone; for that reason he is deemed the Tathāgata.

“Tathañca dhātvāyatanādilakkhaṇaṃ,

Sabhāvasāmaññavibhāgabhedato;

Sayambhuñāṇena jinoyamāgato,

Tathāgato vuccati sakyapuṅgavo.

And the true characteristic of elements, bases, and so on, distinguished by specific nature, general nature, and division, this Victor has come to by his self-originating knowledge; thus the Bull of the Sakyans is called Tathāgata.

“Tathāni [M 1.0146] saccāni samantacakkhunā,

Tathā idappaccayatā ca sabbaso;

Anaññañeyyena [V 1.0123] yato vibhāvitā,

Yāthāvato tena jino tathāgato.

Since the true truths, with his all-round eye, and true specific conditionality in every way, have been made manifest as they really are by his unique knowledge, the Victor is thereby the Tathāgata.

“Anantabhedāsupi lokadhātusu,

Jinassa rūpāyatanādigocare;

Vicittabhede tathameva dassanaṃ,

Tathāgato tena samantalocano.

Even in world-systems of infinite variety, regarding the Victor's domain of the form base and so on, though they are manifoldly distinct, his seeing is ever true; for that reason the All-Seeing One is the Tathāgata.

“Yato ca dhammaṃ tathameva bhāsati,

Karoti vācāyanulomamattano;

Guṇehi lokaṃ abhibhuyyirīyati,

Tathāgato tenapi lokanāyako”ti. (itivu. aṭṭha. 38; dī. ni. ṭī. 1.7);

And since he speaks the Dhamma just as it is, and acts in conformity with his own speech, and proceeds having overcome the world by his qualities, for that reason also the World Leader is the Tathāgata.

Kenaci guṇena attano visiṭṭhassa kassaci abhāvato natthi etassa uttaroti anuttaro. Bhagavato hi avīcito paṭṭhāya yāva bhavaggaṃ tiriyaṃ aparimāṇāsu lokadhātūsu na koci kenaci guṇena samasamopi atthi, kuto pana uttaritaro. Yathāha –

Because there is no one superior to him in any quality, he is called the Unsurpassed. For from the Avīci hell up to the pinnacle of existence, and across in the immeasurable world-systems, there is no one even equal to the Blessed One in any quality—how much less someone superior? As it is said:

“Rūpe sīle samādhimhi, paññāya ca asādiso;

Vimuttiyā samasamo, dhammacakkappavattane”ti.

In form, virtue, concentration, and wisdom he is without peer; in liberation he is without equal, and in setting in motion the Wheel of Dhamma.

Vinditvāti tīhi vandanāhi tanninnatādivasena namassitvā. Kāyavacīmanodvāravasena hi tisso vandanā. Yathāha “tisso imā, bhikkhave, vandanā kāyena vandati, vacasā vandati, manasā vandatī”ti. Tattha buddhādiguṇārammaṇā kāmāvacarakusalakiriyānamaññatarā cetanā kāyaviññattiṃ samuṭṭhāpetvā kāyadvārappavattivasena uppannā kāyavandanāti vuccati, sāyeva vacīviññattiṃ samuṭṭhāpetvā vacīdvārappavattivasena uppannā vacīvandanāti, ubhayaviññattiyo pana asamuṭṭhāpetvā kevalaṃ [M 1.0147] manodvārappavattivasena uppannā manovandanāti. Sirasāti uttamaṅgena karaṇabhūtena. Abujjhi, bodhetīti vā buddho. Ayañhi catusaccadhamme sayampi abujjhi, parepi bodheti[V 1.0124], tasmā bujjhanabodhanaṭṭhena “buddho”ti vuccati. Yathāha “bujjhitā saccānīti buddho, bodhetā pajāyāti buddho”ti (mahāni. 192; cūḷani. pārāyanatthutigāthāniddesa 97; paṭi. ma. 1.162). Atha vā budha-saddassa jāgaraṇavikasanatthesupi pavattanato abujjhi savāsanasammohaniddāya accantaṃ vigato, buddhiyā vikasitavāti vā buddho. Bhagavā hi vatthusabhāvadassanavibandhikāya avijjāsaṅkhātāya niddāya ariyamaggañāṇena saha vāsanāya samucchinnattā tato accantaṃ vigato. Paramarucirasirisobhaggasamāgamena vikasitamiva padumaṃ aparimitaguṇagaṇālaṅkatasabbaññutaññāṇasamāgamena vikasito vikāsamanuppatto, tasmā jāgaraṇavikasanatthavasenapi “buddho”ti vuccati.

'Having paid homage' means having revered with the three kinds of homage, by way of being inclined towards him, etc. For there are three kinds of homage, by way of the doors of body, speech, and mind. As it is said: 'Bhikkhus, there are these three kinds of homage: one pays homage with the body, one pays homage with speech, one pays homage with the mind.' Herein, a certain sense-sphere volition, either wholesome or functional, which has the qualities of the Buddha and others as its object, is called 'bodily homage' when it arises by way of the body-door, having produced bodily intimation. That same volition is called 'verbal homage' when it arises by way of the speech-door, having produced verbal intimation. But when it arises solely by way of the mind-door without producing either kind of intimation, it is called 'mental homage.' 'With the head' means with the foremost limb, which is the instrument. 'He understood' or 'he awakens others,' thus he is Buddha. For he himself understood the four noble truths and awakens others to them; therefore, he is called 'Buddha' in the sense of understanding and awakening. As it is said: 'He understood the truths, thus he is Buddha; he awakens the generation, thus he is Buddha.' Alternatively, since the root 'budh' also has the meanings of waking and blossoming, he is called 'Buddha' as one who has awakened, being utterly rid of the sleep of delusion together with its latent dispositions, or as one who has blossomed by means of wisdom. For the Blessed One, through the knowledge of the noble path, has completely eradicated the sleep called ignorance, which obstructs the seeing of the true nature of things, together with its latent dispositions, and thus has utterly gone beyond it. Like a lotus blossomed by contact with supreme, lovely, auspicious beauty, he has blossomed—has attained full bloom—through the acquisition of the knowledge of omniscience adorned with a collection of limitless qualities. Therefore, he is also called 'Buddha' in the sense of waking and blossoming.

Ettāvatā ca dvīhi ākārehi bhagavato thomanā katā hoti attahitasampattito, parahitapaṭipattito ca. Tāsu attahitasampatti anāvaraṇañāṇādhigamo savāsanasakalasaṃkilesānamaccantappahānaṃ anupādisesanibbānādhigamo ca, parahitapaṭipatti pana āsayappayogavasena duvidhaṃ parahitasamīhanaṃ. Tattha dhammadesanāya abhājanesu devadattādīsu virodhisattesupi niccaṃ hitajjhāsayatā aparipākagatindriyānaṃ indriyaparipākakālāgamanañca āsayo nāma. Tadaññasattānaṃ pana lābhasakkārādinirapekkhacittassa yānattayamukhena sabbadukkhaniyyānikadhammadesanā payogo nāma. Duvidhāsu panetāsu parahitapaṭipattīsu, tividhāsu ca attahitasampattīsu anantakaruṇā-vacanena, tathā āgataṭṭhena ca tathāgata-saddena āsayavasena parahitapaṭipatti dassitā, bodhanaṭṭhena buddha-saddena, tathadassanaṭṭhena [M 1.0148] ca tathāgataṭṭhena ca tathāgatasaddena payogavasena, anantapaññā-vacanena, ñāṇagatidīpakena tathāgata-saddena, bujjhanajāgaraṇavikasanaṭṭhena ca buddha-saddena tividhāpi attahitasampatti, anuttaravacanena ca attahitaparahitasampatti pakāsitāti veditabbā.

Thus, the praise of the Blessed One is made in two ways: through the attainment of his own welfare and through the practice for the welfare of others. Among these, the attainment of his own welfare consists of the acquisition of unobstructed knowledge, the utter abandonment of all defilements together with their latent tendencies, and the attainment of Nibbāna without residue. The practice for the welfare of others, however, is the twofold striving for the welfare of others by way of disposition and application. Herein, disposition means the constant intention for the welfare of beings—even for hostile beings like Devadatta and others who are not fit vessels for the Dhamma—and awaiting the time for the faculties of those with immature faculties to mature. Application, on the other hand, means teaching the Dhamma that leads out from all suffering through the three vehicles, with a mind unconcerned with gain and honor, for the sake of other beings. Now, concerning these two kinds of practice for others' welfare and three kinds of attainment of one's own welfare, it should be understood that the practice for others' welfare is shown, by way of disposition, through the expression 'of boundless compassion' and the word 'Tathāgata' in the sense of 'thus come'; and by way of application, through the word 'Buddha' in the sense of awakening others and the word 'Tathāgata' in the sense of seeing things as they are and being 'thus gone.' The threefold attainment of one's own welfare is shown through the expression 'of boundless wisdom,' the word 'Tathāgata' which indicates the path of knowledge, and the word 'Buddha' in the senses of having awakened, being ever-wakeful, and having blossomed. Furthermore, by the expression 'Unsurpassed,' both the attainment of one's own welfare and the practice for the welfare of others are proclaimed.

Apica hetuphalasattūpakārasampadāvasena tīhākārehipi bhagavato thomanā pavattatīti taṃvasenapettha thomanā daṭṭhabbā. Tattha hetusampadā nāma mahākaruṇāsamāyogo, bodhisambhārasambharaṇañca tammūlakattā sakalabuddhaguṇānaṃ. Phalasampadā pana catubbidhā ñāṇasampadā, pahānasampadā, ānubhāvasampadā, rūpakāyasampadā cāti. Tāsu sabbaññutaññāṇapadaṭṭhānaṃ maggañāṇaṃ, maggañāṇapadaṭṭhānaṃ sabbaññutaññāṇaṃ, tammūlakāni ca dasabalādiñāṇāni ñāṇasampadā nāma. Aggamaggabhāvanāya sabbakilesānaṃ saha vāsanāhi anuppattidhammatāpādanaṃ [V 1.0125] pahānasampadā. Acinteyyāparimitānaṃ sabbalokahitānaṃ nipphādane, sadevakalokābhibhavane ca ādhipaccaṃ ānubhāvasampadā. Sakalalokanayanābhisekabhūtā pana lakkhaṇānubyañjanapaṭimaṇḍitā attabhāvasampatti rūpakāyasampadā nāma. Sattūpakāro heṭṭhā vuttaparahitapaṭipattivaseneva veditabbo. Imāsu pana anantakaruṇā-vacanena, tathā āgataṭṭhena ca tathāgata-saddena hetusampadā dassitā. Phalasampadāsu ñāṇasampadā ceva pahānasampadā ca anantapaññā-vacanena, abhisamayaparidīpakena tathāgatasaddena, bujjhanajāgaraṇavikasanaṭṭhena, ca buddha-saddena dassitā, ānubhāvasampadāpi abhibhavanaṭṭhena tathāgata-saddena, anuttara-vacanena ca vibhāvitā, rūpakāyasampadā pana rūpaggappattidīpakena anuttara-saddena dassitāti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Furthermore, the praise of the Blessed One proceeds in three ways: through the perfection of cause, the perfection of fruit, and the perfection of benefiting beings. Thus the praise should be understood here in this way. Among these, the perfection of cause is the partaking of great compassion and the accumulation of the requisites for enlightenment, for these are the root of all the Buddha's qualities. The perfection of fruit, however, is fourfold: the perfection of knowledge, the perfection of abandonment, the perfection of power, and the perfection of the physical body. Among these, the perfection of knowledge consists of the path knowledge, which is the proximate cause of the knowledge of omniscience, and the knowledge of omniscience, which is the proximate cause of the path knowledge, along with the ten powers and other kinds of knowledge rooted in them. The perfection of abandonment is the bringing of all defilements, together with their latent tendencies, to a state of non-arising through the cultivation of the supreme path. The perfection of power is sovereignty in accomplishing inconceivable and immeasurable benefits for the entire world and in overcoming the world with its gods. The perfection of the physical body is the perfection of the bodily frame, adorned with the major and minor characteristics, which is like a consecration for the eyes of the entire world. The benefiting of beings should be understood in terms of the practice for the welfare of others as explained above. Among these perfections, the perfection of cause is shown by the expression 'of boundless compassion' and by the word 'Tathāgata' in the sense of 'thus come.' Among the perfections of fruit, the perfection of knowledge and the perfection of abandonment are shown by the expression 'of boundless wisdom,' by the word 'Tathāgata' which illuminates realization, and by the word 'Buddha' which signifies awakening, vigilance, and blossoming. The perfection of power is also revealed by the word 'Tathāgata,' which denotes mastery, and by the expression 'unsurpassed.' The perfection of the physical body is shown by the word 'unsurpassed,' which indicates the attainment of the supreme form. This should be understood accordingly.

Evaṃ [M 1.0149] buddharatanassa thomanāpubbaṅgamaṃ paṇāmaṃ katvā idāni sesaratanānampi paṇāmamārabhanto āha “dhammaṃ sādhugaṇampi cā”ti.
