Yathā bhūmivasena bhinnassa gotrabhuvodānavasena ṭhitassa kāmāvacarassa rūpāvacarādīnaṃ āsevanabhāvo dissati, evaṃ jātivasena bhinnassa voṭṭhabbanassa āsevanapaccayabhāve na koci vibandho, apica abhinnavedanassa, abhinnajātikassa ca upekkhāsahagatamahākiriyacittassa vasena yathā “āvajjanā sahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo”ti vuttaṃ, evaṃ “āsevanapaccayena paccayo”tipi vattabbaṃ siyā, na tu vuttaṃ, tasmā vedanāttikepi voṭṭhabbanassa āsevanapaccayattassa abhāvā voṭṭhabbanassa āsevanabhāvadassanavasena vutto dutiyo moghavāro vīmaṃsitvā gahetabbo. Voṭṭhabbanāvajjanānaṃ pana anatthantarabhāvato āvajjanāya ca kusalākusalānaṃ anantarapaccayabhāvassa vuttattā sati uppattiyaṃ voṭṭhabbanaṃ kāmāvacarakusalākusalakiriyājavanānaṃ ekantato anantarapaccayabhāveneva vatteyya, na pana aññathāti muñchāmaraṇāsannavelādīsu javanāpāripūriyā mandībhūtavegatāya ayaṃ dassetabboti.

Here, there might be this conclusion: since it is seen that only states with the same feeling have the nature of a repetition condition, this rejection is made on account of wholesome and unwholesome states having dissimilar feelings from determining. Even so, just as it is said, 'Adverting is a condition for wholesome aggregates and unwholesome aggregates by way of contiguity condition,' so too, on the basis of having the same feeling, it should be said, 'by repetition condition.' But if it is said that because determining is of a different intrinsic nature from wholesome and unwholesome states, its being a repetition condition for them is not stated, this is not correct. For just as the sense-sphere consciousness, which is different by way of plane, is seen to be a repetition condition for the form-sphere states, etc., when it stands as change-of-lineage or purification, so there is no obstacle to determining, which is different by way of intrinsic nature, being a repetition condition. Moreover, with respect to the great functional consciousness accompanied by equanimity, which is of an identical feeling and identical intrinsic nature, just as it is said, 'Adverting is a condition for aggregates with roots by way of contiguity condition,' so too it should be said, 'by repetition condition'; but this is not said. Therefore, since determining does not have the nature of a repetition condition even in the triad of feelings, the second futile process, which was stated to show that determining has the nature of repetition, should be investigated and understood. However, since determining and adverting are not essentially different, and since it is stated that adverting is a contiguity condition for wholesome and unwholesome states, when it arises, determining would invariably function only as a contiguity condition for wholesome, unwholesome, and functional javanas of the sense sphere, and not otherwise. This should be shown in cases such as fainting, at the time of approaching death, etc., when the javanas are incomplete due to weakened momentum.

Ācariyadhammapālattherena panettha idaṃ vuttaṃ – “yaṃ javanabhāvappattaṃ, taṃ chinnamūlarukkhapupphaṃ viyā”ti vakkhamānattā anupacchinnabhavamūlānaṃ pavattassa voṭṭhabbanassa kiriyabhāvo na [M 2.0045] siyā, vutto ca “yasmiṃ samaye manoviññāṇadhātu uppannā kiriyā nevakusalā, nākusalā, na ca kammavipākā upekkhāsahagatā”ti, tasmā aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “javanaṭṭhāne ṭhatvā”ti vacanaṃ javanassa uppajjanaṭṭhāne dvikkhattuṃ pavattitvā na javanabhāvenāti adhippāyena vuttaṃ, “āsevanaṃ labhitvā”ti ca “āsevanaṃ viya āsevana”nti vutte na koci virodhoti. Vipphārikassa pana sato dvikkhattuṃ pavattiyevettha āsevanasadisatā. Vipphārikatāya hi viññattisamuṭṭhāpakattañcassa vuccati. Vipphārikampi javanaṃ viya anekakkhattuṃ appavattiyā dubbalattā na nippariyāyato āsevanapaccayabhāvena pavatteyyāti na imassa pāṭhe āsevanattaṃ vuttaṃ[V 2.0034]. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana pariyāyato vuttaṃ, yathā phalacittesu maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannanti. Yadipi “javanāpāripūriyā…pe… yutto”ti vuttaṃ, “āvajjanādīnaṃ paccayo bhavituṃ na sakkotī”ti pana vuttattā cittappavattivasena paṭhamamoghavārato etassa na koci visesoti.

Here, the Elder Dhammapāla has said this: Because it will be said, 'Whatever has attained the state of javana is like a flower from a tree with its roots severed,' the functional nature would not belong to determining, which occurs for one whose roots of existence are not cut off. And it is said: 'At the time when the mind-consciousness element arises, it is functional, neither wholesome nor unwholesome, nor the result of kamma, and is accompanied by equanimity.' Therefore, in the commentary, the statement 'standing in the place of javana' is said with the intention that it occurs twice at the place where javana arises, but not with the nature of javana. And when it is said 'having obtained repetition' and 'repetition in a figurative sense,' there is no contradiction. For a state that is expansive, its occurring twice is similar to repetition here. Indeed, on account of its expansiveness, it is said to be the originator of intimation. Because the expansive state, unlike javana, is weak due to not occurring many times, it would not function as a repetition condition in the primary sense. Thus its nature as repetition is not stated in this text. In the commentary, however, it is stated figuratively, just as the path factors in the fruition cittas are said to be included in the path. Although it is said, 'Due to the incompleteness of javana... it is fitting,' since it is also stated, 'It cannot be a condition for adverting, etc.,' on account of the cognitive process, this has no distinction from the first futile passage.

Cakkhussāpāthamāgateti cakkhudvārassa yogyadesāvaṭṭhānavasena āpāthamāgate. Tāyāti manodhātuyā bhavaṅgāvaṭṭane pākaṭatāya kiriyāmanodhātuṃ paccāmasati. Āvaṭṭiteti santativasena pavattituṃ adatvā nivattite, pariṇāmite vā. Jātesu jāyateti sambandho. Gateti niruddhe. Tadevāti javanānubhūtameva iṭṭhārammaṇaṃ. Tenevāti javanaṃ hutvā niruddhena tena kāmāvacarakusalacittena. Tadārammaṇasaññitanti javanaggahiteyeva ārammaṇe pavattanato “brahmassaro”tiādīsu viya tassa ārammaṇaṃ ārammaṇamassāti majjhapadalopavasena tadārammaṇanti saññitaṃ. Tulyatoti ārammaṇato visadisabhāvepi somanassasahagatādinā sadisattā. Mūlasadisaṃ [M 2.0046] bhavaṅgaṃ mūlabhavaṅgaṃ. Tadārammaṇampi bhavaṅgasabhāvattā “bhavaṅga”nti vuccati yathā “sahetukaṃ bhavaṅgaṃ ahetukassa bhavaṅgassa anantarapaccayena paccayo”ti (paṭṭhā. 3.1.102). Ettha hi paṭisandhicitte eva pavattiyaṃ “bhavaṅga”nti vuccamāne na tassa hetuvasena bhedoti “sahetukaṃ bhavaṅgaṃ ahetukassa bhavaṅgassa anantarapaccayena paccayo”ti na sakkā vattuṃ. Nāpi cetaṃ “sahetukaṃ cutiṃ ahetukapaṭisandhiñca sandhāya vutta”nti sakkā viññātuṃ. Bhavassa aṅgabhāvābhāvato cuticittassa bhavaṅgavohārālābhatoti “sahetukaṃ bhavaṅga”nti tadārammaṇaṃ vuttanti viññāyati. “Tadārammaṇasaññita”nti vatvā “mūlabhavaṅganti vuccatī”ti vuttattā nāmadvayampi imassa labbhatīti dīpitaṃ hoti.

'Having come within the range of the eye' means having come within range on account of being established in a suitable place for the eye-door. 'By that': he refers back to the functional mind-element, which is the mind-element that is manifest in the turning of the bhavaṅga. 'Turned away': prevented from proceeding in a continuum, or diverted. The connection is: 'it arises among those that have arisen.' 'Gone': ceased. 'That very same': the desirable object itself experienced by the javana. 'By that very': by that sense-sphere wholesome citta that, having been a javana, has ceased. 'Designated as tadārammaṇa': because it arises in the very object grasped by the javana, it is designated 'tadārammaṇa' by elision of the middle term, as in 'brahmassaro,' etc., from 'tassa ārammaṇaṃ ārammaṇam assā' (its object is the object for this). 'On account of similarity': although there is dissimilarity regarding the object, there is similarity on account of being accompanied by gladness, etc. 'Root-bhavaṅga' is a bhavaṅga similar to the root one. Tadārammaṇa, too, is called 'bhavaṅga' because it has the nature of bhavaṅga, as in: 'A bhavaṅga with roots is a condition for a bhavaṅga without roots by way of contiguity condition' (Paṭṭh. 3.1.102). Here, if 'bhavaṅga' were said of the rebirth-linking citta only during its occurrence, then since there is no division of it by way of roots, it would not be possible to say: 'A bhavaṅga with roots is a condition for a bhavaṅga without roots by way of contiguity condition.' Nor can this be understood as stated with reference to 'a death-consciousness with roots and a rebirth-linking without roots,' for the death-consciousness does not obtain the designation 'bhavaṅga' as it is not a factor of existence. Thus it is understood that 'bhavaṅga with roots' refers to tadārammaṇa. By saying 'designated as tadārammaṇa' and then 'it is called root-bhavaṅga,' it is shown that it obtains both names.

392. Tañcāti tadārammaṇañca. Etthāti imesu vīthicittesu. Gaṇanūpagacittānīti vipākagaṇanūpagacittāni.

392. 'And that': and the tadārammaṇa. 'Here': in these process-cittas. 'Cittas that come into the reckoning': resultant cittas that come into the reckoning.

394. Asamānattāti asaṅkhārikabhāvena asamānattā.

394. 'Because of dissimilarity': because of dissimilarity by way of being unprompted.

396. Purimāni pañca vipākacittāni iminā saddhiṃ cha hontīti sambandho. Ettha ca yebhuyyato iṭṭhārammaṇe somanassappavattivasena somanassasahagatajavanānantarameva somanassatadārammaṇaṃ vuttaṃ. Javanassa pana pakappetvā ārammaṇaggahaṇasabbhāvato, vipākassa ca tadabhāvato [V 2.0035] iṭṭhārammaṇe upekkhāsahagatajavanesupi javitesu somanassasahagatameva tadārammaṇaṃ hoti.

396. The connection is: the previous five resultant cittas, together with this one, become six. Here, as a general rule, because gladness occurs with a desirable object, a tadārammaṇa accompanied by gladness is said to occur immediately after a javana accompanied by gladness. However, since javana has the ability to grasp an object by determining it, while the resultant lacks this, even when javanas accompanied by equanimity have run their course with a desirable object, the tadārammaṇa is accompanied by gladness.

399-403. Tasmiṃ dvāreti tasmiṃyeva cakkhudvāre. Vedanā parivattatīti kammassa somanassasahagatabhāvepi ārammaṇassa [M 2.0047] iṭṭhamajjhattatāya somanassavedanā parivattitvā upekkhāvedanā hoti. Atha vā heṭṭhā vipākavedanāya somanassabhāvepi iṭṭhārammaṇassa majjhattabhāvena taṃvasena vedanā parivattatīti attho.

399-403. 'At that door': at that very eye-door. 'The feeling changes': even when the kamma is accompanied by gladness, because the object is moderately desirable, the feeling of gladness changes and becomes a feeling of equanimity. Or else, the meaning is that even though the resultant feeling below is one of gladness, the feeling changes on account of the desirable object's neutral quality.

Javanesu javitesūti sambandho. “Javitesu catūsvapī”ti vā pāṭho. Jāyareti tadārammaṇavasena jāyanti. Vedanāyāti vedanāya karaṇabhūtāya. Asamānattāti paṭisandhiyā saha asamānattā. Purimehīti heṭṭhā vuttatadārammaṇacatukkato. Atha vā “purimehi asamānattā” icceva yojanā. Purimehi saha asamānabhāve vutte tesaṃ sandhiyā saha asamānabhāvopi vuttova hotīti cattāri nāmato piṭṭhibhavaṅgāni ca hontīti yojanā. Ca-saddena āgantukabhavaṅgāni, tadārammaṇāni ca hontīti dasseti. Etthāpi ca yebhuyyena iṭṭhamajjhattārammaṇe upekkhāsahagatajavanassa uppajjanato upekkhāsahagatajavanānantarameva upekkhāsahagatatadārammaṇaṃ vuttaṃ, heṭṭhā vuttanayena pana upekkhāsahagatatadārammaṇaṃ hoti. Ñāṇasampayuttādīsu javitesu ñāṇavippayuttatadārammaṇānaṃ sambhavo heṭṭhā vuttanayena veditabbo. Kiñcāpi asaṅkhārasasaṅkhāravidhānaṃ javanavasena vuttaṃ, tathāpi utubhojanādipaccayānaṃ dubbalabhāve javanasseva asaṅkhārikattābhāvato asaṅkhārajavanāvasāne asaṅkhārameva tadārammaṇaṃ hoti, na sasaṅkhāranti niyamo. Paccayassa pana balavabhāve satipi paresaṃ ussāhabalena sasaṅkhārassa javanassa sambhavato sasaṅkhārajavanāvasāne sasaṅkhārameva tadārammaṇaṃ hoti, sasaṅkhārikattābhāvato asaṅkhārajavanāvasāne asaṅkhāramevāti niyamo natthīti asaṅkhārajavanāvasāne asaṅkhārampi sasaṅkhārampi tadārammaṇaṃ hoti, sasaṅkhārajavanāvasāne sasaṅkhārampi asaṅkhārampi tadārammaṇaṃ hoti.

The connection is 'when the javanas have run their course.' Or the reading is 'when the four have run their course.' 'They arise': they arise as tadārammaṇa. 'By feeling': by the feeling that has become the instrument. 'Because of dissimilarity': because of dissimilarity with the rebirth-linking. 'By the former': from the fourfold tadārammaṇa mentioned above. Or else, the construction is just 'because of dissimilarity with the former.' When dissimilarity with the former is stated, their dissimilarity with the rebirth-linking is also stated. The construction is: 'the four are by name also the immediately preceding bhavaṅgas.' By the word 'ca' (and), he shows that they are adventitious bhavaṅgas and tadārammaṇas. Here too, as a general rule, because a javana accompanied by equanimity arises with a moderately desirable object, a tadārammaṇa accompanied by equanimity is mentioned immediately after a javana accompanied by equanimity. However, a tadārammaṇa accompanied by equanimity occurs in the way stated above. The possibility of tadārammaṇas dissociated from knowledge arising after javanas associated with knowledge, etc., should be understood in the way stated above. Although the distinction between unprompted and prompted is stated with reference to javana, still, when conditions such as climate and food are weak, the javana itself may not be unprompted; hence, there is no rule that at the conclusion of an unprompted javana the tadārammaṇa must be unprompted and not prompted. And since, even when a condition is strong, a prompted javana can occur through the effort of others, there is no rule that at the conclusion of a prompted javana the tadārammaṇa must be prompted, nor that at the conclusion of an unprompted javana it must be unprompted simply due to the javana's unprompted nature. Therefore, at the conclusion of an unprompted javana, the tadārammaṇa can be unprompted or prompted; and at the conclusion of a prompted javana, the tadārammaṇa can be prompted or unprompted.

Pañcimānīti [M 2.0048] iṭṭhamajjhattārammaṇe vuttāni upekkhāsahagatasantīraṇādīni pañca vipākāni. Purimehi sattahīti iṭṭhārammaṇe vuttehi cakkhuviññāṇādīhi sattahi viniddise cakkhudvārasminti adhippāyo.

By 'these five' are meant the five results, beginning with the investigating consciousness accompanied by equanimity, mentioned in connection with a moderately desirable object. By 'by the former seven' is meant that the seven, beginning with eye-consciousness, mentioned in connection with a desirable object, are to be distinguished at the eye-door.

405-6. Ekāya [V 2.0036] cetanāyāti ekāya tihetukasomanassasahagataasaṅkhārikacetanāya. Evaṃ samasaṭṭhi vipākāni uppajjantīti sambandho. Yasmā pana cakkhudvārādīsu anuppajjitvā sotadvārādīsuyeva uppajjamānā sotaviññāṇādayo viya pañcasu dvāresu anuppajjitvā manodvāreyeva uppajjamāno kāmāvacaravipāko natthi, tasmā manodvāre vipākappavatti na vuttā. Atha vā cakkhudvāre gahitānameva manodhātumanoviññāṇadhātūnaṃ sotadvārādīsupi gahaṇena pañcadvāresu gahitāya manoviññāṇadhātuyā manodvārepi gahaṇanayadassanaṃ kataṃ hoti, evaṃ sati chasu dvāresupi samasattati vipākāni honti. Atha vā manodvāre labbhamānāyapi pañcadvārappavattāya manoviññāṇadhātuyā manodvāre aggahaṇena sotadvārādīsu labbhamānānampi cakkhudvāre gahitamanodhātumanoviññāṇadhātūnaṃ sotadvārādīsu aggahaṇassa nayadassanaṃ kataṃ hoti, evaṃ sati pañcadvāresu soḷasa vipākāni honti. Evañca katvā vuttaṃ “gahitāggahaṇenā”tiādi.

405-6. By 'one volition' is meant one three-rooted, unprompted volition accompanied by joy. The connection is that sixty-two results arise thus. However, since there is no sense-sphere result that arises only at the ear-door and so forth without arising at the eye-door and so forth, like ear-consciousness and so forth, and no sense-sphere result that arises only at the mind-door without arising at the five doors, therefore the occurrence of results at the mind-door is not mentioned. Alternatively, by the taking of the mind-element and mind-consciousness-element that are taken at the eye-door, and also by their taking at the ear-door and so forth, the method of taking the mind-consciousness-element that is taken at the five doors is shown as also applying at the mind-door. If this is the case, then there are seventy-two results in all six doors. Or else, by not taking the mind-consciousness-element that occurs at the five doors, even though it is obtainable at the mind-door, the method of not taking the mind-element and mind-consciousness-element that are taken at the eye-door but are obtainable at the ear-door and so forth, is shown. If this is the case, then there are sixteen results in the five doors. And having done thus, it is said: 'By inclusion and non-inclusion,' and so forth.

408-9. Tīhi vipākehīti tehi tīhi kusalacittehi samānehi tīhi vipākehi dinnāya paṭisandhiyāti sambandho. Upekkhāsahitadvayeti upekkhāsahagatapaṭisandhiyugaḷe. Idha ṭhatvā nāḷiyantūpamā veditabbā. Kathaṃ? Ucchupīḷanasamaye kira ekasmā gāmā ekādasa yantavāhā nikkhamitvā ekaṃ ucchuvāṭaṃ disvā tassa paripakkabhāvaṃ ñatvā ucchusāmikaṃ [M 2.0049] upasaṅkamitvā “yantavāhā maya”nti ārocesuṃ. So “ahaṃ tumheyeva pariyesissāmī”ti ucchusālaṃ gahetvā agamāsi. Te tattha nāḷiyantaṃ yojetvā “mayaṃ ekādasa janā aparampi ekaṃ laddhuṃ vaṭṭati, vattanena gaṇhathā”ti āhaṃsu. Ucchusāmiko “ahameva sahāyo bhavissāmī”ti ucchusālaṃ pūrāpetvā tesaṃ sahāyo ahosi. Te attano attano kiccāni katvā phāṇitapācakena ucchurase pakke guḷe baddhe ucchusāmikena tulayitvā bhāgesu dinnesu attano attano bhāgaṃ ādāya sālaṃ sālasāmikaṃ paṭicchāpetvā eteneva upāyena aparāsupi catūsu sālāsu kammaṃ katvā pakkamiṃsu. Tattha pañca yantasālā viya pañca pasādā daṭṭhabbā, pañca ucchuvāṭā viya pañca ārammaṇāni, ekādasa vicaraṇakayantavāhā viya ekādasa vipākacittāni, pañca ucchusālasāmino viya pañca viññāṇāni, paṭhamakasālāya sālasāmikena saddhiṃ dvādasannaṃ janānaṃ ekato hutvā katakammānaṃ bhāgaggahaṇakālo viya ekādasannaṃ vipākacittānaṃ cakkhuviññāṇena saddhiṃ ekato hutvā cakkhudvāre rūpārammaṇe sakasakakiccakaraṇakālo, sālasāmikassa sālāya sampaṭicchitakālo viya cakkhuviññāṇassa dvārasaṅkantiakaraṇaṃ, dutiyatatiyacatutthapañcamasālāya [V 2.0037] dvādasannaṃ ekato hutvā katakammānaṃ bhāgaggahaṇakālo viya ekādasannaṃ vipākacittānaṃ kāyaviññāṇena saddhiṃ ekato hutvā kāyadvāre phoṭṭhabbārammaṇe sakasakakiccakaraṇakālo, sāmikassa sampaṭicchitakālo viya kāyaviññāṇassa dvārasaṅkantiakaraṇaṃ veditabbaṃ.

408-9. 'By three results' means that rebirth-linking is given by those three results, which are similar to the three wholesome consciousnesses. 'The pair accompanied by equanimity' refers to the pair of rebirth-linking consciousnesses accompanied by equanimity. Here, the analogy of the sugarcane press should be understood. How so? It is said that during the sugarcane pressing season, eleven press operators left one village and, seeing a sugarcane field and knowing its ripeness, approached the sugarcane owner and announced, 'We are press operators.' He replied, 'I myself will search for you,' and went to the sugarcane hall. They set up the sugarcane press there and said, 'We are eleven people; it is right to get one more. Take him by turns.' The sugarcane owner said, 'I myself will be your companion,' and having had the sugarcane brought to the hall, he became their companion. They each did their own work. When the sugarcane juice had been cooked by the molasses-cooker, formed into molasses-cakes, weighed by the sugarcane owner, and divided into shares, they each took their own share. After handing the hall back to the hall owner, they worked in the other four halls by this very method and then departed. Therein, the five pressing halls should be seen as the five sense faculties; the five sugarcane fields as the five sense-objects; the eleven wandering press operators as the eleven resultant consciousnesses; the five sugarcane hall owners as the five sense-consciousnesses. The time when the twelve people in the first hall, including the hall owner, gathered together to take their shares for the work done is like the time when the eleven resultant consciousnesses, together with eye-consciousness, perform their respective functions at the eye-door with a visible object as its object. The time when the hall owner received back the hall is like the non-transference of the eye-consciousness from its door. The time when the twelve people in the second, third, fourth, and fifth halls gathered to take their shares for the work done is like the time when the eleven resultant consciousnesses, together with body-consciousness, perform their respective functions at the body-door with a tangible object as its object. The time when the owner received it back is like the non-transference of the body-consciousness from its door.

414. Assāti imassa bījassa. Hetupavattitoti paccayappavattito.

414. 'Assa' means 'of this seed.' 'Hetupavattito' means 'from the occurrence of a cause,' that is, 'from the occurrence of a condition.'

415. Idāni [M 2.0050] tihetukomakakammena gahitaduhetukapaṭisandhikassa vipākappavatti duhetukukkaṭṭhena gahitaduhetukapaṭisandhikassa vipākappavattiyā samānāti taṃ ṭhapetvā duhetukakammena gahitaduhetukapaṭisandhikasseva vipākappavattiṃ dassetuṃ “duhetukena kammenā”tiādi vuttaṃ.

415. Now, because the occurrence of results for one with two-rooted rebirth-linking generated by three-rooted inferior kamma is similar to the occurrence of results for one with two-rooted rebirth-linking generated by two-rooted superior kamma, setting that aside, the phrase 'by two-rooted kamma,' and so forth, is stated to show only the occurrence of results for one with two-rooted rebirth-linking generated by two-rooted kamma.

418-9. Duhetukapaṭisandhikassa kāmāvacaratihetukajavanānaṃ sambhavepi kammasarikkhakāneva javanāni dassetuṃ “somanassa…pe… duhetuke”ti vuttaṃ. Tihetukajavanāvasānepi panassa paṭisandhidāyakakammaṃ tihetukavipākadāne asamatthanti tihetukatadārammaṇābhāvato, javanassa ca kammasarikkhakahetuvasena duhetukabhāvato duhetukatadārammaṇameva hoti.

418-9. Although for one with two-rooted rebirth-linking, three-rooted javanas pertaining to the sense-sphere are possible, to show only javanas similar to the kamma, it is said: 'joy... with two roots.' However, even at the end of a three-rooted javana for such a person, the kamma that produces rebirth-linking is incapable of giving a three-rooted result, because there is no three-rooted tadārammaṇa. And because the javana is two-rooted, by way of its cause being similar to the kamma, there is only a two-rooted tadārammaṇa.

424. Imāni ca bhavaṅgānīti imāni cattāri mūlāgantukapiṭṭhibhavaṅgāni. Aṭṭha hīti aṭṭheva.

424. 'And these life-continuums' means these four: the root, adventitious, and secondary life-continuums. 'Indeed, there are eight' means there are just eight.

426. Sotaghānādināti sotaghānādiviññāṇehi. Etthāpi ambopamā pākaṭikāva. Yantavāhopamāya panettha satta yantavāhā tehi hatthayante nāma sajjite sālasāmikaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ katvā vuttanayānusāreneva yojanā veditabbā.

426. 'By ear, nose, etc.' means by ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, etc. Here too, the mango analogy is clearly evident. But regarding the analogy of the press operator, here seven press operators are mentioned; with the hand-operated press prepared by them, the hall owner is counted as the eighth. The application should be understood in accordance with the method already stated.

434-6. Vuddhimupetassāti mātukucchito nikkhamitvā saṃvarāsaṃvare paṭṭhapetuṃ samatthabhāvena vuḍḍhippattassa. Kiñcāpi ahetukapaṭisandhikassa kammasarikkhakajavanameva dassetuṃ “duhetūnaṃ…pe… vasānasmi”nti vuttaṃ. Tihetukajavanampi pana tesaṃ javati, javanassa duhetukabhāvepi [V 2.0038] kammassa duhetukavipākadāne asamatthatāya “ahetuka…pe… jāyate”ti vuttaṃ.

434-6. 'For one who has attained growth' means for one who, having emerged from the mother’s womb, has attained growth through being capable of establishing restraint or non-restraint. Although it is to show only kamma-conforming javana for one with rootless rebirth-linking that it is said, 'for those with two roots... in the end,' three-rooted javana also occurs for them. And even though the javana has two roots, because the kamma is incapable of giving a two-rooted result, it is said: 'rootless... is born.'

443-8. “Ahetupaṭisandhissā”tiādīsu [M 2.0051] adhippāyo heṭṭhā āgatova. Apāyesu paṭisandhidāyakakammena paṭisandhito hīnatadārammaṇassa anipphannato tassa labbhamānaṭṭhānameva dassetuṃ “sugatiya”nti vuttaṃ, kāmāvacarasugatiyanti attho. Tenāti tena jātapaṭisandhivipākena. “Catūsu apāyesu labbhatī”ti vatvā tassa visayadassanatthaṃ “thero nerayikāna”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Theroti nirayacārikāya pākaṭattā mahāmoggallānattheramāha. Niraye bhavā nerayikā. Dhammaṃ desetīti niraye padumaṃ māpetvā padumakaṇṇikāya nisinno dhammaṃ deseti. Vassatīti antohetvatthaṃ katvā vuttaṃ, vassāpetīti attho. Theraṃ disvāti therassa dassanahetu. Iminā indanīlapaṭimāvaṇṇassa therassa iṭṭhārammaṇabhāvena kusalavipākacakkhuviññāṇuppattiyā kāraṇaṃ dasseti. Esa nayo “dhammaṃ sutvā”tiādīsupi. Gandhanti tena māpitagandhaṃ. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana “candanavane divāvihāraṃ nisinnassa cīvaragandha”nti (dha. sa. aṭṭha. 498 vipākuddhārakathā) vuttaṃ. Ghāyatanti ghāyantānaṃ. Santīraṇadvayanti atiiṭṭhamajjhattassa gandhādino vasena santīraṇadvayaṃ. Kusalavipākānaṃ, iṭṭhārammaṇassa ca niraye sambhavadīpanena sesāpāyattayepi sambhavo dassitova hoti.

443-8. In 'for one with rootless rebirth-linking,' and so forth, the meaning has already been given. Since an inferior tadārammaṇa does not arise in the lower realms from rebirth-producing kamma, to show only the place where it is obtained, 'in a happy destiny' is said, meaning in a sense-sphere happy destiny. 'By that' means by that rebirth-linking resultant that has arisen. After saying 'it is obtained in the four lower realms,' 'the Elder for those in hell,' and so forth, is said to show its scope. 'The Elder' refers to the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, because of his renown for wandering in hell. 'Those in hell' are those existing in hell. 'He teaches the Dhamma' means he teaches the Dhamma, having created a lotus in hell and sitting on its pericarp. 'He rains' is said by construing it as having an internal causal sense, meaning 'he causes to rain.' 'Having seen the Elder' means because of seeing the Elder. By this, it shows that the Elder, whose complexion is like a sapphire image, is the condition for the arising of wholesome resultant eye-consciousness because of being a desirable object. The same method applies in 'having heard the Dhamma,' and so forth. 'Fragrance' means the fragrance created by him. However, in the Commentary it is said: 'the fragrance of the robes of one sitting in a sandalwood grove during the day' (Dhammasaṅgaṇī-aṭṭhakathā, Vipākuddhārakathā). 'They smell' means for those who smell. 'The two kinds of investigating consciousness' means the two kinds of investigating consciousness by way of the extremely desirable and neutral smell, and so forth. By indicating the possibility of wholesome resultants and desirable objects in hell, the possibility in the remaining three lower realms is also shown.

450. Niyamoyeva niyamattaṃ, tadārammaṇacittampi javanena niyāmitanti vuttaniyamoti attho. Kusalaṃ pana sandhāyāti kusalajavanaṃ sandhāya dīpitaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ, kusalassa viya akusalassa sadisavipākābhāvatoti adhippāyo. Ettha ca kusalajavanānantaraṃ sahetukatadārammaṇasseva vacanaṃ. Javanassa kammasarikkhakahetuvasena sahetukattā javanānurūpato vuttaṃ. Paricitavasena pana aññakammenāpi taṃ ahetukatadārammaṇaṃ [M 2.0052] na hotīti na vattabbaṃ. Na hi paṭisandhijanakameva kammaṃ tadārammaṇaṃ janeti, atha kho aññakammampi paṭisandhidāyakakammena nibbattetabbatadārammaṇato visadisampi nibbattetīti. Akusalajavanānantarañca ahetukatadārammaṇampi javanassa kammasarikkhakahetukattā tadanurūpato vuttaṃ. Yathāvuttanayena pana sahetukatadārammaṇampi na hotīti natthi.

450. "Certainty" means the state of being certain; the meaning is that "the stated certainty" is that even the tadārammaṇa consciousness is determined by the javana. However, "with reference to wholesome" means it is explained in the commentary with reference to wholesome javana, the intention being that, unlike wholesome kamma, unwholesome kamma does not have a similar result. And here, the mention is only of a rooted tadārammaṇa after wholesome javana. This is said to be in conformity with the javana, because the javana is rooted, having roots similar to the kamma. However, it should not be said that a rootless tadārammaṇa does not arise even from other kamma due to familiarity. For it is not only the kamma that generates rebirth that generates the tadārammaṇa; rather, other kamma too can generate it, even if it is dissimilar to the tadārammaṇa that should be produced by the kamma that gives rebirth. And after unwholesome javana, even a rootless tadārammaṇa is said to be in conformity with it, as the javana has roots similar to the kamma. But according to the method explained, it is not the case that a rooted tadārammaṇa does not arise.

456-7. Ettāvatā tipiṭakacūḷanāgattheravāde soḷasa vipākacittāni saddhiṃ dvādasakamaggena [V 2.0039] ceva ahetukaṭṭhakena ca vibhāvetvā moravāpivāsimahādattattheravāde visesābhāvato taṃ anāmasitvā mahādhammarakkhitattheravāde kusalākusalakiriyavasena piṇḍitvā dassitānaṃ piṇḍajavanānaṃ vasena tadārammaṇaṃ dassetuṃ “somanassayute citte”tiādi vuttaṃ. Somanassa…pe… javiteti iṭṭhārammaṇe kusalākusalakiriyābyākatavasena somanassayutesu terasasu javanacittesu javitesu. Gavesitabbā…pe… mānasāti heṭṭhā vuttanayena somanassasahagatāni pañceva tadārammaṇacittāni gavesitabbāni. Upekkhā…pe… javitesūti kusalākusalakiriyavasena cuddasasu upekkhāsahagatajavanacittesu javitesu. Cha gavesitabbānīti upekkhāsahagatāni cha eva gavesitabbāni. Khīṇāsavānaṃ pahīnavipallāsatāya kiriyājavanaṃ iṭṭhārammaṇe upekkhāsahagataṃ na hotīti somanassasahagatakiriyājavanesu javitesu somanassasahagatatadārammaṇameva hoti. Iṭṭhamajjhatte, aniṭṭhādīsu ca somanassabhāvato upekkhāsahagatakiriyājavanesu javitesu upekkhāsahagatatadārammaṇamevāti idamettha sanniṭṭhānaṃ. Sekhaputhujjanānaṃ pana appahīnavipallāsatāya iṭṭhamajjhatte, aniṭṭhaaniṭṭhamajjhattārammaṇe ca [M 2.0053] somanassasahagatajavanaṃ uppajjatīti somanassasahagatajavanāvasāne somanassasahagatatadārammaṇameva hoti, natthi upekkhāsahagatanti nāyaṃ niyamo. Iṭṭhārammaṇepi vuttanayānusārena yojetabbaṃ. Tenetaṃ vuccati –

456-7. Having thus explained the sixteen resultant consciousnesses together with the twelve path consciousnesses and the eight rootless consciousnesses in accordance with the doctrine of the Elder Cūḷanāga, the Tipiṭaka master; and without mentioning it in the doctrine of the Elder Mahādatta of Moravāpi due to the absence of any special distinction; but having shown it condensed according to wholesome, unwholesome, and functional impulsions in the doctrine of the Elder Mahādhammarakkhita, in order to show the registering consciousness (tadārammaṇa) by way of the condensed impulsions, it is said: “In a consciousness accompanied by joy,” etc. “Joy … impelled”: when, in regard to a desirable object, impulsion has occurred in the thirteen impulsion consciousnesses accompanied by joy, which may be wholesome, unwholesome, or functional. “Are to be sought … mental state”: in accordance with the method stated previously, the five registering consciousnesses accompanied by joy are to be sought. “Equanimity … impelled”: when impulsion has occurred in the fourteen impulsion consciousnesses accompanied by equanimity, which may be wholesome, unwholesome, or functional. “Six are to be sought”: the six accompanied by equanimity are to be sought. For an arahant, because of the abandonment of distortion, a functional impulsion accompanied by equanimity does not occur in regard to a desirable object. Therefore, when functional impulsions accompanied by joy have occurred, only a registering consciousness accompanied by joy arises. In regard to a desirable-neutral object, and in regard to undesirable objects, etc., because of the absence of joy, when functional impulsions accompanied by equanimity have occurred, only a registering consciousness accompanied by equanimity arises—this is the conclusion here. For trainees and worldlings, however, because of the non-abandonment of distortion, an impulsion accompanied by joy arises in regard to a desirable-neutral object and in regard to undesirable and undesirable-neutral objects. Therefore, it is not a fixed rule that at the end of an impulsion accompanied by joy only a registering consciousness accompanied by joy arises and not one accompanied by equanimity. Even in the case of a desirable object, this should be applied in accordance with the method stated. Therefore it is said:

“Parittakusalādosa-pāpasātakriyājavā;

Pañcasvekaṃ tadālambaṃ, sukhitesu yathārahaṃ.

“After sense-sphere wholesome, unwholesome, and joyful functional impulsions, one of the five registering consciousnesses arises, as is appropriate, in those processes accompanied by pleasant feeling.

“Pāpā kāmasubhā ceva, sopekkhā ca kriyājavā;

Sopekkhesu tadālambaṃ, chasvekamanurūpato”ti.

“After unwholesome, sense-sphere wholesome, and functional impulsions accompanied by equanimity, one of the six registering consciousnesses arises, as is suitable, in those processes accompanied by equanimity.”

458-62. Duhetukāhetukānaṃ vipākāvaraṇehi samannāgatattā jhānuppādoyeva natthīti āha “tihetusomanassenā”ti. Jhānato parihīnassāti uppāditalokiyajjhānato parihīnassa. Vippaṭisārinoti “mahantena vāyāmena uppādito me paṇītadhammo naṭṭho”ti uppannavippaṭisāravantassa. Kiṃ…pe… mānasanti ayaṃ anumatipucchā, tadārammaṇamānasaṃ jāyate kiṃ, na vāti ayañhettha attho. Bhavaṅgapāto vā hotu tadārammaṇaṃ vā, ko ettha vibandhoti āha “paṭṭhāne paṭisiddhā”tiādi. Avacanameva paṭisedhoti katvā āha “paṭisiddhā”ti[V 2.0040]. Yadi somanassānantaraṃ domanassaṃ, domanassānantaraṃ somanassaṃ vā uppajjeyya, tadā “sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto dhammo adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo”tiādi (paṭṭhā. 1.2.45) viya “sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto dhammo dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo, dukkhāya vedanāya…pe… sukhāya vedanāya…pe… paccayo”ti vattabbaṃ siyā, tathā gaṇanavāre ekekavedanāsampayuttassa attanā [M 2.0054] samānavedanāsampayuttassa, itaravedanādvayasamaṅgissa ca paccayabhāvaṃ sandhāya “anantare navā”ti vattabbaṃ siyā, na ca panevaṃ pāḷi āgatā. Domanassasomanassavedanāya sampayuttānaṃ pana aññamaññaanantarapaccayavasena gaṇanadvayaṃ parihāpetvā “anantare sattā”ti vuttaṃ, tasmā yathādhammasāsane avacanampi paṭisedhasadisaṃ abhāvasseva dīpanatoti vuttaṃ “paṭisiddhā”ti. Assa vā anantaraṃ domanassassa uppattīti sambandho. Assāti somanassassa.

458-62. Because two-rooted and rootless resultants are possessed of the obstruction of being resultants, the arising of jhāna is impossible. Thus he says: “by joy with three roots.” “Of one who has fallen away from jhāna” means: of one who has fallen away from a mundane jhāna that he had produced. “Of one who is regretful” means: of one in whom regret has arisen, thinking, “My sublime attainment, produced with great effort, has been lost!” “What … mental state?”: this is a question seeking consent. The meaning here is: “Does a registering consciousness arise or not?” Whether there is a lapse into the life-continuum or a registering consciousness, what is the obstacle here? He says: “In the Paṭṭhāna it is rejected,” etc. Taking non-mention itself as a rejection, he says “rejected.” If displeasure were to arise immediately after joy, or joy immediately after displeasure, then just as it is said, “a state associated with pleasant feeling is a condition for a state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling by way of proximity condition,” etc. (Paṭṭhāna 1.2.45), it would have to be said: “a state associated with pleasant feeling is a condition for a state associated with painful feeling by way of proximity condition; a state associated with painful feeling … is a condition for a state associated with pleasant feeling….” Similarly, in the enumeration section, concerning the conditionality of each state associated with a feeling for a state associated with the same feeling and for one associated with the other two feelings, it would have to be said, “nine by proximity.” But the Pāli text is not transmitted in this way. Rather, for states associated with displeasure and joy, having excluded the two counts by way of mutual proximity condition, it is said, “seven by proximity.” Therefore, since in the teaching of the Dhamma non-mention is equivalent to a rejection because it indicates absence, it is said “rejected.” Or the connection is: “the arising of displeasure immediately after this.” “This” means: after joy.

Evaṃ bhavaṅgapātābhāve kāraṇaṃ vatvā puna tadārammaṇābhāvaṃ dassento āha “mahaggata”ntiādi. Tattheva paṭisiddhanti “parittārammaṇo dhammo mahaggatārammaṇassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo”ti vacanābhāvato tattheva paṭṭhāne paṭisiddhaṃ. Kiṃ nu kātabbanti kiṃ kātabbaṃ. Na hi sakkā ettakena “acittako”ti vattunti adhippāyo. Ettha ca mahaggatārammaṇameva domanassajavanaṃ nidassanavasena vuttaṃ. Iṭṭhārammaṇabhūte pana buddhādiārammaṇepi domanassajavane javite somanassapaṭisandhikassa tadārammaṇasambhavo, bhavaṅgapāto vā natthi.

Having thus stated the reason for the absence of a lapse into the life-continuum, showing again the absence of registering, he says, “exalted,” etc. It is rejected in that very place, for in the Paṭṭhāna, due to the absence of the statement, “A state with a sense-sphere object is a condition for a state with an exalted object by way of kamma condition,” it is rejected. “What, then, is to be done?” means: what is to be done? The intention is: it is not possible on this account to say he is “without consciousness.” And here, an impulsion of displeasure with an exalted object is mentioned only by way of an example. However, when an impulsion of displeasure has occurred even in regard to a desirable object, such as the Buddha, etc., for one with a rebirth-linking consciousness accompanied by joy, there is no possibility of registering, nor is there a lapse into the life-continuum.

464-5. Iṭṭhārammaṇe upekkhāsahagatatadārammaṇassa domanassānantarañca somanassassa abhāvato “upekkhāsahitā hetū”tiādinā ācariyena vutte puna codako anubandhanto āha “āvajjanaṃ kimassā”ti. Ācariyo pana kimettha āvajjanagavesanena, tena vināva idaṃ cittaṃ uppajjatīti dīpento āha “natthi ta”nti. Puna codako āvajjanena vinā cittappavattiṃ avisahanto āha “taṃ jāyate katha”nti. Evaṃ pana vutte ācariyo kimettha āvajjanena, kiñca āvajjanena vinā cittappavatti natthīti idaṃ na ekantikanti dīpetuṃ nirāvajjanacittānaṃ sambhavaṃ dassento [M 2.0055] āha “bhavaṅgāvajjanāna”ntiādi, bhavaṅgāvajjanānaṃ kiṃ āvajjanaṃ, nanu natthevāti adhippāyo. Nanu ca bhavaṅgāvajjanāni tāva sakasakavisayesu ninnattā [V 2.0041] āvajjanena vinā uppattiyaṃ bahulaṃ ciṇṇattāva uppajjanti, ayaṃ pana kathaṃ uppajjatīti idaṃ anuyogaṃ sandhāya puna nirāvajjanacittāni dassento āha “maggassā”tiādi. Maggassa lokuttaramaggassa cittassa. Anantarassa phalassa cāti maggānantarassa phalassa ca atthāya kiṃ āvajjananti sambandho. Evaṃ natthīti yathā etesaṃ, evametassāpi natthi.

464-5. Because, in regard to a desirable object, there is no registering consciousness accompanied by equanimity, and because of the absence of joy immediately after displeasure, when the teacher said, “The causes accompanied by equanimity,” etc., the questioner, pursuing the matter, asked: “What is its adverting?” The teacher, however, clarifying, “What is the use of seeking an adverting here? This consciousness arises even without it,” said: “It does not have one.” Again the questioner, unable to tolerate a cognitive process without adverting, asked: “How does it arise?” When this was said, the teacher, in order to show that the statement “there is no cognitive process without adverting” is not absolute, and to demonstrate the possibility of consciousnesses without adverting, said: “Of the life-continuum and adverting,” etc. The intention is: What adverting is there for the life-continuum and for adverting? Surely there is none. Now, the life-continuum and adverting, being inclined to their respective objects, arise without adverting because they are frequently practiced. Referring to the question, “But how does this one arise?”, to again show consciousnesses without adverting, he says: “Of the path,” etc. “Of the path” means of the supramundane path consciousness. “And of the immediately following fruit”: the connection is, for the fruit immediately following the path, what adverting is there? Thus, “there is none”: just as there is none for these, so too there is none for this.

Ānandācariyo panettha ariyamaggacittaṃ, maggānantarāni phalāni ca parikammāvajjanena sāvajjanāni samānāni asatipi nirāvajjanuppattiyaṃ ninnādibhāve uppattiyā nidassanamattavasena vuttānīti vaṇṇeti. Ayaṃ hissa adhippāyo – yadi hi nibbānārammaṇāvajjanābhāvaṃ sandhāya vuttāni siyuṃ, gotrabhuvodānāni dassitabbāni siyuṃ teheva etesaṃ nirāvajjanatāsiddhito, phalasamāpattikāle ca “parittārammaṇaṃ mahaggatārammaṇaṃ anulomaṃ phalasamāpattiyā anantarapaccayena paccayo”ti vacanato samānārammaṇāvajjanarahitattā maggānantarāni phalacittānīti evaṃ samāpattiphalacittāni na vajjetabbāni siyuṃ, gotrabhuvodānāni pana yadipi nibbāne ciṇṇāni, samudācitāni ca na honti, ārammaṇantare ciṇṇasamudācitāneva. Phalasamāpatticittāni ca maggavīthito uddhaṃ tadatthaṃ parikammasabbhāvāti tesaṃ gahaṇaṃ na kataṃ. Anulomānantarañca phalasamāpatticittaṃ ciṇṇasamudācitaṃ, na nevasaññānāsaññānantaraṃ maggānantarassa viya tadatthaṃ parikammābhāvāti “nirodhā vuṭṭhahantassā”ti tañca nidassitanti.

The teacher Ānanda, however, explains here that the noble path consciousness and the fruits immediately following the path, though they have adverting by way of preliminary adverting, are mentioned by way of being a mere example, because they arise even when there is no state of inclination, etc., in an arising without adverting. This is his intention: If they were mentioned with reference to the absence of an adverting that takes Nibbāna as object, then change-of-lineage and purification should have been shown, since their nature of being without adverting is established by those very moments. And at the time of the attainment of fruition, because it is said, “A sense-sphere object, an exalted object, and conformity are a condition for the attainment of fruition by way of proximity condition,” the fruit consciousnesses immediately following the path, being devoid of an adverting with the same object—thus the fruit consciousnesses of attainment should not be excluded. But as to change-of-lineage and purification, although they are practiced in regard to Nibbāna, they are not accumulated; they are practiced and accumulated only in regard to another object. And the fruit-attainment consciousnesses, being subsequent to the path process, have a preliminary action for that purpose, so they were not included. And the fruit-attainment consciousness immediately following conformity is practiced and accumulated; it is not like the one immediately following the path after the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, as there is no preliminary action for that purpose. And thus, “of one emerging from cessation”—that too is shown as an example.

467. “Kimassārammaṇa”nti vatvā nirāvajjanabhāvaṃ viya anārammaṇabhāvampi vadeyyāti tabbhāvadassanena attano vacanaṃ [M 2.0056] sādhento āha “vinā ārammaṇenā”tiādi. Yaṃ kiñcīti yaṃ kiñci paricitapubbaṃ ārammaṇaṃ ārabbha. Nanu ca tadārammaṇikaṃ siyāti vuttaṃ, tadārammaṇañca javanārammaṇameva gaṇhāti itarathā tadārammaṇabhāvāyogatoti kathamassā parittārammaṇanti? Saccaṃ, kāmāvacaravipākacittānaṃ ekantaparittārammaṇattā nāssā mahaggatārammaṇabhāvo yutto, “tadārammaṇa”nti ca tadārammaṇaṭṭhāne uppattiṃ gahetvā vuttaṃ, na tassā tadārammaṇakiccasambhavato. Kena carahi kiccenāyaṃ uppajjatīti? Tadārammaṇakiccaṃ tāva yathāvuttakāraṇatova natthi, nāpi santīraṇakiccaṃ tathā appavattanato. Paṭisandhicutīsu vattabbameva natthi. Pārisesato pana bhavassa aṅgabhāvato bhavaṅgakiccanti yuttaṃ siyā, paṭisandhibhūtameva [V 2.0042] cittaṃ bhavaṅganti idaṃ yebhuyyavasena vuccatīti. Ācariyadhammapālattherenāpi hi ayamattho dassitova.

467. Lest, after the question 'What is its object?', one might say it has no object just as it is without adverting, the teacher, to establish his own statement by showing that it does have an object, says: 'Without an object,' etc. 'Whatever' refers to any previously familiar object. But would it not then be a tadārammaṇa consciousness? Tadārammaṇa takes only the object of the javana; otherwise, it would not qualify as tadārammaṇa. So how can it have a sense-sphere object? True, since the sense-sphere resultant consciousnesses exclusively take sense-sphere objects, it is not fitting for it to have a sublime object. 'Tadārammaṇa' is said with reference to its arising in the place of tadārammaṇa, not because it performs the function of tadārammaṇa. By what function, then, does this arise? First, the function of tadārammaṇa does not exist for the reason stated, nor does the function of investigating, since it does not proceed in that way. Regarding rebirth-linking and death, there is nothing to be said. However, by way of elimination, it might be proper to say it has the function of bhavaṅga, being a factor of existence, for the rebirth-linking consciousness itself is generally called bhavaṅga. Indeed, this meaning was also shown by the Elder Ācariya Dhammapāla.

468-73. Avijjamāne kārake kathaṃ kassaci nirāvajjanappavattikassa sāvajjanabhāvenāti codanaṃ sandhāya cittaniyāmanibbattametanti dassetuṃ “utubījaniyāmo cā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Utubījaniyāmo cāti utuniyāmo ceva bījaniyāmo ca, utusabhāvaniyāmo bījasabhāvaniyāmoti vuttaṃ hoti. Kammadhammānaṃ niyāmo eva kammadhammaniyāmatā. Ekappahārenāti taṃ taṃ utusamayamanatikkamitvā ekasmiṃyeva kāle. Phalapupphādīti ādi-saddena pallavādīnaṃ saṅgaho. Sabbesanti tasmiṃ samaye phalādinibbattanakānaṃ sabbesaṃ. Taṃtaṃtulyaphalubbhavoti tehi tehi bījehi sadisānaṃ phalānaṃ nibbatti, tesaṃ tesaṃ bījānaṃ anurūpaphalanibbattīti attho. “Kulatthagacchassa uttaraggabhāvo, dakkhiṇavalliyā dakkhiṇarukkhapariharaṇaṃ, sūriyāvattapupphānaṃ sūriyābhimukhabhāvo, māluvalatāya rukkhābhimukhagamana”nti [M 2.0057] evamādīnipi ettheva samodhānaṃ gacchanti. Chiddattanti chiddavantabhāvo, chiddaṃyeva vā. Bījajoti bījasambhavo niyāmo. Yato detīti yato yato paccayabhāvaniyāmato deti. Ayanti ayaṃ attano anurūpassa, sadisassa, visadisassa ca phalassa nibbattane niyāmo. Apica –

468-73. With reference to the objection, 'When there is no agent, how can anything have a process without adverting?', to show that this is produced by the order of the mind, it is said: 'The order of seasons and seeds, etc.' 'The order of seasons and seeds' means both the order of seasons and the order of seeds; that is to say, the order of the nature of seasons and the order of the nature of seeds. The orderliness of kamma-phenomena is simply the order of kamma-phenomena. 'At one stroke' means at that very time, without transgressing that particular season. 'Fruits, flowers, etc.'—by the word 'etc.' shoots and so on are included. 'Of all' means of all those capable of producing fruits and so forth at that time. 'The arising of a fruit corresponding to each' means the production of fruits similar to those respective seeds, that is, the arising of fruits appropriate to those particular seeds. 'The upward growth of the horse gram plant, the southern creeper's encircling of a southern tree, the sunflowers' facing the sun, the māluva creeper's moving towards trees'—such examples as these are also included here. 'Perforation' means the state of being perforated, or simply the perforation itself. 'Seed-born' means the order originating from seeds. 'From which it gives' means from whatever order of conditionality it gives. 'This' means this order in the production of a fruit that is corresponding, similar, or dissimilar to itself. Moreover—

“Na antalikkhe na samuddamajjhe,

Na pabbatānaṃ vivaraṃ pavissa;

Na vijjatī so jagatippadeso,

Yatthaṭṭhito mucceyya pāpakammā”ti. (dha. pa. 127) –

Not in the sky, nor in the middle of the ocean, nor by entering a cleft of the mountains; there is no place on earth to be found where one, abiding, could be freed from an evil deed.

Imissā gāthāya aṭṭhuppattiyaṃ āgataṃ tiṇakalāpassa gahitaaggino uṭṭhahitvā ākāse gacchato kākassa gīvāya paṭimuccanaṃ, nāvikassa bhariyāya vālukaghaṭaṃ kaṇṭhe bandhitvā samuddudake pakkhipanaṃ, pabbatakūṭassa patitvā leṇe vasantānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ dvārapidahananti taṃtaṃkammasarikkhakavipākanibbattanampi kammaniyāmoyevāti veditabbaṃ. Jātiyanti paṭisandhiggahaṇe ceva mātukucchito nikkhamane ca, nidassanamattañcetaṃ abhisambodhidhammacakkappavattanādīsupi medanīkampanādikassa sambhavato. Bodhisattassāti pacchimabhavikabodhisattassa. Medanīkampanādikanti pathavīkampanādikaṃ dvattiṃsapubbanimittaṃ. Visesattamanekampīti pubbanimittato [V 2.0043] aññaṃ tadā pātubhūtaṃ sabbaṃ acchariyaṃ. Uppattāvajjanādīnanti “tvaṃ āvajjanaṃ hohi, tvaṃ dassana”ntiādinā niyuñjakassa abhāvepi taṃtaṃkiccavasena tesaṃ tesaṃ uppatti.

In the origin story of this verse, the incidents of a sheaf of grass that had caught fire, risen up, and was going through the sky getting fastened to a crow's neck; of a sailor's wife tying a pot of sand to her neck and throwing herself into the ocean; and of a mountain peak falling and blocking the door for the bhikkhus dwelling in a cave—the production of results corresponding to these respective kammas should also be understood as precisely the order of kamma. 'At birth' means both at the taking of rebirth-linking and at the exit from the mother's womb. And this is merely an illustration, since the trembling of the earth and so on also occurs at the supreme full enlightenment, the turning of the wheel of Dhamma, and so on. 'Of the Bodhisatta' means of the Bodhisatta in his final existence. 'The trembling of the earth, etc.' means the thirty-two portents, such as the trembling of the earth. 'Its special and manifold nature' means all the marvels, other than the portents, that appeared at that time. 'The arising of advertence, etc.' means the arising of each of these according to its respective function, even in the absence of a director saying, 'You be advertence! You be seeing!,' and so on.

474. Hadaye andhakāro viyāti hadayandhakāro, sammohoti attho, tassa viddhaṃsanaṃ pahānakaraṇanti hadayandhakāraviddhaṃsanaṃ. Payuttoti anupādāparinibbānaṃ appatvā [M 2.0058] anosakkamānena vīriyena vīriyavā. Mohandhakārāpagamanti arahattamāha.

474. ‘Darkness in the heart’ is heart-darkness; the meaning is delusion. Its shattering, the act of abandoning it, is ‘the shattering of heart-darkness.’ ‘Striving’ means one who is energetic, with energy that does not retreat before attaining final Nibbāna without residue of grasping. ‘The removal of the darkness of delusion’ refers to arahantship.

Iti abhidhammatthavikāsiniyā nāma

Thus in the Abhidhammatthavikāsinī,

Abhidhammāvatārasaṃvaṇṇanāya

the commentary on the Abhidhammāvatāra,

Vipākacittappavattiniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

the commentary on the Exposition of the Process of Resultant Consciousness is concluded.

8. Aṭṭhamo paricchedo

8. The Eighth Chapter

Pakiṇṇakaniddesavaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Exposition of the Miscellaneous

475-6. Idāni yathāvuttānaṃ sabbesampi cittānaṃ pākaṭabhāvatthaṃ –

475-6. Now, in order to make clear all the cittas that have been mentioned—

“Suttaṃ dovāriko ceva,

Gāmillo ambagoḷiyo;

Jaccandho pīṭhasappī ca,

Upanissayamatthaso”ti. (dha. sa. aṭṭha. 498 vipākuddhārakathā) –

“The thread and the doorkeeper, the villager, the mango-ball; the one born blind and the snake on the stool, and support: thus for the sake of the meaning.”

Aṭṭhakathāya āgatamātikāya vasena pakiṇṇakanayaṃ dassetuṃ “idāni panā”tiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha manasanti cittānaṃ. “Mānasa”ntipi paṭhanti, taṃ na sundaraṃ. Panthamakkaṭakoti pāṇakapaṭaṅgādīnaṃ [V 2.0044] sañcaraṇaṭṭhāne jālaṃ pasāretvā tesaṃ maggarakkhaṇato “panthamakkaṭako”ti laddhanāmo uṇṇanābhi. Disāsu pana pañcasūti upametabbānaṃ pañcapasādānaṃ vasena vuttaṃ. Tatthāti magge, tattha jālamajjheti vā sambandho. Suttaṃ pasāretvāti jālabandhanamāha.

The passage beginning “Now then,” etc., is introduced to explain the miscellaneous method by means of the matrix that comes in the Commentary. Herein, 'manasā' means 'of cittas.' Some also read 'mānasa,' but that is not good. 'Panthamakkaṭako' (path-spider) refers to the spider (uṇṇanābhi), which gets its name from guarding the path by spreading a web in the roaming place of creatures such as insects and moths. 'In the five directions' is stated with reference to the five sense faculties that are the basis for the comparison. 'Therein' refers to the path, or the connection is with 'in the middle of the web.' 'Spreading the thread' refers to the weaving of the web.

478-80. Nti rudhiramāha. Disāsu dutiyādīsu sutte…pe… ghaṭṭiteti sambandho. “Pasādā pañca daṭṭhabbā”tiādi upamāsaṃsandanaṃ[M 2.0059]. Cittaṃ…pe… viyāti hadayavatthuṃ nissāya pavattamānacittaṃ jālamajjhe nipannamakkaṭako viya daṭṭhabbaṃ.

478-80. 'Nti' refers to blood (rudhira). In the second and other directions, on the thread… (etc.) …when it is struck: this is the connection. The passage beginning, “The five sense faculties should be seen,” is the application of the simile. The citta… (etc.) …like: the citta that arises depending on the heart-base should be seen as like a spider lying in the middle of the web.

482-5. Pasādaghaṭṭananti pasāde ghaṭṭitaṃ. Bhavaṅgāvaṭṭananti bhavaṅgaṃ āvaṭṭentaṃ. Dhammato aññā kāci kiriyā nāma natthīti dhammameva calanena saha upameti. Suttānusāraṃvāti suttānusārena gamanaṃ viya. Javanassa ārammaṇarasānubhavanato tassa pavatti yūsapānena saddhiṃ upametvā vuttā. Vatthuṃyevāti yathā purimacittāni hadayavatthunissitāni pasādavatthuṃ anugatāni aññārammaṇāni ca honti, na evaṃ bhavaṅgaṃ. Taṃ pana vatthārammaṇantararahitaṃ kevalaṃ hadayavatthumeva nissāya pavattatīti dīpeti. Parivattananti puna bhavaṅgabhāvena parivattanaṃ. Bhavaṅgāvajjanādīnaṃ dhammato bhedepi santativasena ekattaṃ gahetvā ekeneva makkaṭakena upamāsaṃsandanaṃ vuttaṃ.

482-5. 'Striking the sense faculty' means striking on the sense faculty. 'Causing the bhavaṅga to turn' means making the life-continuum turn. Since there is no activity apart from the mental object itself, it is compared with mere movement. 'Following the thread' is like going along the thread. Because javana experiences the flavor of the object, its occurrence is compared to drinking broth. 'Only the base itself': this explains that while preceding cittas are dependent on the heart-base, follow the sense-bases, and have other objects, the bhavaṅga is not like that. It arises dependent only on the heart-base, devoid of another base or object. 'Revolving' means revolving again in the state of bhavaṅga. Although bhavaṅga, adverting, etc., are different as individual states, their unity is taken on account of their continuity, and the application of the simile is stated with a single spider.

486-90. Upamā eva opammaṃ. Tato pasādavatthuto cittāti sambandho. Dīpitaṃ iminā opammena. Ekekārammaṇanti rūpādīsu pañcasu ekekaṃ ārammaṇaṃ. Sabbasoti sabbesu cakkhādīsu yattha katthacīti attho. Idāni ekekārammaṇassa dvīsu dvīsu āpāthagamanaṃ pakāsetuṃ “rūpaṃ cakkhupasādamhī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Khe ākāse gacchatīti khago, pakkhi. Sākhinoti rukkhassa.

486-90. A simile (upamā) is a comparison (opammaṃ). From that, the connection is 'citta from the sense-faculty base.' This is illustrated by this comparison. 'A single object' means one object among the five, such as form, etc. 'In all' means in any of the sense faculties, such as the eye, etc., whatsoever. Now, to show how a single object comes into the range of two at a time, the passage beginning, 'Form in the eye-sensitivity…' is stated. Khaga is one that goes in the sky (khe), a bird. Sākhino means 'of a tree.'

492-3. Rūpassāti sambandhe sāmivacanaṃ, tassa pana ghaṭṭanaṃ, āpāthagamanampi cāti dvīhi saha sambandho. Pasādassāti kammatthe sāmivacanaṃ, atthato āpāthagamanampi cāti sambandho. Ārammaṇavasena, āpāthaṃ āgacchantassapi pasādaghaṭṭanena ca bhavaṅgacalanassa paccayabhāvena āpāthaṃ viya upagamananti attho.

492-3. 'Of form' (rūpassa) is the genitive case indicating relation; it is connected with two things: its impinging and its coming into range. 'Of the sense faculty' (pasādassa) is the genitive case in the sense of object; in meaning, it is connected with 'coming into range.' The meaning is: by way of object, for that which is coming into range, its approach is considered as coming into range because the impinging on the sense faculty and the vibration of the bhavaṅga are the condition for it.

494-5. Tatoti [M 2.0060] bhavaṅgacalanato paraṃ, kusalaṃ javanaṃ cittanti kāmāvacarakusalajavanacittaṃ[V 2.0045]. Akusalameva vāti vā-saddena kiriyābyākatacittampi saṅgaṇhāti. Ettha siyā – ko panetaṃ javanaṃ kusalatāya vā akusalatāya vā niyametīti? Yonisomanasikāro ceva ayonisomanasikāro ca. Yassa hi catucakkasampadāvasena yonisomanasikāro pavattati, āvajjanaṃ, voṭṭhabbanañca yonisova āvaṭṭeti, vavatthāpeti ca, tassa akusaluppatti natthi. Yassa pana vuttavipariyāyena ayonisomanasikāro ca hoti, āvajjanaṃ, voṭṭhabbanañca ayoniso ca āvaṭṭeti, vavatthāpeti ca, tassa kusalajavanuppatti natthi, tasmā yonisomanasikāro kusalatāya, ayonisomanasikāro akusalatāya ca niyametīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Kiriyājavanaṃ pana arahattameva niyameti. Keci pana “kiriyājavanaṃ pana manasikāro ca niyameti. Yathā hi āvajjanaṃ kusalākusalānaṃ visuṃ visuṃ paccayo hoti, evaṃ kiriyājavanassāpī”ti vadanti.

494-5. 'Thereafter' means after the vibration of the bhavaṅga. 'Wholesome impulsion-citta' means sense-sphere wholesome impulsion-citta. Or 'only unwholesome': by the word 'or,' functional-indeterminate citta is also included. Here the question might arise: 'What determines this impulsion to be wholesome or unwholesome?' It is wise attention and unwise attention. For one in whom wise attention occurs by means of the fourfold wheel, adverting and determining also turn and determine wisely, and for him no unwholesome state arises. But for one in whom, in the opposite way, unwise attention occurs, adverting and determining also turn and determine unwisely, and for him no wholesome impulsion arises. Therefore, it should be understood that wise attention determines wholesomeness, and unwise attention determines unwholesomeness. Functional impulsion, however, is determined only by arahantship. But some say: 'Functional impulsion is also determined by attention. For just as adverting is a distinct condition for wholesome and unwholesome states, so is it for functional impulsion.'

497. Dovārikopamādīnīti ettha eko rājā sayanagato niddāyati, tassa paricārako pāde parimajjanto nisīdi, badhiradovāriko dvāre ṭhito, tayo paṭihārā sayanassa, dvārassa ca majjhe paṭipāṭiyā ṭhitā. Atheko paccantavāsī manusso paṇṇākāraṃ ādāya dvāraṃ ākoṭesi, badhiradovāriko saddaṃ na suṇāti, pādaparimajjako saññaṃ akāsi, tāya saññāya dvāraṃ vivaritvā passi, paṭhamapaṭihāro paṇṇākāraṃ gahetvā dutiyassa adāsi, dutiyo tatiyassa, tatiyo rañño, rājā paribhuñji. Tattha rājā viya javanaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ, pādaparimajjako viya āvajjanaṃ, badhiradovāriko viya cakkhuviññāṇaṃ, tayo paṭihārā [M 2.0061] viya sampaṭicchanādīni tīṇi vīthicittāni, paccantavāsino paṇṇākāraṃ ādāya dvārākoṭanaṃ viya ārammaṇassa pasādaghaṭṭanaṃ, pādaparimajjakena saññāya dinnakālo viya kiriyāmanodhātuyā bhavaṅgassa āvaṭṭitakālo, tena dinnasaññāya badhiradovārikassa dvāravivarakālo viya cakkhuviññāṇassa ārammaṇe dassanakiccasādhanakālo, paṭhamapaṭihārena paṇṇākārassa gahitakālo viya vipākamanodhātuyā ārammaṇassa sampaṭicchitakālo, paṭhamena dutiyassa dinnakālo viya vipākamanoviññāṇadhātuyā ārammaṇassa santīritakālo, dutiyena tatiyassa dinnakālo viya kiriyāmanoviññāṇadhātuyā ārammaṇassa vavatthāpitakālo, tatiyena rañño dinnakālo viya voṭṭhabbanena javanassa niyyātitakālo, rañño paribhogakālo viya javanassa ārammaṇarasānubhavanakāloti ayaṃ dovārikopamā.

497. The Simile of the Doorkeeper and others: Here, a king lies asleep in his bed. His attendant sits massaging his feet, while a deaf doorkeeper stands at the door. Three gatekeepers stand in succession between the bed and the door. Then a man from the borderlands, bringing a gift, comes and knocks on the door. The deaf doorkeeper does not hear the sound. The foot-massager makes a sign. With that sign, the doorkeeper opens the door and looks. The first gatekeeper takes the gift and gives it to the second, the second to the third, and the third to the king, who enjoys it. Here, the king should be seen as javana; the foot-massager as adverting; the deaf doorkeeper as eye-consciousness; the three gatekeepers as the three process-cittas of receiving, investigating, and determining. The knocking on the door by the man from the borderlands with his gift is like the impinging of an object on a sense faculty. The time when the foot-massager gives the sign is like the time when the functional mind-element causes the bhavaṅga to turn. The time when the deaf doorkeeper opens the door on account of the sign is like the time when eye-consciousness accomplishes the function of seeing the object. The time when the first gatekeeper takes the gift is like the time when the resultant mind-element receives the object. The time when the first gives it to the second is like the time when the resultant mind-consciousness-element investigates the object. The time when the second gives it to the third is like the time when the functional mind-consciousness-element determines the object. The time when the third gives it to the king is like the time when determining delivers the object to javana. The time when the king enjoys it is like the time when javana experiences the flavor of the object. This is the Simile of the Doorkeeper.

“Idaṃ [V 2.0046] pana opammaṃ kiṃ dīpetī”tiādi ucchuyantūpamāya vuttanayena veditabbā. Sambahulā gāmadārakā antaravīthiyaṃ paṃsuṃ kīḷanti, tatthekassa hatthe kahāpaṇo paṭihaññi. So “mayhaṃ hatthe paṭihataṃ, kiṃ nu kho eta”nti āha. Atheko “paṇḍaraṃ eta”nti āha. Aparo saha paṃsunā gāḷhaṃ gaṇhi. Añño “puthulaṃ caturassaṃ eta”nti āha. Aparo “kahāpaṇo eso”ti āha. Atha āharitvā mātu adaṃsu, sā kamme upanesi. Tattha sambahulānaṃ dārakānaṃ antaravīthiyaṃ kīḷantānaṃ sannisinnakālo viya cittappavatti daṭṭhabbā, kahāpaṇassa hatthe paṭihatakālo viya ārammaṇena pasādassa ghaṭṭitakālo, “kiṃ nu kho eta”nti vuttakālo viya taṃ ārammaṇaṃ gahetvā kiriyāmanodhātuyā bhavaṅgassa āvaṭṭitakālo, “paṇḍaraṃ eta”nti vuttakālo viya cakkhuviññāṇena dassanakiccassa [M 2.0062] sādhitakālo, saha paṃsunā gāḷhaṃ gahitakālo viya vipākamanodhātuyā ārammaṇassa sampaṭicchitakālo, “puthulaṃ caturassaṃ eta”nti vuttakālo viya vipākamanoviññāṇadhātuyā ārammaṇassa santīritakālo, “kahāpaṇo eso”ti vuttakālo viya kiriyāmanoviññāṇadhātuyā ārammaṇassa vavatthāpitakālo, mātarā kamme upanītakālo viya javanassa ārammaṇarasānubhavanaṃ veditabbanti ayaṃ gāmadārakopamā.

The passage beginning, 'But what does this simile illustrate?' should be understood in the way stated for the simile of the sugarcane mill. Many village boys were playing with sand in a street. A coin struck the hand of one of them. He said, 'Something struck my hand. What could it be?' Another said, 'It is white.' Another grasped it tightly with the sand. Another said, 'It is broad and square.' Another said, 'This is a coin.' Then they brought it and gave it to their mother, and she put it to use. Here, the time when the many boys were sitting together playing in the street should be seen as the occurrence of a cognitive process. The time when the coin struck the hand is like the time when the object impinges on the sense faculty. The time when it was said, 'What could it be?' is like the time when the bhavaṅga is turned by the functional mind-element taking up that object. The time when it was said, 'It is white,' is like the time when the function of seeing is accomplished by eye-consciousness. The time when it was grasped tightly with the sand is like the time when the object is received by the resultant mind-element. The time when it was said, 'It is broad and square,' is like the time when the object is investigated by the resultant mind-consciousness-element. The time when it was said, 'This is a coin,' is like the time when the object is determined by the functional mind-consciousness-element. The time when the mother put it to use should be understood as the experiencing of the object's flavor by javana. This is the Simile of the Village Boys.

Idaṃ opammaṃ kiṃ dīpeti? Kiriyāmanodhātu adisvāva bhavaṅgaṃ āvaṭṭeti, vipākamanodhātu adisvāva sampaṭicchati, vipākamanoviññāṇadhātu adisvāva santīreti, kiriyāmanoviññāṇadhātu adisvāva vavatthāpeti, javanaṃ adisvāva ārammaṇarasaṃ anubhavati, ekantena pana cakkhuviññāṇameva dassanakiccaṃ sādhetīti dīpeti. Jaccandhapīṭhasappīupamā upari āgamissati.

What does this simile illustrate? It illustrates this: The functional mind-element turns the bhavaṅga without seeing. The resultant mind-element receives without seeing. The resultant mind-consciousness-element investigates without seeing. The functional mind-consciousness-element determines without seeing. Javana experiences the flavor of the object without seeing. It is exclusively eye-consciousness that accomplishes the function of seeing. The simile of the one born blind and the snake on the stool will come later.

498-509. Ettakā upamā saṅgahetvā “dovārikopamādīnī”ti vatvā “upanissayamatthaso”ti ettha upanissayabhāvaṃ pakāsetuṃ “asambhedenā”tiādimāha. Asambhedenāti avinaṭṭhabhāvena, vātapittādīhi anupahatabhāvena ca. Vātapittādiupahatampi hi cakkhuviññāṇassa paccayabhāvānupagamanato sambhinnameva nāma hoti, pañcindriyānaṃ atthikkhaṇeyeva nissayabhāvūpagamanato khaṇavasena asambhedopi yujjati. Esa nayo sotapasādādīsupi. Rūpāpāthagamenāti dūre ṭhitassa phalikādīhi antaritassa cakkhuviññāṇuppattiyā paccayo bhavituṃ yogyadese avaṭṭhitavasena rūpassa āpāthagamanena. Evañca [V 2.0047] katvā dūre ṭhitaṃ, parammukhe ṭhitampi dibbacakkhussa āpāthagatameva [M 2.0063] nāma hoti. Ālokanissayenāpīti rūpāvabhāsanasamatthaālokasaṅkhātanissayena. Āloke sati sambhavo cettha ālokanissayatā, na ālokassa nissayapaccayattā. Manakkārova hetu manakkārahetu, tena saha vattatīti samanakkārahetu. Tena ālokanissitaṃ dasseti. Sametehīti saṃyuttehi ekībhūtehi, na ekassapi virahenāti attho.

498-509. Having collected these similes and said, "like the gatekeeper, etc.," in order to explain the nature of support in the phrase "in accordance with the meaning of support," he said, "unimpaired," etc. "Unimpaired" means in an undestroyed state, and unafflicted by wind, bile, etc. For even if afflicted by wind, bile, etc., it is called "impaired" because it does not become a condition for eye-consciousness. But since the five sense faculties become a basis at the very moment of their existence, non-impairment is also applicable on a momentary basis. This same method applies to the ear sensitivity, etc. "By the coming of a form into range" means by a form's coming into range through being situated in a suitable place to be a condition for the arising of eye-consciousness, even if it is distant or obstructed by crystal, etc. And thus, even what is far away or turned away is said to be within the range of the divine eye. "And by dependence on light" means by dependence on what is called light, which is capable of illuminating form. Here, dependence on light is the possibility of its arising when light is present, not because light is a support condition. Attention itself is the cause, hence 'attention-cause'; it occurs together with that, hence 'with-attention-cause'. By this, he shows it is dependent on light. "By 'united'" means conjoined, unified; the meaning is, not with the absence of even one.

Ākāsanissayenāti kaṇṇacchiddasaṅkhātaākāsanissayena. Teneva hi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “na hi pihitakaṇṇacchiddassa sotaviññāṇaṃ pavattatī”ti vuttaṃ. Bāhirākāsampi pana icchitameva. Tathā hi avivare gehe nisīditvā vuccamānānaṃ bahi ṭhitā na suṇanti. Vāyosannissayenāti nāsikacchiddaṃ pavisanavāyusannissayena. Āposannissayenāti kheḷasaṅkhātaāposannissayena. Pathavīsannissayenāti kāyapasādavatthussa pathavīdhātusannissayena. Manoviññāṇanti javanamanoviññāṇaṃ.

"By dependence on space" means by dependence on the space reckoned as the ear orifice. For this very reason it is said in the commentary: "Indeed, ear-consciousness does not arise for one whose ear orifice is blocked." But external space is also intended. For example, those standing outside do not hear those speaking while sitting in a closed house. "By dependence on air" means by dependence on the air entering the nostril orifice. "By dependence on water" means by dependence on the water element reckoned as saliva. "By dependence on earth" means by dependence on the earth element, which is the basis of bodily sensitivity. "Mind-consciousness" means impulsion mind-consciousness.

510-11. Mano…pe… veditabbanti “asambhedā manassā”ti ettha vuttaṃ mano bhavaṅgacittanti veditabbaṃ. Taṃ pana cutivasena niruddhampi kiriyāmayacittassa paccayabhāvaṃ anupagantvā kevalaṃ bhavaṅgappavattivasena mandathāmagataṃ hutvā pavattanampi sambhinnamevāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Nāyaṃ sabbattha gacchatīti catuvokāre alabbhanato. Tenāha “bhavaṃ tu pañcavokāra”ntiādi. Tattha pañcannaṃ khandhānaṃ vokāro etthāti pañcavokāro. Hoti hi bhinnādhikaraṇampi aññapadatthasamāso yathā “urasilomo”ti. Atha vā yathāpaccayaṃ pañcahi khandhehi vokarīyatīti pañcavokāro. “Atthato”ti evamādikaṃ padaṃ cakkhādīni dassanādikiccānīti ettakameva sandhāya vuttaṃ, na aññaṃ kiñci visesananti na tattha vinicchayo vutto.

510-11. "The mind... should be understood": the mind mentioned here in the phrase "the mind being unimpaired" should be understood as the life-continuum consciousness. It should be seen that even though it has ceased by way of death-consciousness, it does not become a condition for a functional consciousness, but its proceeding, having become weak in force, merely by way of the life-continuum process, is still to be regarded as impaired. This does not go everywhere because it is unobtainable in the four-constituent existence. Therefore it is said: "But existence is five-constituent," and so on. Here, "five-constituent" (pañcavokāra) means that in which there are five constituents. For there can be a possessive compound with a different referent, as in "hairy-chested." Or, it is called "five-constituent" because it is constituted by the five aggregates according to conditions. The phrase "In meaning," etc., is said only with reference to the functions of seeing, etc., of the eye, etc., and not to any other special quality; therefore no determination is stated there.

512-4. Sabbānīti [M 2.0064] kāmāvacarādibhedaṃ anāmasitvā sabbāni. Kammanti paṭisandhinibbattakā upapajjavedanīyabhūtā, aparāpariyavedanīyabhūtā vā cetanā. Kammanimittanti yaṃ vatthuṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā āyūhanakāle kammaṃ āyūhati, taṃ dānūpakaraṇādikaṃ, pāṇaghātopakaraṇādikañca. Gatinimittanti bhavantaramupapajjitabbabhavapariyāpannavaṇṇāyatanaṃ, taṃ pana sugatiyaṃ manussaloke nibbattantassa rattakambalasadisamātukucchivaṇṇavasena, devaloke nibbattantassa uyyānakapparukkhavaṇṇavasena, duggatiyaṃ nibbattantassa [V 2.0048] aggijālādivaṇṇavasena, petatiracchānayonīsu petatiracchānānaṃ nibaddhasañcaraṇaṭṭhānapariyāpannatāvaṇṇavasena ca daṭṭhabbaṃ. “Tividha”nti idaṃ yathāsambhavavasena vuttaṃ, rūpārūpasambandhīnaṃ pana kammanimittameva ārammaṇaṃ hoti. Tathā hi mahaggatavipākāni ekantena kammasadisārammaṇāni vuttāni.

512-4. "All": all without specifying the distinctions of sense-sphere, etc. "Kamma": the volition that produces rebirth-linking and is either experienceable in the next life or experienceable in some subsequent life. "Kamma-sign": the object taken as a basis at the time of accumulating kamma, such as the requisites for giving or the instruments for killing living beings. "Destiny-sign": the base of visible form pertaining to the existence in which one is to be reborn. For one being reborn in a good destination, in the human world, this should be seen as the color of the mother's womb, which resembles a red blanket; for one being reborn in the deva world, as the color of a park or a wish-fulfilling tree. For one being reborn in a bad destination, it appears as the color of flames, etc. For rebirth among ghosts or animals, it appears as the color pertaining to the places constantly frequented by ghosts and animals. "Threefold": this is said according to possibility. For those connected with the form and formless realms, however, only the kamma-sign is the object. For it is said that the sublime resultants invariably have an object similar to the kamma.

Paccuppannamatītaṃ vāti khaṇavasena paccuppannamatītaṃ vā. Tattha gatinimittaṃ ekantena paccuppannameva, kammanimittaṃ paccuppannamatītaṃ vā, kammaṃ pana atītameva. Anāgatārammaṇaṃ pana paccuppannakammanimittagatinimittaṃ viya anāpāthagatattā, atītakammakammanimittaṃ viya ananubhūtattā ca vibhūtaṃ hutvā nopatiṭṭhātīti atisantabhāvena pavattamānā paṭisandhi taṃ ārabbha pavattituṃ na sakkotīti vuttaṃ “natthi anāgata”nti. Mahaggatapaṭisandhīnaṃ ekantena kammasadisārammaṇabhāvena kammassa viya atītanavattabbārammaṇattā na tāsaṃ visuṃ ārammaṇaṃ uddhaṭaṃ. Tattha dutiyacatutthārūpapaṭisandhīnaṃ atītameva ārammaṇaṃ itarāsaṃ navattabbanti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

"Present or past": in terms of the moment, it is present or past. Herein, the destiny-sign is exclusively present; the kamma-sign is present or past; but the kamma is exclusively past. A future object, however, does not appear clearly because, like a present kamma-sign or destiny-sign, it has not come into focus, and because, like a past kamma or kamma-sign, it has not been experienced. Therefore, because it proceeds in an extremely subtle state, rebirth-linking is unable to take it as its object. Hence it is said: "There is no future." For the sublime rebirth-linkings, since their object is invariably similar to the kamma and, like the kamma, their object must be spoken of as past, a separate object is not specified for them. Herein, it should be understood that for the second and fourth immaterial rebirth-linkings the object is exclusively past, while for the others it is unspecifiable.

517-20. Mahāvipākānaṃ paṭisandhādicatukiccavaseneva pavattanato rūpārūpabhave paṭisandhibhavaṅgacutivasena taṃtaṃvipākasseva pavattito, tadārammaṇassa ca abhāvena tattha na labbhatīti āha “mahāpākā…pe… dvaye”ti. Aniṭṭharūpānaṃ [M 2.0065] brahmaloke asambhavepi tattha ṭhatvā idha aniṭṭhārammaṇaṃ passantānaṃ akusalavipākāni na uppajjantīti na vattabbanti rūpabhavepi santīraṇattayaṃ vuttaṃ. Abhidhammatthasaṅgahasaccasaṅkhepādīsupi hi imināva adhippāyena rūpaloke akusalavipākappavatti dassitā. Apare pana “kāmabhave santīraṇattayaṃ, rūpabhave santīraṇadvayanti yathālābhavasena yojetabba”nti vadanti.

517-20. Because the great resultants proceed only by way of the four functions beginning with rebirth-linking, and because in the form and formless existences only the respective resultants of those planes proceed by way of rebirth-linking, life-continuum, and death, and because of the absence of registration, they are not obtained there. Hence it is said: "The great resultants... in the two." Even though undesirable forms do not exist in the Brahma-world, it should not be said that unwholesome resultants do not arise for those who, while abiding there, see an undesirable object here; thus the triad of investigating consciousnesses is said to exist even in the form existence. Indeed, in the Abhidhammatthasaṅgaha, Saccasaṅkhepa, and other texts, the occurrence of unwholesome resultants in the form world is shown with this same intention. Others, however, say: "In the sense-sphere existence there are three investigating consciousnesses, in the form existence there are two; this should be connected according to what is obtained."

Kadācipīti parittārammaṇesu parittajavanānaṃ uppādepi. “Bījassābhāvato”ti rūpārūpabhavadvaye tadārammaṇābhāvassa kāraṇaṃ vatvā tameva pakāsetuṃ “paṭisandhibīja”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Paṭisandhiyeva bījabhūtanti paṭisandhibījaṃ. Tassāti tadārammaṇassa.

"At any time": even when limited impulsions arise in relation to limited objects. "Because of the absence of a seed": having stated this as the reason for the absence of registration in the two existences, the form and formless, in order to explain that very point, "rebirth-linking seed," etc., is said. Rebirth-linking itself is the seed, hence "rebirth-linking seed." "Of that" means of that registration.

521. Yadi evaṃ cakkhuviññāṇādīnampi kāmāvacarapaṭisandhibījattā tattha abhāvo āpajjatīti codento āha “cakkhuviññāṇādīna”ntiādi. Indriyānanti cakkhuviññāṇādīnaṃ vatthudvārabhūtānaṃ cakkhādīnamindriyānaṃ. Pavattānubhāvatoti tesaṃ tattha atthitānubhāvato[V 2.0049]. Ayañhettha adhippāyo – cakkhusotaviññāṇānaṃ vatthubhūtāni cakkhusotindriyāni tattha pavattantīti tesaṃ pavattiānubhāvato cakkhusotaviññāṇāni pavattanti. Sati ca tesaṃ pavattiyaṃ vīthicittuppādo niyatoti cakkhuviññāṇādīnaṃ viya sampaṭicchanasantīraṇānampi tattha sambhavo siddhoti.

521. Raising an objection, he says, "of eye-consciousness, etc.," meaning: if so, since eye-consciousness and so on are also a seed for sense-sphere rebirth-linking, their absence there would follow. "Of the faculties" means of the faculties of the eye, etc., which are the bases and doors for eye-consciousness, etc. "By the power of their proceeding" means by the power of their existence there. This is the intention here: because the eye and ear faculties, which are the bases for eye- and ear-consciousness, proceed there, by the power of their proceeding, eye- and ear-consciousness also proceed. And when they proceed, the arising of a cognitive process is certain; thus the possibility there of receiving and investigating consciousnesses, just like eye-consciousness, etc., is established.

523-4. Akāmāvacaradhammeti kāmāvacaradhammato aññe mahaggatalokuttaradhamme. Nānubandhatīti nānuvattati. Janakaṃ…pe… anubandhatīti yathā nāma gehato nikkhamitvā bahi gantukāmo taruṇadārako attano janakaṃ pitaraṃ vā aññaṃ vā pitusadisaṃ hitakāmaṃ ñātiṃ aṅguliyaṃ gahetvā anubandhati, na aññaṃ rājapurisādiṃ, tathā etampi [M 2.0066] bhavaṅgārammaṇato bahi nikkhamitukāmasabhāgatāya attano janakaṃ paṭhamakusalādikaṃ sadisaṃ vā dutiyakusalādikāmāvacarajavanameva anubandhati, na aññaṃ mahaggataṃ lokuttaranti ayamettha attho. Kusalākusalādinti ādi-ggahaṇena kiriyābyākataṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Ānandācariyo pana paṭṭhāne “kusalākusale niruddhe vipāko tadārammaṇatā uppajjatī”ti (paṭṭhā. 3.1.98) vipākadhammadhammānamevānantaraṃ tadārammaṇaṃ vuttaṃ. Vipphāravantañhi javanaṃ nāvaṃ viya nadīsoto bhavaṅgaṃ anubandhati, na pana chaḷaṅgupekkhāvato santavuttiṃ kiriyājavanaṃ paṇṇapuṭaṃ viya nadīsototi kiriyājavanānantaraṃ tadārammaṇaṃ na icchati, ācariyajotipālattherādayo pana “labbhamānassapi kenaci adhippāyena katthaci avacanaṃ dissati, yathā taṃ dhammasaṅgahe akusalaniddese labbhamānopi adhipati na vutto, tasmā yadi abyākatānantarampi tadārammaṇaṃ vucceyya, tadā voṭṭhabbanānantarampi tassa pavattiṃ maññeyyunti kiriyājavanānantaraṃ tadārammaṇaṃ na vuttaṃ, na pana alabbhanato.
